Aure.Vict.Eutr.li.9.& Bap.Egna.li.1.
units.tr: DIOCLETIAN, a Dalmatian, a freedman of the senator Anulinus, son of a mother named Dioclea, from which town he was also called Diocles, reigned in the year of the world 4247, from the birth of Christ 285. He defeated Carinus, who was hated by all, in battle. But in the second year of his reign, perceiving that so great a burden, too heavy to be borne by one man alone, was pressing upon him, he created Maximian Herculius Augustus and chose him as partner in the empire. In the sixth year he created Constantius Chlorus and Galerius Maximian, also called Maximinus, with the surname Armentarius, Caesars, in Egypt; he took Alexandria after an eight-month siege; he threw Achilleus, who aspired to rule in Alexandria, to the wild beasts. In the twenty-second year of his reign he abdicated at Nicomedia, and Herculius Maximian did so on the same day at Milan. When, growing old on his own estates, he was asked by Herculius and Galerius to take up the empire again, he refused as if shunning some plague, and replied: Would that you could see the vegetables planted by my own hands at Salona; you would surely never think of trying that. So for ten years he lived in private life, relieved of the weight of empire. Yet he wished at some point to be worshipped; he also afflicted the Christians. He lived seventy-eight years and reigned twenty-two. He died either from derangement of mind or from drinking poison, while he feared Licinius and Constantine. See Aurelius Victor, Eutropius, book 9, and Baptista Egnatius, book 1.

units.la: MAXIMIANVS Herculius in consorte Imperij à Diocletiano ascitus,tâquam filius patri obtemperauit: in Gallia & Africa exortos tumultus,armis repressit:Romę cum Diocletiano triûphauit : Dein à Diocletiano persuasus,se Imperio abdicauit:rem miram,vt sponte,nec grauate senecta,vel rerû mole (nam pacatus erat orbis)vterq; in ordinê se redegerit. At verò Imperium iterû affectans Maximianus,dum insidias Constantino,genero suo ex Fausta,parat, Massiliæ captus,strangulatur. regnauit annos 21.vnà cum Diocletiano.Pom.Eutro.lib.9.
units.tr: MAXIMIAN Herculius, taken by Diocletian as partner in the empire, obeyed him as a son obeys his father. He suppressed by arms the tumults that had arisen in Gaul and Africa; he triumphed at Rome with Diocletian. Then, persuaded by Diocletian, he abdicated the empire. A remarkable thing, that both of them, willingly and without reluctance in old age, or from the weight of affairs (for the world was at peace), reduced themselves to private rank. But Maximian, again aspiring to the empire, while he was preparing plots against Constantine, his son-in-law by Fausta, was captured at Marseilles and strangled. He reigned twenty-one years together with Diocletian. See Pomponius Laetus and Eutropius, book 9.
HELENA AUGUSTA, CONIUX MAGNI AUGUSTI... [unreadable remainder of the inscription]

units.la: CONSTANTIVS Chlorus & Galerius Maximinus fi[?]tue Maximianus,ambo à Diocletiano & Maximiano Herculio, priusquâ se imperio abdicarent,Cæsares facti ac adoptati sunt, propter varia bella in diuersis locis pullulantia. Constátius natus patre Eutropio, qui genus ab Ænea deducebat, & matre Claudia,Claudii Augusti filia,Galliis,Hispaniis, Italiæ & Africæ præfuit:Galerius Illyrico,Græciæ & Orieti. At verò hac diuisione Imperii facta,Constantius natura mitis, & diuitiarum spretor,Italiæ & Africæ Imperiū recusat, quòd putaret ab vno tantū pōdus minimè sustineri posse:in Galliis & Hispaniis tantùm regnat,propensus ad promerendā Gallorum gratiam,nec à vera pietate abhorres.Vxores habuit duas,prior fuit Helena, ex qua Constantinū magnum suscepit:posterior fuit Theodora,priuigna Maximiani Herculii: quā dimissā Helena, coactus est ducere. obiit Constantius Eboraci, quod est oppidū in Britannia, anno 2. postquam Imperio se Diocletianus abdicauit: nam longè antea Cæsar factus,& à Diocletiano adoptatus fuerat.duos igitur veri Imperii annos Constátio tribuo,ab ipsa abdicatione Imperii à Diocletiano,quæ facta est an. mun. 4 2 6 9. à Christo nato 3 0 7. hoc regnante nulli motus in suis ditionibus extitere, hostes popu. Rom. ab armis cessauere. Dictus est Chlorus,à colore,quasi virens.Vide Pom.Læ.Egna.li.1.
units.tr: Constantius Chlorus and Galerius Maximinus, also called Maximianus, were both made Caesars and adopted by Diocletian and Maximian Herculius before they laid down the imperial power, because of various wars breaking out in different places. Constantius, born of the father Eutropius, who derived his family from Aeneas, and of the mother Claudia, daughter of the Emperor Claudius, governed Gaul, Spain, Italy and Africa; Galerius governed Illyricum, Greece and the East. But when this division of the empire had been made, Constantius, gentle by nature and a despiser of riches, refused the rule of Italy and Africa, because he thought that one man alone could not bear so great a burden. He reigned only in Gaul and Spain, inclined to win the favour of the Gauls, and not far removed from true piety. He had two wives. The first was Helena, by whom he begot Constantine the Great. The second was Theodora, stepdaughter of Maximian Herculius; Helena having been dismissed, he was forced to marry her. Constantius died at York, which is a town in Britain, in the second year after Diocletian laid down the empire, for he had been made Caesar and adopted by Diocletian long before. I therefore assign two years of true rule to Constantius, counting from the very abdication of the empire by Diocletian, which took place in the year of the world 4269, the year 307 after the birth of Christ. Under his reign there were no uprisings in his dominions, and the enemies of the Roman people ceased from arms. He was called Chlorus from his colour, as if "green." See Pomponius Laetus, Egnatius, book 1.

units.la: HELENA, prior uxor Constantii,ac magni Constantini mater,annos nata 80.divinitus monita,Ierusalē perrexit: crucem in qua Christus pendit, non sine labore reperit: Romæ diem obiit,superstite filio, Deo hominibúsq; gratissima,anno mundi 4 2 8 6. à Christo nato 3 2 4. Vide Eusc. lib. 10. cap. 7. & Supple.Chro.
units.tr: HELENA, the first wife of Constantius and mother of Constantine the Great, at the age of 80, warned by God, went to Jerusalem. She found, not without labour, the cross on which Christ hung. She died at Rome, her son surviving, most dear to God and to men, in the year of the world 4286, the year 324 after the birth of Christ. See Eusebius, book 10, chapter 7, and Supplementum Chronicorum.

units.la: SEVERVS à Galerio Maximiano, siue Mraximino, adoptatus est, postquam Constantius Italiam & Africam reliquit: adoptatum Italiæ & Africæ postea præfecit. Romæ autē prætoriani Imperatorem fecere Maxentiū, non abnuente Senatu. Aberat tunc ab vrbe Seuerus, qui citò rediit: sed Maxētij vires statim creuerat: quare impar viribus Seuerus, fugit, cupiés adire Maximianum qui in Illyriis erat: at verò interim Rauennæ captus occisúsque est. Vide Pom.Læ in Constantio.
units.tr: SEVERUS was adopted by Galerius Maximinus, or Maximinus, after Constantius left Italy and Africa; he later placed the adopted man in charge of Italy and Africa. But at Rome the Praetorians made Maxentius emperor, and the Senate did not object. Severus was then away from the city, and he returned quickly; but Maxentius's forces had at once grown strong, so Severus, unequal in strength, fled, wishing to reach Maximian, who was in Illyricum. Meanwhile, however, he was captured at Ravenna and killed. See Pomponius Laetus on Constantius.

units.la: MAXENTIVS Romæ à Prætorianis Imperator factus, vt tyran-us imperauit. Porrò Maximianus sororis Galerij filius, relicto in Illyriis Licinio, quem adoptauit, mortuo Seuero, Romam proficiscitur, pugnaturus cōtra Maxentiū: in itinere certior fit de futura suorum militum defectione, si in prælium descenderet: quare in Illyriā reuertitur. Interea bona pars nobiliū Romanorum nuntium clam mittunt ad Constantinum, qui apud Gallos imperabat: exorant vti Romam, Imperij caput, tyrannide Maxentij liberet: tandē horum precibus cedens, Maxentium vincit: qui vnà cum equo in Tiberim insiluit, submersúsque est, nec vspiam inuētus. periit anno mundi 4276. à nato Christo 315. imperauit an.6. Constatino imperāte: hic haud fuit absimilis Maximiano Herculio, Domitiano, & Cōmodo: plerosque claros viros occídit, bona eorū diripuit, noua vectigalia excogitauit ac exegit: in occidendo & exigendo inexorabilis fuit, libidine item inexplebilis. Vide Pompo.Læ.in Constantio & Galerio.
units.tr: MAXENTIUS was made emperor at Rome by the Praetorians and ruled as a tyrant. Next, Maximian, son of Galerius's sister, left Licinius in Illyricum, whom he had adopted, and after Severus's death set out for Rome, intending to fight against Maxentius. On the way he learned for certain that his soldiers would desert him if he engaged in battle; so he turned back into Illyricum. Meanwhile a good part of the Roman nobility secretly sent word to Constantine, who ruled among the Gauls, and begged him to free Rome, the capital of the empire, from the tyranny of Maxentius. At last, yielding to their prayers, he defeated Maxentius, who leapt into the Tiber with his horse, was drowned, and was never found anywhere. He died in the year of the world 4276, the year 315 after the birth of Christ, having reigned six years while Constantine was emperor. He was not unlike Maximian Herculius, Domitian and Commodus: he killed many distinguished men, plundered their goods, and devised and exacted new taxes; he was merciless in killing and exacting, and likewise insatiable in lust. See Pomponius Laetus on Constantius and Galerius.
IMP. LICINIVS LICINIANVS, PIVS FELIX AVGVSTVS. [inscription, partly unreadable]
CONSTANTIA, WIFE OF M. IVL. LICINIVS. [inscription, partly unreadable]

units.la: LICINIVS in Dacia natus, mortuo Severo, consors Imperij factus est à Maximiano Galerio, anno mundi 4270. à Christo nato 308 idque ob virtutem rei militaris. Prius Illyriis, post Orieti præfuit: parentes habuit agricolas, ipse rusticus & barbarus rusticis & agrariis æquus, at crudelis etiā in Galerij liberos. literarum hostis fuit infensissimus, quas venenum ac pestem appellabat: quippe qui harū rudis ac expers adeò esset, ut ne nomen quidē suum decretis subscribere posset. Christianis adversabatur, nec destitit, sæpius rogatus ab Constantino: quare Constantinus contra illum vires Gallicanas & Italicas iure expertus est. primis congressibus in Pannonia victus, concessit in Macedoniam Licinius: ubi vires reparantē, Constantinus iterum adoritur, fugat in Asiam. Tandē navalibus & terrestribus præliis victus, mittitur Thessalonicē, ut privatus cum uxore degat. Sed cum rebelles adhuc animos homo ille vecors retineret, interfici iubetur. vixit an. 60. imperavit 14. Constantino imperante. laudatur quòd aulicorum insolētiam mirè compescuerit, tineas soricésque palatinos eos appellans. Pomp.Læt.
units.tr: LICINIUS was born in Dacia. After the death of Severus he was made co-ruler of the empire by Maximian Galerius, in the year of the world 4270, the year 308 after the birth of Christ, and this because of his skill in war. He first governed Illyricum and afterwards the East. His parents were farmers; he himself was a rustic and a barbarian, fair to country folk and farmers, but cruel even towards the children of Galerius. He was most bitterly hostile to learning, which he called poison and plague; indeed he was so untaught and without experience of letters that he could not even sign his own name to decrees. He opposed the Christians and did not stop, though often asked by Constantine; therefore Constantine, rightly, tested the forces of Gaul and Italy against him. Defeated in the first encounters in Pannonia, Licinius withdrew into Macedonia; there, while he was rebuilding his forces, Constantine attacked him again and put him to flight into Asia. At last, defeated in naval and land battles, he was sent to Thessalonica, to live as a private man with his wife. But since that foolish man still kept rebellious intentions, he was ordered to be put to death. He lived 60 years and reigned 14, while Constantine was emperor. He is praised because he marvellously restrained the insolence of the courtiers, calling them the moths and mice of the palace. See Pomponius Laetus.

units.la: CONSTANTIA, vxor fuit Licinij, ac soror Constantini, quæ (ut fertur) fratrem adiit, pro Imperio mariti rogavit, deinde pro titulo tantum, nec impetravit: tandem pro salute rogans, impetravit. Vide Pomp.Læt. hæc Licinium iuniore peperit, quem Constantinus Magnus Cæsarem creavit. CONST[?] ANTINVS MA[?] FAVSTA[?] AVGVST[?]
units.tr: CONSTANTIA was the wife of Licinius and sister of Constantine. As is said, she went to her brother and asked on behalf of her husband's empire, then only for his title, and did not obtain it; at last, praying for his safety, she obtained it. See Pomponius Laetus. She bore Licinius the younger, whom Constantine the Great made Caesar. CONSTANTINUS MAXIMUS, FAUSTA AUGUSTA. [inscription, partly unreadable]

units.la: CONSTANTINVS Magnus, Constantij & S. Helenæ filius,cæteris fratribus patris etiam testamento, prælatus est. A Galerio Maximiano adhuc adolescens missus aduersus Sarmatas,præter opinionē hostes profligauit : Ducem catenatum ad Galerium duxit. veritus ex ea laude glisccetem Galerij inuidiam , Roma ad patrem in Angliam transfugit,qui paulò pòst moritur. Tum cunctis qui aderant annitentibus , sed præcipuè Eroco,Alemannorū rege, imperat Constantinus,anno mundi 4271.àChristo nato 309.Regnum Galliarum Hispaniarúmque, & Alpium Cottiarū testamento relictum accepit.veteranis militibus agros assignatos,vt ad filios suos trásirent, primus instituit. Accersitus in Italiam ab iis qui Maxentij tyrânidem ferre non poterant, biénio totam Italiam vrbémque Romam pristinæ maiestati asseruit. hæc laurus Italiam ei adiecit & Africam: fuisséq; his cótentus nisi Licinius qui Oriente regebat,vltimi belli ciuilis causam præbuisset,quem vicit. Túncq; cognomen assumpsit Magni,quod antea soli Alexáder & Pōpeius acceperant.ita insoles[?] factus,plurimorum se nobiliū , fuorúmq; etiam cæde polluit. Attamen Christū amplexus est,bonáq; quamplurima in Ecclesiam contulit:Nicenā synodum 322. prælatorum, multis diffidetibus , indixit:literis impensè studuit,eáfq; fouit. Bizátium instaurauit,imperatoriámq; vrbem,& nouā Romam appellauit. vixit annos 66. imperauit 31.Pomp.Læt.obiit Nicomediæ in qua baptizatus fuerat ab Eufe.epifc.huius mortē denuntiauit crinita stella. Eutro.li.10. veneno aiunt periisse à domesticis parato,cùm ille in Persas bellum pararet.
units.tr: CONSTANTINE the Great, son of Constantius and St Helena, was preferred to his other brothers, even by his father's will. Sent against the Sarmatians by Galerius Maximian while still a young man, he routed the enemy beyond expectation and led their leader in chains to Galerius. Fearing that the glory of this deed would stir up Galerius's envy, he fled from Rome to his father in Britain, who soon afterwards died. Then, with all who were present striving for him, but especially Erocus, king of the Alemanni, Constantine took command, in the year of the world 4271, the year 309 after the birth of Christ. He received the kingdom of Gaul, Spain and the Cottian Alps, left to him by will. He was the first to assign lands to veteran soldiers, so that they might pass them on to their sons. Summoned into Italy by those who could not bear the tyranny of Maxentius, he in two years restored all Italy and the city of Rome to its former majesty. This victory added Italy and Africa to him; he would have been content with these, had not Licinius, who ruled the East, provided the occasion of the last civil war, and he defeated him. Then he took the surname "the Great," which before him only Alexander and Pompey had received. Having become so insolent, he polluted himself with the slaughter of many nobles, even of his own kin. Nevertheless he embraced Christ and conferred very many goods on the Church. In the year 322 he summoned the synod of Nicaea, with many bishops, though some distrusted it. He pursued literature eagerly and fostered it. He restored Byzantium, the imperial city, and called it New Rome. He lived 66 years and reigned 31. See Pomponius Laetus. He died at Nicomedia, where he had been baptised by Eusebius, bishop; a comet announced his death. See Eutropius, book 10. They say he perished by poison prepared by his household, while he was preparing war against the Persians.

units.la: FAVSTA, Herculij filia, & Constantini vxor, peperit ei Constantinum,Constantem & Constantium, Helenámque & Constantiam.Faustam occidit Constantinus vir.Pomp.Læt.
units.tr: FAUSTA, daughter of Herculius and wife of Constantine, bore him Constantine, Constans and Constantius, and Helena and Constantia. Constantine her husband killed Fausta. See Pomponius Laetus.

units.la: CONSTANTINVS, natu maximus filiorum Constantini Magni,patre mortuo,anno mundi 4301.à Christo nato 338.imperat vnà cum fratribus Constante & Constantio. hi, siue ex testamento patris,siue ex propria eorum voluntate, Imperium ita partiti sunt, vt Constantinus Gallias, Hispanias,Britanniamque insulam obtineret: Constans Italiam cum Illyrico & Græciam:Constantius Byzantiū cum Oriente,qui Dalmatium patruelē Imperij socium haberet, quē postea militari factione oppressit. Nec durat diu fratrum cōcordia:nam Constantinus Gallico exercitu fretus, Constãti bellum infert:quod dum cupidius quàm cautius gerit,exceptus insidiis,vulneribúsq; confossus perit,ad Aquileiam,anno ætatis suæ 25.Imperij 3.Consulito Pomp.Læt.& Bap. Egna.li.1.
units.tr: CONSTANTINE, the eldest of the sons of Constantine the Great, after his father's death, in the year of the world 4301, the year 338 after the birth of Christ, reigned together with his brothers Constans and Constantius. These, whether by their father's will or by their own agreement, divided the empire so that Constantine held Gaul, Spain and the island of Britain; Constans held Italy with Illyricum and Greece; Constantius held Byzantium with the East, and had as his partner in the empire his cousin Dalmatius, whom he later destroyed in a military coup. Nor did the concord of the brothers last long: for Constantine, relying on the Gallic army, made war on Constans; and while he waged it more eagerly than carefully, he was caught in an ambush, pierced with wounds, and died at Aquileia, in the twenty-fifth year of his age and the third of his rule. See Pomponius Laetus and Baptista Egnatius, book 1.

units.la: LICINIVS,iunior,Constantini Magni ex sorore Constantia nepos,creatus est Cæsar vnà cum Crispo,eiusdem Constantini ex Mineruina concubina filio,anno mundi 4278.à Christo nato 316. verùm hi factione infaustæ Faustæ interficiuntur.Aur. Vict. Pomponius Læt.hic Crispus à Lactantio fuit eruditus. D.N. CONSTANTIVS P.F.AVG IMP.C. CONSTANTINVS.III
units.tr: LICINIUS the younger, grandson of Constantine the Great through his sister Constantia, was made Caesar together with Crispus, son of the same Constantine by his concubine Minervina, in the year of the world 4278, the year 316 after the birth of Christ. But these two were killed through the plotting of the ill-fated Fausta. Aurelius Victor; Pomponius Laetus. This Crispus was educated by Lactantius. D.N. CONSTANTIVS P.F. AVG. IMP. C. CONSTANTINVS III. [inscription]

units.la: CONSTANS, devicto fratre Constantino, omni conatu superatis Alpibus Galliam intrat, varióq; eventu biennio pugnans, patre fratris in potestatem redigit. Primùm agit bonum principē, mox sive adversa valetudinē, sive rerum prosperitate mutatus, ingratus omnibus esse coepit, donec & ipse Magnentij dolo, quem etiam servaverat, dormiēs[?] intra tentorium, non longe ab Hispaniis, ad Helenam oppidum, opprimitur, anno ætatis 30. Imperij 13. Consulito Pomp. Læt. & Bap. Egna. li.1.
units.tr: CONSTANS, after defeating his brother Constantine, entered Gaul by crossing the Alps with every effort; fighting for two years with varying fortune, he brought the brother's father's territories under his power. At first he acted as a good prince, but soon, changed either by ill health or by prosperity, he began to be hateful to everyone, until he himself, through the treachery of Magnentius, whom he had also spared, was overwhelmed while sleeping inside his tent, not far from Spain, at the town of Helena, in the thirtieth year of his age and the thirteenth of his rule. See Pomponius Laetus and Baptista Egnatius, book 1.

units.la: CONSTANTIVS, cædem fratris Constantis ulturus, magno exercitu adversus Magnētium cōparato, ingenti illum prælio, & memorabili, ad Murtiū, sive Mursam, vicit, quo Romani vires Imperij penè cōciderē, 53. millibus utrinque desideratis. Mox cum Magnentius bellū reparasset, & ad Lugdunum iterum victus esset, gladio sibi latus aperuit. Cæterùm Cōstantius, iterum in Persas cōtendens, dum ægrè fert Iulianum à militibus Augustū esse dictum, iuxta Tauri mōtis radices æstuantissima febre correptus, moritur, anno ætatis 40. Imperij 2 4. Hic orbis dominum se vocavit:Iulianum adoptavit. Consulito autores quos supra.
units.tr: Constantius, having set out to avenge the murder of his brother Constans, assembled a great army against Magnentius and defeated him in a huge and memorable battle at Mursa, or Mursa Major, a battle by which the strength of the Roman Empire was nearly broken, with 53,000 men lost on both sides. Soon afterwards, when Magnentius had renewed the war and was defeated again at Lyons, he opened his side with his own sword. Constantius, however, hastening once more against the Persians, was seized by a burning fever near the foot of the Taurus mountains, taking it badly that the soldiers had hailed Julian as Augustus, and died at the age of 40, in the 24th year of his reign. He had called himself lord of the world, and he adopted Julian. Consult the authors cited above.

units.la: MAGNENTIVS, Comes duorum ordinum Augustæ (vrbs est Germaniæ) cōuiuiū militibus exhibuit, à mane ad vesperam, more gentis. inde in cubiculū ingressus, statim egressus est, indutus purpura, ac multis satellitibus cinctus: qui cōscij non erat, coacti sunt assentiri: donatiuum dedit, posuitq; custodes ne quis rem aperiret. deinde cum lectissimis Gaisone mittit, qui Constantem in tentorio occidit, anno mundi 4313. à Christo nato 351. Hic Cæsare facit Decentium fratrem, mittitq; cum exercitu vti Gallias tueatur iamq; tota Italia: & Africa Magnentij erant. Constātius tunc in Oriente aduersam fortunam cōtra Persas experiebatur: ad quē legatos misit cum literis, vti Oriēte & Thraciis cōtentus esset: qui nihil respondet, sed Gallum patruelem Cæsarē faciēs, eum in Oriēte relinquit: ipse Hesperios adit, vlturus fratris cædē. attamen ne sua Roma bello vexaretur ciuili Gallia Magnentio permittit, si arma deponat: Tyrānus sperans vincere, non paruit. pugnatur ad Mursam, magnis vtrinque viribus: vincitur Magnentius: bellū reparat: victus iterum, tandem gladio occultè prouisso mortem sibi consciscit. Pom. Læ. in Constāte. Aurel. Victo. Hic Desiderium fratrem per furorem vulnerauit, & quosdam ex amicis occidit, paulò ante quàm seipsum occideret.
units.tr: Magnentius, count of the two orders at Augusta (a city in Germany), gave a banquet for the soldiers from morning until evening, in the custom of the people. Then he went into his bedchamber and came out at once, dressed in purple and surrounded by many bodyguards. Those who were not aware of the plot were forced to agree; he gave a donative and posted guards so that no one would reveal the matter. Then, with his most select men under Gaison, he sent them out, and they killed Constans in his tent, in the year of the world 4313, from the birth of Christ 351. He made his brother Decentius Caesar, and sent him with an army to defend the Gauls, while all of Italy and Africa were under Magnentius. Constantius at that time was experiencing adverse fortune in the East against the Persians. To him Magnentius sent envoys with a letter, urging him to be content with the East and Thrace; he gave no answer, but made his cousin Gallus Caesar and left him in the East, while he himself went to the West to avenge his brother's murder. Yet, so that his own Rome should not be harried by civil war, he granted Gaul to Magnentius on condition that he lay down his arms; the tyrant, hoping to win, did not obey. They fought at Mursa, with great forces on both sides; Magnentius was defeated; he renewed the war, was defeated again, and at last, having secretly thrust a sword through himself, took his own life. Pomponius Laetus on Constans; Aurelius Victor. He wounded his brother Desiderius in a fit of madness and killed some of his friends, shortly before he killed himself.

units.la: DECENTIVS qui Gallias tuebatur, audito fratris sui Magnentij casu, laqueo apud Senonas vitam finiuit, sibi metuens. horum frater Desiderius Constantiū adiit, à quo humanissimè exceptus est anno mundi 4316. à Christo nato 354. Pomp. Læt. Aurel. Vict.
units.tr: Decentius, who was defending the Gauls, on hearing of the fall of his brother Magnentius, ended his life by a noose at Senones, fearing for himself. Their brother Desiderius went to Constantius, by whom he was received most kindly, in the year of the world 4316, from the birth of Christ 354. Pomponius Laetus; Aurelius Victor.

units.la: FL. CL. IVLIANVS natus Constantinopoli, patre Constantio, Constatini Magni fratre, matre Basilina, forma liberali fuit, ingenio callido, ad literas & ad arma apto. Huc Constantius patruelis, Magni filius Constantini, adoptauit, Cæsarē fecit, ad Gallias tuedas misit. hostes hinc profligat, Gallias Alemannorum incursu vastatas, sub primum accessum, præter omnium spem asserit, regemq; Germanorum capit. Agrippinam (quę nunc Colonia dicitur) recipit. Deinde assensu totius exercitus Parisiis Imperator & Augustus vocatur an. mun. 4325. à Christo nato 3 6 3. Ad Constantium literas mittit exorans vt qui licet repugnans, Imperator fit à militibus appellatus, in cōsortiū Imperij admittatur: renuit Constatius. Ad bellum ciuile parat se Iulianus, item & Constatius, qui nihilominus febre correptus, cum deficeret successore statuit Iulianum. Adepto itaq; Imperio solus rerum summa potitus Iulianus, Persis bellū mouet: verùm à transfuga quodā Persa in insidias deductus, cùm eum hinc inde Parthi vrgeret, ab vno ex hostibus, & quidē fugiente, conto percutitur: & cū Philosophis de immortalitate animæ tractās, paulò post moritur, anno ætatis 31. Imperij, mensibus 19. à morte Constantini patruelis. Hic aduersus fidem Christianam libros edidit. Egna. lib. 1. Pomp. Læ. Aure. Vict.
units.tr: Flavius Claudius Julianus was born at Constantinople, of the father Constantius, brother of Constantine the Great, and the mother Basilina; he was handsome in appearance, clever in mind, and fit for letters and for arms. His cousin Constantius, son of Constantine the Great, adopted him, made him Caesar, and sent him to defend the Gauls. He defeated the enemies there, and, when the Gauls had been devastated by the incursions of the Alemanni, he recovered them, beyond everyone's hope, at the first approach, and took captive the king of the Germans. He recovered Agrippina, which is now called Cologne. Then, with the assent of the whole army, he was called Emperor and Augustus at Paris, in the year of the world 4325, from the birth of Christ 363. Julian sent a letter to Constantius, pleading that, although he himself was reluctant, he had been named Emperor by the soldiers, and that he be admitted to a share of the empire; Constantius refused. Julian prepared for civil war, and so did Constantius, who, nevertheless, was seized by fever, and, as he was dying, appointed Julian as his successor. Having thus obtained the empire, Julian held the supreme power alone and made war on the Persians; but, led into an ambush by a certain Persian deserter, and pressed on all sides by the Parthians, he was struck by a spear from one of the enemy, and that while fleeing. While he was discussing the immortality of the soul with the philosophers, he died shortly after, at the age of 31, in the 19th month of his reign, counted from the death of his cousin Constantine. He published books against the Christian faith. Lib. 1 of Egnatius; Pomponius Laetus; Aurelius Victor.

units.la: IVVIANVS, seu Iouianus, è Pannonia, mortuo Iuliano electus est princeps, & statim Antesignani Iuuianum clamauerunt: tunc qui in medio, quíque postremi erant milites, opinati Iulianum reuixisse, ingenti lætitia effusi, choreas ducebāt. Hic cum Parsis fœdus icit, Trāstigritanas provincias quinq; reddidit: atq; Arsaci Armeniæ regi, Ro. socio, & amico, opē ferre vetitus est. At è Persīde rediēs hyeme aspera, ingressus cubiculum noui tectorij, positis etiam ibi prunis, ex cruditate insuper stomachi periit, anno ætatis 33. Imperij mensibus 7. Vide vt supia, DN VALENTINIANVS PF AVG SEVERINA AVGVSTA
units.tr: Jovianus, or Iovianus, from Pannonia, was chosen as prince after Julian's death, and at once the vanguard soldiers shouted "Jovian!"; then the soldiers in the middle and at the rear, thinking that Julian had come back to life, poured out in great joy and led dances. He made a treaty with the Persians and gave back five Transtigritane provinces; and he was forbidden to bring help to Arsaces, king of Armenia, a Roman ally and friend. But returning from Persia in a harsh winter, he entered a bedroom of a new building, where braziers had been set out, and died there, through indigestion of the stomach, at the age of 33, in the seventh month of his reign. See above: Dominus noster Valentinianus, Pius Felix Augustus, and Severina Augusta.

units.la: VALENTINIANVS Gratiani filius, è Pannonia ortus, quemadmodum & Iuviani, apud Niceā, quæ urbs est Bithyniæ, Imperator à militibus post excessum Iuviani creatur, anno mundi 4328. à Christo nato 366. huic resistenti Imperium aggeritur: deinde Valentem fratrem consortem imperij facit. Hi Procopium imperium invadente Constantinopoli oppressere. Inde Gothi, ac barbarae nationes à Valentiniano Thracia exturbatae: Septētriōq; omnis cum Saxonibus ad officiū, eiusdem opera redacti sunt. Parthi è Syria per legatos eiecti. Inquieta Germania sub eo pacata est, Theodosij maioris auspiciis. Ipse dum Quadorum legatione latrocinia excusante audit, subita accensus ira incidit in morbū, quo arescētibus venis, cum nihil sanguinis emitti posset, obiit anno ætatis 55. Imperij 11. Pomp. Læt. Bap. Egna. alij scribūt eum subita sanguinis eruptione, voce amissa, sensu integro expirasse: idque ob intemperatiam ciborum, quibus artus suos diffuderat. Aurel. Victor.
units.tr: Valentinian, son of Gratian, born in Pannonia like Jovian, was made Emperor by the soldiers at Nicaea, a city of Bithynia, after Jovian's death, in the year of the world 4328, from the birth of Christ 366. Although he resisted, the empire was forced upon him; then he made his brother Valens a partner in the empire. Together they crushed Procopius, who was trying to seize the empire at Constantinople. Then the Goths and other barbarian nations were driven out of Thrace by Valentinian, and all the North, together with the Saxons, was brought back to obedience through his efforts. The Parthians were expelled from Syria by envoys. Germany, restless, was pacified under him, under the auspices of Theodosius the Elder. While he was listening to an embassy of the Quadi, who were excusing their robberies, he was suddenly seized by anger and fell into an illness, in which, as his veins dried up and no blood could be let out, he died at the age of 55, in the 11th year of his reign. Pomponius Laetus; Egnatius. Others write that he died by a sudden burst of blood, losing his voice but with his senses intact, and that this was due to the immoderate eating of foods with which he had swollen his limbs. Aurelius Victor.

units.la: SEVERA, uxor fuit Valentiniani, ex qua suscepit ille filium nomine Gratianum, quem Augustū creavit pater Valentinianus. unà cum Severa, quinetiā ipsa operam dante, in uxorem accepit Iustinam, ex qua suscepit Valentinianū filium alterum ac filias tres, Iustam, Gratam, & Gallam: lata, priusquam secundò nuberet, lege, ut qui vellet, duas impunè uxores assumeret: sic populosas fore gentes prædicabat. Eutro. auctus li.12.
units.tr: Severa was the wife of Valentinian, by whom he had a son named Gratian, whom his father Valentinian made Augustus. Together with Severa, and indeed with her active help, he took as wife Justina, by whom he had another son, Valentinian, and three daughters, Justa, Grata and Galla. Before she married a second time, a law had been passed allowing anyone who wished to take two wives with impunity; she used to say that in this way the peoples would be made populous. Eutropius, enlarged, book 12.

units.la: VALENS, Valentiniani frater,qui cum eo, eiusdémque gratia & benignitate, imperauit in Oriēte,mortuo fratre cum Gratiano fratris filio imperat, anno mundi 4339. à Christo nato 377. hic post prædicti fratris obitū infeliciter cum Hunnis, Tartaris, Scythis & Gothis pugnauit: qui olim à regione trans Tanaim venerant,& superato nuper Istro ( qui limes regionis erat)vagi Pannonias,Epirúmque & Thessaliam,direptis & incensis aliquot urbibus,depopulabātur. Valens itaque propere ex Antiochia accitus,tantā peste auertere non potuit, sed magna clade victus, terga dedit, & in fuga vulneratus decidit ex equo:deportatúsq;in vile turguriū,ibidē,ab hostibus septus, concrematur anno Imperij ferè 14. post fratris mortem tertio. sic miserè interit,qui paulò ante terror Oriētis fuerat:sed enim Christianos post mortem fratris afflixit, Arrianæ factionis fautor:monachos pugnare coëgit,repugnátes occîdit. Pomp.Læt. Egna.li.1.Abbas Vrspergensis,Paulus Diaconus li.1.
units.tr: Valens, brother of Valentinian, who ruled together with him, and by his favour and kindness, ruled in the East; after his brother's death he ruled with Gratian, his brother's son, in the year of the world 4339, from the birth of Christ 377. He, after the death of his aforementioned brother, fought unluckily against the Huns, Tartars, Scythians and Goths, who had long ago come from the region beyond the Tanais and, having lately crossed the Danube (which was the boundary of the region), wandered through Pannonia, Epirus and Thessaly, plundering and burning several cities. Valens, therefore, hastily summoned from Antioch, could not turn aside so great a plague, but, defeated with great slaughter, he turned his back and, wounded in flight, fell from his horse; carried into a poor hut, there, surrounded by the enemy, he was burned, in about the fourteenth year of his reign, the third after his brother's death. Thus he miserably perished, who a little before had been the terror of the East. But he afflicted the Christians after his brother's death, being a supporter of the Arian faction; he forced monks to fight and killed those who resisted. Pomponius Laetus; Egnatius, book 1; the Abbot of Ursberg; Paulus Diaconus, book 1.

units.la: DOMINICA, Valentis uxor fuit,quæ Constantinopolim obsidione liberauit, magna vi pecuniæ data Hūnis, Alanísque & Gothis,qui victricibus signis,superato Valētio, eam obsidebant.Pompon.Lætus.in Fla.Val.Valentiniano. Claruerunt hoc tēpore Basilius magnus,Cyrillus,Ambrosius, Epiphanius, Gregorius Nazianzenus,Theologi.
units.tr: Dominica was the wife of Valens, who freed Constantinople from siege, by giving a great sum of money to the Huns, Alans and Goths, who, after Valens had been defeated, were besieging it with victorious standards. Pomponius Laetus, on Flavius Valens and Valentinian. At this time flourished the theologians Basil the Great, Cyril, Ambrose, Epiphanius, and Gregory of Nazianzus.

units.la: GRATIANVS, Valentiniani filius,à patre factus Augustus,cum eo imperauit annos 8.cum patruo Valete 3.cũ Theodosio 6. attamen post patruum Valente tunc demũ ipse imperat annos 6. auspicatúrque anno mundi 4342. à Christo nato 380.Hic pietate in suos egregius.Valentinianũ fratrem ex patre, Iustinæ filium,adhuc puerũ, Augustũ dixit, patre patruóq; extinctis. Mox Theodosium Hispanum in consortem Imperij assumit(ad exemplum Neruæ,qui Traianũ ex Hispania asciuerat)eiq; Orientem comittit vt esset velut vallum quoddam adversus Gothos,& Hunnos,qui Thraciam & Daciam,tanquam naturale solum,occupabat.Gratianus admodũ iuuenis,bellum apud Argentoratũ formidolosissimum ingenti felicitate confecit:nam plusquam 30000. Alemannorum interfecit. At verò dum tandẽ tantum spicula & arcus meditatur,& paucos ex Alanis,quos ingeti auro ad se vocarat,veteri ac Rom. militi præfert,Maximus qui apud Britanniam tyrannidem arripuerat,in Galliam traiiciens , ab infensis Gratiano legionibus excipitur. Gratianum Parisiis fundit,& Lugduni ex improuiso adortum, & in Italiam transfire properante,dolo circumuenit, & occidit. Eutro.auctus li.12.Pom.Læt.Aure.Vict.Egna.li.1.Oro.li.7.ca.33.
units.tr: Gratian, son of Valentinian, was made Augustus by his father, and ruled with him for eight years, with his uncle Valens for three, and with Theodosius for six; yet after his uncle Valens he himself ruled for six years more, and began his reign in the year of the world 4342, from the birth of Christ 380. He was outstanding for his piety towards his own people. He named his brother Valentinian, son of his father by Justina, still a boy, Augustus, after his father and uncle had been put to death. Soon afterwards he took Theodosius, a Spaniard, as partner in the empire (after the example of Nerva, who had adopted Trajan from Spain), and entrusted the East to him, so that he might be a kind of rampart against the Goths and Huns, who were occupying Thrace and Dacia as if it were their natural land. Gratian, while still quite young, brought to a successful end the most dangerous war at Argentoratum with great good fortune, for he killed more than 30,000 Alemanni. But when, at last, he devoted himself only to spears and bows, and preferred a few Alans, whom he had called to himself with great sums of gold, to the old and Roman soldiers, Maximus, who had seized the tyranny in Britain, crossed into Gaul; and he was met by the legions hostile to Gratian. He routed Gratian at Paris, and when Gratian, having been attacked unexpectedly at Lyons, was hurrying to pass into Italy, Maximus surrounded him by a trick and killed him. Eutropius, enlarged, book 12; Pomponius Laetus; Aurelius Victor; Egnatius, book 1; Orosius, book 7, chapter 33.

units.la: VALENTINIANVS Gratiani supradicti frater,à Maximo ex Italia pulsus ad Theodosium,qui Orienti præerat,vnà cum Iustina matre adiit:à quo benignè susceptus,& particeps Imperij factus,cum eo 7.annos imperauit.tandem in occidentis regnum restitutus , dum Viennæ negligentius moratur, fraude Eugenij & Arbogastis ,à cubicularíis noctu strangulatur, vt voluntariam sibi mortem conscivisse putaretur. Pom. Læt.Eutro.auctus lib.13.
units.tr: VALENTINIAN, brother of the aforesaid Gratian, driven out of Italy by Maximus, went to Theodosius, who presided over the East, together with his mother Justina. Kindly received by him and made a partner in the empire, he reigned with him for seven years. At length he was restored to the realm of the West; but while he lingered carelessly at Vienna, he was strangled at night by his chamberlains through the treachery of Eugenius and Arbogast, so that it would be thought he had brought about his own death voluntarily. Pomp. Laet.; Eutropius, augmented, book 13.

units.la: ARCADIVS & Honorius, Imperatoris Theodosij filij, imperarút cum eo 3. annos: attamen post mortem patris ipsissimum eorum Imperium incipit, anno mundi 4359. à Christo nato 397. Arcadius Constantinopoli imperat, Honorius Romæ: sed cùm per ætate tantæ rerū moli impares essent, tres Imperij tutores testamento sanxit pater: Arcadio Rufinū, Honorio Stiliconem cōmendauit: Africæ verò Gildoné præesse voluit. Quis autem animorū recessus intueri possit? sanctissimū legati ius cupido regnadi violat.Rufinus,clam missis muneribus, Alarico Gothorum regi capere arma cōtra Arcadium, persuadet, vt eo metu imperiū ipse ab Arcadio extorqueat. Re intellecta, à militibus Italicis,perniciosus tutor obtrūcatur.caput cū dextra ante Constantinopolis portas pendens, spectatibus ludibrio fit. Caianus Rufini sceleris æmulus, eundē vitæ exitum habet. Imperauit Arcadius an.13.obiit Constantinopoli.Pom.Læ.Bap. Egna.lib.1.
units.tr: ARCADIUS and Honorius, sons of the Emperor Theodosius, reigned with their father for three years; yet after his death their whole empire began, in the year of the world 4359, from the birth of Christ 397. Arcadius reigned at Constantinople, Honorius at Rome. But since by reason of their age they were unequal to so great a weight of affairs, the father by his will appointed three guardians of the empire: he committed Arcadius to Rufinus and Honorius to Stilicho, and he wished Gildo to preside over Africa. But who can see into the recesses of men's hearts? Lust for rule violated that most sacred law of guardianship. Rufinus, by secretly sending gifts, persuaded Alaric, king of the Goths, to take up arms against Arcadius, so that, through fear of this, he himself might wrest the empire from Arcadius. When this became known, the pernicious guardian was cut down by the Italian soldiers; his head, hanging with his right hand before the gates of Constantinople, became a mockery to the onlookers. Gainas, an emulator of Rufinus's crime, met the same end of life. Arcadius reigned thirteen years and died at Constantinople. Pom. Laet.; Bap.; Egnatius, book 1.

units.la: HONORIVS imperat Romæ eodé anno quo Arcadius Constantinopoli. post annos 3. Gildo, Africam sibi vendicat: Mascezelis fratris filios enecat, à quo superatus, strangulatur. Mascezelem insolescentem vicit Honorius. Stilico Honorij socer regnum filio suo affectans, Sueuos, Vandalos, Alemannos magna prædæ spe sollicitat: illi properant cum 200000. & Rege Radagaso, qui in Italiam irrumpens capitur, & in carcere strangulatur: in cuius locum hostes Alaricum Regem creant, qui Romam capit anno mundi 4373. à Christo nato 411. Tandē fraude cognita Stilico Vandalus vna cum filio sublatus est. imperat Honorius annos 31. cum patre 2. cum fratre 3. cum fratris filio 16. obiit Romæ.Pau.Diaco.lib.4.Pomp.Læt. Bap.Egna.lib.2.
units.tr: HONORIUS reigned at Rome in the same year in which Arcadius reigned at Constantinople. After three years Gildo claimed Africa for himself and killed the sons of his brother Mascezel; when he was defeated by Mascezel, he was strangled. Honorius conquered Mascezel, who had grown insolent. Stilicho, Honorius's father-in-law, aspiring to the kingdom for his son, stirred up the Suevi, Vandals and Alemanni with the great hope of plunder; they hastened with 200,000 men and their king Radagaisus, who, breaking into Italy, was captured and strangled in prison. In his place the enemies made Alaric king, who took Rome in the year of the world 4373, from the birth of Christ 411. At length, when the treachery was discovered, Stilicho the Vandal was removed together with his son. Honorius reigned 31 years: two with his father, three with his brother, sixteen with his brother's son. He died at Rome. Paul the Deacon, book 4; Pomp. Laet.; Bap.; Egnatius, book 2.

units.la: THEODOSIUS Junior, Arcadij filius, Orientale Imperium post patrem tenuit anno mundi 4372. à Christo nato 410. hunc puerum admodum, moriens pater reliquit sub tutela Isdigerdis Persarum Regis: quod bene cessit: nam barbarus Rex tutelam summa fide gessit, & pacē cum Romanis quoad vixit habuit. Honorio patruo defuncto Valentinianum Constantio & Placidia natum, Cæsarem facit, & peropportunē Romā mittit: nam Joannem factione Castini Imperatorem factum, atque etiam Africam sibi vendicantē, novus princeps oppressit. Gensericus, Vandalorum Rex, post insignē victoriam & magnam stragem, Carthaginē occupat. Ad Aquilonem Bleda & Attila, fratres, Hunnorum Reges, Illyricum & Thraciam Thermopylas usque depraedantur: tamen omnia Theodosius magna gloria tutatus est. Vide Pom. Læ. & Bap. Egn. li. 1. vixit, imperavitq; annos 48. cum Honorio 21. postea 27. obiit morbo apud Constantinopolim. Vide Pau. Diac. li. 4. Hoc principe Venetiæ felicibus auspiciis in aquis habitari cœpere. Nestorius cum hæresi nominis sui, & cum Pelagianis, synodo Ephesina damnatur: & Pharamundus apud Francos primus regnat.
units.tr: THEODOSIUS the Younger, son of Arcadius, held the Eastern empire after his father, in the year of the world 4372, from the birth of Christ 410. His father, dying, left this boy, still very young, under the guardianship of Isdigerdes, king of the Persians; which turned out well, for the barbarian king discharged the guardianship with the utmost good faith and kept peace with the Romans as long as he lived. When his uncle Honorius died, he made Valentinian, born of Constantius and Placidia, Caesar and sent him to Rome at a very opportune moment, for a new prince overthrew John, who had been made emperor through the faction of Castinus and was also claiming Africa for himself. Gaiseric, king of the Vandals, after a notable victory and great slaughter, occupied Carthage. In the north, Bleda and Attila, brothers, kings of the Huns, plundered Illyricum and Thrace as far as Thermopylae; yet Theodosius defended all things with great glory. See Pom. Laet. and Bap.; Egnatius, book 1. He lived and reigned 48 years: 21 with Honorius, afterwards 27. He died of disease at Constantinople. See Paul the Deacon, book 4. Under this prince Venice began to be inhabited in the waters, under favourable auspices. Nestorius, with the heresy that bears his name and with the Pelagians, was condemned by the Synod of Ephesus; and Pharamond first reigned among the Franks.

units.la: EUDOXIA, Leonis Atheniensis Philosophi filia, Theodosij uxor fuit, quæ præter egregiam formam, singularemq; pudicitiam, etiam literis excelluit: hæc filiam eiusdē nominis peperit, quæ Valentiniano nupsit, quo Romæ occiso, ut viri mortem ulciscerētur Genfericum ex Africa vocavit: qui Romā venit, ac rediens Eudoxiam viduam abduxit.
units.tr: EUDOXIA, daughter of Leo the Athenian philosopher, was the wife of Theodosius. Besides her outstanding beauty and singular chastity, she also excelled in letters. She bore a daughter of the same name, who married Valentinian. When Valentinian was killed at Rome, she summoned Gaiseric from Africa to avenge her husband's death; he came to Rome and, on his return, carried off the widowed Eudoxia.

units.la: GENSERICVS, Alanorum, Vandalorumque Rex ab Hispaniis euocatus à Bonifacio Africæ præfecto, in Libyam intromittitur, vt eidem Bonifacio aduersus Sigisuldũ siue Suuldum opem ferat, nam Bonifacius ille Africa vsurpare conabatur. Genfericus itaque cum suis Alanis & Vandalis tota pene Africam ferro, flamma, rapinis crudelissimè deuastans, catholicam insuper fidem Arriana impietate subuertit: anno mundi 4390. à Christo nato 428. post treis annos Hipponen obsedit: mense 3. obsidionis D. Augustinus, in illa ipsa vrbe cuius erat Episcopus, obiit annos natus 76. nec vrbis suæ ruinam vidit. Pom.Læt.Paul.Diac.li.14. Ab Vrsper.
units.tr: Genseric, King of the Alans and Vandals, was summoned from Spain by Bonifacius, prefect of Africa, and admitted into Libya, so that he might bring help to the same Bonifacius against Sigisuldus, or Suuldus, for Bonifacius was attempting to seize Africa for himself. Genseric therefore, with his Alans and Vandals, laid almost the whole of Africa waste with sword, fire and plunder, cruelly; and moreover he overthrew the Catholic faith with Arian impiety. In the year of the world 4390, from the birth of Christ 428, after three years he besieged Hippo. In the third month of the siege, Augustine, Bishop of that very city, died at the age of 76, and did not see the ruin of his city. Pom. Læt. Paul. Diac. bk. 14. From Ursper.

units.la: ATTILA Hunnorum Rex omniúmq; Septentrionalium pene nationum, fratre suum occidit, eiusq; subditos sibi parere compulit. Hic Imperium Occidentale ambiens, ac Visigothis inuidęs, exercitum 500000. hominum comparauit: in Galliam irrupit: cum Ætio, Imperatoris vice gerente, & cum Theodorico Visigothorũ Rege, in campis Catalaunicis grauissimo prælio pugnauit: cæsa sunt 180000. (alij scribunt 200000.) vtrinque hominũ, inter quos Theodoricus: tantúmq; sanguinis effusum est, vt paruulus qui ibi labebatur riuulus, immodicus subito torrens effectus, cadauera secum traheret peremptorum. commissum est id prælium anno mundi 4414. post Christum natum 452. nullus pedè retulit, nullus retro vulnus accepit: tanta contentione pugnatum est. At superatus Attila, tandémq; resipiēs, Italiā peruasit furibundus, actúmq; effet de ea, ni Papa supplex illum adiēs, totius Italiæ salutem reportasset. Vxorem exinde duxit Imperatoris Valentiniani filiam, alias minitatus Imperatori: dein alteram duxit: cúmque nuptiarum die nimio se vino ingurgitasset, expirauit. Pau.Diac.li.15. Ab, Vrsper. I. F. REX I. PHARAMOND F. REX 2. CLODIO
units.tr: ATTILA, King of the Huns and of nearly all the Northern nations, killed his brother and compelled his subjects to obey him. Aspiring to the Western Empire, and envious of the Visigoths, he assembled an army of 500,000 men, and burst into Gaul. In a very fierce battle on the Catalaunian Plains he fought with Aëtius, who was acting in the place of the Emperor, and with Theodoric, King of the Visigoths. On both sides 180,000 men (others write 200,000) were slain, among them Theodoric; and so much blood was poured out that the little stream which flowed there suddenly became a raging torrent, carrying the corpses of the slain along with it. That battle was fought in the year of the world 4414, after the birth of Christ 452. Nobody retreated a step, nobody received a wound in the back; so fierce was the contest. But Attila, defeated, and at last coming to his senses, attacked Italy in a fury, and it would have been all over with it, had not the Pope, by a humble embassy, obtained the safety of all Italy. Afterwards he took as wife the daughter of the Emperor Valentinian, having threatened the Emperor otherwise; then he took another; and when on his wedding day he had gorged himself with too much wine, he died. Paul. Diac. bk. 15. From Ursper. I. F. KING I. PHARAMOND F. KING 2. CLODIO

units.la: FARAMVNDVS, primus Francorum Rex incepit apud eos imperare anno mundi 4383. à Christo nato 421. fuit hic Marcomiri Francorū Ducis filius, sed ut paulò altius rem repetam, Franci Troia oriundi (qua capta, Duce primùm Francione, ad Mœotim paludē se contulerant, nec procul ab ea urbem condiderant, quā ad Valentinianum usque Valentiani filium ac Gratiani fratrem incoluerant) Duce Marcomiro, Faramundi patre, in eam Germaniæ regionem, quæ nunc Franconia dicitur, concesserant tum cum ad vectigal pensitandum reuocati, Imperium, circa paludem Mœotidē agentes, detrectassent. Sub Faramûdo primùm usi sunt legibus Fràci:tunc enim quatuor ex primoribus qui cōtrouersias dirimeret, elegerunt: tunc etiam lex Saliqua cōdita Regnat. Faramundus apud Francos annos 11. Robertus Gaguin. li.1. Paul. item Æmyl. li.1.
units.tr: FARAMUNDUS, the first King of the Franks, began to rule over them in the year of the world 4383, from the birth of Christ 421. He was the son of Marcomir, Duke of the Franks; but to go back a little further, the Franks, descended from Troy (when it was taken, under their leader Francio, they had betaken themselves to the Lake Maeotis, and not far from it had founded a city, which they inhabited until the time of Valentinian, son of Valentinian and brother of Gratian), under their leader Marcomir, father of Faramundus, had moved into that region of Germany which is now called Franconia, when, being summoned back to pay tribute, they had refused the rule of the Empire while dwelling around the Lake Maeotis. Under Faramundus the Franks first used laws; for then they chose four of the leading men to settle disputes. Then also the Salic law was drawn up. Faramundus reigned among the Franks for 11 years. Robert Gaguin, bk. 1. Also Paul; likewise Aemilius, bk. 1.

units.la: CLODIO, secundus Francorum Rex Faramundo patri succedit, anno mundi 4394. à Christo nato 432. Hic Thuringos subegit: Cameracum cepit: Romanos ad Rhenum proftrauit: traiecto flumine, Tornacum etiam cepit, in Galliam traiecit, finitimos Reges vicit: Burgundiam, Tholosam, totámque Aquitaniam in potestatem redegit: comatos voluit esse Francos, libertatis indicium, comatus ipse dictus. Rexit annos 18. Vide ut supra. R. FRAN. 3 MEROVEVS REX 4 CHILDERICVS
units.tr: CLODIO, the second King of the Franks, succeeded his father Faramundus in the year of the world 4394, from the birth of Christ 432. He subdued the Thuringians; he took Cambrai; he drove the Romans back to the Rhine; having crossed the river, he also took Tournai, crossed into Gaul, and defeated the neighbouring kings; he brought Burgundy, Toulouse, and all Aquitaine under his power. He wished the Franks to be long-haired, as a sign of freedom, and was himself called "the long-haired." He reigned 18 years. See above. R. FRAN. 3 MEROVEUS KING 4 CHILDERICUS

units.la: MEROVEVS tertius Francorum Rex, succedit Clodioni anno mundi 4412. à Christo nato 450. siquidem occisis à Bonifacio in Africa pueris Valentiniani Cæsaris, aduersus eum à matre Placidia missis, ad tantæ cladis famam Franci, velut nouo classico exciti, hoc Rege in Galliam regressi sunt. Cogitur Aëtius, exercitus Romani dux, cũ pristinis hostibus Francis, Burgundionibúsq; fœdus ferire: cui etiã opem tulerunt aduersus Attilã in campis Catalaunicis, vbi prostrata sunt vtrinque 200000. armatorum: tũc rediit Attilã in suam Hungariam. Porrò Aëtius Francos cum eximiis laudibus dimittit. Franci longius spe promota, Senonum etiam, Parisiorúmque ac Aurelianensium ciuitates occupauere. Quicquid in Gallia Meroveus Rex cum suis possedit, Francia dici cœpit. Expectatione autem magnorum nouorúmque motuum cõsiliorúmque, Meroveus obiit, anno regni 10. Vide Paul. Æmy.li.i.Gag.li.i.
units.tr: MEROVEUS, the third King of the Franks, succeeded Clodio in the year of the world 4412, from the birth of Christ 450. For when the boys of the Caesar Valentinian, who had been sent by his mother Placidia against him, were slain in Africa by Bonifacius, the Franks, as if roused by a new trumpet call at the news of so great a disaster, returned to Gaul under this king. Aëtius, commander of the Roman army, was forced to make a treaty with his former enemies the Franks and the Burgundians; and they also gave him help against Attila on the Catalaunian Plains, where 200,000 armed men were laid low on both sides. Then Attila returned to his Hungary. Moreover, Aëtius dismissed the Franks with high praise. The Franks, their hopes raised further, also occupied the cities of the Senones, the Parisii and the Aurelianenses. Whatever Merovus the King possessed in Gaul with his men began to be called France. But, while waiting for great and new movements and plans, Merovus died, in the tenth year of his reign. See Paul. Aemil. bk. 1; Gaguin, bk. 1.

units.la: CHILDERICVS, Merouei filius, vir bello clarissimus, pacis artibus minus nobilis, successit patri anno mundi 4422. à nat. Christi 460. Hic cum pudicitiam illustrium fœminarum attentare diceretur, ob cõiurationem procerum, sibi fuga consulere coactus, in Thuringiam ad paternos amicos se contulit, expectaturus fortunam aliquam redeundi: datis prius occultis mandatis amico Vidomaro, acerrimi ingenij viro: nummúmq; aureum cum in duas partes Childericus diuisisset, alteram sibi retinuit, alterà illi dedit, vt nulli nuntio fides haberetur, nisi qui parte nummi deferret. Sic itaque bello nil opus fuit ad recuperandum regnū: plus amicitiæ necessitudo, quàm vlla arma, valuit. Rexit annos 26. Vide vt supra.
units.tr: CHILDERICUS, son of Merovus, a man most famous in war, less noble in the arts of peace, succeeded his father in the year of the world 4422, from the birth of Christ 460. When he was said to have attempted the chastity of noblewomen, and because of a conspiracy of the nobles, he was forced to look to his own safety by flight; he betook himself to Thuringia, to his father's friends, to await some chance of returning. Having first given secret instructions to his friend Vidomarus, a man of the keenest mind, and having split a gold coin into two parts, he kept one himself and gave the other to him, so that no messenger should be trusted unless he brought the part of the coin. Thus there was no need of war to recover the kingdom: the bond of friendship counted for more than any arms. He reigned 26 years. See above.

units.la: VALENTINIANVS tertius, Constantio & Placidia genitus, ab Honorio cum matre pulsus, in oriente proficiscitur, à Theodosio iuniore suscipitur: subinde mortuo ipso Honorio, Eudoxia Theodosij filia in vxore accepta, Romam opportunè missus, Ioannem tyrannum obterit: à Theodosio Augustus appellatur, Romæque Imperat, anno mundi 4329. à Christo nato 427. cum Genserico statim fœdus init, parte Africæ, vt videri voluit, cōtento: & aduersus Attilam Aëtij ductu, feliciter confixit: quem Aëtium postea iussit occidi: à cuius militibus, in vltionē, ipse Imperator paulò post occiditur. Hoc principe Fræci[?] Gallias, Angli & Scoti Britanniam occupant. Vandali Africam populantur. Hunni Europam vexant & Italiam: tunc imperium Romanum funditus est collapsum ad Carolum magnū vsque: nihilominus tamen interea Constantinopolitani Imperatores, Romanos se quoque Imperatores nuncupabant. imperauit annos 30. Pomp. Læ. Egna. Pau. Dic. lib. 5.
units.tr: VALENTINIAN III, born of Constantius and Placidia, was driven out by Honorius together with his mother, and set out for the East; he was received by the younger Theodosius. Then, when Honorius himself had died, having taken Eudoxia, daughter of Theodosius, as his wife, he was sent opportunely to Rome, and crushed the tyrant John. He was called Augustus by Theodosius, and reigned at Rome in the year of the world 4329, from the birth of Christ 427. He at once made a treaty with Genseric, content, as he wished it to seem, with a part of Africa; and under the leadership of Aëtius he successfully defeated Attila; Aëtius he afterwards ordered to be killed, and a little later the Emperor himself was killed by Aëtius's soldiers in revenge. Under this prince the Franks occupied Gaul, the Angles and Scots occupied Britain, the Vandals ravaged Africa, the Huns harassed Europe and Italy. Then the Roman Empire collapsed utterly, down to Charlemagne; nevertheless, in the meantime, the Emperors of Constantinople still styled themselves Roman Emperors. He reigned 30 years. Pomp. Læt. Egn. Paul. Diac. bk. 5.

units.la: MARTIANVS humili loco natus, militia tamen clarus, Pulcheriæ Archadij filiæ opera, Constantinopoli, post Theodosium primum admodū senex imperauit. Cum Vandalis fœdus percussit: arma nunquam nisi prouocatus mouit: dicere solitus, Non decere principē arma sumere, dum licet ei in pace viuere. Is Talianum Iuliúmque (ambo fratres erant, qui eum olim ægrum hospitio susceperāt, & aquilæ superuolantis eius caput, auspicium retexerant, viaticóque 200. aureorū inopē & ægrum recrearāt) statim vt princeps est dictus, illum Constantinopoli, hunc Illyrico præfecit. Imperauit Martianus annis septem, auspicatus anno mundi 4413. à Christo nato 451. Vide vt supra.
units.tr: MARTIAN, born of humble station, yet famous in military service, through the efforts of Pulcheria, daughter of Arcadius, became Emperor at Constantinople after Theodosius the Younger, being quite an old man. He made a treaty with the Vandals; he never took up arms unless provoked, and was accustomed to say: "It is not fitting for a prince to take up arms while he may live in peace." He appointed Talianus and Julius (who were brothers, and who had once taken him in as a guest when he was sick, and had interpreted the flight of an eagle hovering over his head as an omen, and had relieved him, who was needy and sick, with 200 gold pieces for his journey) as soon as he had been named prince, the one at Constantinople, the other over Illyricum. Martian reigned seven years, beginning in the year of the world 4413, from the birth of Christ 451. See above.

units.la: FL A. Vale.Leo,primus Græcanici sanguinis, Asparis Patricij factione,post Martianū Constātinopoli imperat anno mundi 4420. à Christo nato 458. Aspar convenerat cum Leone, ut factus Imperator, Ardaburiū eius filiū adoptaret:quod Leo præstitit:populus , ubi hæc novit, Ardaburium cum patre interemit:vel ut alij sentiunt,insidiarū in se autores occidit:Anthemium Cæsarē fecit Leo, Romámque misit : deinde Olybrium misit qui Anthemiū regno pelleret:at factione Richomeri iam iam fuerat Severus Lucanus Ravennæ Imperator electus. Leo Basiliscum Patritiū adversus Genfericū misit,qui eum propulsavit,cùm iterum in Italiam irrumpere tētaret. Cum Ostrogothis fœdus pepigit,(nam Illyrium vastabant)eisq; Pannoniam, acceptis obsidibus , incolendam concessit.Hic Leo paulò ante obitum Leonem, Ariadnæ filiæ suæ filium , consortem imperij fecit.Byzantium magna ex parte conflagravit:præterquā quòd Italia in perpetuo motu fuit. Imperavit annos 17. Pomp. Læt. Egna.lib.2.Pau.Diac.lib.16.
units.tr: FL A. VALENTINIAN? LEO, the first of Greek race, by the faction of the patrician Aspar, reigned at Constantinople after Martian in the year of the world 4420, from the birth of Christ 458. Aspar had agreed with Leo that, once he was made Emperor, he would adopt Ardaburius, Aspar's son; Leo carried this out; the people, when they learned of this, killed Ardaburius together with his father, or, as others think, they killed the instigators of the plot against himself. Leo made Anthemius Caesar and sent him to Rome; then he sent Olybrius to drive Anthemius from the throne; but by the faction of Ricimer, Severus Lucanus had already been elected Emperor at Ravenna. Leo sent Basiliscus, the patrician, against Genseric, who drove him off when he attempted to break into Italy again. He made a treaty with the Ostrogoths (for they were laying waste Illyricum), and, having received hostages, allowed them to settle in Pannonia. This Leo, shortly before his death, made Leo, the son of his daughter Ariadne, his co-ruler in the empire. Byzantium was for the most part burned down, and Italy was in constant turmoil. He reigned 17 years. Pomp. Læt. Egn. bk. 2; Paul. Diac. bk. 16.

units.la: LEO iunior, puer ab avo relictus , cum annum præfuisset, Zenoni patri,aut saltē vitrico,manibus suis diadema impo-suit, patremque pro se deinceps imperare iussit.Egna.lib.2.
units.tr: LEO the Younger, a boy left by his grandfather, after he had ruled for one year, placed the diadem with his own hands on Zeno his father, or at least his stepfather, and afterwards ordered his father to rule in his place. Egn. bk. 2.

units.la: ZENO Constantinopoli imperat anno mundi 4437. à Christo nato 475. fuit ex Isauris Ciliciæ, obscuri sanguinis, facie deformis, moribus tyrannus, ut Isaurũ agnoscas. Hic Theodoricum Ostrogothorum Regẽ cum unicè diligeret, Cõsulem fecit, ac in Italiam aduersus Odoacrẽ misit: occurrẽtem Odoacrem Theodoricus prælio vicit, fugauit: fugiẽs Odoacer, intra mœnia vrbis non admissus, citissimè Rauẽnam cõtendit. triennium ibi obsessus, tãdémque à Theodorico in fidem receptus, contra fidem truculeter excarnificatur. Pellitur regno Zeno à Basilisco factione vxoris Augustæ, cùm in Isauriam cõcesisset maritus Imperator: non multò pòst reuersus Zeno Basiliscũ expulit, quẽ vnà cum filio inedia mori coëgit. Sunt qui viuum adhuc inclusum ab vxore sepulchro tradant. Hoc principe incendium odeò graue fuit, ut præter maximã vrbis partem conflagratam, centum & viginti librorum millia combusta sint: inter quæ & Homeri poëma, intestino draconis 120. pedũ, aureis literis descriptum. Pom. Læt.Pau.Diac.lib.6.Egna.lib.2.
units.tr: ZENO reigned at Constantinople in the year of the world 4437, from the birth of Christ 475. He was from the Isaurians of Cilicia, of obscure birth, deformed in face, and a tyrant in character, so that you would recognise him as an Isaurian. He, loving Theodoric, King of the Ostrogoths, above all others, made him consul, and sent him into Italy against Odoacer. Theodoric defeated Odoacer, who came to meet him, in battle, and put him to flight; Odoacer, fleeing, was not admitted within the walls of the city and hurried most swiftly to Ravenna. Besieged there for three years, at last he was received by Theodoric under a pledge of good faith, and, contrary to his pledge, was savagely butchered. Zeno was driven from the kingdom by Basiliscus, through the faction of the Empress, while the Emperor, her husband, had withdrawn into Isauria; not long afterwards Zeno, returning, expelled Basiliscus, whom he forced to die of starvation together with his son. Some relate that the wife kept him shut up alive in a tomb. Under this prince the fire was so severe that, besides the greater part of the city which was burned down, one hundred and twenty thousand books were consumed; among them the poem of Homer, written in golden letters on the intestine of a dragon 120 feet long. Pom. Læt. Paul. Diac. bk. 6; Egn. bk. 2.

units.la: ARIADNA, supradicti Zenonis uxor, fratrem Basiliscum Imperatorem fecit, filiúmque eius Cæsarem, absente quidem viro suo, qui rediés[?] supplicium de patre & filio sumpsit, uti iam dictum est. Bap.Egna.lib.2.Romanorum Principum. P.F.AVG IMP.ANASTAS IMP.IVSTINVS.MAIORI
units.tr: ARIADNE, the wife of the aforementioned Zeno, made her brother Basiliscus emperor and his son Caesar, while her husband was away; he returned and exacted punishment from the father and son, as has already been said. Baptista Egnatius, book 2, Roman Princes. P.F.AVG IMP.ANASTAS IMP.IVSTINVS.MAIORI

units.la: F L A. Vale. Anastasius, Constantinopoli post Zenonem, Ariadnæ opera, imperat, anno mundi 4454. à Christo nato 492. Hic à Græcis cognominatus est Dicoros, à discoloribus oculorum pupillis, quarū dextra nigricās, sinistra cœrulea fuit. inter bonos principes referedus veniret, quanquam humili loco ad imperiū sit euectus, nisi postea mutatus Eutychianæ hæ-resi adhæsisset: vnde illi aduersus orthodoxos graue dissidium conflatum. Legatos Indorum cum muneribus venientes, placidissimè audiuit. à mari ad Selymbriā longum murum duxit, ne incursiones Mysorum, Bulgarorū, & Scytharū obesse possent. Athenodorus Tyrānus in Cilicia pœnas luit: & Longinus tanquam fera dilaniatus est. Hunni, non cōtenti Armenorum spoliis, Cappadociā vastauerunt, & vsque ad Lycaoniam vrbes diripuerunt. Ad Aquilonem Vitalianus rebellauit: vt quiesceret nongēta pondo auri ab Imperatore accepit. Getæ Macedoniā, Thessaliam, Epirum diripuerunt: quibus, pro captiuis redimendis aurum cùm misset Anastasius, nec sufficeret hostiū votis, Barbari captiuos aut in domibus suffocarūt, aut pro mœnibus in cōspectu multitudinis trucidarunt. obiit octuagenario maior, subita morte, vel fulmine tactus, ob herefim vt aiunt, imperij anno 28. Pom. Læ. Egna. lib. 2.
units.tr: F L A. Vale. Anastasius, at Constantinople, succeeded Zeno, by the work of Ariadne; he reigned in the year of the world 4454, from the birth of Christ 492. He was called Dicorus by the Greeks, from the differently coloured pupils of his eyes, the right being dark and the left blue. He should be counted among the good princes, although he was raised to the empire from a humble station, had he not afterwards changed and adhered to the Eutychian heresy, whence a grave dissension arose against the orthodox. He most graciously received Indian envoys who came with gifts. He built a long wall from the sea to Selymbria, so that the incursions of the Mysians, Bulgarians and Scythians might be prevented. Athenodorus, tyrant in Cilicia, paid the penalty, and Longinus was torn apart like a wild beast. The Huns, not content with the spoils of the Armenians, laid waste Cappadocia and plundered cities as far as Lycaonia. In the north, Vitalian rebelled; to keep quiet he received nine hundred pounds of gold from the emperor. The Getae plundered Macedonia, Thessaly and Epirus; when Anastasius sent gold to redeem the captives, and it did not satisfy the demands of the enemy, the barbarians either suffocated the captives in their houses or butchered them before the walls in full view of the crowd. He died at over eighty years of age, by a sudden death, or struck by lightning, as some say, because of heresy, in the twenty-eighth year of his reign. Pompon. Laetus, Egnatius, book 2.

units.la: IVSTINVS Thrax, dolo imperiū adeptus est: nam mortuo Anastasio, accepta ab Amantio eunucho pecunia vt militi pro Theocritiano eligendo distribueret, in se cautè Thrax suffragia vertit. fuit primùm suùm custos, deinde boum, post lignarij cuiusdā minister, postea miles, deinde princeps ordinis, hinc Comes, dein Imperator: annis 9. optimè præfuit, & feliciter. Vide vt supra.
units.tr: Justin the Thracian obtained the empire by trickery: for when Anastasius died, having accepted money from the eunuch Amantius to distribute to the soldiers in order to choose Theocritianus, the Thracian cunningly turned the votes to himself. He was first a keeper of pigs, then a herdsman of oxen, afterwards a servant of some woodcutter, later a soldier, then a leader of a rank, thence a count, and then emperor. He governed very well and successfully for nine years. See above.

units.la: AMALASIUNTHA Theodorici filia Athalaricíque Gothorũ Regis mater fuit, cum qua imperauit ipse filius octo annos, auspicatus anno mundi 4488. à Christo nato 526. hæc mortuo filio Athalarico Theodatum cognatum in consortem imperij legit: verum ingratus hic, ac perfidus, eam paulò post relegauit, tandẽ etiam obtruncari iussit: nec ita diu postea imperauit: quinetiã ipsum Optaris occidit: quare Gothi Vitigem Regem crearunt: quẽ captũ Belisarius Rauenna potitus, Constantinopolim duxit. Blondus lib.3. Deca.1. Pau.Diac.lib.7. Ab. Ursper. Pom.Læ.in Iustiniano. Pau.Emy.lib.1.de rc.Franc.
units.tr: AMALASUNTHA was the daughter of Theodoric and the mother of Athalaric, king of the Goths, with whom her son reigned for eight years, having begun in the year of the world 4488, from the birth of Christ 526. When her son Athalaric died, she chose Theodatus, her kinsman, as partner in the empire; but he, ungrateful and treacherous, soon afterwards banished her and at last ordered her to be killed. Nor did he reign long after this; indeed he himself killed Optaris; therefore the Goths made Vitiges king, whom Belisarius captured, took Ravenna, and led to Constantinople. Blondus, book 3, Decade 1. Paulus Diaconus, book 7. Abbot Urspergensis. Pompon. Laetus in Justinian. Paulus Aemilius, book 1, on the French affairs.

units.la: ATHALARICUS Gothorum Rex, Theodorico auo materno, (qui Gothorum primus in Italia imperauit 34. annis) iuuenis admodũ, nempe octo annorum, successit: huius immaturam ætate mater rexit, erudiendámque ciuilibus, priusquam bellicis artibus curauit: nam pater Eutharicus obierat. hic ætatis anno 16. imperij 8. decessit. Vide ut supra.
units.tr: ATHALARIC, king of the Goths, succeeded his maternal grandfather Theodoric (who was the first of the Goths to rule in Italy, for 34 years) while still quite young, namely eight years old. His mother ruled during his immaturity and took care to educate him in civil rather than military arts; for his father Eutharic had died. He died in the sixteenth year of his age and the eighth of his reign. See above.

units.la: CLODOVEVS hoc nomine primus, Francorum Rex quintus, Francicæ vtique religionis conditor, successit patri Childerico anno mundi 4448. à Christo nato 486. Hic vxorem duxit Christianam Clotildem Burgundionem. Syagrius, Egidij Romani filius (eius qui, expulso Childerico, Francis præfuerat) à Sueffionibus expulsus, Tolosam confugit ad Alaricum Visigothorum Regem: à quo proditus, & Clodoueo redditus, securi percutitur. Sic defiere expulsi & cæsi in Galliis imperium habere Romani. Deinde Clodoueus Turingiam debellat: à Rheno ad Sequanam regnum ampliat: ad Ligerim vsque fines suos extendit. In bello quod ad Tolbiacum gessit, periculi magnitudine, idolorúmque diffidentia, repente vouit se Christianum fore: voto facto Germanos hostes vicit, subegit, tributa imposuit: à D. Remigio Remensi Episcopo cum Francis omnibus baptizatur. Post hæc Gundebaldum Burgúdiæ Regé regno & patria cedere coëgit: Alaricum Regem cum suis Visigothis fudit. Moenia Engolismæ ruinosa in cōspectu Clodouei vrbem aggressuri ruunt: illinc Burdegalâ vsq; hostes insecutus, iterum vicit. Omnes tum feré Gallias, & vniuersam Alemaniâ Rex sub ditione tenuit: ab Anastasio Imper. dona recepit, Patritiatus & Consulatus titulum, & insignia, coronâ insuper auream, multis vnionibus distinctam, quam postea Româ D. Petro offerendam remisit. rexit an. 30. Hic Lutetiæ sepultus est in æde quâ D. Petro & Paulo erexerat: hodie Fanü D. Genouefes vocatur. Æmy. li. 1.
units.tr: CLOVIS, the first of this name, fifth king of the Franks, and founder of the Frankish religion, succeeded his father Childeric in the year of the world 4448, from the birth of Christ 486. He married the Christian Clotilde, a Burgundian. Syagrius, son of Aegidius the Roman (who had governed the Franks after Childeric was expelled), was driven out by the Suessiones and fled to Toulouse to Alaric, king of the Visigoths; betrayed by him and handed over to Clovis, he was beheaded. Thus the Romans, expelled and cut down, ceased to hold power in Gaul. Then Clovis subdued Thuringia; he enlarged his kingdom from the Rhine to the Seine and extended his borders as far as the Loire. In the battle he fought at Tolbiac, in the great danger and distrust of their idols, he suddenly vowed to become a Christian; after making the vow he defeated the German enemies, subdued them, and imposed tribute; he was baptized with all his Franks by St Remigius, bishop of Reims. After this he forced Gundobad, king of Burgundy, to yield his kingdom and country; he routed Alaric, king of the Visigoths, with his men. The walls of Angoulême, in full view of Clovis, collapsed in ruins just as he was about to attack the city; from there, pursuing the enemy as far as Bordeaux, he conquered them again. Then the king held almost all of Gaul and all of Germany under his sway; from the emperor Anastasius he received gifts, the title and insignia of patrician and consul, and moreover a golden crown set with many pearls, which he afterwards sent back to be offered to St Peter at Rome. He reigned for 30 years. He was buried at Paris in the church which he had built to Saints Peter and Paul; today it is called the church of St Genevieve. Aemilius, book 1.

units.la: CHILDEBERTVS patri Clodoueo successit ann. mundi 4478. à Christo nato 516. Hic Almaricum fundit, occidit: Hispanias populatur: sororē, quòd ab Arriana hæresi abhorreret, à viro Almarico Alarici filio duiè tractatâ, reducit. Tādem obiit sine liberis anno regni 45. Sepelitur in æde D. Germani ad Parisios ab eo erecta, & dicata D. Vincentio.
units.tr: CHILDEBERT succeeded his father Clovis in the year of the world 4478, from the birth of Christ 516. He defeated and killed Almaric; he ravaged Spain; he brought back his sister, who had been treated badly by her husband Almaric, son of Alaric, because she abhorred the Arian heresy. At last he died without children in the forty-fifth year of his reign. He was buried in the church of St Germanus at Paris, which he had built and dedicated to St Vincent.

units.la: IUSTINIANUS, Iustini ex sorore nepos, ab avunculo, paulò ante obitum successor instituitur, imperatq; anno mundi 4491. à Christo nato 529. Hic Romani imperij gloriam Plurimum ampliavit. Primùm Persæ, Belisarij opera, intra suos fines cōtinuit, fudit, fugavit, trans Eufrate abire coëgit: iura imperij toto Orieti posuit: Belisarium cum victoria redeuntem, & aureo curru triumphantem Iustinianus magno plausu excepit. Inde eodem duce Romā à Gothorum servitute asseruit: Africa quoque recuperata, Gelimerem, Vandalorum Regem, catenis vinctum Constantinopolim misit Belisarius: triumphus maior Persico fuit. Narsete duce, occupato aliunde Belisario, tandem Gothos deleuit Iustinianus. Leges, fusissimè antea dispersas, opera Triboniani cōtraxit: Institutionū libros quatuor edidit: Codicem invulgavit. Maximus sanè princeps, nisi avariciæ, & delirij Eutychiani reus fuisset: Serici usus è Persis ad Græcos hoc tempore trāsiit, jampridè desitus. Moritur morbo, & mente captus, anno ætatis &c. imperij 38. Pom. Læt. Pau. Diaco. lib. 7. & 8. Egna. lib. 2. Eutr. auctus lib. 16. autor est, Iustinianum morte præventum cum edictum ubiq; à pietate alienum transmisisset.
units.tr: JUSTINIAN, nephew of Justin through his sister, was named successor by his uncle shortly before the latter's death, and reigned in the year of the world 4491, from the birth of Christ 529. He greatly extended the glory of the Roman empire. First, by the work of Belisarius, he held the Persians within their borders, routed, put to flight, and forced them to withdraw beyond the Euphrates; he established the authority of the empire over the whole East. Justinian received Belisarius with great applause when he returned in victory and triumphed in a golden chariot. Then, under the same general, he freed Rome from the servitude of the Goths; Africa too was recovered, and Belisarius sent Gelimer, king of the Vandals, bound in chains, to Constantinople; his triumph was greater than the Persian one. When Belisarius was occupied elsewhere under the command of Narses, Justinian at last destroyed the Goths. He gathered the laws, which had been very widely scattered before, by the work of Tribonian; he published four books of Institutes; he made the Code known to all. He would have been a most excellent prince, had he not been guilty of avarice and the madness of Eutyches; the use of silk passed at this time from the Persians to the Greeks, though it had long been unknown. He died of a disease, and with his mind impaired, in the year of his age etc. and the thirty-eighth of his reign. Pompon. Laetus; Paulus Diaconus, books 7 and 8; Egnatius, book 2. Eutropius, enlarged, book 16, is the authority that Justinian, prevented by death, had sent out an edict everywhere that was alien to piety.

units.la: THEODORA uxor fuit Iustiniani, ex quo matrem Iustinæ suscepit Iustinianus. Hæc fraudē molita est in Sylverium Papam, quem Belisarius falsit testibus convictū in exilium misit, ubi etiam mortuus est. consulito Eutropium auctum li. 16.
units.tr: THEODORA was the wife of Justinian, from whom Justinian had received his mother Justina. She plotted against Pope Silverius, whom Belisarius, having falsely convicted him by false witnesses, sent into exile, where he also died. Consult Eutropius, enlarged, book 16.

units.la: CLOTARIVS Francorum Rex septimus, atque huius nominis primus, succedit fratri Childeberto, imperatq; Francis anno mundi 4522. à Christo nato 560. Hic tertiam redituum ecclesiæ partem sibi dari iusit: cui dationi Turonum Archiepiscopus liberè & fortiter se opposuit, vaticinatus regno spoliatum iri Regem, si pauperum bona imminueret aut eriperet. Cranũ filium bello subactum, cum vxore, liberis, & vniuersa familia exurendum curauit. is enim patri non obsecundans, multa Galliæ dãna intulerat, primùm à Childeberto patruo instigatus, deinde socero Aquitaniæ duce eius causam defendente. Conabus Britânus eum excepit, ac tutatus est. Socerum illum Rex ferè perdiderat. Britannum autem paulò ante filij necem interemerat. Rex Compendij obiit anno regni quinto. Pau.Æmy.lib.1.Robertus Gaguinus lib.2.
units.tr: CLOTAIRE, seventh king of the Franks and the first of this name, succeeded his brother Childebert and ruled the Franks in the year of the world 4522, from the birth of Christ 560.
