From this Geoffrey of the Great Tooth several Kings of the island of Cyprus, of the surname Lusignan, traced their origin. See part three of the Annals of Aquitaine; for book 15 is divided into four parts.

units.la: MICHAEL Paphlago, Zoës adulter, quíque eius virum Romanú Argyropylum intra balneas immerserat, ab eadem Imperatrice Zoë Imperator instituitur Constantinopoli, anno mundi 4996. à Christo nato 1034. Fuit hic mancipium barbarum, nulla re nisi forma commendatum, mente etiam commotum, labénsque ad singula momenta, spuma insuper oris fœda. Quis non effrenem in quinquagenaria muliere Zoë libidinê, amorémque fœdissimum execretur, aut fortunæ aleam in hoc principe non admiretur? ascivit primùm illa omnem sibi potestatem, Michaële velut ministro vsa, sed non diu durauit hæc observantia: nam Michaël imperij habenas retinuit, nec malè rexit. Tricénales inducias cum Ægyptio Rege percussit: Edeffam obsidione liberauit: domi in suos facilis, vni Zoë, propter expertam libidinem, parum æquus fuit. Intercutis morbo laborans, Michaëlem Calaphaten hæredê imperij dixit. imperauit annos ferè septem. Vide Egna.lib.2. Cosmo.Mun.lib.4.
units.tr: MICHAEL the Paphlagonian, lover of Zoe, who had drowned her husband, the Roman Argyropylus, in the baths, was instituted Emperor at Constantinople by that same Empress Zoe, in the year of the world 4996, from the birth of Christ 1034. This man was a barbarian slave, commended by nothing but his looks, troubled also in mind, and falling into fits at every moment, with foul foam at his mouth besides. Who would not curse the unbridled lust of Zoe in a woman of fifty, and her most foul love, or not wonder at the gamble of fortune in this prince? At first she assumed all power to herself, using Michael as a mere servant, but this arrangement did not last long; for Michael retained the reins of empire and did not govern badly. He struck a truce of thirty years with the King of Egypt; he freed Edessa from siege; at home he was mild towards his own people, but towards Zoe alone, on account of her experienced lust, he was little fair. Suffering from dropsy, he named Michael Calaphates heir of the empire. He reigned about seven years. See Egnatius, book 2; Cosmographia Munsteri, book 4.

units.la: MICHAEL Calaphates à Zoë adoptatus, eius pedibus aduolutus iurat se titulo tenus imperaturum, potestatem penes eam mansuram: his blandiciis ad imperium euehitur Constantinopolitanum, anno mundi 5004. à Christo nato 1042. paulò pòst in Zoën machinatur, fingés ab ea sibi structas vitæ insidias, ac venenum positum, à quibus innocens erat: relegat itaque eam in insulam, detondet, ac monacham facit: interim genio ipse indulget. Id inique ferens plebs, Theodorâ Zoës sororè, Imperatricem creant: Zoën reuocant: Michaëlem fugiente, capiunt, exoculant, vnà cum fratre: quæ familiaris Græcis pœna est. Sic præter sordes parentû, qui naues apud Paphlagonas pice oblinerent, vnde Calaphates etiam dictus, auarè, perfidè, ac crudeliter imperat Michaël hic, menses quatuor. Vide vt supra. III PF AVG. IMP. HENRICVS HENRICI III. AGNES VXOR
units.tr: Michael Calaphates, adopted by Zoë, threw himself at her feet and swore that he would reign only in name, with the power remaining in her hands. By these flatteries he was raised to the throne of Constantinople, in the year of the world 5004, from the birth of Christ 1042. Shortly afterwards he plotted against Zoë, pretending that she had laid traps for his life and set poison for him, though he was innocent. He therefore banished her to an island, had her head shaved, and made her a nun; meanwhile he himself indulged his pleasures. The common people, taking this badly, created Theodora, Zoë's sister, as Empress, and recalled Zoë. When Michael fled, they captured him, gouged out his eyes together with his brother. This is a punishment familiar among the Greeks. Thus Michael, who was called Calaphates because his parents had been tar-makers (pitch-smearers of ships) among the Paphlagonians, ruled greedily, treacherously and cruelly for four months. See above.

units.la: HENRICVS, huius nominis tertius, dictus Niger, post Conradum 2. Romæ imperat anno mundi 5001[?]. à Christo nato 1039. Hic Conradi Franci filius siue gener, primùm Bohemos bello inuasit, sed ab his Hungarorum præsidio adiutis, vincitur: sequente anno adeò illos bello fatigat, vt Regem eorum tributarium fecerit. Lotaringiæ Ducem parêre imperio compulit: apud Capuam Saracenos vicit. Cæterum pertæsus eorum quæ Romæ circa Pontifices per summum scelus agerêtur, Romā contendens, abdicatis adulterinis Pontificibus aliquot, Clementem secundum Pontificiæ sedi præfecit: & vt caveret in posterum Pontificum securitati, iureiurando Romanos adegit, neminem creationi eorum interfuturum sine eius permissu. Petrum Regem ab Hungaris eiectum, regno restituit: Capuam aduersus Saracenos nouo præsidio firmauit. Henricum filium annos quinque natum, Cæsarem eligi, & Aquisgrani coronari curauit: qui sub matris Agnetis tutela aliquandiu fuit. Imperat Henricus Niger ann. 17. Egna. lib.3.
units.tr: Henry, the third of that name, called the Black, ruled at Rome after Conrad II, in the year of the world 5001[?], from the birth of Christ 1039. He was the son or son-in-law of Conrad the Frank. At first he attacked the Bohemians in war, but, when they were aided by a Hungarian garrison, he was defeated. In the following year he so wore them down in war that he made their king a tributary. He compelled the Duke of Lorraine to obey his rule, and he defeated the Saracens at Capua. Moreover, weary of the wicked deeds that were being done at Rome concerning the Popes, he hastened to Rome, deposed several adulterous Popes, and set Clement II over the papal see. And so that in future he might secure the Popes' safety, he bound the Romans by oath that no one would take part in their election without his permission. He restored King Peter to his kingdom after he had been driven out by the Hungarians, and he strengthened Capua with a new garrison against the Saracens. He arranged for his son Henry, five years old, to be elected Caesar and crowned at Aachen; the boy was for some time under the guardianship of his mother Agnes. Henry the Black reigned for seventeen years. See Egnatius, book 3.

units.la: AGNES Gulielmi Aquitaniæ principis filia, nata in Pictonum Comitatu in Gallia, vxor fuit huius Henrici tertij, quæ suscepit ex eo Henricum quartum huius nominis Imperatorem: hæc non sine laude imperio præfuit annos quinque, dum adolesceret filius: sed Coloniensis Episcopus Otho, clam abducto puero, imperio eam deturbat. Vide Chron.
units.tr: Agnes, daughter of William, Prince of Aquitaine, born in the county of the Pictavians in Gaul, was the wife of this Henry III, and by him she bore Henry IV, later Emperor. She governed the empire for five years, not without praise, while her son was growing up. But Otto, Bishop of Cologne, secretly carried off the boy and drove her from power. See the Chronicle.

units.la: ZOE, ab exilio & monasterio assentiente universa plebe (uti dictum à me est) reuocata, & Michaële Calaphate exoculato, imperij faces suscipit Constantinopolitani, unà cum sorore Theodora. anno mundi eodem quo Michaël Calaphates quatuor mensesimperauit: itaque flagitia Imperatorum essecere ut muliebre æquius videretur imperium. At verò, cùm sit varium, ac mutabile semper Fœmina, ut inquit poëta, Zoë sexagenaria, ardens tamen adhuc libidine, Constantinum Monomachum ab exilio reuocat, sibíque eum maritû adiungit: curátque ut sceptrû imperij illi tradatur, cùm fœminarum vix treis mēses durasset imperiû. Vide Egna.lib.2.Cosmog.Munst.lib.4.
units.tr: Zoë, recalled from exile and from the convent with the assent of the whole populace (as I have said), and with Michael Calaphates blinded, took up the torch of the imperial power at Constantinople together with her sister Theodora, in the same year of the world in which Michael Calaphates had ruled for four months. So the crimes of the emperors had made female rule seem more fitting. But since, as the poet says, woman is always a changeable and fickle thing, Zoë, sixty years old yet still burning with lust, recalled Constantine Monomachus from exile and joined him to herself as husband, and she saw to it that the sceptre of empire was handed over to him, after the rule of the women had hardly lasted three months. See Egnatius, book 2, and the Cosmography of Münster, book 4.

units.la: CONSTANTINUS Monomachus, imperatorij quidem & ipse stemmatis, quem sibi in virum asciuit Zoë, Constantinopoli imperat anno mundi 5005. à Christo nato 1043. Hic ignauus, & luxu totus diffluens, concubinam, egregia alioqui forma, iustæ uxoris loco habuit, quam efflictim deperiit. Sustinuit tamen duo grauissima bella ciuilia, alterum à Maniace Georgio, alterum à Leone Tornicio, illata: & multa externa. Turcarum arma tunc primù per Asiam latius sunt euagata: victi tamen Roxolani, & Patzinacæ, Scythicum genus hominum. Zoë uxore septuagenaria fato mox functa, & ipse tandem podagricus, & pleuritide correptus obiit, anno imperij fere 13. Vide ut supra.
units.tr: Constantine Monomachus, himself also of imperial lineage, whom Zoë took as her husband, ruled at Constantinople in the year of the world 5005, from the birth of Christ 1043. He was lazy and wholly given over to luxury; he treated a concubine, otherwise of outstanding beauty, as if she were his lawful wife, and he passionately loved her. Nevertheless he endured two very grave civil wars, one waged against him by George Maniaces and the other by Leo Tornicius, and many foreign ones. Then for the first time the arms of the Turks spread more widely through Asia; yet the Roxolani and the Patzinaks, a Scythian people, were defeated. When Zoë, then seventy years old, soon died by fate, Constantine himself, at last afflicted with gout and pleurisy, died after about thirteen years of rule. See above.

units.la: THEODORA Zoës soror, quæ iam etiam cum ea menses circiter treis imperium tenuerat Constantinopolitanū (vti in Zoë dixi) nunc denuo, sed sola, post Constantinum Monomachum imperat, anno mundi 5017. à Christo nato 1055. Nec verò est quòd pudeat hanc in ordine ac serie Imperatorum inferere, cùm non muliebriter se gesserit: quinimo tanta domi, forísque hac imperante quies & ocium fuit, tanta rerum omnium ubertas, ut fœminei imperij neminem pœniteret. Verùm ingrauescente cum ætate morbo, illecebris Eunuchorum adducta, Michaëlem iam senem imperij ac curæ participem fecit: nec ita diu superuixit: annos propè duos imperauit. Vide Egna.lib.2.Rom.prin.& Cosmo. Munst. ubi de Græcia tractat, libro quarto.
units.tr: Theodora, Zoë's sister, who had also before this held the imperial power at Constantinople together with her for about three months (as I said under Zoë), now ruled again, but alone, after Constantine Monomachus, in the year of the world 5017, from the birth of Christ 1055. Nor is there any reason to be ashamed of listing her in the order and series of emperors, since she did not conduct herself in a womanly manner. Indeed, under her rule there was such peace and leisure at home and abroad, and such abundance of all things, that no one regretted the rule of a woman. But as her illness grew worse with age, she was led on by the enticements of eunuchs and made Michael, now an old man, a partner in the empire and in its cares. Nor did she survive long; she reigned for nearly two years. See Egnatius, book 2, Roman section, and the Cosmography of Münster, where he treats of Greece, book four.

units.la: MICHAEL senior, post Theodoram supradictam, qua dixi via, Constantinopoli imperat, anno mundi 5019. à Christi natiuitate 1057. Fuit quidem hic Michaël genere & opibus clarus: cætera minus ad imperij fasces ac administrationem suscipiendam, aut exequendam, idoneus, vel propter ætatem decrepitam & prægrauantem. Quare cùm vix etiam annum imperitasset, Isaacij Comneni factio eum imperio deturbauit, & in ordinem redegit: priuatus itaque factus, paulò post fatis ac naturæ concessit. Videto ut supra. D·N·HENRICVS·P·F·AVG IMP·CAES·HENRICVS·V·AVG
units.tr: Michael the Elder, after the aforementioned Theodora, in the manner I have described, ruled at Constantinople in the year of the world 5019, from the birth of Christ 1057. This Michael was indeed distinguished by birth and wealth, but in other respects he was less suited to taking up or carrying out the duties of empire, on account of his decrepit and burdensome old age. Therefore, when he had scarcely reigned even a year, the faction of Isaac Comnenus threw him from the throne and reduced him to the ranks; made a private man, he shortly afterwards yielded to fate and nature. See above.

units.la: HENRICVS quartus (tertium facit Egnatius) Henrici Nigri filius, Romanus Imperator patri Romanorum Imperatori succedit anno mundi 5018. à Christo nato 1056. Hic dicitur M. Marcellum & Julium Cæsarem supergressus, bis & sexagies pugnasse. In hoc huius generis Imperatorum virtus defecit: & totius Germaniæ imperium adeò corruere cœpit, ut postea in veterem statum redigi nunquam potuerit. Tragœdię huius autor Papa Hildebrandus fuit: qui statuit Pontificatus confirmationem à Cæsare non esse petendam, contra sanctionem Henrici Nigri, quam patris constitutionem ratam haberi voluit: quamobrem non tantum à Papa excommunicatur, sed & principibus potentioribus mandat Papa, ut Imperatorem alterum creent: Rudolfus creatur, adversus quem mouet Henricus, & multis præliis tandem vincit. Deinde Romam venit, & urbe per vim capta, Papam cepit. Obiit Henricus Leodij, carcere detentus à filio, ab Episcopis solicitato, quem etiam Imperatorem delegerat pater: imperat Henricus quartus annos 50. Rodulfo misit Hildebrandus coronam cum hac inscriptione,
units.tr: Henry IV (Egnatius makes him the third), son of Henry the Black, Roman Emperor, succeeded his father as Emperor of the Romans in the year of the world 5018, from the birth of Christ 1056. He is said to have surpassed Marcus Marcellus and Julius Caesar and to have fought sixty-two times. In this man the virtue of this line of emperors failed, and the empire of all Germany began to fall to such a degree that afterwards it could never be restored to its former state. The author of this tragedy was Pope Hildebrand, who decided that confirmation of the papacy was not to be sought from the Emperor, contrary to the decree of Henry the Black, which he wished to be held as valid as his father's constitution. For this reason the Pope not only excommunicated him, but also ordered the more powerful princes to create another emperor. Rudolf was created, against whom Henry moved, and at last he conquered him in many battles. Then he came to Rome, and having taken the city by force, he captured the Pope. Henry died at Liège, held in prison by his son, who had been urged on by the bishops, and whom his father had himself chosen as emperor. Henry IV reigned for fifty years. Hildebrand sent Rudolf a crown with this inscription:
The rock gave it to Peter, Peter gave the diadem to Rudolf.

units.la: HENRICVS quintus, Henrici quarti filius, qui patrem bello & carcere est infestatus, post eum imperat anno mundi 5068. à Christo nato 1106. Recusat eum coronare Papa, nisi prius statuat Pontificem & Episcopos sine Cæsaris consensu creandos: Romam & Papam capit, coronam extorquet, & investituram. Tertiò Italiam intrans Gelasium Papam urbe pepulit. Obiit nullis relictis liberis anno imperij 20. Vide Chron. Egnat. lib.3.
units.tr: Henry V, son of Henry IV, who harassed his father with war and prison, succeeded him in the year of the world 5068, from the birth of Christ 1106. The Pope refused to crown him unless he first agreed that popes and bishops should be created without the Emperor's consent. He took Rome and the Pope, and extorted the crown and the right of investiture. For the third time, entering Italy, he drove Pope Gelasius from the city. He died without leaving children, in the twentieth year of his reign. See the Chronicle; Egnatius, book 3.

units.la: ISAACIVS Comnenus post Michaëlem seniorem imperat Constantinopoli, anno mundi 5020. à Christo nato 1058. Hic Michaëlem Seniorem in ordinem redegit: fuit tamen vir alioqui strenuus, pace ac bello clarus, ac infractus[?], moribusque arrogantioribus. Cooperante Patriarcha Imperium sumpsit, in quem tamen postea ingratus, ac velut collati beneficij immemor, ipsum cum suis in exilium misit. Comnena hic gente nobili ortus, in negociis obeundis expeditus fuit. Cæterum lateris morbo inter venandum subito correptus, cum de salute desperat, cucullam induit, atque imperio se abdicat. Constantinus Ducas de Senatus populíque consensu ei successor declaratur. Tanta continentia fuisse perhibetur Isaacius, uti nec uxorem cognoscere vellet post prolem semel ex ea susceptam, cùm tamen ad morbi subleuationē medici in primis consulerent ut coitu uteretur frequentiore. Imperauit annos 4. Vide Egna.lib.2.
units.tr: Isaac Comnenus, after Michael the Elder, ruled at Constantinople in the year of the world 5020, from the birth of Christ 1058. He reduced Michael the Elder to the ranks; yet he was otherwise a vigorous man, distinguished in peace and in war, unbroken, though rather arrogant in his manners. With the help of the Patriarch he took up the empire, but afterwards he proved ungrateful to him, and, as if forgetful of the benefit conferred, sent him into exile with his followers. Born of a noble Comnenian family, he was skilled in carrying out affairs. But when he was suddenly struck down by a pain in the side while hunting, and despaired of his health, he put on a monk's cowl and renounced the empire. Constantine Ducas was declared his successor with the consent of the Senate and the people. Isaac is said to have been so continent that he did not even wish to know his wife after the one child he had had by her, although the physicians especially advised him, for the relief of his illness, to have more frequent intercourse. He reigned four years. See Egnatius, book 2.

units.la: CONSTANTINVS Ducas Constantinopoli imperat post Isaacium, anno mundi 5024. à Christo nato 1062. hunc conspiratio sub initia grauis excepit, quam non sine discrimine compressit: pietatem coluit, æquitatem obseruauit: sed auaricię supra modum operam dedit, hinc suis odiosus, hostibus etiam ludibrio, res imperij undique vexantibus, fuit. Ad externa mala familiaris Constantinopoli clades accessit, nempe grauis terræ motus, quo templa, ædésq; multæ pessum ïere. Obiitsexagenarius, anno imperij sexto, Eudociæ uxori & liberis tribus imperium tradens. Vide ut supra,& Chron.Phry. EVDOCIA DIOGENES ROMANVS
units.tr: CONSTANTINUS Ducas reigns at Constantinople after Isaacius, in the year of the world 5024, from the birth of Christ 1062. At the start a conspiracy arose against him, which he suppressed, though not without danger. He cultivated piety and observed fairness, but he devoted himself excessively to avarice, and for this reason he was hateful to his own people and an object of mockery to his enemies, while the affairs of the empire were being harassed on every side. Along with these external evils, a familiar calamity struck Constantinople: a severe earthquake, by which many temples and houses were destroyed. He died at the age of sixty, in the sixth year of his reign, leaving the empire to his wife Eudocia and three children. See above, and the Chronicon of Phrantzes. EUDOCIA DIOGENES ROMANUS

units.la: EVDOCIA cum filiis imperat Constantinopoli post Constantinum Ducam,anno mundi 5031. à Christo nato 1069. Poterat muliebri fortasse prudentia hęc,si foris cessassent bella, imperiũ domi administrare: sed lacessentibus undique imperium barbaris,vicit eorum sententia,qui rebus præficiendũ virum appositum ac idoneum contendebāt. Quare iurisiurandi oblita,quo marito Ducæ,morieti, se obstrinxerat, non superinducturam se virum, etiam si coacta esset, Romanū cognomine Diogenem,post menses imperij septem,in virum Eudocia assumit, qui republ. prudentia ac fortitudine tueretur: at pœnituit statim Eudociam,quòd vir hic insolens rem ad se totam traheret. Vide Egna. lib.2.Cosmog. Mun.lib.4.
units.tr: EUDOCIA, together with her sons, reigns at Constantinople after Constantinus Ducas, in the year of the world 5031, from the birth of Christ 1069. She might perhaps have managed the empire at home with a woman's prudence, had the wars abroad ceased; but since the barbarians were assaulting the empire from every side, the opinion of those prevailed who argued that a man fit and suited to affairs should be set over them. Therefore Eudocia, forgetting the oath by which she had bound herself, that she would not take another husband in place of her late husband Duke Constantine, even if she were compelled, after seven months of her reign took as her husband a Roman named Diogenes, so that he might protect the commonwealth with prudence and courage. But Eudocia soon repented, because this man, being arrogant, drew the whole business to himself. See Egnatius, book 2, and the Cosmography of Munster, book 4.

units.la: ROMANVS Diogenes Eudociæ vir,imperat Constantinopoli, anno mundi 5032. à Christo nato 1070. duas hic suscepit expeditiones vario rerum successu : prior quidē optimè cessit,posteriorautem pessimè:nam vel fugatis vel cæsis militibus suis ipse Imperator Constantinopolitanus capitur:quod ad eam diem nunquã contigerat. Ferunt tamen Turcam nomine Azan,ad primũ huius euentus nuncium, vix credentem constitisse:mox ad se adductum Ro.Diogenem, & cognitū, in precio habuisse: ac amplis donatum muneribus, pace inita, dimisisse. Sed ad primum aduersæ cladis nuncium, ut ferè fit, omnia Constantinopoli iam mutata erat:Eudocia nempe relegata est:Romano abdicatum est imperium : Michaël Imperator creatus, Romanum Diogenē victum, deditúmque , contra iusiurandũ exoculat, ac in insulam deportat, ubi ab uxore Eudocia sepelitur, post annos imperij ferè quotuor. Vide ut supra. PARAPIN MICHAEL BOTONIAT NICEPHORVS
units.tr: ROMANUS Diogenes, husband of Eudocia, reigns at Constantinople in the year of the world 5032, from the birth of Christ 1070. He undertook two campaigns here, with varying success: the first turned out very well, but the second very badly, for after his soldiers were routed or slain, the emperor himself was captured by the Turks, which had never happened before. They report, however, that the Turk named Azan, when first he received news of this event, hardly believed it; soon, however, Romanus Diogenes was brought before him and recognised, and he held him in honour, and after making peace, dismissed him, loaded with generous gifts. But by the time the first news of the disaster arrived, as usually happens, everything at Constantinople had already changed: Eudocia, indeed, had been banished; Romanus had been deposed from the throne; Michael was created emperor, and he, contrary to his oath, had Romanus, now defeated and surrendered, blinded and deported to an island, where he was buried by his wife Eudocia, after a reign of about four years. See above. PARAPINACE MICHAEL BOTANIATES NICEPHORUS

units.la: MICHAEL Constantini Ducæ filius, Parapinaceus à fame, quæ sub eo inualuit, dictus, imperauit Constantinopoli anno mundi 5036. à Christo nato 1074. post Romanum Diogenem vitricum suum. Hic ad imperium administrandū ineptus, studiis tantùm literarum intentus, ac sub Psello præceptore versus factitans, à Turcis interim vndecunque premebatur, maximè ab Orientalibus regionibus: quare præfecti etiam, velut coacti, alterum sibi delegerunt Impetatorem: putà Nicephorum, sanè nobilissimum, quem, in principis ignaui inuidiam, facilè ciues admisere: Michaele prius, cum vxore & filio, in monasteriū detruso, ac monacho facto. Imperauit Michaël annos sex. Vide Egna.lib.2. & Gosmogra.Mun.lib.4.
units.tr: MICHAEL, son of Constantine Ducas, called Parapinaceus from the famine which prevailed under him, reigned at Constantinople in the year of the world 5036, from the birth of Christ 1074, after Romanus Diogenes, his stepfather. He was unfit to administer the empire, being devoted only to literary studies and practising verse under his tutor Psellus; meanwhile he was pressed on all sides by the Turks, chiefly from the eastern regions. For this reason the commanders, as if compelled, chose another emperor for themselves, namely Nicephorus, a most noble man, whom the citizens readily admitted, out of resentment against the idle prince. Michael was first thrust into a monastery with his wife and son and made a monk. Michael reigned six years. See Egnatius, book 2, and the Cosmography of Munster, book 4.

units.la: NICEPHORVS Botaniates, à Phoca imperatore originem trahens, tanquam omniū nobilissimus, facilè Michaële deturbato, imperium obtinuit Constantinopolitanum, anno mundi 5042. à Christo nato 1080. Hic Constantinum Constantini Ducæ filium, imperium sibi asserere contendentem, cepit: totondit, ac in sacerdotem inunxit. Paulò post Nicephorus qui Comnenorum fratrum forti, fidelique opera vsus fuerat (nam hi Bryennium & Basilatium imperij inuasores sustulerant) ab illis deiicitur, anno imperij tertio, in cœnobiumque cõiicitur, vbi aliquamdiu vixit. Post hunc Alexius Comnenus, natu minor, militibus acceptior, imperat: qui die ipso Paschæ Bizantium clam ingressus, hostilem in modum vrbem diripit. Vide vt supra.
units.tr: NICEPHORUS Botaniates, tracing his origin from the emperor Phocas, as the most noble of all, easily overthrew Michael and obtained the throne at Constantinople in the year of the world 5042, from the birth of Christ 1080. He seized Constantine, son of Constantine Ducas, who was trying to claim the throne for himself; he shaved him and anointed him as a priest. Shortly afterward Nicephorus, who had used the strong and faithful service of the Comneni brothers (for these had destroyed Bryennius and Basilacius, the usurpers of the empire), was himself deposed by them in the third year of his reign and shut up in a monastery, where he lived for some time. After him, Alexius Comnenus, the younger by birth and more acceptable to the soldiers, became emperor; on the very day of Easter he secretly entered Byzantium and plundered the city as if it were an enemy. See above.

units.la: GOTFRIDVS Bolionius, seu Bilionensis, Lotaringiæ Dux, Bulionis Ducatum Sperto Eburonum Episcopo magna vi auri vendidit: primúsque Dux huius expeditionis in Iudæam aduersus Saracenos extitit: quem illustrissimi ac præstantissimi è Gallia principes comitati sunt, diuenditis vel oppigneratis bonis suis. Habuerat siquidem orationem Pontifex Vrbanus secundus, super hac re in cōcilio Claromontano, qua huiusmodi primores ad suscipiendā hāc expeditionē extimularat: idipsum suaserat Petrus heremita, qui apud Iudæam peregrinatus Christianos à Saracenis valde opprimi renunciarat. Itaque tercentum hominum milibus cruce signatis comitatus Bolionius, Ierusalē ipsam trigesimonono obsidionis die cepit, idibus Iulij, nempe ann. mun. 5060. à Christo nato 1098. Corbana Persa victo, cæsa sunt infidelium centum milia: ipse Gotfridus Rex Ierosolimitanus designatus est: attamē auream recusauit coronam, quòd eò loci, corona spinis contexta capiti Christi imposita fuisset. Contigit id post annos fere quingentos quàm Persæ Ierusalem etiam cœperant, atque ad centum Christianorum milia occiderant: quam urbem exactis decem annis Heraclius receperat, Saraceni quoque post annos 16. expugnarant. At verò dux Bolionius, anno post quàm rex creatus fuerat, febre correptus obiit, sepultúsq; est ad nobile illud Christi sepulchrū. Regnatū est Ierosolymis à Christianis Regibus septem, spacio annorū 88. Vide Blondum lib.4.decade 2.& Chro.Chronicorū.
units.tr: GODFREY of Bouillon, or Bilionensis, Duke of Lorraine, sold the Duchy of Bouillon for a large sum of gold to Otto, Bishop of Liège; and he was the first leader of this expedition into Judaea against the Saracens. He was accompanied by the most illustrious and distinguished princes from France, who sold or pawned their goods. Indeed, Pope Urban the Second had delivered a speech on this matter at the council of Clermont, by which he had roused such leading men to undertake this expedition; Peter the Hermit had also urged the same, having reported that the Christians who had travelled in Judaea were being greatly oppressed by the Saracens. Accordingly, Godfrey of Bouillon, accompanied by three hundred thousand men marked with the cross, took Jerusalem itself on the thirty-ninth day of the siege, on the Ides of July, that is, in the year of the world 5060, from the birth of Christ 1098. After Corbanas the Persian was defeated, a hundred thousand infidels were slain. Godfrey himself was named King of Jerusalem; yet he refused the golden crown, because in that place a crown woven of thorns had been placed on the head of Christ. This had happened about five hundred years after the Persians had also taken Jerusalem and slain about a hundred thousand Christians; that city, after ten years had passed, Heraclius had recovered, and the Saracens had also stormed it again after sixteen years. But Duke Godfrey, in the year after he had been made king, was seized by fever and died, and he was buried at that noble sepulchre of Christ. Seven Christian kings reigned at Jerusalem, over a span of 88 years. See Blondus, book 4, decade 2, and the Chronicon of Chronicles.

units.la: BALDVINVS Gotfrido Bolionio fratri in regno Ierosolimitano succedit die natalitio Christi, anno mundi 5061. à Christo nato 1099. atque post suscepta, ac confecta multa bella, in hostes nominis Christiani, mortuus est anno regni 18. Vide ut supra.
units.tr: BALDWIN succeeded his brother Godfrey of Bouillon in the kingdom of Jerusalem on Christmas Day, in the year of the world 5061, from the birth of Christ 1099; and after undertaking and completing many wars against the enemies of the Christian name, he died in the eighteenth year of his reign. See above.

units.la: ALEXIUS Comnenus Isaacij Imperatoris filius, Constantinopoli post Nicephorum Botaniatem imperat,anno mūdi 5045. à Christo nato 1083. Hic Roberto Guiscardo cum Venetis occurrens, victus, fugatúsque est.praeterea memorabilem illam Gallorum in terra sancta recuperanda expeditionē turbare conatus est: sed Bohemundus Apuliae Dux, exercitum adversus eum duxit, ac Dyrachium obsedit. Alexius, eius potentiam reformidans, cum eo fœdus init, comeatúque, & aliis rebus adiuturum se Gallos pollicetur. Inde ad pacis artes conversus orphanotropheion, & Musæum erigit: in altero pueros, puellasque parentibus orbos, alendos, in altero instituendos curat, sumptus ex regio vectigali suppeditat. ad supplicia minimè præceps, moribusque moderatus fuit. Longo tandem pressus morbo, obiit anno ætatis 70 imperij 33. Vide Aemy.li.5. Egna.lib.2.Cof.Mun.lib.4.& Platinam.fauit omnibus qui egregias artes, virtutémque amplexarentur, quos & euexit.
units.tr: ALEXIUS Comnenus, son of the emperor Isaac, reigns at Constantinople after Nicephorus Botaniates, in the year of the world 5045, from the birth of Christ 1083. Meeting Robert Guiscard together with the Venetians, he was defeated and put to flight. Moreover, he tried to disrupt that memorable expedition of the French to recover the Holy Land; but Bohemond, Duke of Apulia, led an army against him and besieged Dyrrachium. Alexius, fearing his power, made a treaty with him and promised that he would assist the French with provisions and other supplies. Then, turning to the arts of peace, he founded an orphanage and a museum: in the one he took care that boys and girls bereft of parents were fed, in the other that they were educated, and he supplied the expenses from the royal revenue. He was not inclined to severe punishments, and he was moderate in his conduct. Finally, worn down by a long illness, he died in the seventieth year of his age and the thirty-third of his reign. See Aimoin, book 5; Egnatius, book 2; the Cosmography of Munster, book 4; and Platina. He favoured all who embraced liberal arts and virtue, and he also raised them up.

units.la: CALOIOANNES Alexij filius, post patrem imperat anno mūdi 5078. à Christo nato 1116. Variis hic expeditionibus in Asiam usus, Turcas, Persasque aliquot præliis vicit, urbesque illis non paucas ademit. Gallis & Venetis infestus fuit, qui focia arma iunxerant. Dux tamen Venetus Rhodum, Samum, Lesbum, Andrúmque cepit. Perit Caloioannes manum faucius, telo à seipso intoxicato, quod in aprum tendebat, anno imperij 25.Hic initio imperij sui dignitatibus suos omnes consanguineos ornavit: Manuelem fratrem natu minorē imperij hærede dixit, cum alterū minus aptum sentiret. Vide ut supra.
units.tr: CALOJOHN, son of Alexius, after his father reigns in the year of the world 5078, from the birth of Christ 1116. Making use of various expeditions in Asia, he defeated the Turks and Persians in several battles, and took from them not a few cities. He was hostile to the French and the Venetians, who had joined their arms against him. Nevertheless the Venetian duke took Rhodes, Samos, Lesbos and Andros. Caloiohn perished, his hand having been infected by a poisoned arrow which he had himself aimed at a boar, in the twenty-fifth year of his reign. At the beginning of his reign he honoured all his relatives with dignities; he named Manuel, his younger brother, heir to the empire, although he judged the other less suitable. See above.

units.la: LVDOVICVS Crassus mortuo Philippo patre, continuò Aureliani inungitur à Gilberto Senonum Archiepiscopo, causante Remensia sacra expectari, nimis longum: nempe anno à mundo condito 5071. à Christo nato 1109. Nobiles & Principes ab Anglo Rege adiuti in Regem seditionem mouent, quem diu multúmque vexarunt: tandem tamen superior euadit Rex. Tunc coepit initium belli Anglici, quod sexcentis foederibus compositum semper renouatur. Gelasius Papa in Galliam venit, opem implorans aduersus Caesarem. Henricus Caesar ab Anglo socero impulsus Galliam inuadit: timore perculsus, Regis potentia cognita, domum reuertitur: paulò post in amicitiam cum Rege rediit, re cum Papa composita. Ludouicus iunior Remis praesente patre, à Papa Innocentio vngitur in Regem. post sex annos Parisiis obit pater Crassus, anno regni 28.
units.tr: LOUIS the Fat, after the death of his father Philip, was at once anointed at Orléans by Gilbert, Archbishop of Sens, who alleged that waiting for the Rheims rite was too long: this was in the year from the creation of the world 5071, from the birth of Christ 1109. Nobles and princes, aided by the English king, stirred up sedition against the king, whom they harassed long and hard; in the end, however, the king prevailed. Then began the English war, which, composed of six hundred treaties, is always renewed. Pope Gelasius came into France, seeking aid against the Emperor. Emperor Henry, urged on by his English father-in-law, invaded France; struck with fear when the king's power became known, he returned home; shortly afterward he returned to friendship with the king, the matter with the Pope having been settled. Louis the Younger was anointed king at Rheims by Pope Innocent, in the presence of his father. Six years later his father Louis the Fat died at Paris, in the twenty-eighth year of his reign.

units.la: LVDOVICVS iunior, proximè supradicti filius, succedit patri in regno Franciae anno mundi 5099. à Christo nato 1137. Hic D. Bernardi consilio, Conradum Imperatorem secutus, exercitum in Saracenos duxit, atque vnà cum vxore per Germaniam & Hungariam, Constantinopolim se contulit: deinde Ierosolymam. ipse & Conradus, cladem cum vterque accepisset, Regem Balduinum adeunt. tunc coniunctis viribus Damascum oppugnant, sed dissidio ac dolo obsidionem relinquere coguntur. Redit ad suos Conradus. Galli in Syria multa mala patiuntur: Rex in reditu penè captus, Georgij Siculi Regis Praetoris ope euadit. multae ingentes pugnae à nostris in Asia & Ierusalem ante reditum commissae. Aemyl.lib.5.Regnat an. 43.
units.tr: Louis the Younger, the son of the one mentioned just before, succeeded his father on the throne of France in the year of the world 5099, from the birth of Christ 1137. On the advice of St Bernard, he followed Emperor Conrad and led an army against the Saracens, and together with his wife he made his way through Germany and Hungary to Constantinople, and then to Jerusalem. He and Conrad, each having suffered a defeat, went to King Baldwin. Then, joining their forces, they attacked Damascus, but because of quarrels and treachery they were forced to abandon the siege. Conrad returned to his own people. The French suffered many misfortunes in Syria: the King, on the return journey, was nearly captured, but escaped with the help of George the Sicilian, the King's praetor. Many great battles were fought by our men in Asia and Jerusalem before the return. Aemilius, book 5. He reigned 43 years.

units.la: LOTARIUS, huius nominis secundus, Saxoniæ Dux, ab Electoribus Cæsar creatus est anno mundi 5088[?]. à Christo nato 1126. fuit huic cum Conrado tertio de imperio controversia, qui cum esset nepos ex sorore Henrici quinti, ut Lotarium anteverteret, Italiam ingressus, Longobardiam occupavit, ubi & ferrea corona insignitus est. Interea à Lotario obsessæ sunt & captæ urbes Spira, Ulma, & Norimberga: exinde persequitur Conradum in Italiam: at ubi resciuit Conradus urbes Germanicas amissas, nilque sibi præsidij expectandum è Germania, pacis conditiones Divi Bernardi opera, cum Lotario pactus est, atque ultro imperio cessit: post Lotarium tamen etiam imperavit[?]. bis in Italiam profectus est Lotarius, primùm ad compescendos motus contra Innocentium, alio Pontifice electo, Romæ coortos: deinde contra Rogerium, qui Campaniam & Apuliam invaserat. Imperat Lotarius hic annos undecim.
units.tr: Lothair II, Duke of Saxony, was created Emperor by the electors in the year of the world 5088[?], from the birth of Christ 1126. He had a dispute over the empire with Conrad III, who, being a nephew through a sister of Henry V, invaded Italy in order to get ahead of Lothair, and occupied Lombardy, where he was also crowned with the iron crown. Meanwhile, the cities of Speyer, Ulm and Nuremberg were besieged and taken by Lothair; afterwards he pursued Conrad into Italy. But when Conrad learned that the German cities were lost and that he could expect no help from Germany, he made terms of peace with Lothair through the work of St Bernard and voluntarily ceded the empire. Nevertheless, after Lothair, he also reigned. Lothair set out for Italy twice: first to put down disturbances that had arisen in Rome against Innocent, after another pope had been elected, and then against Roger, who had invaded Campania and Apulia. This Lothair reigned eleven years.

units.la: CONRADUS tertius Lotario succedit, imperatque Romæ anno mundi 5099. à Christo nato 1137. hic movit in Saracenos, uti iam dictum est in Carolo iuniore. postea in bello cum Catulis gesto, urbem quandam cum cepisset, mulieribus abire permittit cum tanta bonorum sarcina, quantam ferre possent. Hæ vero relictis rebus, nobiles pueros omnes asportare malunt: quos cum quidam captivos retinere vellent (bonorum non puerorum asportandorum copiam causati) adeò delectatus est Cæsar nobilium fœminarum virtute, ut eis non solùm puerorum, sed & omnium opum copiam fecerit.
units.tr: Conrad III succeeded Lothair and reigned at Rome in the year of the world 5099, from the birth of Christ 1137. He made war on the Saracens, as has already been said in the account of Louis the Younger. Later, in a war waged against the Catalans, after he had taken a certain city, he allowed the women to leave with as much of their goods as they could carry. But they, leaving their possessions behind, preferred to carry off all their noble sons; and when some wanted to keep them captive, on the pretext that they were carrying off goods and not boys, the Emperor was so delighted by the courage of the noble women that he granted them not only their sons but all their wealth.

units.la: MANVEL, sive Emanuel, Caloioannis, ut quidā putant, filius, ut alij volunt, frater, post eum Constantinopoli imperat, anno mundi 5103. à Christo nato 1141. Ab hoc Conradus Germanus Ro. Imperator, sollicitatus est ut opem ei ferret, sive adversus Rogerium, utriusque invasorem imperij, sive ut in Turcas Conradus ipse moveret: sed mutatus Manuel, fame laborantibus Conradi militibus, gypsum contusum farinæ immiscet: nec sat illi fuit semel id sceleris perpetrasse: simili fraude Ludovicum Francorum Regem, impius ille, decipit: sic brevi magna militum nostrorum vis consumpta est: inde Manuelis nomen Francis odiosum. Rogertus Siciliæ Rex, omnē Græciæ oram vastavit: Byzantium etiam per suos duces adeò oppressit, ut sagittas argenteas, aureásque hortis regiis immiserit. Contra ius gentium Manuel legatum violat Venetūm: negotiatores, quos simulata pace evocarat, uno die comprehendit: quare armis pressus Venetis, æquis pensionibus pacem impetrat. Prælium cum Turcis gessit funestissimū, in quo pene captus est. Imperauit annos 38. quibus exactis, monasticam secutus vitam, morbo periit. Vide Blon.lib.5.Deca.2. Egna. lib.2. Cos.Mun.lib.4.
units.tr: Manuel, or Emmanuel, son of John Komnenos, as some think, or brother, as others hold, reigned after him at Constantinople in the year of the world 5103, from the birth of Christ 1141. Conrad, the German Roman Emperor, was urged by him to bring help, either against Roger, the invader of both their empires, or so that Conrad himself would move against the Turks. But Manuel changed his mind, and when Conrad's soldiers were suffering from hunger, he mixed crushed plaster into their flour. Nor was it enough for him to have committed such a crime once: by a similar fraud that impious man deceived Louis, King of the French. Thus in a short time a great force of our soldiers was destroyed, and from then on the name of Manuel was hateful to the Franks. Roger, King of Sicily, laid waste the whole coast of Greece; he also oppressed Byzantium through his commanders so greatly that he put silver and golden arrows into the royal gardens. Against the law of nations, Manuel violated the envoy of the Venetians: he seized on a single day the merchants whom he had summoned under a feigned peace; therefore, pressed by arms, he obtained peace from the Venetians on fair terms of payment. He fought a most deadly battle with the Turks, in which he was nearly captured. He reigned 38 years, and when they were over, he took up the monastic life and died of disease. See Blondus, book 5, decade 2; Egnatius, book 2; Cosmographia Munsteri, book 4.

units.la: ALEXIUS, Manuelis filius, puer adhuc, patri successit: Andronico Comneno à patre commissus fuit, qui primò tutorem egit, dein imperii consortem, demum Alexium cognatum quindecim annos natum, cum treis à patris morte annos rerum esset potitus, clam miserè necat, capitéque truncato, reliquum cadaver sacco inclusum in mare proiicit. Vide ut supra. IMP CAES FRIDERICVS AVG IMP HENRICHVS VI AVG
units.tr: Alexius, son of Manuel, still a boy, succeeded his father. He had been entrusted by his father to Andronicus Komnenos, who first acted as his guardian, then as his co-ruler of the empire, and at last, after three years from his father's death, when he had taken control of affairs, he secretly and cruelly put to death his cousin Alexius, who was fifteen years old: he cut off his head and threw the rest of the corpse into the sea, sewn in a sack. See above. EMPEROR CAESAR FREDERICK AUGUSTUS, EMPEROR HENRY VI AUGUSTUS.

units.la: FRIDERICVS, huius nominis primus, natione Sueuus, cognomento Aenobarbus, à colore barbæ russæ, nepos Conradi ex fratre, post eundem Conradum tertium Romæ imperat anno mundi 5114. à Christo nato 1152. Hic Dertonam (nunc Tortonam vocant) portas sibi claudere ausam, obsessam capit: inde Romam contendens ab Adriano coronatur. Euersa Dertona quæ in partibus Alexandri stabat, in cuius locum Octauianum Pontificem crearat, Mediolanum inde solo æquat: Galliámque omnem Cisalpinam eadem sentientem vastat: tertiò & quartò Italiam intrans Alexandrum fugat. Tandem Friderici filio, nauali prælio victo, utitur Fridericus summa humilitate: nam pro templi foribus humi prostratus ante Pontificem, pedibus eius se opprimi permittit. Pontifex clamari præcipit, Super aspidem & basiliscum ambulabis, & conculcabis leonem, & draconem, ac tum eum absoluit. Fridericus eam à se exhiberi humilitatem Petro, non Alexandro, dixit: respondit Alexander, & mihi & Petro. Hic deinde Saracenos ac Turcas prostrauit, Sultanum in Aegyptum fugauit: verùm capta iam Armenia, cùm in equo rapidum amnem ingreditur, strenuissimus heros perit, anno imperij 37. Egna.lib.3.
units.tr: Frederick I, of this name, a Swabian by birth, surnamed Barbarossa from the colour of his red beard, nephew of Conrad through his brother, reigned at Rome after the same Conrad III in the year of the world 5114, from the birth of Christ 1152. He took by siege Dertona (now called Tortona), which had dared to shut its gates against him; then, hastening to Rome, he was crowned by Adrian. He overthrew Dertona, which stood on the side of Alexander, and in whose place he had installed the pope Octavian; then he levelled Milan to the ground; and he laid waste all Cisalpine Gaul, which thought the same way. On his third and fourth entries into Italy he put Alexander to flight. At last, when his son had been defeated in a naval battle, Frederick showed the greatest humility: lying prostrate on the ground before the doors of the church, he allowed himself to be trampled under the feet of the pope. The pope ordered it to be proclaimed, "You shall walk upon the asp and the basilisk, and you shall trample the lion and the dragon," and then absolved him. Frederick said that this humility was shown by him to Peter, not to Alexander; Alexander replied, "to me and to Peter." He then crushed the Saracens and Turks, and put the Sultan to flight in Egypt; but when Armenia had already been taken, as he was riding his horse into a rapid river, that most valiant hero perished, in the 37th year of his reign. Egnatius, book 3.

units.la: HENRICVS Friderici filius post patrem imperat anno mundi 5151. à Christo nato 1189. huic Papa Clemens tertius Constantiam virginem sacram, Rogerij Normani filiam, vxorem dedit. Siciliam obtinuit, Tancredo spurio expugnato. Philippum fratrem, qui postea imperat, cum exercitu in Syriam misit: ducibus etiam Archiepiscopo Maguntino, & Saxoniæ Duce existentibus. Aemy. lib. 6. Blond. lib. 6. Egna. lib. 3. imperat ann. 10. PHILIPPVS F. REX 42[?] LVDOVICVS F. REX 43[?] [illegible, ~10 letters]
units.tr: Henry, son of Frederick, reigned after his father in the year of the world 5151, from the birth of Christ 1189. Pope Clement III gave him Constance, a consecrated virgin, daughter of Roger the Norman, as his wife. He obtained Sicily, having overcome the bastard Tancred. He sent his brother Philip, who afterwards reigned, to Syria with an army, the leaders being also the Archbishop of Mainz and the Duke of Saxony. Aemilius, book 6. Blondus, book 6. Egnatius, book 3. He reigned 10 years. PHILIP, SON, KING 42[?]; LOUIS, SON, KING 43[?]; [illegible, about 10 letters].

units.la: PHILIPPVS à Deo datus hoc nomine secundus, Ludovici iunioris filius, apud Francos regnat anno mundi 5142. à Christo nato 1180. Hic Ædiles, quos Scabinos appellant, Parisiis creandos curat: bonam urbis partem muro cingit, forum venale, Hallas vocat, reædificat. Saltum Vicenarum mœnibus cingit. cū Ricardo Angliæ Regis filio ad recuperandā Ierusalem, quæ victori Saladino reddita fuerat, expeditione suscipit: Ptolemaida expugnat. Deinde grassante per exercitum peste, in Galliam reuertitur. Totam Normaniam & Aquitaniam iure belli recipit 260. an. postquā Rolloni data fuerat Normania. Galli Græcorum imperium, Byzantio recepto, tenet, à Venetis, & quibusdam aliis adiuti, quibus impensas refundunt. Otho quintus, Saxonum Dux, qui post Philippum Henrici sexti fratrem imperat, à rege victus in pugna Bouinensi, fugatur: Ferdinandus, siue Ferrandus, Lusitanus, Flandriæ Comes, in arcem Luparam recens ædificatam, captiuus ducitur. Ioannes Brennus Rex Ierusalem, Philippum invisit, moribundum, à quo 60000 librarum ex testamento accipit. regnat an. 43. quartana febre Medunte interiit: ad fanum D. Dionysij sepultus est. Æmyl. lib. 6.
units.tr: Philip, given by God, the second of this name, son of Louis the Younger, reigned among the Franks in the year of the world 5142, from the birth of Christ 1180. He arranged that the aediles, whom they call scabini, should be appointed at Paris; he surrounded a good part of the city with a wall; he rebuilt the market, which he called the Halles, as a place for sale. He enclosed the Forest of Vincennes with walls. He undertook an expedition with Richard, son of the King of England, to recover Jerusalem, which had been given back to the victor Saladin; he stormed Ptolemais. Then, when a plague was raging through the army, he returned to France. He took back all Normandy and Aquitaine by right of war, 260 years after Normandy had been given to Rollo. The French hold the empire of the Greeks, having recovered Byzantium, aided by the Venetians and certain others, to whom they repaid the expenses. Otto V, Duke of the Saxons, who after Philip reigned as brother of Henry VI, was defeated by the king in the battle of Bouvines and put to flight; Ferdinand, or Ferrand, of Portugal, Count of Flanders, was led away captive into the newly built fortress of Lupara. John of Brienne, King of Jerusalem, visited Philip when he was dying, and from him received 60,000 pounds according to his will. He reigned 43 years and died of a quartan fever at Melun; he was buried at the church of St Denis. Aemilius, book 6.

units.la: LVDOVICVS Octauus, Philippi filius, post patrem apud Francos regnat anno mundi 5185. à Christo nato 1223. Hic cum Anglo Rege fortiter cōflixit, quo tempore pater cum Othone. Cum Friderico Imperatore colloquitur: fœdere inito, fraternum nomen inter Francos & Germanos redintegratur. Albigensium errorem extirpauit Rex, Auenione capta, & muris deiectis. Regnat an. 3. obiit Montisperij: sepultus est in æde D. Dionysi. Gagui. lib. 7. Æmyl. lib. 7. huic succedit D. Ludouicus.
units.tr: Louis VIII, son of Philip, reigned among the French after his father in the year of the world 5185, from the birth of Christ 1223. He fought bravely with the English King, at the time when his father was fighting with Otto. He held a conference with Emperor Frederick; a treaty having been made, the brotherly name between the Franks and the Germans was renewed. The King wiped out the error of the Albigenses, Avignon having been taken and its walls torn down. He reigned 3 years, and died at Montpensier; he was buried in the church of St Denis. Gaguin, book 7. Aemilius, book 7. After him succeeded St Louis.

units.la: LIBUSSA, Craci, secundi Bohemiae Regis filia, aliquot annos principatum tenuit: tandem cum litem aliquam, quanquam iure ac recte definiisset, attamen qui causa ceciderat, humi procumbens, clamavit, indigne viros a foemina gubernari: accurrens multitudo Regem postulat. Quare haec Primislao agricolae, nescio quo modo (vel quod sic collibuerit, vel forte quadam) nupsit, qui Bohemos rexit, & Pragam primus aggere & muro cinxit circiter annum mundi 5165. a Christo nato 1123. Videto Chronographiam Ioannis Naucleri, generatione trigesimanona.
units.tr: Libussa, daughter of Krok, second King of Bohemia, held the principality for some years. At last, when she had decided a certain lawsuit, justly and rightly, yet the man who had lost the case, falling prostrate on the ground, cried out that men were unworthily governed by a woman; the crowd rushing up demanded a king. Therefore she married, I know not how (whether because it so pleased her, or perhaps by some chance), a farmer named Premysl, who ruled the Bohemians and was the first to surround Prague with an embankment and a wall, about the year of the world 5165, from the birth of Christ 1123. See the Chronography of John Naucler, generation 39.

units.la: VALASCA, una quidem ex puellis Libussae, ingentis animi & generosi, Amazonicae gentis virgo, mortua Libussa, accersiuit mulieres ac virgines, quas his verbis compellavit: Heram perdidimus, quae non passa est nos viris subiici: adeste mihi, & ego vobis imperium polliceor: coniurant in viros singulae, quos obvios habent ex improviso trucidant: armatae postea, bella multa feliciter conficiunt, virorum semper victrices: & more Amazonum viuere statuunt. Tandem vero Primislai dolo & insidiis captae, omnes ad internecionem usque mactantur. Vide ut supra. COMNEN ANDRONICVS ANGELVS ISACIVS
units.tr: VALASCA, one of Libussa's girls, a woman of great and noble spirit and a virgin of the Amazon people, after Libussa died, summoned the women and virgins and addressed them in these words: We have lost our mistress, who would not suffer us to be subjected to men: stand by me, and I promise you rule. Each of them conspires against the men, and they kill whichever men they meet unexpectedly. Afterwards, armed, they fight many wars successfully, always victorious over the men, and they resolve to live after the manner of the Amazons. At last, however, captured by the trickery and ambushes of Primislaus, they are all slaughtered to the last one. See above. COMNEN ANDRONICVS ANGELVS ISACIVS

units.la: ANDRONICVS Cōnenus, Ifacio , Caloioannis fratre natu maiore, natus, post Alexium cognatum, quem crudeliter necarat,Constantinopoli imperat anno mundi 5144. à Christo nato 1182. huic Gulielmus Siciliæ rex , bellum intulit, Alexij mortem vindicaturus, à quo cùm undique premeretur, tandem ab Ifacio Angelo præter suam , omniúmque opinionem,prælio victus,imperio deiicitur, capitur, ignominiosè occiditur.Nam altero effosso oculo, asinæ præposterè imponitur: caput alliorum recte, diadematis loco præcingitur : cauda manibus sceptri vice alligatur: per urbem sic ornatus circumuehitur: vulgi turbæque tumultu lacer, perit fœdissimè : quippe in cuius faciem pueri, puellæ , viri , fœminæ, præter probra, lutum , stercus, & fœdissima quæque coniiciunt ac cogerunt: deinde laqueo suspensus , uncis à mulieribus frustillatim discerpitur,anno imperij altero. Vide Eg.lib.2.Cof.Mun.lib.4.
units.tr: ANDRONICUS Comnenus, the elder brother of Isaac, the brother of Calojohannes, was born. After killing his cousin Alexius cruelly, he reigned at Constantinople in the year of the world 5144, from the birth of Christ 1182. William, king of Sicily, made war on him, intending to avenge the death of Alexius. When he was hard pressed on every side, he was at last defeated in battle by Isaac Angelus, contrary to his own and everyone's expectation, and was deposed from the empire and captured, and was shamefully put to death. For one of his eyes was gouged out, and he was set backwards on a she-ass; a head of garlic was girded on him in place of a diadem; his tail was tied to his hands in place of a sceptre; decked out thus, he was paraded through the city. Torn by the uproar of the mob, he perished most foully, for boys, girls, men and women, besides insults, threw and forced mud, dung and every kind of filth into his face. Then, hanged by a noose, he was torn to pieces in bits by the women with hooks, in the second year of his reign. See Aeg. book 2, Cosm. Munst. book 4.

units.la: ISACIVS Angelus post Andronicum, Comnenorum stirpe sublatâ è medio, Constantinopoli imperat anno mundi 5146. àChristo nato 1184. Hic varias multorum tyrannides oppressit: Fridericum Aenobarbum Ro. Imperatorem in Syriam properante m magnificè excepit. Alexium fratremnatu minorem, àTurcis captum, magno redemit: à quo postea, ingratissimo homine , per summum scelus imperio oculisque priuatus, incarcerem truditur: donec filius Ifacij, Alexius alter, & longè ab illo dispar, àFrancisac Venetis opem implorans, patrem lachrymis obtinuit. Sed carcere post longam captiuitatem eductus, morbo ex aëre contracto, non diu superuixit.Imperauit annos 16. Vide ut supra.
units.tr: ISAAC Angelus, after Andronicus, the Comneni line having been removed from the midst, reigned at Constantinople in the year of the world 5146, from the birth of Christ 1184. He suppressed the various tyrannies of many men. He received with great honour Frederick Barbarossa, the Roman emperor, who was hastening into Syria. He ransomed for a large sum his younger brother Alexius, who had been captured by the Turks. Later, by the greatest crime, he was deprived of the empire and his eyes by this most ungrateful man, and thrown into prison, until the son of Isaac, another Alexius, very unlike him, imploring help from the French and the Venetians, won his father back with tears. But after a long captivity he was led out of prison, and having caught a disease from the air, he did not survive long. He reigned for 16 years. See above.

units.la: PHILIPPVS Henrici sexti (Friderici primi filij) frater, mortuo ipso eodē fratre Romanis imperat anno mundi 5161. à Christo nato 1199. huic fuit de imperio contentio cū Othone, cui Innocentius, tertius huius nominis Papa, præterea Angliæ Rex fauebat: Sed Galliæ Rex eiusdem nominis, Philippi, Philippo opem tulit, qui fugato sæpius Othone, rerum[?] tandem potitur. Hic cum annos nouem imperasset, ab Othone[?] Comite Palatino (cuius genus celebre & clarum fecerat Fridericus primus) occiditur, die quodam cum esset ei à medico vena incisa, & nihil iam ab aduersariis suspicaretur optimus princeps. Credo Othonorum nomen illi fatale fuisse. Imperauit annis nouem. Vide Aemyl.5.Egna.lib.3.& Carionem lib.3. Philippus Bambergæ occisus, Bambergæ sepelitur: cuius corpus humatum postea Spiram, iubente Friderico secundo, translatum est.
units.tr: PHILIP, brother of Henry VI (son of Frederick I), after that same brother's death, ruled over the Romans in the year of the world 5161, from the birth of Christ 1199. There was a contest for the empire between him and Otto, whom Innocent III, the Pope of that name, and also the King of England, favoured. But the King of France of the same name, Philip, gave aid to Philip, who, having often routed Otto, at last gained power. After he had reigned nine years, he was killed by Otto, Count Palatine (whose famous and illustrious family Frederick I had made), on a certain day when a vein had been opened for him by a physician, and the best of princes suspected nothing from his enemies by then. I believe the name of Otto was fatal to him. He reigned nine years. See Aemilius book 5, Egnatius book 3, and Carion book 3. Philip was killed at Bamberg and buried at Bamberg; his body, later interred, was transferred to Speyer by order of Frederick II.

units.la: OTHO Saxonum Dux (Comitem Palatinum vocat Aemylius) quem Imperatorem elegerat Innocentius aduersatus Philippo, eidem Philippo mactato surrogatur, & à Papa, omnium consensu, ad tollendam discordiam coronatur anno mundi 5170. à Christo nato 1208. Sed cum hic Pontificiæ ditionis oppida quædam caperet, & Friderici iunioris inuadere cuperet regnum, diris Pontificiis petitus, imperio priuatur anno imperij 3. Fridericúsque Henrici sexti filius, adnitente etiam Innocentio, Imperator creatur: qui cum Philippo Francorum Rege in Othonem arma sumpsit: nec sine manifesta vi numinis, & Gallorū virtute, clade memorabili affectus Otho, etiam ab Anglo adiutus, in patriam inglorius se recipit. neque vero suo tandem supplicio caruit, nam & ipse non multo post trucidatus periit. Vide Aem.lib.5.Egn.lib.3.Carionem lib.3. TRICID ALEXIVS FRA ISA FIL. ALEXIVS IVN
units.tr: OTTO, Duke of the Saxons (Aemilius calls him Count Palatine), whom Innocent, opposing Philip, had chosen as emperor, is substituted for Philip, who had been slain, and was crowned by the Pope with the consent of all, to end the discord, in the year of the world 5170, from the birth of Christ 1208. But when he began to seize certain towns of the papal dominion and wished to invade the kingdom of the younger Frederick, he was assailed by the Papists' curses and deprived of the empire in the third year of his reign. Frederick, son of Henry VI, was then created emperor, with Innocent also assisting. He took up arms against Otto together with Philip, King of the Franks. Otto, struck by a memorable defeat, not without a clear power of God and the valour of the French, was also aided by the Englishman, and withdrew ingloriously to his homeland. Yet he did not escape his punishment at last, for he too was slaughtered not long after and perished. See Aem. book 5, Egn. book 3, Carion book 3. TRICID ALEXIVS FRA ISA FIL. ALEXIVS IVN

units.la: ALEXIVS Angelus fratricida,post Ifacium Angelum fratrem, Constantinopoli imperat, anno mundi 5162. à Christo nato 1200. Hic plane impius,maiori fratri imperium per scelus ademit: & Alexium Ifacij filium, nepotem suum,voluit perdere : qui fugiens,in Dalmatiamq; delatus, Francorum proceres, Balduinum & Venetos in patruum mouit, paciscendo 30000. marcarum auri, & cõmeatum, si eorum ope,vel solus,vel cum patre, qui in carcere agebat, imperio restitueretur. Quare hi proceres classe parata,Byzantium versus navigant,expugnant, fracta prius catena,que ab urbe ad Peram tensa erat. Fratricida fuga saluti suæ consulit: Ifacius carcere liberatur: & Alexius iunior,post subitam patris liberati mortem,imperat. Vide Egna.. lib.2.. Cosmo.Munst.lib.4..
units.tr: ALEXIUS Angelus, the fratricide, after Isaac Angelus his brother, reigned at Constantinople in the year of the world 5162, from the birth of Christ 1200. He was plainly impious: by crime he took the empire from his elder brother, and wished to destroy Alexius, Isaac's son, his nephew. He fled and was carried to Dalmatia, and by promising thirty thousand marks of gold and provisions, if he were restored to the empire by their help, alone or with his father, who was in prison, he stirred the French nobles, Baldwin and the Venetians, against his uncle. Therefore these nobles, with a fleet made ready, sail towards Byzantium, and storm it, after first breaking the chain that was stretched from the city to Pera. The fratricide, by flight, looked to his own safety. Isaac was freed from prison, and Alexius the younger, after the sudden death of his father, who had been freed, reigned. See Egn. book 2, Cosm. Munst. book 4.

units.la: ALEXIVS iunior,Ifacij filius,qua dixi ope,imperio restituitur Constantinopolitano, anno eodem quo supra imperasse dicitur Alexius Angelus. In fœdere sanciendo inter hunc, & Gallos,ac Venetos,cautum est vt Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus Romano subesset Pontifici,& damna Francis,Venetisq; à Manuele illata compensaret: at mense post restitutionem vix exacto,cum rerū quas promiserat satageret, à Murziphlo quodam ignobili,quem tamen ad summū dignitatis gradū euexerat,iuuenis admodum necatur. Murziphlus frustra se hostibus opponens, urbe Byzantio amissa,noctu cum uxore , pellicibus ac thesauro fugit: paulò post in Peloponnefo captus,ac Byzantium retractus,miserè perit. Urbs Francis, Venetisq; dedita cum omni milite , ab eis est possessa: & res imperij deinde ad Francos translata: è quibus primus fuit Græcorum Imperator Balduinus. Vide vt supra.. FLANDR. BALDVINVS CVSA[?] HENRI
units.tr: ALEXIUS the younger, son of Isaac, was restored to the Constantinopolitan empire by the help I have mentioned, in the same year in which Alexius Angelus is said to have reigned. In the treaty made between him and the French and the Venetians it was provided that the Patriarch of Constantinople should be subject to the Roman Pontiff, and should make good to the French and Venetians the losses inflicted by Manuel. But scarcely a month after his restoration, while he was busy with the things he had promised, he was killed, being still quite a young man, by a certain Murtzuphlus, a base man whom he had nonetheless raised to the highest rank of dignity. Murtzuphlus, opposing himself vainly to the enemies, lost the city of Byzantium; he fled by night with his wife, mistresses and treasure. Shortly afterwards he was captured in the Peloponnese, brought back to Byzantium and miserably perished. The city, surrendered with all its soldiers to the Franks and Venetians, was held by them; and the power of the empire was then transferred to the Franks, the first of whom was Baldwin, emperor of the Greeks. See as above. FLANDR. BALDVINVS CVSA[?] HENRI

units.la: BALDVINVS, Flandriæ Comes, ab omni milite, & exercitu,Flandrensi scilicet,Montisferratensi,Allobrogum & Venetorum , Imperator Constantinopolitanus creatur post Alexium iuniorem anno mundi 5162. à Christo nato 1200. hac conditione vt si ex Francis designaretur Imperator,Veneti Patriarcham darent: quod & euenit. Balduinus cuncta præter Adrianopolim recepit:in qua imperauit Theodorus,. Alexij Imperatoris pessimi gener, quam & nomine dotis accepit. Cum Franci eam obsiderent ac prope expugnarent,captus & mortuus est Balduinus,qui annum imperio vix præfuerat. Vide Egna.lib.2.Ro.prin.& Cosm.Mun.lib.4.
units.tr: BALDWIN, Count of Flanders, was created Constantinopolitan emperor after Alexius the younger, in the year of the world 5162, from the birth of Christ 1200, by the whole army and host, namely the Flemish, Montferrat, Allobrogian and Venetian, on this condition: that if the emperor were chosen from among the French, the Venetians would give the Patriarch. This came to pass. Baldwin received everything except Adrianople, in which Theodore, son-in-law of the most wicked Emperor Alexius, reigned, whom he also took as a dowry. When the Franks besieged it and nearly stormed it, Baldwin was captured and died, having scarcely held the empire a year. See Egn. book 2, Rom. prin., and Cosm. Munst. book 4.

units.la: HENRICVS Balduini frater,Imperator post eius mortem creatur, anno mundi 5163.à Christo nato 1201. Hic expugnationem Adrianopolitanam persequitur, ac repetit: sed irruentibus Saracenis, obsidionem soluit: Constantinopolim rediit, quam & munit. Fœdere cum Valachis firmato, & filia Ducis eorum in vxorem ducta,domi,forisque cum prudenter se Henricus gereret, Gulielmum Bonifacij filium, Regem Thessaliæ designat. mox moriens, Iolantem filiam, Petro Altisiodorensi nuptam, hæredem relinquit,anno imperij 13. Vide vt supra. IMP. FRIDERICVS II AVGVSTVS JOBE UXOR FRIDERICI II
units.tr: HENRY, brother of Baldwin, was created emperor after his death, in the year of the world 5163, from the birth of Christ 1201. He pursued and renewed the siege of Adrianople, but when the Saracens attacked, he lifted the siege and returned to Constantinople, which he also fortified. A treaty having been made with the Vlachs, and the daughter of their duke taken as his wife, Henry, conducting himself prudently at home and abroad, designated William, son of Boniface, as King of Thessaly. Dying soon afterwards, he left as heir Yolanda, his daughter, married to Peter of Auxerre, in the thirteenth year of his reign. See as above. IMP. FRIDERICVS II AVGVSTVS JOBE UXOR FRIDERICI II

units.la: FRIDERICVS, secundus huius nominis, deturbato Othone quarto, imperat anno mundi 5173. à Christo nato 1211. Viguere in hoc principe corporis animíque dotes, avo similimus Aenobarbo, militaris laudis appetentiff. fuit: Græcam, Latinam, Germanicam & Saracenicam linguam calluit: bonarum artium disciplinas promouit: Sed has virtutes animi calliditas ac perfidia, & in Guelphum nomen sæuitia, neque non in Pontifices odium obscurarunt. Guelphos ac Gibellinos, perniciosissima Italiæ nomina, primus invexit: hi Imperatori, illi Papæ fauebant. Mediolanenses, qui stabant à Pontifice, vicit. A Papa Innocentio quarto, imperio priuatur, ac excommunicatur. Henricus Thuringiæ, dictus Lanthgrauius, Imperator dicitur: bona Italiæ pars in Fridericum armatur: Parma ei adimitur: Victoria quoque, vrbs quam condiderat, & multis ornamentis decorarat, diripitur. Hic Ierofolymam prosectus, ita negotium confecit, ut à Sultano non solùm Ierofolyma, sed & multæ aliæ urbes ei sint redditæ, coronatúsque est Ierofolymæ, quam muniuit, & Joppen item aduersus hostium vim. Panormum profectus, Manfredi filij nothi dolo necatur: sunt qui veneno extinctum scribunt, conscio Pontifice. imperauit an. 35. Vide Egn.lib.3. & Carionem lib.3. & Chr. Phry.
units.tr: FREDERICK, the second of that name, after Otto IV was deposed, reigned in the year of the world 5173, from the birth of Christ 1211. In this prince the gifts of body and mind flourished; he resembled his grandfather Barbarossa most closely and was eager for military glory. He knew the Greek, Latin, German and Saracen languages; he advanced the disciplines of the good arts. But his cunning and perfidy of mind, his cruelty against the name of the Guelphs, and no less his hatred of the Popes, obscured these virtues. He first introduced the Guelphs and Ghibellines, the most pernicious names in Italy: the former favoured the emperor, the latter the Pope. He defeated the Milanese, who stood with the Pope. He was deprived of the empire and excommunicated by Pope Innocent IV. Henry of Thuringia, called the Landgrave, was called emperor; a good part of Italy was armed against Frederick; Parma was taken from him; Victoria, the city he had founded and adorned with many ornaments, was also plundered. He went to Jerusalem and so managed the business that not only Jerusalem but many other cities were restored to him by the Sultan; and he was crowned at Jerusalem, which he also fortified, and likewise Joppa against the force of the enemy. Setting out for Palermo, he was killed by the treachery of Manfred, his bastard son; some write that he was poisoned, with the Pope's knowledge. He reigned 35 years. See Egn. book 3, Carion book 3, and Chr. Phry.

units.la: JOLE Joannis Ierosolymorum Regis filia, nupsit huic Friderico secundo, cui pater in dotem omne ius in Ierosolymæ regnum dedit. inde etiam hodie Siciliæ Reges, Ierosolymitanos se Reges vocitant: Nam erat Fridericus Siciliæ Rex, & Sueviae Dux. Ex hac uxore filium nomine Conradum sustulit Fridericus, quem regnorum hæredem reliquit: & Manfredum nothum Tarentinum principem instituit. Aemy.lib.7. Blon.lib.7.deca.2.
units.tr: JOLE, daughter of John, King of Jerusalem, married this Frederick II, to whom her father gave as dowry all right to the kingdom of Jerusalem. From this comes the custom that even today the kings of Sicily call themselves kings of Jerusalem. For Frederick was king of Sicily and duke of Swabia. By this wife Frederick had a son named Conrad, whom he left as heir to the kingdoms; and he appointed Manfred, his illegitimate son, prince of Taranto. Aemilius, book 7; Blondus, book 7, decade 2.

units.la: PETRVS, Altisiodorensis Comes, vxorio innixus iure, Henrico vitrico (quando mascula supererat nulla proles) succedit, imperióque Constantinopolitano præest, anno mundi 5176. à Christo nato 1214. Hic Roma rediens, vbi imperij insignia sumpserat, Dyrachium in Venetorum gratiam cùm frustra tentasset, à Theodore Lascare, qui se Adrionopolitanum, ac Græcorum Imperatorem dicebat, ac pro tali se gerebat, per assimulationem pacis, præter iurisiurâdi religionem & fidem, medio conuiuio obtruncatur. Scribunt alij Lascarem in nemorosis Thessaliæ locis (Tempe ea vocant) insidias collocasse, captúmque Petrum abduxisse: tandémque eum in vincula coniectum, occidisse. Vide Egna.lib.2.Cosmo.Mun.lib.4. Imperauit Petrus Altisiodorensis annos quinque.
units.tr: PETER of Auxerre, Count of Auxerre, relying on the right of his wife, succeeded Henry, his stepbrother, when no male offspring remained, and presided over the empire of Constantinople in the year of the world 5176, from the birth of Christ 1214. Returning from Rome, where he had received the insignia of empire, he attempted in vain to take Dyrrhachium for the sake of the Venetians. Then, by the pretence of peace, Theodore Lascaris, who called himself Emperor of Adrianople and of the Greeks and behaved as such, had him cut down at a banquet, despite the sanctity of his oath and pledge. Others write that Lascaris laid an ambush in the wooded places of Thessaly (they call it Tempe), captured Peter and led him away, and finally threw him into chains and killed him. See Egnatius, book 2; Cosmographia Mundi, book 4. Peter of Auxerre reigned five years.

units.la: ROBERTVS, Petri supradicti filius, ex Galliis accersitus, ad paternæ calamitatis nuntium, Byzantium aduolans, Imperator dicitur, anno mundi 5181. à Christo nato 1219. Puellam hic nobili cuidam Burgundo pactam, matrimonio sibi copulauit: quare Burgundus animi impotens, in regiam irrupit, nares puellæ abscidit: matrem, quæ noui erat connubij conciliatrix, proximum in mare proiecit. Nec est ausus ad iniuriam hanc vel mutire quidem Imperator, Romam adiens pro diademate impetrando: at inde rediens iniuriâ vlturus, in Achaia morbo decessit, anno imperij 7. Vide vt supra. NVS II. BALDVI PALÆO. MICHAEL
units.tr: ROBERT, son of the aforesaid Peter, was summoned from Gaul; on news of his father's misfortune he hastened to Byzantium and is said to have been made emperor, in the year of the world 5181, from the birth of Christ 1219. Here he betrothed a girl to a certain noble Burgundian, but married her himself. Therefore the Burgundian, unable to control his anger, burst into the palace, cut off the girl's nose, and threw the mother, who had been the go-between of the new marriage, into the sea nearby. The emperor did not dare even to murmur about this wrong, but went to Rome to obtain the diadem; yet returning thence, intending to avenge the injury, he died of disease in Achaia, in the seventh year of his reign. See above. NUS II. BALDWIN. PALAEOLOGUS. MICHAEL.

units.la: BALDVINVS secundus, Roberti Constantinopolitani Imperatoris prædicti, filius, post patrē Imperator creatur anno mundi 5188. à Christo nato 1226. sed cùm per ætatem haud esset idoneus, Ioannes Brennius Ierosolymitanus quidem nomine solum Rex, Italia euocatus, adiutor ei datur: cuius filiam in uxorem duxit, spreta quæ illi offerebatur Regis Pontici filia: unde bellum atrox obortū. Balduinus multis bellis exhaustus, ac pressus filium, & crucis dominicæ partem Venetis oppignerat, templorum omnium donaria aufert, exercitum ingentem ad Bosphori fauces obiicit: interim Byzantium proditione amittit: profugus cū patriarcha, naui in Euboeam delatus est: ita dum externam vim timet, à domestica opprimitur, anno imperij 33. tunc Græci imperium recipiunt Costantinopolitanum, quod Franci annos 58. tenuerant. Vide Blon. lib.7. deca.2. Egna.lib.2. Volater.lib.23. Aem.lib.7. Cosm.Mun.lib.4.
units.tr: BALDWIN II, son of the aforesaid Robert, Emperor of Constantinople, was created emperor after his father in the year of the world 5188, from the birth of Christ 1226. But since he was not fit for it by reason of his age, John of Brienne, king of Jerusalem in name only, was summoned from Italy and given to him as helper. Baldwin took as wife John's daughter, having rejected the daughter of the King of Pontus who was offered to him, whence a fierce war arose. Exhausted and pressed by many wars, Baldwin pawned his son and a part of the Lord's cross to the Venetians, carried off the offerings of all the temples, and threw a huge army against the straits of the Bosphorus. Meanwhile he lost Byzantium through treachery; a fugitive with the patriarch, he was carried by ship to Euboea. Thus, while he feared foreign force, he was crushed by a domestic one, in the thirty-third year of his reign. Then the Greeks recovered the Constantinopolitan empire, which the Franks had held for 58 years. See Blondus, book 7, decade 2; Egnatius, book 2; Volaterranus, book 23; Aemilius, book 7; Cosmographia Mundi, book 4.

units.la: MICHAEL Palæologus pulso Balduino, Byzantium capit, imperat quo anno mundi 5221. à Christo nato 1259. Hic Ioanni Lascari tutor datus à patre Theodoro moriente, puerum interemit: imperium sibi ac suis destinans, primum Achaiæ regno Guillelmum spoliat, Genuensium classe fretus: deinde Balduini opes frangit, urbem (ut dixi) capit. Bellum cum Venetis diu gessit, quem facile imperio deturbassent, nisi Genuenses obstitissent. induciis factis Lugdunum ad concilium quod Gregorius decimus indixerat, venit: faciléque illi cum Pontifice convenit: unde tantam suæ gentis invidiam contraxit, ut mortuo sepultura negarint. mansit tamen imperium in familia eius annis 193. donec in Turcarum manus devenit, Mahomete, ui capto Byzantio, Constantinum obtruncante, anno mundi 5414. à Christo nato 1452. Vide ut supra. regnat an.34. F REX 44 LVDOVICVS FRANC. 25 PHILIPPVS R.
units.tr: MICHAEL Palaeologus, Baldwin having been driven out, took Byzantium and reigned in the year of the world 5221, from the birth of Christ 1259. Appointed guardian of John Lascaris by his dying father Theodore, he put the boy to death, intending the empire for himself and his own people. First he despoiled William of the kingdom of Achaia, relying on a Genoese fleet; then he broke the resources of Baldwin and took the city (as I said). He waged war with the Venetians for a long time; they could easily have overthrown his rule, had the Genoese not opposed them. After a truce was made, he came to the council that Gregory X had called at Lyons, and he easily came to terms with the Pope. For this he drew such hatred upon his own people that they refused him burial after his death. Nevertheless the empire remained in his family for 193 years, until it came into the hands of the Turks: Mahomet, having taken Byzantium by force and cut down Constantine, did so in the year of the world 5414, from the birth of Christ 1452. See above. He reigned 34 years. KING 44. LEWIS. FRANCE 25. PHILIP R.

units.la: D. LVDOVICVS post patrem Ludouicum octauum, Philippi secundi filium, apud Fracos regnat anno mundi 5188. à Christo nato 1226. huius mater Blancha rectrix testamento relicta, moderata & sapiens, partim obscuras, partim apertas inimicitias, initio regni exortas sedat, tum vi, tum beneuolētia cōcilians sibi principes, aliosque qui secesserant, facta in filium coiuratione. Innocetius quartus Fridericum metuens cum in Galliam fugisset, Lugduni concilium habuit, in quo ruber pileus & purpura primū Cardinal. data sunt. Spinea corona, & sacrosancta Christi monimēta, q̄ Balduinus Venetis oppignerauerat, D. Ludouicus redemit: hæc apud sacrū palatij sacellū quod Lutetiæ erigebat, asseruanda cōmisit. Ad juvandas res Christianas cū ingēti exercitu in Asiam nauigauit: Aegyptū ingressus, Damiatā expugnauit. Christianos barbarorū seruos gregatim undique coges, redemit. Pastores, inges manus perditorū hominum, cū Regē captum esse audissent, arma capiūt, sed à Biturigibus, Aurelianensibúsque delentur. Robertus Regis frater, Lutetiæ Sorbonā instituit. Rex histriones & parasitos ab Aula exegit: Magistratuum ambitū coercuit: honorū dignitates non erāt tūc venales, nec ausi fuissent toto jurisdictionis tractu aut fundos emere, aut sacerdotia liberis accipere: blasphemis in fróte cauterium inussit. Rex in Africā traiecit, Carthaginē expugnauit, Tunetū obsedit: pestilentia grassante obiit ex profluuio anno regni 44. sepultus est in æde D. Diony. Gag. & Aem. lib. 7.
units.tr: SAINT LOUIS, after his father Louis VIII, son of Philip II, reigned among the French in the year of the world 5188, from the birth of Christ 1226. His mother Blanche, left as regent by will, moderate and wise, allayed partly hidden and partly open enmities that had arisen at the beginning of the reign, winning over the princes and others who had withdrawn, partly by force and partly by goodwill, after a conspiracy against the son had been formed. Innocent IV, fearing Frederick, fled into Gaul, and held a council at Lyons, in which the red hat and purple were first given to cardinals. Saint Louis redeemed the thorn crown and the most sacred memorials of Christ, which Baldwin had pawned to the Venetians; he committed them to be kept in the chapel of the sacred palace that he was building at Paris.
