To help Christian affairs he sailed to Asia with a huge army; entering Egypt, he took Damietta. He gathered the Christian slaves of the barbarians from everywhere in droves and redeemed them. When the shepherds and an immense band of desperate men heard that the king had been captured, they took up arms, but they were destroyed by the people of Bourges and Orléans. Robert, the king's brother, founded the Sorbonne at Paris. The king drove actors and parasites from the court; he restrained the ambition of magistrates; offices and dignities were then not for sale, nor would men have dared to buy estates throughout the whole extent of their jurisdiction, or to receive priesthoods for their children; he branded blasphemers on the forehead with a hot iron. The king crossed into Africa, took Carthage, and besieged Tunis; in the forty-fourth year of his reign he died of dysentery while a plague was raging, and was buried in the church of Saint Denis. Gaguin; Aemilius, book 7.

units.la: PHILIPPVS D. Ludouici filius, mortuo patre Rex in castris salutatur, postea Remis inungitur anno mundi 5232. à Christo nato 1270. Hoc Rege gesta sunt bella Flussatium, Hispanicum Castulonense, & Tarraconese. Siculi, die Paschæ, ingenti Gallorum cædefacta, à Carolo Regis patruo deficiunt. Obiit Rex Perpeniani, sepultus est in templo D. Dionysij.
units.tr: PHILIP, son of Saint Louis, on his father's death was greeted as king in the camp, and afterwards was anointed at Rheims, in the year of the world 5232, from the birth of Christ 1270. In this king's reign the wars of Flussates, the Spanish war of Castulo, and that of Tarragona took place. The Sicilians, on Easter day, after a great slaughter of the French, revolted from Charles, the king's uncle. The king died at Perpignan and was buried in the church of Saint Denis.

units.la: RVDOLPHVS, Comes Habispurgius, Imperator eligitur anno mundi 5234. à Christo nato 1272. Interregnum imperij à deturbato Friderico per 26. annos durauit. Hic Othocarum Bohemiæ Regem acie victũ occidit: Pfeudofridericum qui se in Sueuis erexerat, combusit. In Italiam non est profectus Rudolphus, solitus Æsopi fabulâ recitare de Vulpe, & Leone in spelunca ægrotante, apud se reputans maiores suos ingressos quidem sæpe magnis copiis Italiam, sed male acceptos demum plerunque rediisse. Hic redacta sub ditionem Austria, constituit in ea Ducem filium suum Albertum, à quo originem trahunt Austriaci principes, ad Carolum quintum usque, & Ferdinandum eius fratrem. Vuenceslao Othocari filio, Bohemiæ regnũ, humanitate summa usus Rudolphus, reliquit, dedítque ei in uxorẽ filiã suam. Imperat annis 19.
units.tr: RUDOLPH, Count of Habsburg, was elected emperor in the year of the world 5234, from the birth of Christ 1272. The interregnum of the empire, after Frederick had been deposed, had lasted for 26 years. He killed Ottokar, King of Bohemia, defeated in battle, and burned the false Frederick who had set himself up in Swabia. Rudolph did not set out for Italy, being accustomed to recite Aesop's fable of the fox and the lion sick in a cave, reflecting to himself that his forebears had indeed often entered Italy with great forces, but had for the most part returned badly received. He brought Austria under his rule and established as duke there his son Albert, from whom the Austrian princes are descended, down to Charles V and his brother Ferdinand. He left the kingdom of Bohemia to Wenceslaus, son of Ottokar, using great kindness, and gave him his daughter as wife. He reigned 19 years.

units.la: ADOLPHVS post Rudolphum imperat anno mundi 5253. à Christo nato 1291. Hic Comes de Naffau cũm esset, Imperator eligitur. Sed ab electoribus pertræsis[?] eius sordes ac ambitionem, imperio destituitur, in cuius locum subrogatur Albertus Austriæ Dux, ac Rudolphi frater: cum quo dum congreditur Adolphus, occumbit anno imperij 7. Consulito Aem. lib.8. Egna. lib.3. R. FRAN. 46 PHILIPPUS F. REX 47. LUDOVICUS
units.tr: ADOLPH, after Rudolph, reigned in the year of the world 5253, from the birth of Christ 1291. While he was Count of Nassau, he was elected emperor. But the electors, having seen through his meanness and ambition, deprived him of the empire, and in his place was substituted Albert, Duke of Austria and brother of Rudolph; when Adolph engaged him in battle, he fell in the seventh year of his reign. Consult Aemilius, book 8; Egnatius, book 3. KING OF THE FRANKS 46. PHILIP THE FAIR. KING 47. LEWIS.

units.la: PHILIPPVS Pulcher, post patrem Philippũ apud Francos regnat anno mundi 5247. à Christo nato 1285. Hic Palatium in insula quam Sequana Lutetiæ facit,extruxit magnificum : vbi forum est quod Parlamentum vocant. Universam Flandriam Rex,opera Caroli Valesij subigit:Vido Comes cum liberis Lutetiam captiuus adducitur.Rex à Flandris magnificè excipitur.Comes cum filio Hilermo Regi data fide,in patriam ad tumultus sedandos proficiscitur : qui vbi nil promouet, ad Regem redit, obitque Compendij. tribus deinde præliis plus 20000. Flandrorum cæsa sunt.Certis tandem conditionibus Roberto Vidonis filio maximo , Comitatus Flandriæ redditur. Hoc Rege, Clemens quintus Lugduni in Papam coronatur:sedes Papalis Roma Auenionem transfertur,vbi 70. constitit annos, tribus Cardinalibus missis cum potestate Senatoria , quorum auspiciis Roma & Italia regeretur. Turcis expulsis, D. Ioannis Hospitalarij Rhodum capiunt : qui ob id ipsum postea vocari cœperunt Equites Rhodij. Templariorum nomen Papa abolet , quorum reditus D. Ioannis Hospitalariis conceduntur. Obiit Philippus Pulcher ad fontem Blaudi locum natiuitatis , anno regni 28. in æde D. Dionysij sepultus. Gagui.lib.7. Æmy.lib.8.
units.tr: PHILIP the Fair, after his father Philip, reigned among the Franks in the year of the world 5247, from the birth of Christ 1285. He built a magnificent palace at Paris on the island that the Seine makes, where there is the forum that they call the Parliament. The king, through the work of Charles of Valois, subdued all Flanders; Guy, the count, was led captive to Paris with his children. The king was splendidly received by the Flemings. The count, having pledged his faith to the king, went to his country to quell the uprisings; when he accomplished nothing there, he returned to the king and died at Compiègne. Then in three battles more than 20,000 Flemings were slain. Finally, on certain conditions, the county of Flanders was returned to Robert, the eldest son of Guy. In this king's reign, Clement V was crowned pope at Lyons; the papal seat was transferred from Rome to Avignon, where it remained for 70 years, three cardinals being sent with senatorial power, under whose auspices Rome and Italy would be governed. With the Turks expelled, they took Rhodes for the Knights Hospitallers of Saint John; for this reason they afterwards began to be called Knights of Rhodes. The pope abolished the name of the Templars, and their revenues were granted to the Knights Hospitallers of Saint John. Philip the Fair died at the spring of Blaud, the place of his birth, in the twenty-eighth year of his reign, and was buried in the church of Saint Denis. Gaguin, book 7; Aemilius, book 8.

units.la: LUDOVICVS Hutinus Puchri filius, patri succedit, atque apud Francos regnat anno mundi 5275. à Christo nato 1313. Hic iam ante matri Ioanæ in regno Nauarræ succefferat. Engerranus Marinius suspenditur ,eius statua è summis palatij gradibus deiicitur. Regnat Hutinus annos fere duos : ad Vicenarum saltum moritur, ad fanum Dionysij sepultus. Vide vt supra.
units.tr: Louis Hutin, son of Philip the Fair, succeeded his father and reigned over the Franks in the year of the world 5275, from the birth of Christ 1313. He had already succeeded his mother Joan in the kingdom of Navarre. Enguerrand de Marigny was hanged, and his statue was thrown down from the top steps of the palace. Hutin reigned for almost two years; he died at Vicenarum Saltus and was buried at the abbey of St Denis. See above.

units.la: ANDRONICVS, ex tribus maribus, filiis Michaëlis Paleologi, natu maximus, patri in imperio Constantinopolitano succedit, anno mundi 5255. à Christo nato 1293. Andronicus Michaëlem quendam, matre natum Hungarica, generum ac imperij cõsortem assumpsit: quo mox defuncto, Andronicũ Constantinum Despotem iuniorem, ad imperij successionem inuitat: id Michaëlis prædicti filius Andronicus, moleste ferês, in auum insurgit, Genuësium ope fretus, ius omne ad se trahit. At Veneti seniorem cum restituissent Andronicum, tandem prægrauantibus Bulgaris & Genuensibus, Venetos destituit, partésque Ligusticas, à nepote coactus, amplectitur: & septuagenario maior tandem moritur, anno postquam imperare coeperat decimo octauo. Vide Egna.lib.2.Cosmo.Munst.lib.4.
units.tr: Andronicus, the eldest of three sons of Michael Palaeologus, succeeded his father in the Constantinopolitan empire in the year of the world 5255, from the birth of Christ 1293. Andronicus took a certain Michael, born of a Hungarian mother, as his son-in-law and partner in the empire; when he soon died, Andronicus invited Constantine, the younger Despot, to the succession of the empire. Michael's son Andronicus, the aforementioned, bearing this badly, rose up against his grandfather, relying on the help of the Genoese, and drew all the rights to himself. But when the Venetians had restored the elder Andronicus, and at last the Bulgarians and Genoese pressed hard, he abandoned the Venetians and, forced by his grandson, embraced the Ligurian party; and he died at over seventy years of age, in the eighteenth year after he had begun to reign. See Egnatius, book 2, and Cosmas Münster, book 4.

units.la: ANDRONICVS iunior, Michaëlis filius ex superioris Andronici filia, sex & amplius annis cum Andronico auo prædicto, varium ac anceps bellum gessit, sæpe tamen reconciliatis animis, amicorum opera, & gratia malè sarta non coëunte. Byzantium tandem clam ingressus, in auum nil molitur: quin illum quoad vixit, secum imperare permisit: quo mortuo, cùm aduersus hostes fortem se præstitisset, quinquagenarius obiit, febre capitisque dolore intra quatriduum confectus, anno imperij circiter 16. coepit imperare anno mundi 5273. à Christo nato 1311. Vide ut supra, & Chron. Phry. De hoc Andronico, sequentibusque Imperatoribus ad Constantinum vsque, qui à Mahomete, capto Byzantio, est obtruncatus, quot annis imperarint, ac quo anno definito singuli coeperint, nil certi statuunt autores: ordine tamen vniuscuiusque imago, ac vita, descriptæ sequuntur. IMP. ALBERTVS I AVG. IMP. HENRICHVS VII AVG.
units.tr: Andronicus the younger, son of Michael and of the daughter of the aforementioned Andronicus, waged a varied and doubtful war with his grandfather Andronicus for more than six years, though their minds were often reconciled through the work of friends, yet the friendship, badly mended, did not hold together. At last he secretly entered Byzantium and attempted nothing against his grandfather; indeed, he allowed him to rule jointly with himself for as long as he lived. When he died, having shown himself brave against the enemy, he died at the age of fifty, worn out by fever and headache within four days, in about the sixteenth year of his reign; he began to reign in the year of the world 5273, from the birth of Christ 1311. See above, and the Chronicle of Phrygius. Concerning this Andronicus and the emperors who followed him down to Constantine, who was cut down by Mahomet when Byzantium was taken, the authors state nothing certain about how many years each reigned, or in what year each began; nevertheless the portrait and life of each are described in order as follows. Emperor Albert I Augustus. Emperor Henry VII Augustus.

units.la: ALBERTVS Rudolphi filius,& Auftrię Dux,vti dictum est, deuicto, ac occiso Adolpho, imperat anno mundi 5260. à Christo nato 1298. Noluit primò Bonifacius Papa ratum habere imperium Alberti: postea tamen vltro confirmauit in odium Philippi Pulchri Gallorum Regis: quinetiam donatum Albertü titulo regni Gallici, extimulauit eum aduersus eüdem Franciæ Regem. At Philippus data filia in vxorem filio Alberti, placauit Albertum. Porrò Albertus filium suum Bohemiæ Regem cõstituit: Bauaros & Maguntinos hostilia fœdera incëtes, ita domuit vt parêrent imperio. Tandem à Ioanne fratris filio prope Renum interficitur, anno imperij 10. Consulito Aemyl. lib.8. Egna. li. 3.
units.tr: Albert, son of Rudolph and Duke of Austria, as has been said, having defeated and killed Adolf, reigns in the year of the world 5260, from the birth of Christ 1298. At first Pope Boniface was unwilling to approve Albert's empire; afterwards, however, he freely confirmed it out of hatred for Philip the Fair, King of the French; moreover, having granted Albert the title of the kingdom of France, he urged him against the same King of France. But Philip, having given his daughter in marriage to Albert's son, won Albert over. Furthermore, Albert made his son King of Bohemia; he stirred up hostile alliances against the Bavarians and the men of Mainz and subdued them so that they obeyed the empire. At last he was killed near the Rhine by John, his brother's son, in the tenth year of his reign. Consult Aemilius, book 8, and Egnatius, book 3.

units.la: HENRICVS Lucelburgensis, mortuo Alberto Imperator creatur anno mundi 5270. à Christo nato 1308. Hic Comitem Vuirtembergensem ,quòd Imperatori parêre nollet, iugúmq; detrectaret,fortunis omnibus exuit. Deinde in Italiam penetrans , Longobardiam capit, & Mediolani ferrea insignitur corona. inde Romam profectus, post diadema acceptum,, ab Vrsinis expellitur. Tandem graui obsidione Florentiam premens, veneno in Eucharistia dato, opera Dominici cuiusdam, è medio tollitur,anno imperij 5. Hic Ioàni filio suo Regis Bohemici filiam vxorem dedit: éstque ac occasione princeps Lucelbulgensis Caroli quarti pater, Rex Bohemiæ factus. Vide Aemy, lib.8.Egna. lib.3.
units.tr: Henry of Luxembourg was created emperor after the death of Albert, in the year of the world 5270, from the birth of Christ 1308. He stripped the Count of Württemberg of all his possessions because he was unwilling to obey the emperor and refused the yoke. Then, penetrating into Italy, he took Lombardy and was crowned with the iron crown at Milan. Thence he went to Rome and, after receiving the diadem, was driven out by the Orsini. At last, while besieging Florence fiercely, he was removed from the world by poison given in the Eucharist, through the work of a certain Dominican, in the fifth year of his reign. He gave his son John, the King of Bohemia, a daughter as wife; and by this occasion he became the father of Charles IV, Prince of Luxembourg, who was made King of Bohemia. See Aemilius, book 8, and Egnatius, book 3.

units.la: OTHOMANNUS regnat apud Turcas anno mundi 5261. à Christo nato 1299. Hic primus in ea gente hoc nomen tulit, à castello Galatiæ à se capto: primúsque veterem gentis gloriam asserere ausus est: nam gens ea Ierosolymam ceperat anno mundi 4970. à Christo nato 1008. Sed à Christianis Gothofredo Bolione duce victi, ac pugna non incruenta, fusi, fugatíque ad Niceam Turcæ, nullum dehinc Ducem cuius extet memoria præcipuum habuere, ad hunc usque Othomannum, qui primus neglecta paucorum potentia, Monarchiam inuasit, primúmque in Turcica historia inter Imperatores locum tenet. Hic cùm esset obscuriore loco natus, attamen ingenio felix,cautus,diligens,ambitiosus regna semper meditabatur: cui etiam impense fauit fortuna: nam magnam Bithyniæ partem, plurimáque loca munita Ponto adiacentia subegit: sed egregias suas victorias maximè nobilitauit, expugnata Siua, quæ olim Sebastia dicebatur. Regnat annos 28. obiit affecta ætate anno primo Philippi Valesij Regis. Pau. Iouius,& Munst.in Cosm.
units.tr: Othomannus reigns among the Turks in the year of the world 5261, from the birth of Christ 1299. He was the first of that people to bear this name, from a castle of Galatia that he had taken; and he was the first to dare to claim the ancient glory of the nation. For that people had taken Jerusalem in the year of the world 4970, from the birth of Christ 1008. But they were defeated by the Christians under the leader Godfrey of Bouillon, and routed in a battle not without bloodshed, and the Turks fled to Nicaea; from then on they had no leader of note whose memory survives, down to this Othomannus, who first, despising the power of the few, invaded the monarchy and first holds a place among the emperors in Turkish history. Although he was born in a humble place, he was nevertheless fortunate in talent, cautious, diligent and ambitious, and he always planned kingdoms; fortune also favoured him greatly. For he subdued a large part of Bithynia and many fortified places bordering on Pontus; but he especially made his outstanding victories famous by taking Sivas, which was formerly called Sebastia. He reigned 28 years and died in extreme old age, in the first year of Philip of Valois, King. Paulus Jovius and Münster in the Cosmography.

units.la: ORCHANES Othomanni supradicti filius, post patrem imperat anno mundi 5289. à Christo nato 1327. Hic noua dignitate auctus,nihil mutatus,nec patri absimilis, quinetiam militaris disciplinæ peritior, liberalitate, facilitate, & dexteritate fauorem & multitudinem undique comparans, rem à patre inchoatam industria, studio, & prudentia auxit, Mysiam, Lycaoniam, Phrygiam & Cariam domuit: Prusiam (quæ nunc Bursia) Regum olim Bithyniæ sedem vi cepit, accepto ibi graui vulnere, quo postea interiit, anno primo Ioannis Francorum Regis. Regnat anno 22. Pau. Io. Christoph. Recherius lib. 1[?]. IMP. LUDOVICUS IIII. IMP. CAROLUS IIII AUG.[?]
units.tr: Orchanes, son of the aforesaid Othomannus, reigns after his father in the year of the world 5289, from the birth of Christ 1327. Raised to his new dignity, changed in nothing and not unlike his father, and more skilled in military discipline, winning favour and a multitude from every side by generosity, affability and skill, he increased by industry, zeal and prudence the affair his father had begun; he subdued Mysia, Lycaonia, Phrygia and Caria; he took by force Prusa (now Bursa), formerly the seat of the kings of Bithynia, and there he received a serious wound, from which he afterwards died, in the first year of John, King of the Franks. He reigned 22 years. Paulus Jovius, Christoph Richer, book 1[?]. Emperor Louis IV. Emperor Charles IV Augustus[?].

units.la: LUDOVICUS Bavariæ Dux, Rudolphi Imperatoris ex filia nepos, & Fridericus Austriæ Dux, variantibus Electorum suffragiis, ambo Imperatores eliguntur anno mundi 5276. à Christo nato 1314. His varia fortuna sæpe congressis, tandem anno 8. victor Ludouicus, capto Friderico rerum potitur: sed cùm se Imperatorem citra Papæ assensum scriberet, excommunicatur. nihilominus Mediolanum venit, ubi ferream accipit coronam: deinde Romæ summo acceptus honore à Stephano Columnio coronatur. Petrum Corbariensem in Pontificem creat: & oppidis iuris Pontificij alios dedit præfectos, Pontificem æmulatus, qui & ipse Galliæ Cisalpinæ multos autoritate sua Regulos præfecerat. Imperauit Ludouicus annos 33. sumen do[?] initium imperij eius ab excessu, & fato venenato Henrici Lucelburgensis. Aemyl.lib.8.Egna.lib.3.
units.tr: Louis, Duke of Bavaria, grandson through a daughter of Emperor Rudolph, and Frederick, Duke of Austria, were both elected emperors, with the votes of the electors varying, in the year of the world 5276, from the birth of Christ 1314. After their varied fortunes, often contesting against each other, at last in the eighth year Louis, the victor, took Frederick prisoner and gained power; but since he wrote himself emperor without the Pope's consent, he was excommunicated. Nevertheless he came to Milan, where he received the iron crown; then at Rome, received with the highest honour, he was crowned by Stephen Colonna. He created Peter of Corvara pope, and gave other men as prefects over towns under papal jurisdiction, imitating the Pope, who had himself set many petty rulers over Cisalpine Gaul by his own authority. Louis reigned 33 years, his reign beginning from the death and poisoned fate of Henry of Luxembourg. Aemilius, book 8, and Egnatius, book 3.

units.la: CAROLUS quartus Bohemus, Ioannis Lucelburgensis Bohemiæ Regis, de quo dictum est supra in Henrico, filius, post Edoardum Anglum & Guntherum Cæsares electos, Cæsar quoque designatur: ad hunc Carolum res devenit, altero subinde post alterum vita functo. Romæ itaque coronam hac conditione accepit, ut confestim Italia excederet. laudem meruit ob Auream bullam, in qua multa quæ ad pacem publicam pertinent, complexus est. Rerum Bohemicarum imprimis studiosus fuit: Pragæ gymnasium publicum instituit. obiit anno imperij 32. Venceslao filio prius Cæsare creato, promissa Electoribus pecunia, vectigalíque imperij illis obligato. Vide ut supra.
units.tr: Charles IV of Bohemia, son of John of Luxembourg, King of Bohemia, of whom it was said above under Henry, after Edward of England and Günther were elected emperors, was also named Caesar; the rule came to this Charles, one after another dying in turn. He therefore received the crown at Rome on this condition, that he should leave Italy at once. He earned praise for the Golden Bull, in which he embraced many matters pertaining to the public peace. He was especially zealous for Bohemian affairs; he founded a public university at Prague. He died in the 32nd year of his reign, after his son Wenceslaus had first been created Caesar, with money promised to the electors and the revenues of the empire pledged to them. See above.

units.la: DANTES Aligerus, Florentinus, cùm humanioribus tum diuinis literis instructissimus, Philosophus ac Poëta, nulli suo seculo secundus, pulsus patria, in Gallia aliquandiu maximè Parisiis, posteà apud Arragonum Regem exulans, de sua calamitate varia edidit opera. Tandem exul etiam apud Rauennam obiit, Ludouico Bauaro Imperante, anno mundi 5283. à Christo nato 1321. Videto Trithemium de Scriptoribus Ecclesiasticis, & Supplementum Chronicorum lib.13.
units.tr: Dante Alighieri of Florence, most learned in both humane and divine letters, a philosopher and poet second to none of his age, driven from his homeland, lived in exile for some time in France, especially at Paris, and afterwards among the King of Aragon, and produced various works about his calamity. At last, also an exile, he died at Ravenna, in the reign of Louis of Bavaria, in the year of the world 5283, from the birth of Christ 1321. See Trithemius, On Ecclesiastical Writers, and the Supplement of the Chronicles, book 13.

units.la: CANIS Scaliger, à rebus gestis, cognomento Magnus, Veronæ urbis dominium sibi vendicans, rexit eam annos ferè 20. quam etiam variis ac superbis ædificiis ornauit. Picenum & Romandiolam omnem sua potius virtute ac liberali humanitate, quàm armis subegit. Princeps hic eloquens, comis, liberalis, oratoribus, historicis, poëtis, omnibus denique doctis fauēs, Dantem Florentinum ad se accersiuit, & præmiis ac honoribus eum donauit. Hic sine virili prole moriens, duobus nepotibus, Alberto inquam & Mastino fratribus, urbis tantæ dominium reliquit: obiit Veronæ, atque inibi maxima funeris pompa sepultus est, anno à mundo condito 5291. atque à Christo nato 1329. Videto Chronicorum Supplementum lib.13. FRAN. 18. PHILIPPVS F.REX 52 CAROL[?]VS
units.tr: Can Grande della Scala of Verona, called the Great because of his deeds, claiming for himself the lordship of the city of Verona, ruled it for nearly 20 years, and adorned it with various and splendid buildings. He subdued Picenum and all Romagna, more by his own virtue and liberal humanity than by arms. This prince was eloquent, courteous and generous, favouring orators, historians, poets and, in short, all learned men; he summoned Dante of Florence to himself and rewarded him with prizes and honours. He died without male offspring, and left the lordship of so great a city to two nephews, Albert and Mastino, brothers; he died at Verona and was buried there with the greatest funeral pomp, in the year 5291 from the creation of the world and 1329 from the birth of Christ. See the Supplement of the Chronicles, book 13. Francis 18. Philip, King of the French, 52. Charles[?].

units.la: PHILIPPVS Longus Ludouici Hutini Francorum Regis frater, successit ei in regno Franciæ anno mundi 5277. à Christo nato 1315. Hic Longus dictus est ob corporis proceritatem ac gracilitatem: id vnum mirum est, quòd neque ab ecclesia, neque à populo quæ petebat tributa & vectigalia impetrare potuerit. Puteos elephantiaci à Iudæis persuasi, veneno infecerunt: quæ res occasionem vt pestis grassaretur præbuit: sed vtrique miserè, dato supplicio, perierunt. Constituerat Rex efficere vt vbique ponderis, mensuræ & pecuniæ rario eadem esset: sed morte præuentus id præstare non potuit. obiit anno regni, quod per Saliquam legem adeptus erat, quinto, nullis confectis bellis: nam festa pax vndique ridebat. in æde D. Dionysij conditus est. Vide Paulum Æmylium de rebus Francorum lib.8. Gaguin.lib.7. & Carionem lib.3.
units.tr: Philip the Tall, brother of Louis X of the Franks, succeeded him in the kingdom of France in the year of the world 5277, from the birth of Christ 1315. He was called "the Tall" on account of his great height and slenderness. One thing is remarkable: he could not obtain from the Church or from the people the taxes and duties he demanded. Lepers were persuaded by the Jews to poison the wells, and this gave the plague an occasion to spread; but both were miserably punished with execution and perished. The King had resolved to make weights, measures and money uniform everywhere, but, forestalled by death, he could not accomplish it. He died in the fifth year of the reign he had obtained by the Salic law, with no wars waged, for a festive peace smiled everywhere. He was buried in the church of St Denis. See Paulus Aemilius, On the Deeds of the Franks, book 8; Gaguin, book 7; and Carion, book 3.

units.la: CAROLVS huius nominis quartus, cognominatus Pulcher, Philippi Longi frater, Nauarræ Rex, quemadmodum & tres Francorum Reges superiores, succedit fratri in Franciæ regno anno mundi 5282. à Christo nato 1320. Hic in scelera seuerissimè animaduertit, iustitiæ & æquitatis cultor fuit. Aquitaniam ingressus, Regum hic primus Papæ decimas permisit, vt quæstus particeps fieret. has autem colligebat Papa, vt bello lacesseret Ludouicum Bauarum Imperatorem, quem hostem scilicet ecclesiæ iudicauerat. Regnat annos septem: moritur ad saltum Vicenarum, sepultus in æde D. Dionysij, relicta vxore grauida. Vide autores quos supra. R. FRAN. 50 PHILIPPVS REX FRAN. 51. IOANNES
units.tr: Charles, the fourth of that name, surnamed the Fair, brother of Philip the Tall, King of Navarre, as were also the three Kings of the Franks before him, succeeded his brother in the kingdom of France in the year of the world 5282, from the birth of Christ 1320. He punished crimes most severely and was a cultivator of justice and equity. Entering Aquitaine, he was the first of the Kings to allow the Pope to collect tithes, so that he might share in the profit. The Pope, however, collected these in order to wage war on Louis the Bavarian, the Emperor, whom he had judged an enemy of the Church. He reigned seven years and died at Vincennes, leaving behind a pregnant wife; he was buried in the church of St Denis. See the authors cited above. [Royal list: Philip King of the Franks, 51; John.]

units.la: PHILIPPVS Valesius trium superiorum Franciae Regum patruelis, Carolo Pulchro succedens, regnat apud Francos anno mundi 5289. à Christo nato 1327. Flandri à Gallis profligantur: Casletum capitur, spoliatur, incenditur. Ad Ambianos Regum Franci, Angli, Bohemi, & Balearici fit coëuentus, Anglus clientem se Franci Regis profitetur. Sacra arma Valesius induit contra fidei Christianae aduersarios. Petrus Cunerius frustra conatur temporalem Episcopis auferre iurisdictionem. Incipit maximum bellum Anglicu. Iacobus Arteuilla plebeius multas in Flandria excitat turbas contra Flandrensem Comitē, qui se in Franciam recipit. Galli & Angli Regum acies in conspectu fere sine conflictu veniunt. Anglus quando Francus praelio abstinet, Flandriam repetit, vbi Arteuillae consilio, lilia & Regis Franciae titulum adsumit: quae hucusq; sibi arrogat. Ad Crefciacum pugnatur tandem à nostris infeliciter. Calitium Anglis deditur, à quibus recuperari nunquam potuit. Trapezitę Lõgobardi & Itali capti, pulsi, ac proscripti sunt ex Francia ob immanes vsuras. Rex forte accipit, interfurio relicto. Humbertus Princeps vili Delphinatum vendit, ea lege vt primus Regis filius Delphinus vocaretur, & Delphinatum obineret: itaque Dominicanum Humbertus profitetur. Initio regni immanes exactiones fuere, ac primum ex sale vectigal institutum. Regnat annis 22.obit ad Nogentum regium, sepultus ad D. Dionysium. Æmy. lib. 8. & 9.
units.tr: Philip of Valois, cousin of the three preceding Kings of France, succeeding Charles the Fair, reigned among the Franks in the year of the world 5289, from the birth of Christ 1327. The Flemings were routed by the French; Cassel was taken, plundered and burned. A meeting of the Kings of the French, English, Bohemians and Balearics took place at Amiens; the Englishman declared himself a vassal of the French King. Valois took up arms against the enemies of the Christian faith. Peter Cunerius tried in vain to strip the bishops of their temporal jurisdiction. The great English war began. James Arteville, a commoner, stirred up many disturbances in Flanders against the Count of Flanders, who withdrew into France. The armies of the French and English Kings came face to face, almost without conflict. When the Frenchman refrained from battle, the Englishman returned to Flanders, where, on Arteville's advice, he assumed the lilies and the title of King of France, which he has claimed for himself until now. At Crécy battle was finally joined, unhappily for our side. Calais was surrendered to the English, and it could never be recovered from them. Lombard and Italian money-changers were seized, driven out and banished from France on account of their huge usury. The King, by chance, received them back, having abandoned his madness. Humbert, Prince, sold the Dauphiné for a price, on the condition that the first son of the King should be called the Dauphin and hold the Dauphiné; and so Humbert professed himself a Dominican. At the beginning of the reign there were immense exactions, and first a tax on salt was instituted. He reigned 22 years and died at the royal château of Nogent, and was buried at St Denis. Aemilius, books 8 and 9.

units.la: IOANNES Philippi Valesij filius, patri in regno succedit anno mundi 5311. à Christo nato 1349. Hic ab Anglo, capitur, ad quartum lapidem ab vrbe Pictonum, ac post annos 4. liberatur: nec multo post iterum in Angliam traiicit vt de suis obsidibus liberandis transigat: at morbo ante reditum praeuentus, Londini moritur anno regni 14. ad D. Diony. Carolus quintus patris Ioannis cadauer transtulit. Æmy. lib. 9.
units.tr: John, son of Philip of Valois, succeeded his father in the kingdom in the year of the world 5311, from the birth of Christ 1349. He was captured by the Englishman at the fourth milestone from the city of the Poitevins, and after four years was freed; not long afterwards he crossed again into England to settle the matter of the release of his hostages, but, forestalled by illness before his return, he died in London in the fourteenth year of his reign. He was buried at St Denis. Charles V transferred the body of his father John. Aemilius, book 9.

units.la: IOANNES Palæologus,dictus etiam Calo-ioannes,patri Andronico iuniori succedit,licet Ioannes Cantacuzenus,tutor prudens,imperium administret Constantinopolitanum circa annum mundi 5290. à Christo nato 1328. Tutor itaque Cantacuzenus,ac imperij consors Apocauci fraude (viri quidem obscuri,sed solertis & callidi,ac inter principis amicos ob eiusmodi mores,præcipuæ dignationis) & Patriarchæ ambitione, in exilium truditur. iniuriæ impatiens bellum quinquennale aduersus Reginam & Ioannem Cantacuzenum Imperatorem, Andronici filium gerit,Turcarum arma Europæ primus infert. Huic tandem proditur Byzantium:quod cum occupasset,nulli molestus fuit,imperij tantum consortem egit,filia in vxorem Ioanni tradita. Inde in Genuenses,sociis Venetis & Arragoniis,varia fortuna bellum gerit Cantacuzenus:cui & statim ab Ioanne Palæologo exule prædicto bellum indictum,Turcarum in primis ope geritur,quibus etiam in Europa locum primum inhabitandum tradidit. Cum autem improuisus Byzantium, ex Tenedo soluens,ingressus esset Palæologus,tandem Cantacuzenus imperio relicto,monachum egit. Palæologus Matthæum Cantacuzeni filium participe imperij agere volentem, imperium deponere coëgit. & cum multa bella confecisset Palæologus,moriens filio Manueli imperiu reliquit. Vide Egnat. lib.2.& Cofm.Mun.lib.4.
units.tr: John Palaeologus, also called Calo-John, succeeded his father Andronicus the Younger, although John Cantacuzenus, a prudent guardian, administered the empire of Constantinople, around the year of the world 5290, from the birth of Christ 1328. Thus the guardian Cantacuzenus, and his partner in the empire, through the treachery of Apocaucus (a man indeed obscure, but clever and crafty, and of the highest standing among the prince's friends because of such manners) and the ambition of the Patriarch, was thrust into exile. Unable to bear the injury, he waged a five-year war against the Empress and against John Cantacuzenus, the Emperor, son of Andronicus; he was the first to bring the arms of the Turks into Europe. At last Byzantium was betrayed to him; when he had occupied it, he did no harm to anyone, but ruled only as partner in the empire, having given his daughter in marriage to John. Thereafter Cantacuzenus waged war with varying fortune against the Genoese, in alliance with the Venetians and the Aragonese; and John Palaeologus, the aforesaid exile, declared war on him too, chiefly with the help of the Turks, to whom he also gave the first place to settle in Europe. But when Palaeologus, setting out from Tenedos, entered Byzantium unexpectedly, Cantacuzenus at last laid down the empire and became a monk. Palaeologus forced Matthew, son of Cantacuzenus, who wished to be a partner in the empire, to lay down the imperial power. And after Palaeologus had fought many wars, he died and left the empire to his son Manuel. See Egnatius, book 2, and Cosmas Munsterus, book 4.

units.la: MANVEL prædicti Ioannis Palæologi filius,post patrem imperat Constantinopoli: septem mares filios hic reliquit,quorum Ioannes natu maximus,morienti successit. Vide vt supra.
units.tr: Manuel, son of the aforesaid John Palaeologus, ruled at Constantinople after his father. He left seven male sons, of whom John, the eldest, succeeded him on his death. See as above.

units.la: AMVRATHES huius nominis primus, Orchanis filius, mortuo patre, apud Turcas imperat anno mundi 5311. à Christo nato 1349. Is auitam paternámque felicitatem æmulatus est: at vero in Caramanum auum maternum non minus infestus quàm pater fuit, qui socerum occiso eius filio adolescente non minima Ciliciæ parte exuerat. Cæterùm à Constantinopolitano Imperatore Ioanne Palæologo solicitatus Amurathes 12000. Turcarum ei in auxilium mittit: idque initium ac origo ruinæ imperij Constantinopolitani fuit. Nam Europeis opibus illectus Amurathes, opis denuo adferendæ simulatione, potiundæ tamen Græciæ animo, Genuensium nauibus vsus Amurathes, Thurcarum 60000. in Græciam transportat: Hellespontum ad Abydum superat: Callipolim cum aliis oppidis occupat: in ipsum quoque Imperatorem inexpectato grauem impetum facit. Postea Seruiam, Bulgariamque ingressus, Lazarum Seruiæ, & Marcum Bulgariæ principes, cum paratissimis copiis ei occurentes, ingenti cæde profligat, prius occupata Adrianopoli: sed Lazaro cæso, mox à feruo in domini vindictam Amurathes occiditur, anno regni 23. Vide Egna.lib.2. Pau.Io.& Christop.Richerium de rebus Turcarum lib.1.
units.tr: Amurath, the first of that name, son of Orchan, ruled among the Turks after his father's death, in the year of the world 5311, from the birth of Christ 1349. He emulated the happiness of his grandfather and father; yet he was no less hostile to Caramanus, his maternal grandfather, than his father had been, for Caramanus had stripped his father-in-law of no small part of Cilicia after killing his adolescent son. Moreover, solicited by John Palaeologus, the Emperor of Constantinople, Amurath sent him 12,000 Turks as help; and this was the beginning and origin of the ruin of the Constantinopolitan empire. For Amurath, lured by European wealth, under the pretext of bringing help again but with his mind set on seizing Greece, used Genoese ships and transported 60,000 Turks into Greece; he crossed the Hellespont to Abydos, occupied Gallipoli with other towns, and made a severe, unexpected attack on the Emperor himself. Afterwards, entering Serbia and Bulgaria, he routed with great slaughter Lazarus, prince of Serbia, and Marcus, prince of Bulgaria, who met him with very well-prepared forces; first Adrianople was taken. But after Lazarus was slain, Amurath was soon killed by a servant, in vengeance for his master, in the twenty-third year of his reign. See Egnatius, book 2; Paulus Jovius; and Christophorus Richerius, On the Affairs of the Turks, book 1.

units.la: SOLIMANVS Amurathis filius, patri in imperio succedens, confestim hæreditariæ dignitati eripitur, atque per insidias occiditur à fratre æmulo Baiazete: quamobrem à nonnullis inter Turcicos Imperatores minimè annumeratur. Vide vt supra. F.REX.49 CAROLVS IOH[?] CAROLVS 6 FR
units.tr: Suleiman, son of Amurath, succeeded his father in the empire, but was immediately snatched from his hereditary dignity and killed by treachery by his rival brother Bayezid; for this reason he is by some not counted among the Turkish emperors at all. See as above.

units.la: CAROLVS quintus, Ioannis Francorum Regis filius, patri in regno succedit anno mundi 5325. à Christo nato 1363. Hic sapiēs cognominatur ob morum probitatem, & egregiam regni administrationem: literas,& literatos coluit: Bibliorum libros syncerè transferri iussit: ius ex æquo vt diceretur in primis curauit, iudiciisq; frequenter adfuit.togatus omnino fuit, nec arma vnquā induit:tantum loca Lutetiæ vicina peragrans, longinqua & grauia negotia, & bella, per fratres ac præfectos suos administrauit:per quos quicquid patri ab Anglis ablatum erat,id omne ferè recuperauit.vt belli impensis sufficeret,vectigal sali,ac promercali vino imposuit. Aduersus Anglos exercitus quinque potentisimos habuit.Carolus quartus,Imperator ac Venceslaus filius Cæsar, in Franciā veniunt, vt inter Anglos & Francos pacem componant:sed re infecta redeunt ob Reginæ,ac Isabellæ filiæ interitum. Lex Regis in Senatu promulgatur,vt Regum Franciæ filij anno 14.inungantur,& coronentur. Bastildæ fundaméta iaciuntur Lutetiæ,Regis sumptibus. obiit an.regni 16.in castro pulchritudinis ad saltum Vicenarum: sepultus ad D.Dionysium.Turlupini, qui se paupertatis societatem vocitabant,delentur.Æmyl.lib.9.
units.tr: Charles V, son of John, King of the Franks, succeeded his father in the kingdom in the year of the world 5325, from the birth of Christ 1363. He was surnamed "the Wise" on account of the uprightness of his character and his excellent administration of the kingdom. He cultivated letters and men of letters; he ordered the books of the Bible to be faithfully translated; he took particular care that law should be administered evenly, and he often attended the courts. He was entirely a man of the gown and never put on arms; only wandering about the places near Paris, he managed distant and weighty affairs and wars through his brothers and his officers, and through them he recovered almost everything that had been taken from his father by the English. To meet the costs of war, he imposed a tax on salt and on wine sold retail. He kept five very powerful armies against the English. Charles IV, the Emperor, and Wenceslas, his son, the Caesar, came into France to make peace between English and French, but returned with nothing done, because of the death of the Queen and of Isabella, his daughter. A royal law was promulgated in the Senate that the sons of the Kings of France should be anointed and crowned in their fourteenth year. The foundations of the Bastille were laid at Paris at the King's expense. He died in the sixteenth year of his reign at the castle of Beauté, near Vincennes, and was buried at St Denis. The Turlupins, who called themselves a society of poverty, were wiped out. Aemilius, book 9.

units.la: CAROLVS sextus,Caroli quinti filius,adhuc adolescēs, in Regem Franciæ consecratur, anno mundi 5342. à Christo nato 1380. Hic Rex tres tantùm Liliorum flores pro insigni Regum Franciæ gestare instituit. huic pater duodeuicies 100000. aureorum reliquit:initio tamē regni filij, magnæ fisci angustiæ fuerunt:huius adolescentia & crebra gubernantium mutatio, tantam vim pecuniæ dissiparat. Armeniæ Rex à Turcis pulsus in Franciam venit. Africum bellum conficitur. Regnat an. 42. ad D. Dionysium sepultus. Vide vt supra.
units.tr: Charles VI, son of Charles V, still a youth, was consecrated King of France in the year of the world 5342, from the birth of Christ 1380. This King began the practice of bearing only three lilies as the badge of the Kings of France. His father left him 1,800,000 gold pieces; yet at the beginning of his son's reign there were great shortages in the treasury, and his youth and the frequent changes of regents squandered so much money. The King of Armenia, driven out by the Turks, came into France. The African war was concluded. He reigned 42 years and was buried at St Denis. See as above.

units.la: FRANCISCUS Petrarca, natione Hetruscus, vir doctissimus, Philosophus, Rhetor, & Poëta celeberrimus, literas velut intermortuas quasi ab inferis revocauit:nec minus sancta conversatione quàm scientia claruit, multa opera tam in lingua Latina, quàm in sua vernacula conscripsit. Amore Christi & Philosophiæ salutaris vitam solitariam elegit, in qua Philosophando, orando & scribendo perseuerans, moritur in Eremitorio suo agri Patauini, sub Carolo Imperatore huius nominis quarto, & Gregorio Papa huius nominis undecimo, anno à mundo condito 5536.à Christo nato 1374. Videto Trithemium.
units.tr: Francis Petrarch, an Italian by birth, a most learned man, and a very celebrated philosopher, rhetorician and poet, called back literature as if it had been almost dead and buried. He was no less distinguished for his holy way of life than for his learning, and wrote many works both in Latin and in his own vernacular. Out of love for Christ and for saving philosophy, he chose a solitary life, and persevering in philosophy, prayer and writing, he died in his hermitage in the fields of Padua, under the emperor Charles IV of that name and Pope Gregory XI of that name, in the year of the world 5536, from the birth of Christ 1374. See Trithemius.

units.la: IOANNES Boccatius Florentinus itidem Poëta, Philosophus, & Astronomus eruditissimus, multa præclara volumina tum Latino, tum vulgari suo idiomate conscripsit. moritur statim post Petrarcam. Videto etiam Trithemium.
units.tr: John Boccaccio of Florence, likewise a poet, philosopher and most learned astronomer, wrote many excellent volumes both in Latin and in his vernacular tongue. He died immediately after Petrarch. See also Trithemius.

units.la: IO. GALEATIVS Vicecomes, Galeatij Mariæ filius, anno mundi 5333. à Christo nato 1371. postquam more patrum suorum, annos 17. Mediolani imperauerat, à Ladislao Cæsare, Dux Mediolani creatur. Ut autem à suis inciperet, Barnaba patruo occiso, opes eius & imperium occupauit. Hinc Veronam, Vicentiam, & Paduam subiugauit. ad Occidentem, Vercellas, Albam, atque Astam subegit. ad meridiem debellauit Aquas, Alexandriam, Tortonam, Bubbium, Placentiam, Parmam, Regium, Bononiam, Pisas, Massam, Senas, Grossetum, atque Clusium. & reuertens Perusium, Assisium, Noceam, Ciuitatem, Bellonam cepit & Feltrum: &(ut velut circulum absoluueret) Brixiam, Bergamum, Laudem, Cremonam, atque Cremam, subegit. Lucenses in deditionem accepit. tota ipsum Italia reformidauit. Ticini ædificauit arcem superbam, ad quartum verò lapidem, septum admodum ingens, ad feras omnis generis asseruandas, cum cænobio magnifico extruxit. fuit pulcher, doctus, & eloquens: sed imprimis sagax. Tandem 55. ætatis anno, post 24. imperij obiit, relicta Valentina, Caroli Regis Franciæ postea uxore. Paul. Iouius, & Supplementum Chro.
units.tr: John Galeazzo Visconti, son of Galeazzo Maria, in the year of the world 5333, from the birth of Christ 1371. After he had ruled Milan for seventeen years in the manner of his fathers, he was created Duke of Milan by the emperor Wenceslaus. But to begin with his own people, he seized the wealth and power of his uncle Barnabas after having him killed. From there he subdued Verona, Vicenza and Padua. To the west he conquered Vercelli, Alba and Asti. To the south he subdued Acqui, Alessandria, Tortona, Bobbio, Piacenza, Parma, Reggio, Bologna, Pisa, Massa, Siena, Grosseto and Chiusi. Returning, he took Perugia, Assisi, Nocera, Città di Castello, Bellona and Feltre; and (so as to complete the circle) he subdued Brescia, Bergamo, Lodi, Cremona and Crema. He received Lucca into surrender. All of Italy stood in dread of him. At Pavia he built a proud citadel, and at the fourth milestone he constructed a very large enclosure, with a magnificent monastery, for keeping wild animals of every kind. He was handsome, learned and eloquent, but above all shrewd. Finally, in the fifty-fifth year of his age, after twenty-four years of rule, he died, leaving behind Valentina, who was afterwards the wife of Charles, King of France. Paulus Jovius, and the Supplementum Chronicorum.

units.la: IO. MARIA Vicecomes, adhuc paruulus, & sub materna custodia, anno Salutis 1402. felicissim. patri successit. Hic cum adoleuisset, multos innocentes occidit, & non paucos inimicos canibus vivos devorandos tradidit. Piam matrem detrusit in carcerem, ibíque eam sæuissimè mori coegit. Verùm mox quasi Deo vindice, nudatus amplissim. bonis paternis, à domesticis, post decem annorum tyrannidem, in templo trucidatur. Paul. Iou. & Supplementum.
units.tr: John Maria Visconti, still a little child and under his mother's care, succeeded his father in the year of salvation 1402, most unhappily. When he grew up, he killed many innocent people, and handed over not a few enemies to be devoured alive by dogs. He thrust his pious mother into prison and forced her to die there most cruelly. But soon, as if God were his avenger, he was stripped of his ample paternal wealth by his own household servants, and after ten years of tyranny he was butchered in a church. Paulus Jovius and the Supplementum.

units.la: BAIAZETES Turcarum Rex quartus, siue Pazaites, huius nominis primus, mortuo patre Amurathe Solimanum fratrem per insidias occidit, folúsq; imperio potitur anno mundi 5335. à Christo nato 1373. Hic Marcum Bulgariæ principem prælio superatum trucidat, patris mortem vlturus: bonámque Bulgariæ partem debellat: neque ita multò post, crudelissimas in Hungaria, Albania, & Valachia excursiones fecit: Christianos quamplurimos ligatos in Thraciam duxit. In negotiis exequendis tanta vsus est celeritate, vt Baiazetes Hildrin, id est cœli fulgur cognominaretur. Animi itaq; ac corporis doribus adiutus totam ferè Græciâ subegit. Constantinopolim obsedit annis 8. cuius Imperator in Galliam nauigat, auxilium imploraturus, quod & obtinet. Baiazetes autem Gallos, Hungaros, Germanos ac Seruianos, siue Mysios, semel ac strenuè superat: atque ad obsidionem Constantinopolitanam reuertitur: neque vlla ratione imperij caput illud seruari poterat, ni Tamberlanes, Orientalis Scythiæ Rex, ei occurrisset, qui Baiazetem ad Stellam montē, vbi cum Mithridate Pompeius pugnarat, vicit, catenísq; aureis ligatum, atque in ferream caueam detrusum, per totam Asiam ac Syriam circunduxit, donec etiam in fata concederet. Vide Egna.lib.3.Pau.Iouium, de re.Turc.
units.tr: Bayezid, the fourth king of the Turks, or Pazaites, the first of that name, after his father Murad died, killed his brother Suleiman by treachery and took sole power, in the year of the world 5335, from the birth of Christ 1373. He slaughtered Marko, prince of Bulgaria, after defeating him in battle, wishing to avenge his father's death, and he subdued a large part of Bulgaria. Not long after, he made the most cruel raids into Hungary, Albania and Wallachia, and led very many Christians away bound into Thrace. He showed such speed in carrying out his undertakings that Bayezid was surnamed Ilderim, that is, the lightning of heaven. Aided by the gifts of mind and body, he subdued nearly all of Greece. He besieged Constantinople for eight years, while its emperor sailed to France to seek help, which he obtained. Bayezid, however, defeated the French, Hungarians, Germans and Serbians, or Mysians, once and for all with vigour, and returned to the siege of Constantinople; nor could that capital of the empire have been saved in any way, unless Tamerlane, king of Eastern Scythia, had come against him. He defeated Bayezid at Mount Stella, where Pompey had fought with Mithridates, and, bound in golden chains and thrust into an iron cage, he led him around all Asia and Syria, until at last he died. See Egnatius, book 3, Paulus Jovius, on Turkish affairs.

units.la: TAMBERLANES Zagataiæ Orientalis Scythiæ regionis, versus Parthiam ac Sogodianam princeps, peditum ac equitum infinita pene multitudine fretus, Turcarum 200000. vnico congressu cecidit, Regémque eorum Baiazetem, vti dictum est, cepit, circa annum Domini 1397. Vide vt supra.
units.tr: Tamerlane, prince of the Zagatai region of Eastern Scythia, towards Parthia and Sogdiana, relying on an almost endless multitude of foot and horse, cut down 200,000 Turks in a single engagement, and captured their king Bayezid, as has been said, around the year of the Lord 1397. See above.

units.la: VENCESLAVS succedit Carolo patri Imperatori huius nominis quarto, imperatq; post eum anno mundi 5340. à Christo nato 1378. hic nec patri, nec avo similis fuit: cum patre tamen annos 8. regnarat: tandem solus ignauissimè rem administrat annis 22. Cæterum à Sigismundo fratre captus est, móxque Electores ei imperium abrogant, in cuius locum Robertum Bauarum sufficiunt. Porrò Galeatius Vicecomes Mediolanensis bonam Italiæ partem suo dominio adiicit, atque à Venceslao, pro Vicecomite, Dux Mediolanensis dicitur. tunc igitur in Ducatum erectus est primùm Vicecomitatus Mediolanensis. Apud fratrem in carcere apoplexia obiit Venceslaus. Blond.lib.io.[?]deca.2.Egna.lib.3.
units.tr: Wenceslaus succeeded his father Charles IV, emperor of that name, and reigned after him in the year of the world 5340, from the birth of Christ 1378. He resembled neither his father nor his grandfather. Although he had reigned for eight years together with his father, he afterwards administered affairs alone, most negligently, for twenty-two years. Moreover, he was taken captive by his brother Sigismund, and soon the electors deprived him of the empire and put Robert of Bavaria in his place. Meanwhile Galeazzo Visconti, Duke of Milan, added a good part of Italy to his dominion, and was called Duke of Milan by Wenceslaus, as Visconti. Then for the first time the Viscounty of Milan was raised to a duchy. Wenceslaus died of apoplexy in prison, at his brother's court. Blondus, book 10, decade 2; Egnatius, book 3.

units.la: ROBERTVS, qui & Rupertus, Bauariæ Dux, deiecto Venceslao, imperat anno mundi 5362. à Christo nato 1400. Hic ut Florentinis gratum faceret, ad comprimendam Galeatij potentiam, in Italiam traiicit: verùm cum eo ad Benacum congressus, facilè repellitur: unde mox ad Venetos deflexit: & incassum Florentinis adnitecibus[?] ne Italia exiret, in Germaniam retro abiit, paci, religionique vacaturus, Florentinos interim in magno relinquens discrimine. Obiit post annos ex quo imperauit decem. Vide ut supra.
units.tr: Robert, also called Rupert, Duke of Bavaria, having deposed Wenceslaus, reigned in the year of the world 5362, from the birth of Christ 1400. He crossed into Italy to do the Florentines a favour, to check the power of Galeazzo; but when he engaged him at Lake Garda, he was easily driven back. From there he soon turned towards the Venetians, and, when the Florentines strove in vain to prevent him from leaving Italy, he withdrew back into Germany, intending to devote himself to peace and religion, leaving the Florentines meanwhile in great danger. He died after ten years of reign. See above.

units.la: CYRISCELEBES, quem alij falsò Calapinum dicunt, Baiazetis filius natu maximus, cū fratribus post patris cladem fugiens, Asiáque à Tamberlane spoliatus, & ad Imperatorem Constantinopolitanum pro singulari præda deductus, regiéq; apud eum educatus, postea summa Imperatoris clementia solutus est: in Asiámque discedens, paternum imperium recuperat. Instauratis itaq; imperij viribus, aduentanti Sigismundo Hungariæ Regi fortiter se opposuit, qui Salumbezenes campos occuparat, sperans vires non resumpturos Turcas post tantam à Tamberlane acceptam cladem: sed non magis sibi fauente fortuna quàm, cùm ad Nicopolim pugnas cum Baiazete, fauerat, fugere cogitur Sigismundus: cuius pedites ante sagittis cōfossi sunt, quàm in phalangē dispositi cominus congredi cùm hoste potuerint: equites verò ad primum statim aduentantis hostis impetum terga verterunt. Victor Cyriscelebes cum Despotam bello lacessere inciperet, morbo præventus in ipso ætatis flore obiit anno regni 6. Pau.Iouius de rebus Turcicis.
units.tr: Cyriscelebes, whom others falsely call Calapinus, the eldest son of Bayezid, fleeing with his brothers after his father's defeat, and despoiled of Asia by Tamerlane, was led before the emperor of Constantinople as a single prize, and, being brought up at his court as a royal ward, was afterwards released by the great clemency of the emperor. Departing into Asia, he recovered his father's empire. Having thus restored the strength of the empire, he bravely opposed Sigismund, King of Hungary, who was approaching, and who had occupied the plains of Salumbezenes, hoping that the Turks would not recover their strength after so great a defeat received from Tamerlane. But Fortune favoured him no more than she had favoured Sigismund when he fought with Bayezid at Nicopolis, and Sigismund was forced to flee. His infantry were pierced by arrows before they could be arranged in a phalanx and engage the enemy at close quarters, and his cavalry turned their backs at the very first charge of the advancing enemy. Victorious, Cyriscelebes was beginning to provoke the Despot to war, when he was forestalled by illness and died in the very flower of his age, in the sixth year of his reign. Paulus Jovius, on Turkish affairs.

units.la: ORCHANES patri Cyriscelebæ, tenella adhuc ætate adolescentulus, ac unicus imperij hæres, ad imperium cùm conaretur paucorum studio atque opera admitti, à Mose patruo interficitur. Moses statim dignum illo parricidio exitium tulit, à fratre Ma-hometé vita bonísque priuatus. Sunt qui hunc Mahometem, nulla prorsus facta de Cyriscelebe, Orchane, & Mose mentione, à morte Baiazetis statim imperasse tradant: quare nullam hîc supputationis annorum rationem habuimus, sicuti nec Chronici. Vide ut supra.
units.tr: Orchanes, son of Cyriscelebes, a youth still of tender age and the sole heir of the empire, when he tried to be admitted to the throne through the zeal and efforts of a few, was killed by his uncle Moses. Moses at once suffered a destruction worthy of that parricide: he was deprived of life and property by his brother Mahomet. There are those who report that this Mahomet ruled immediately after the death of Bayezid, with no mention at all made of Cyriscelebes, Orchanes and Moses; for this reason we have taken no account of years here, nor in the Chronicle. See above.

units.la: MOSES Orchanem nepotem,cui erat patruus interfecit, ipse quoque à fratre Mahometo vicissim interfectus est. nec connumeratur ambo in serie Turcicorum Imperatorum, quòd paucis admodum diebus imperitarint. Vide Richerium de rebus Turcicis lib.i.
units.tr: MOSES killed Orchanes, his nephew, whose uncle he was; he himself was in turn killed by his brother Mahomet. Neither of them is counted in the series of Turkish emperors, because they ruled for only a very few days. See Richerius, on Turkish affairs, book 1.

units.la: MAHOMETES huius nominis primus, Mustaphæ & Mosis,eius inquam qui Orchanem ex fratre nepotem è medio sustulerat,frater, post Baiazetem Turcis imperat anno mundi 5359. à Christo nato 1397. Sunt qui ea quæ de Cyriscelebe feruntur,huic vni tribuant. Is itaque Bulgaros & Valachos præ dis & cladibus afflixit, tributúmque magnum imposuit. Arma deinde in Satrapas Asiæ vertit, loca omnia quæ Tamberlanes occupauerat recepit : nihil generis propinquitate commotus, Turcicæ nationis complures principes ex Galatia, Ponto & Cappadocia pulsos extirpauit : alios autem integros atque incolumes seruauit. Reuersus in Græciam, Adrianopolim, quæ caput est Thraciæ, sedis imperatoriæ loco habuit, pulsis illinc Christianis. Obiit anno imperij sui 17. regni verò Caroli hoc nomine sexti Francorum Regis 35. Vide Richer.lib.i. & Cosm. Munst.lib.4. IMP. SIGIS MVNDVS. AVG. IMP. ALB ERTVS. AVG.
units.tr: MAHOMET, the first of that name, brother of Mustafa and of Moses (I mean him who had removed his nephew Orchanes, son of his brother, from the midst), ruled the Turks after Bayezid in the year of the world 5359, from the birth of Christ 1397. Some attribute to him alone what is told of Cyriscelebes. He afflicted the Bulgarians and Wallachians with plunder and slaughter, and imposed a heavy tribute. Then he turned his arms against the satraps of Asia and recovered all the places which Tamerlane had occupied; moved by no consideration of kinship, he exterminated several Turkish princes who had been driven out of Galatia, Pontus and Cappadocia, but he spared the others whole and unharmed. Returning to Greece, he made Adrianople, which is the chief city of Thrace, the seat of his empire, after the Christians had been driven out from there. He died in the seventeenth year of his reign, and in the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Charles VI, King of the French of that name. See Richerius, book 1, and Sebastian Münster, book 4.

units.la: SIGISMVNDVS, Hungariæ & Bohemiæ Rex, Venceslai frater, mortuo Alberto communi omnium assensu Imperator creatur anno mundi 5372. à Christo nato 1410. Hic Imperatoriæ planè indolis, sapientia, eruditione, probitate ac liberalitate clarus, doctos fouit, ac dignitatibus ornauit. Attamen ab Amurathe Turcarum principe graui prælio victus, castris etiam exuitur. Hic per triennium magnam Europæ partem peragrauit, quò schisma Christiano nomini calamitosissimum extirparet: quare effecit ut reiectis adulterinis tribus Pontificibus qui Barionæ sedem inuaserat, Od[illegible, ~2 letters]olumnius omnium consensu Pontifex declararetur. obiit Sigismundus nulla relicta virili prole, cum annos 27. imperasset. Vide Egna.li.3.
units.tr: SIGISMUNDUS, King of Hungary and Bohemia, brother of Wenceslaus, is created Emperor by the common consent of all, after the death of Albert, in the year of the world 5372, from the birth of Christ 1410. He was plainly distinguished by an imperial character, wisdom, learning, uprightness and generosity; he cherished learned men and honoured them with dignities. Yet he was defeated in a severe battle by Amurath, prince of the Turks, and even stripped of his camp. For three years he travelled through a great part of Europe, so that he might extinguish the schism, most calamitous to the Christian name. Hence he brought it about that, the three adulterine Popes having been rejected, Oddo Colonna, the one who had seized the see of Bari, was declared Pope by the consent of all. Sigismund died leaving no male offspring, after he had reigned 27 years. See Egnatius, book 3.

units.la: ALBERTVS Dux Austriacus, post Sigismundi obitum Imperator designatur anno mundi 5399. à Christo nato 1437. Hic Sigismûdi gener cùm esset, post eius obitum hæres regnorum Bohemiæ & Hungariâ factus est. Morauos ac Sarmatas intra suos fines quiescere compulit. Bohemiæ factiones compescuit: Amurathe Turcam, qui Hungariâ inuaserat, fugauit: Synderouiam in deditionem accepit: inde in Græciam contendes, Thessalonicam expugnauit. Austriam repetens, moritur anno imperij sui (proh dura fata) secundo. Vide ut supra.
units.tr: ALBERT, Duke of Austria, is designated Emperor after the death of Sigismund, in the year of the world 5399, from the birth of Christ 1437. Since he was Sigismund's son-in-law, he became heir to the kingdoms of Bohemia and Hungary after his death. He compelled the Moravians and Sarmatians to keep quiet within their own borders. He checked the factions of Bohemia; he put to flight Amurath the Turk, who had invaded Hungary; he received Synderovia into surrender; from there he hastened into Greece and took Thessalonica by storm. Returning to Austria, he died in the second year of his reign (O hard fate!). See as above.

units.la: PHILIPPVS Maria, obtruncato Ioanne fratre supradićto, armis paternum Mediolanensem inquam ducatum repetit anno mundi 5379. à Christo nato 1417. Callidus hic in bello pacem, in pace bellù poscere visus est. Discendi auidus semper fuit, callidus, sagax, liberalis, in iniuriis relaxandis facillimus, statura procerus, vultu formidabilis, maturo consilio, arte, ac validissimis armis, tyrannos qui suae ditionis ciuitates occuparant, è medio sustulit. Recuperauit Comum, Tricium, Bergamum, Brissiam, Placentiam, Laudem, Cremonam quoque subegit. Io. Iacobus M[illegible, ~3 letters]ferrati Marchio, veritus huius potentiam, Vercellas, Alexandriam, Astamque sponte Philippo restituit. Suo praeterea dominio Genuam maritimam vrbem potentissimam adiecit. Genuenses itaque subacti, ac eius subditi, Alphonsum Neapoli, & Io. Nauarrae Reges, & magnum magistrum S. Iacobi Compostellani fratres, cum aliis primoribus supra 100. & equitibus clarissimis vltra 200. praelio nauali ceperūt: quos ad se perductos humanissimè excepit: ac multis donatos muneribus dimisit: cum illorum regnū ac ditionem totam sibi vindicare, aut occupare facile potuerit. Tandem foedissima libidine insaniuit, & mutata fortuna, nulla relicta virili prole, obiit ventris profluuio anno salutis 1447. Vide Paul. Ioui. & Supplem. Chro. lib. 14.
units.tr: PHILIP MARIA, after his brother John, mentioned above, was cut down, recovered by arms the paternal duchy of Milan, I say, in the year of the world 5379, from the birth of Christ 1417. Crafty in war, he seemed to seek war in peace. He was always eager to learn, cunning, shrewd, generous, most ready to remit injuries, tall of stature, formidable of countenance; by mature counsel, skill and very strong arms he removed the tyrants who had seized the cities of his dominion. He recovered Como, Trezzo, Bergamo, Brescia, Piacenza and Lodi, and also subdued Cremona. John James, Marquis of Monferrato, fearing his power, voluntarily restored Vercelli, Alessandria and Asti to Philip. Besides, he added to his dominion the maritime city of Genoa, a most powerful city. The Genoese, thus subdued and his subjects, were captured in a naval battle, together with Alfonso, King of Naples, and John, King of Navarre, and the brothers of the Grand Master of St James of Compostela, and more than 100 other nobles and over 200 most distinguished knights. He received them most courteously when they were brought before him, and dismissed them loaded with many gifts, although he could easily have claimed for himself, or seized, their kingdoms and their whole dominion. At last he went mad with the most shameful lust, and, his fortune changed, died of a flux of the bowels in the year of salvation 1447, leaving no male offspring. See Paulus Jovius and the Supplementum Chronicorum, book 14.

units.la: BEATRICINA, antea Facini Canis vxor, iam vetula, nupsit praedicto Philippo, & numerauit dotē aureorū 400000. hanc postea vt suspectam interfecit. Deinde Mariam Amidei Sabaudiae Ducis filiam in coniugem ductam, praeuentus morte, intactam dimisit. Vide autores quos supra. MAHVS.R. AMVR[?] TVR[?] DVX EPIRI ALB. SCANDERBERGVS
units.tr: BEATRICE, formerly the wife of Facino Cane, now an old woman, married the aforesaid Philip and paid a dowry of 400,000 gold pieces; afterwards, as suspect, he had her killed. Then, having been taken by death, he left unharmed Maria, daughter of Amadeus, Duke of Savoy, whom he had taken as his wife. See the authors cited above. MAHOMET, Emperor... AMURATH... Duke of Epirus; ALBANIAN SCANDERBEG.

units.la: AMVRATHES, hoc nomine secundus, Mahometis supradicti filius, patri in Turcarum imperio succedit anno mundi 5378. à Christo nato 1414. Hic cognita patris morte, ex Asia in Thraciam cupiens traiicere, Mustapham patruum cui Græci fauebant, auxiliúmque ferebant, fundit, ac delet. Primus pro tuitione corporis, Ianizaros, Christũ abnegantes, instituit, quorum viribus & ipse, & qui ipsi succedere, totum pene debellarunt Orientem. Is Hungariam, Bosinam, Albaniam, Valachiam & Græciam infestauit: Venetis Thessalonicam ademit. Ladislaum Poloniæ Regem, & Iulianum Cardinalem, ac Huniadem vicit. Regnat annos 34. Vide Riche. lib.1. Paul. Iou. & Cosm.Munst. lib.4.
units.tr: AMURATH, the second of this name, son of the aforesaid Mahomet, succeeds his father in the Turkish empire in the year of the world 5378, from the birth of Christ 1414. When he learned of his father's death, desiring to cross from Asia into Thrace, he routed and destroyed Mustapha, his uncle, whom the Greeks favoured and aided. He was the first to institute the Janissaries, who renounced Christ, for the protection of his person; by their strength both he himself and those who succeeded him subdued almost the whole East. He harassed Hungary, Bosnia, Albania, Wallachia and Greece; he took Thessalonica from the Venetians. He defeated Ladislaus, King of Poland, Cardinal Julian, and Hunyadi. He reigned 34 years. See Richer, book 1, Paulus Jovius and Cosmographia Münster, book 4.

units.la: SCANDERBEGVS, siue Scanderbechus, sic dictus à Turcis inter circuncidendum: antea enim vocabatur Georgius Castriotus, is inquam à patre, Epiri atque Albaniæ, seu Macedoniæ, principe, datur obses Amurathi Turcarum Regi septimo: qui eum tandem post multa egregia facinora, expeditioni, quam aduersus Hungaros parabat, præficit: porrò ad hos cùm res malè Turcis cederet, desciscit Scanderbegus, atque à secretario Bassa literas ad Croiæ magistratus extorquet, in quibus nomine Amurathis, ciuitas ac præfectura sibi tradatur. sic Croiam patriam recipit circiter annum mundi 5409. à Christo nato 1447. Cæterum Amurathes Epirum cum ingenti exercitu repetit: at Croia frustra per aliquot menses oppugnata, mœrore animi obiit. Vide vt supra. & Marinum Barletium lib.1. CAROLVS REX FRA. VII. LVDOVICVS XI. FRAN. REX
units.tr: SCANDERBEG, or Scanderbeg, so called by the Turks at his circumcision; before that he was called George Castriot. He was given as hostage to Amurath, the seventh Turkish king, by his father, the prince of Epirus and Albania, or Macedonia. After many distinguished exploits, Amurath at last put him in command of the expedition he was preparing against the Hungarians. Then, when matters went badly for the Turks on that front, Scanderbeg revolted, and from the Pasha's secretary he extorted letters to the magistrates of Croia, in which, in Amurath's name, the city and its government were handed over to him. Thus he recovered his homeland Croia in about the year of the world 5409, from the birth of Christ 1447. Meanwhile Amurath led a great army back into Epirus, but Croia, besieged in vain for some months, he died of grief. See as above, and Marinus Barletius, book 1.

units.la: CAROLVS huius nominis septimus Francorum Rex, vnicus Caroli sexti filius, patri in regno succedit anno mundi 5384. à Christo nato 1422. Tunc regnum Francicum turbulentissimum fuit, nam Anglorum Burgundionúmque bello petitus Carolus, omnibus pene regni finibus amissis, ad Bituricen-ses se contulit, apud quos mansit: quare ab hoste Bituricensium Rex per iocum dictus est. Henricus sororis Caroli filius inter titulos, Angliæ, Franciæq; Regem se scribebat: qui etiam Parisiis in Franciæ Regem coronatus est. Ioanna puella, armis instructa, militis subit munus: obsessos Aurelianenses iuuat, hostes cogit obsidionem soluere: per loca ab hostibus occupata Regem Carolum Remis consecrandum ducit, multásque in itinere vrbes recipit: tandem ab hostibus capta, Rothomagi exuritur. Lutetia Francorum Armis Angli pelluntur. Pragmatica sanctio in concilio Basilienfi ædita, à Rege probatur, & in Senatu Lutetiæ promulgatur. Vniuersam Normaniam Carolus recuperat: Angli expulsi, præter Calitium & vicina aliquot loca nil in Gallia possident. Delphinus secundò à patre deficit, aduersus quem pater bellum mouet, & spoliatum rebus omnibus, ne à quoquam excipiatur inhibet: porrò ad Burgundiæ Ducem ille profugit. Regnat Carolus an.38. Vide Gaguin.li.9. & 10.& Æmy.lib.10.
units.tr: CHARLES VII, King of the French, the only son of Charles VI, succeeds his father in the kingdom in the year of the world 5384, from the birth of Christ 1422. The French kingdom was then most turbulent, for Charles, assailed by the English and the Burgundians, having lost almost all the borders of the kingdom, withdrew to the people of Bourges, among whom he stayed; hence, by way of jest, he was called the King of Bourges by his enemies. Henry, son of Charles's sister, styled himself among his titles King of England and France, and was crowned King of France at Paris. Joan the Maid, equipped with arms, took up the office of a soldier; she aided the besieged people of Orléans and forced the enemies to lift the siege; through regions occupied by the enemy she led King Charles to Reims to be consecrated, and she recovered many cities on the way. At last, taken by the enemy, she was burned at Rouen. The English were driven out of Paris by French arms. The Pragmatic Sanction, issued at the Council of Basel, was approved by the King and promulgated in the Parliament at Paris. Charles recovered all Normandy; the English, expelled, hold nothing in France except Calais and a few neighbouring places. The Dauphin revolted from his father a second time, against whom the father made war, and, stripping him of all his possessions, forbade anyone to receive him; he then fled to the Duke of Burgundy. Charles reigned 38 years. See Gaguin, books 9 and 10, and Aemilius, book 10.

units.la: LVDOVICVS Caroli septimi filius, apud Burgundiones agens, nuntio paternæ mortis accepto, in Galliam cõfestim transit, ac Francorum Rex creatur anno mundi 5422. à Christo nato 1460. Bellum geritur, bonum publicum, vulgò dictum, de quo fusissimè tractat Philippus Cominius, & syncerissimè: nam huic bello interfuit. Regat Ludo.an.23. IMP. IOANNES MANVS VII. CONST. IMP. CONSTANTI
units.tr: LOUIS, son of Charles VII, while staying among the Burgundians, on receiving news of his father's death, at once crossed into France and was created King of the French in the year of the world 5422, from the birth of Christ 1460. The war called the "public good" was waged, which Philippe de Commynes treats at great length and most sincerely, for he was present at this war. He reigned 23 years. IMPERATOR JOHN MANUEL VII, CONSTANTINE IMPERATOR CONSTANTINE.

units.la: IO ANNES, Manuelis Palæologi filij, filius natu maior, post mortem patris in imperio succedit Constantinopolitano, circiter annum mundi 5395. à Christo nato 1433. Paci hic ac concordiæ magis quàm bello studens,comitatus totius Græcię comitibus, cùm sacris, tum profanis , atque Eugenij huius nominis quarti Pontificis autoritatem sccutus[?], Ferrariensi, quod deinde Florentiam translatum est, concilio interfuit : susceptúsque est ab Eugenio Imperatorum more: atque ex duabus, nempe Græcorum ac Latinorum Ecclesiis, una facta est. Tunc à Græcis ac Latinis de processione Spiritus sancti damnatus est error.Reversus Imperator,haud ita diu supervixit. Vide Egna. lib.2.& Cosmog.Munst.lib.4.Plati.& Volater.
units.tr: JOHN, the elder son of Manuel Palaeologus, succeeds his father in the Constantinopolitan empire after his death, about the year of the world 5395, from the birth of Christ 1433. Studying peace and harmony rather than war, he, accompanied by all the counts of Greece, both ecclesiastical and lay, and following the authority of Pope Eugenius IV, took part in the Council of Ferrara, which was afterwards transferred to Florence. He was received by Eugenius in the manner of emperors, and from the two churches, namely of the Greeks and of the Latins, one was made. Then the error concerning the procession of the Holy Spirit was condemned by the Greeks and Latins. The Emperor, on his return, did not survive long. See Egnatius, book 2, and Cosmographia Münster, book 4, Platina and Volaterranus.

units.la: CONSTANTINVS, septimus Manuelis filius, mortuo sine liberis fratre Ioanne supradicto, Constantinopoli imperat, circiter annum mundi 5406. à Christo nato 1447. hic ab initio Peloponnesi Rex,Draconis cognomen inditum accepit, ob eam quam in Turcas exercebat ferocitatem. At verò à Mahomete Amurathis secundi filio capta Constantinopoli, ipse Constantinus ad portam trepidus se recipiens,fugientium trepidatione oppressus obiit:cuius caput pilo affixum,totis castris ad ludibrium hostis gestauit: anno mundi 5414. à Christo nato 1452. Id mirum , atque in fatis quasi habendum , nempe quòd à Constantino Magno Helenæ filio Constantinopolis, urbs Romæ semper æmula, condita aut instaurata sit, ac sub Constantino, qui eiusdem nominis matrem haberet, capta, Turcarúmque iugo ad hanc diem sit subdita. Vide ut supra. DVX KAROLVS BVRGVNDIVS BARTHOL·CAR[?] LEO·MA·CL[?]·SE[?]
units.tr: CONSTANTINE, the seventh son of Manuel, after his brother John, mentioned above, died without children, reigns at Constantinople about the year of the world 5406, from the birth of Christ 1447. At first he was king of the Peloponnese, and received the surname Draco, because of the ferocity he showed against the Turks. But when Constantinople was taken by Mahomet, son of Amurath the Second, Constantine himself, retreating in alarm to the gate, was overwhelmed by the panic of those fleeing and died; his head, fixed on a pike, was carried through the whole camp to the mockery of the enemy, in the year of the world 5414, from the birth of Christ 1452. This is remarkable, and to be counted almost among the fates: that Constantinople, a city always a rival of Rome, was founded or restored by Constantine the Great, son of Helena, and that under a Constantine, who had a mother of the same name, it was taken and to this day has been subjected to the Turkish yoke. See as above.

units.la: CAROLVS, Philippi Burgundiæ Ducis filius, patri succedens, bellicosus ac strenuus, bellum gesit aduersus Ludovicum Francorum Regem, huius nominis vndecimum, cum quo postea fœdere inito, in Leodienses bellum mouit, quos & debellauit. Nouesium quod alij Nusiam vocant, agri Coloniensis oppidum, diu obsedit, hoc est annum integrum. Huc autem maximè spectabat Carolus, vt imperio Diocesim Coloniensem adimeret: aduersus hunc expeditionem parat Fridericus Imperator: Tandem fœdus hac conditione ineunt, vt Maximilianus Friderici filius, Mariam Caroli Ducis filiam vnicam, in vxorem accipiat. Pugnauit Carolus semel atque iterum, infeliciter quidem, cum Heluetiis. Cæterum ad Nansen contra Argentinensium Heluetiorúmque auxiliares copias dimicans, à Renato Lotaringo victus miserè occubuit, anno mundi 5437. à Christo nato 1475. Hic antequam pater moreretur, bellum etiam Gandauis intulerat. Vide Chron. Philippi Cominij, & rerum memorabilium Paraleipomena.
units.tr: Charles, son of Philip Duke of Burgundy, succeeded his father. He was warlike and vigorous. He waged war against Louis, King of the Franks, the eleventh of that name; after forming an alliance with him, he then made war on the people of Liège, whom he also defeated. He besieged for a whole year the town of Neuss, which others call Nusia, a town in the territory of Cologne. Charles aimed especially at this: to take the diocese of Cologne away from the Empire. Against him the Emperor Frederick prepared an expedition. At last they concluded an alliance on this condition: that Maximilian, son of Frederick, should take Mary, the only daughter of Duke Charles, as his wife. Charles fought once and again with the Swiss, though unsuccessfully. Moreover, fighting at Nancy against the auxiliary forces of Strasbourg and the Swiss, he was defeated by René of Lorraine and miserably fell, in the year of the world 5437, from the birth of Christ 1475. Before his father died he had also made war on Ghent. See the Chronicle of Philippe de Commynes, and the Paraleipomena of Memorable Things.

units.la: BARTOLOMÆVS Coglio siue Coleo, Bergoma, clarissima ortus familia, Dux exercitus Venetorum creatus est, atque à Carolo Duce Burgundionum supradicto, & Ioanne Andegauensi Duce, per priuilegia autentica in familiis eorum ascriptus. Hic bellicis artibus instructus, consilio item, prudentia, ac humanitate maximè pollebat: huius etiam aulæ amplitudo, pompa & gloria, omnium ferè principum aulas æquabat. Videto Supplementum Chronicorum lib.16.
units.tr: Bartolomeo Coglio or Coleo, born of Bergamo, from a most distinguished family, was created commander of the army of the Venetians, and was enrolled among their families by authentic privileges from Charles Duke of the Burgundians, mentioned above, and John Duke of Anjou. He was equipped with the arts of war, and was especially outstanding in counsel, prudence and affability as well. The magnificence, splendour and glory of his court also rivalled the courts of nearly all the princes. See the Supplement of the Chronicles, book 16.

units.la: CALIXTVS Papa huius nominis secundus, in Pontificem eligitur post Gelasium huius nominis secundum, anno mundi 5080. à Christo nato 1118. fuit hic natione Burgundus, frater Ducis Burgundiæ, prius Archiepiscopus Viénensis, divinarum scripturarum peritissimus, nec ab humanioribus literis abhorrens. Sanctum Iacobum Apostolum coluit: in cuius honorem Compostellanam ecclesiam in Archiepiscopatum erexit. Videto Trithemium. præfuit Ecclesiæ in summo Pontificatu annos ferè sex.
units.tr: Calixtus II, the second of that name, was elected Pope after Gelasius II, in the year of the world 5080, from the birth of Christ 1118. He was by birth a Burgundian, brother of the Duke of Burgundy, formerly Archbishop of Vienne, most skilled in the divine Scriptures, and not averse to the humane letters. He honoured the Apostle St James, in whose honour he raised the church of Compostela to an archbishopric. See Trithemius. He presided over the Church as supreme pontiff for nearly six years.

units.la: PIVS, huius nominis Papa secundus, creatur Pontifex anno mundi 5419. à Christo nato 1457. Hic Æneas Syluius antea vocatus, natione Tuscus, patria Senensis, vir undecunque doctissimus, Philosophus, Orator, & Poëta insignis, multa doctrinæ ac ingenij sui monimenta posteris reliquit. In concilio Basiliensi Prælato cuidam minister fuit: deinde in Scribā Cancellariæ Friderici Imperatoris, huius nominis tertij, assumptus, & Poëta ab eo, Laurea recepta creatus, primò Episcopus, postea Cardinalis, tandem Papa omnium suffragio electus est. Obiit Anconæ, Friderico, huius nominis tertio, imperante. Videto ut supra. Pontificatum gesit annos sex. PAVLVS 2 PONM 223 [?] P. M. SAC. CV [?] IIII. [?] SALXIS [?]
units.tr: Pius II, the second of that name, was created pontiff in the year of the world 5419, from the birth of Christ 1457.
