He was formerly called Aeneas Silvius, a Tuscan by nation, from the country of Siena, a man learned in every respect, a philosopher, orator, and distinguished poet, who left many monuments of his learning and genius to posterity. At the Council of Basel he served a certain prelate as secretary; then he was taken on as secretary of the chancery of the Emperor Frederick III, and was created poet by him, having received the laurel; first he became bishop, afterwards cardinal, and at last was elected pope by the vote of all. He died at Ancona while Frederick III was emperor. See above. He held the pontificate for six years.

units.la: PAVLVS, hoc nomine Papa secundus, Pio supradicto in Pontificatu successit, anno mundi 5425. à Christo nato 1463. Hic Petrus Barbarus antea dictus, Eugenij huius nominis quarti Pontificis ex sorore nepos, sedit annis ferè 7. corpore fuit amplo, & maiestatis Pontificiæ digno. Duo bella toto suo Pontificatu in Italia suscepit.Robertum Sigismundi Malatestę filium aggressus est. Cæterum pauperum curam gessisse perhibetur, imperiosus tamen ac fastu plenus cùm esset, odiosus omnibus fuit. Eius prima cura fuit, ut quæ victui essent necessaria, urbi non deessent. Die quadam cùm iucundissimè coenasset, apoplexia correptus obiit. Vide Chronicorum Supplementum.
units.tr: Paul II, the second Pope of this name, succeeded Pius in the pontificate above, in the year of the world 5425, from the birth of Christ 1463. Formerly called Pietro Barbo, he was nephew by his sister of Eugene IV, the fourth pontiff of that name. He reigned for nearly seven years. He was of ample body and worthy of the majesty of the pontificate. During his whole pontificate he undertook two wars in Italy, attacking Robert, son of Sigismondo Malatesta. Moreover, he is said to have taken care of the poor; yet, since he was imperious and full of pride, he was hated by all. His first concern was that the things necessary for living should not be lacking in the city. One day, after dining most pleasantly, he was seized by apoplexy and died. See the Supplement of the Chronicles.

units.la: SIXTVS huius nominis Papa quartus in locum Pauli supradicti suffectus est, Pontificarumque obtinuit anno mundi 5432. à Christo nato 1470. Hic natione Ligur, ordinis Minorum generalis antea minister,sedit annis tredecim.Hic cùm alioqui fuisset vitæ pientissimæ, ac in pauperes & religiosos munificentissimus,attamen suos nimis amavit,eis diuina & humana contribuens,id est ecclesiastica & temporalia bona,præter Dei & Romanæ Ecclesiæ dignitatem ac honestatem: & quædam bella iudicio multorum præter æquum suscepit: imprimis contra Laurentium Medicen, & Florentinos, quibus multa damna intulit: & contra Ferdinandum Apuliæ Regem, dein contra Venetos. Tandem febre correptus, cùm audisset fœdus ictum inter Venetos & reliquos principes, expirauit. Hic festa seraphici Francisci, conceptionis & præsentationis D.Mariæ,& S.Annæ & Ioseph celebrari iussit. Vide ut supra. ALEXANDER TARTAGNVS ANDREAS BARBATIVS[?]
units.tr: Sixtus IV, the fourth Pope of this name, was appointed in place of Paul above, and obtained the pontificate in the year of the world 5432, from the birth of Christ 1470. He was by nation a Ligurian, formerly minister general of the Order of the Minors. He reigned thirteen years. Although otherwise he was of most devout life and most generous towards the poor and the religious, yet he loved his own relatives too much, bestowing on them divine and human things, that is, ecclesiastical and temporal goods, beyond the dignity and honour of God and of the Roman Church. And he undertook certain wars beyond what was just in the judgement of many: especially against Lorenzo de' Medici and the Florentines, to whom he inflicted many losses, and against Ferdinand, King of Apulia, and afterwards against the Venetians. At last, seized by fever, when he heard that a league had been struck between the Venetians and the other princes, he expired. He ordered that the feasts of the seraphic Francis, of the Conception and Presentation of the Blessed Mary, and of St Anne and Joseph be celebrated. See above.

units.la: ALEXANDER Targinus de Imola, siue Imolensis, Iureconsultus doctissimus claruit temporibus Friderici Imperatoris huius nominis tertij, & Sixti Papæ, huius nominis quarti, de quibus supra mentionem fecimus. Hic Alexander, in usum eorum qui iurisperitiæ operam dant aliquot libros conscripsit, quos nominatim descriptos habes apud Ioannē Trithemium.
units.tr: Alexander Tartagnus of Imola, or the Imolese, a most learned jurist, flourished in the times of the Emperor Frederick III and of Pope Sixtus IV, of whom we have made mention above. This Alexander wrote several books for the use of those who study law, which you will find listed by name in John Trithemius.

units.la: ANDREAS Barbatias legum peritissimus, multa præclara in iure edidit opuscula, quorum nomenclaturam pores[?] etiam apud Trithemium legere. FRIDERICVS III ROM. IMP. LEONORA IMP. FRIDERICI III. UXOR.
units.tr: Andreas Barbatius, most skilled in the laws, published many excellent little works on law, the list of which you may also read in Trithemius. Frederick III, Roman Emperor; Leonora, wife of Emperor Frederick III.

units.la: FRIDERICVS Austriæ Dux, post Albertum imperat anno mundi 5401. à Christo nato 1439. hic pacis atque otij studiosissimus fuit: seditionem mouentes Austriacos facilè compescuit. bellum à Matthia Pannoniæ inferioris Rege illatum, composuit: in Flandros mouẽs, qui filium Maximilianum ceperant, & asseruabant, recepto filio paucorum pœna contentus, omnem discordiarum fomitem sustulit. Romæ unà cum uxore Heleonora, siue Leonora, Lusitani Regis filia, coronatus, inde Neapolim ad Alphonsum uxoris necessarium ac sanguine cognatum, diuertit, à quo, & ab ipsis postea Venetis, summo honore, & apparatu excipitur. Iterum Romam voti reus petit, priuati more, atque humili veste indutus: quo voto damnatus ad suos redit: & quiescente Germania, moritur anno imperij 53. Maximiliano prius Cæsare designato. Vide Baptistam Egnatium, Romanorum principum lib.3.
units.tr: Frederick, Duke of Austria, reigned after Albert, in the year of the world 5401, from the birth of Christ 1439. He was most devoted to peace and leisure. He easily suppressed the Austrians who stirred up sedition. He settled the war waged against him by Matthias, King of Lower Pannonia. Moving against the Flemings, who had captured his son Maximilian and were insisting on it, when the son was recovered, he was content with the punishment of a few, and removed every source of discord. At Rome, crowned together with his wife Eleonora, or Leonora, daughter of the King of Portugal, he then went on to Naples to his wife's kinsman and blood relation Alfonso, by whom, and afterwards by the Venetians themselves, he was received with the highest honour and display. Again he went to Rome as one bound by a vow, dressed in the manner of a private person and in humble garb; condemned by this vow, he returned to his own people, and while Germany was at rest he died, in the 53rd year of his reign, with Maximilian having been previously designated Caesar. See Baptista Egnatius, Lives of the Roman Princes, book 3.

units.la: HELEONORA, siue Leonora, supradicta, Lusitaniæ Regis filia, uxórque Friderici Imperatoris, Romæ cum marito Imperij corona insignitur anno mundi 5412. à Christo nato 1450: Ex hac Maximilianum, qui postea imperat, sustulit Fridericus. Vide Egnatium ad calcem libri tertij, in Friderici Imperatoris supradicti vita. RENATVS APVRE[?] IOANNES D. CALABER
units.tr: Eleonora, or Leonora, mentioned above, daughter of the King of Portugal and wife of Emperor Frederick, was crowned with the imperial crown at Rome with her husband, in the year of the world 5412, from the birth of Christ 1450. By her Frederick had Maximilian, who afterwards reigned. See Egnatius at the end of book 3, in the life of the Emperor Frederick mentioned above.

units.la: RENATVS Lotaringiæ Dux, Apuliæ Regis ex filia nepos, à Venetis solicitatus spe regni Apuliæ obtinendi, quod sibi hæreditate materna debebatur, Venetias iuit. Fœdere cum Venetis percusso, in Ferrariensem agrum bellum mouet, atque urbis ipsius, Ferrariæ inquam, oppugnationem adgreditur. Verùm ab Alphonso Aragonum Rege fortiter pulsus, cum exercitum viribus eneruari, ac se ob aëris intemperiem mala valetudine affici sentiret, inglorius in patriâ rediit, circiter annum à mundo condito 5404. à Christi natiuitate 1442. hunc perhibent fuisse probitatis eximiæ principem, nec à maioribus degenerasse, qui verè pij, & synceræ fidei cultores semper sunt habiti. Videto Supplem. Chronicorum lib.16.
units.tr: René, Duke of Lorraine, grandson through his daughter of the King of Apulia, was urged by the Venetians with the hope of obtaining the kingdom of Apulia, which was owed to him by maternal inheritance. He went to Venice. After an alliance was struck with the Venetians, he began war on the territory of Ferrara and undertook the siege of that city, Ferrara I mean. But he was vigorously driven off by Alfonso, King of Aragon, and, feeling that his army was weakened by strength and that he was suffering ill health from the unhealthiness of the air, he returned inglorious to his homeland, about the year 5404 from the foundation of the world, from the birth of Christ 1442. They report that he was a prince of outstanding integrity, and had not degenerated from his ancestors, who have always been considered true lovers of piety and sincere faith. See the Supplement of the Chronicles, book 16.

units.la: IOANNES, Calabriæ ac Lotaringiæ Dux, primogenitus Siciliæ Regis filius, magnanimus, bellicosus, & æquitatis amantissimus extitit. Videto ut supra. FRANCIS SFORTIA DVX [?] CŌ. D. MILIS GALEAZ MAVI [?]
units.tr: John, Duke of Calabria and of Lorraine, first-born son of the King of Sicily, was magnanimous, warlike, and a great lover of justice. See above.

units.la: FRANCISCVS Sforza, Sforzæ à Cutiniola filius, Philippi Marię Vicecomitis gener, ab eodē adoptatus est, &angue[?], insigni familiæ donatus, anno salutis 1430. socero defuncto, proximo statim anno, ob singularem virtutem Mediolani principatum adeptus est. Hic Sforzæ cognomen à Sforza patre bellicofo traxit: qui humilis & abiectus, cum se militiæ tradidiffer, per vim ab aliis quicquid cuperet extorquebat, sicque Sforzæ cognomen assecutus, vt proprium nomen semper postea habuit, & ad posteros cognomen trānsmisit. Hic per cunctos gradus, ad summum militiæ culmen conscendit. Contra Eugenium Papam, contra Florentinos, Venetos, Mediolanenses, non semel victor, Guelforum, ac Gibellinorum nomen ferè è medio tulit, Italiæ vniuersæ propemodum factus terror. Composita cum Venetis pace, multæ Italiæ ciuitates eius exēpla secutæ, arma deposuere. Intus forisque pacatis omnibus, à fundamentis denuò erexit castrū Mediolani, quod Iouis dicitur, à populo antea dirutum. Magnum illud hospitale, ægrotis recipiendis, ædificauit, quod regali censu ditauit, opus in orbe rarum. Vt diui Ambr. têplum erigeret, multum auri expendit. Tandem verò hic tantus vir, adeò libidine exarsit, vt adolescentum flagitia superarit. rexit an. 16. obiit, sex filiis duabúsque filiabus relictis, anno salutis 1466. Vide Supplem.lib.15. & Archie. Antonium.
units.tr: Francis Sforza, son of Sforza by Cutiniola, was son-in-law of Philip Maria Visconti, and was adopted by him, and, the (?) family being distinguished, in the year of salvation 1430, after his father-in-law's death, in the very next year, on account of his singular virtue, obtained the principality of Milan. He took the surname Sforza from his warlike father Sforza, who, being humble and abject, when he had given himself to soldiering, extorted by force whatever he desired from others; and thus having acquired the surname Sforza, he afterwards always had it as his proper name, and passed the surname on to posterity. He climbed through every rank to the highest summit of military command. Against Pope Eugene, against the Florentines, the Venetians and the Milanese, he was victor more than once, and almost wiped out the names of Guelfs and Ghibellines, becoming the terror of almost all Italy. When peace was made with the Venetians, many cities of Italy followed his example and laid down their arms. With everything at peace at home and abroad, he rebuilt from the foundations the castle of Milan which is called of Jove, which the people had earlier torn down. He built that great hospital for receiving the sick, which he endowed with royal revenue, a work rare in the world. To erect the church of St Ambrose he spent much gold. But at last this so great man burned so greatly with lust that he surpassed the shameful acts of young men. He reigned sixteen years and died in the year of salvation 1466, leaving six sons and two daughters. See the Supplement, book 15, and Antonius of Archiepiscopal ...

units.la: GALEATIVS Maria, Francisco Sforzæ patri defuncto, statim in Mediolani principatu succedit, pulsa matre quæ rem cum eo administrabat: multis hic se inquinauit flagitiis: quamobrem adulteriis, homicidiis, incestibus, sacrilegiisque pollutus anno administrationis 9. liberis 4. relictis, in æde Diui Stephani vulneribus est confossus. Vide Supplem.Chron. IVTVRC. IMP. [?] MAHOMETES
units.tr: GALEATIUS Maria succeeded immediately to the principality of Milan on the death of his father Francesco Sforza, the mother who had been governing jointly with him having been driven out. He defiled himself here with many crimes; and so, stained with adulteries, murders, incests and sacrileges, in the ninth year of his rule, leaving four children, he was stabbed with wounds in the church of St Stephen. See the Supplement of the Chronicles. TURKISH EMPEROR [?] MAHOMET

units.la: MAHOMETES, hoc nomine secundus, Turcarũ verò Rex octauus, Amurathi, etiam huius nominis secūdo, succedit anno mundi 5411. à Christo nato 1449. Hic regnum à parricidio auspicatur. fratrem paruulum, ne pater solus sepeliretur, opera Mosis interficit. Impiissimus nullum Deum credidit: Mahometem suum, Pseudoprophetam sui similem dixit: Prophetas ac Patriarchas risit, ac nugas duxit: huic tametsi impio, fauit aliquando fortuna. Nam magni cognomentum Othomannicæ familiæ quæsiuit. Duo Christianorum imperia Constantinopolitanum & Trapezuntinum subuertit: regna 12. ademit: ducentas urbes Christianas cepit: Ipse colico dolore correptus, quarto demum die moritur, anno ætatis 58. regni 31. Richer. lib. 4. Paul. Iou. Egna. lib. 2. Cosm. Munst. lib. 4.
units.tr: MAHOMET, the second of that name, and eighth Sultan of the Turks, succeeded Murad, likewise the second of that name, in the year of the world 5411, from the birth of Christ 1449. He began his reign with a parricide: he had his infant brother put to death by Moses' agency, so that his father would not be buried alone. Most impious, he believed in no God; he called Mahomet, his pseudo-prophet, a man like himself; he mocked the prophets and patriarchs and treated them as trifles. Fortune, though he was impious, sometimes favoured him: for he obtained the surname "the Great" for the Ottoman family. He overthrew the two Christian empires, that of Constantinople and that of Trebizond; he took away twelve kingdoms; he captured two hundred Christian cities. Himself seized by colic, he died on the fourth day, in the 58th year of his age and the 31st of his reign. See Richer, book 4; Paulus Jovius; Egnatius, book 2; Cosmas Münster, book 4.

units.la: BAIAZETES hoc nomine secundus, Mahometis supradicti filius Ianizarorū opera Turcis imperat anno mundi 5442. à Christo nato 1480. Hic minorem fratrem Zizimum, quem primores Imperatorem exposcebat, vincit ac fugat: qui à Rhodi praefecto ad Carolum octauum in Galliam mittitur. Porrò Baiazetes Caramanno fuso, quaecunque is cis & trans Taurum Turcis ademerat, recepit: Valachiam subegit: In Sultanum Ægyptium mouit: Sed is potentior, vtpote qui Mamaluchos, post Caramanni cædem fugitiuos exceperat, ac Arabum maximas copias ad sui tuitionem alebat, Baiazete sæpe debilitat, ac profligat: postea Cerauniorum montium accolas subdit. Venetis Methonem, nunc Modonem, Nepathum, olim Naupactum, & Dyrrachium ademit. Acomathem primogenitum decrepitus Baiazetes absentem in locū suum substituit: Sed, Ianizaris Zelimo suffragantibus, cogitur pater Zelimum pro Acomathe substituere. paulò post imperio deturbatus à filio Zelimo, ab eodē filio veneno necatur, anno regni 30. Vide ut supra. SIGIS. MAL. TE ROBER. MALATE NOTHVS [?]
units.tr: BAYAZID, the second of that name, son of the aforesaid Mahomet, reigned over the Turks by the agency of the Janissaries, in the year of the world 5442, from the birth of Christ 1480. He defeated and put to flight his younger brother Cem, whom the nobles demanded as emperor; Cem was sent by the governor of Rhodes to Charles VIII in France. Moreover, Bayazid, having routed the Karamanid, recovered whatever of the lands on this and that side of the Taurus he had lost to the Turks; he subdued Wallachia; he moved against the Egyptian Sultan. But that man was the stronger, since he had received the fugitive Mamluks after the slaughter of the Karamanid and maintained the very large forces of the Arabs for his own defence; he often weakened and crushed Bayazid. Afterwards Bayazid subjected the dwellers of the Ceraunian mountains. From the Venetians he took Methone, now Modon, Nepanto, formerly Naupactus, and Durazzo. Bayazid, decrepit, appointed his eldest son Ahmed as his successor in his place while Ahmed was absent; but, with the Janissaries supporting Selim, the father was forced to put Selim in place of Ahmed. Shortly afterwards, Bayazid was deposed by his son Selim, and was poisoned by that same son, in the thirtieth year of his reign. See above. SIGISMUND MALATESTA, TE ROBERTO MALATESTA NOTHUS [?]

units.la: SIGISMVNDVS Malatesta Arimini princeps, Pandulphi Malatestæ filius spurius, bellicosus admodum, splendidus & liberalis fuisse perhibetur: interim tamen multis flagitiis inquinatus turpi nota nomen suum inussit: ideoque diris & armis Pontificum obnoxius fuit. Hic tres duxit uxores, primam Crimignolæ comitis filiam, quam mortuo patre repudiauit: cum tamen dotem ex ea amplissimam percepisset: Secundam Nicolai Estensis, Ferrariæ principis filiam, generosam ac probam: hanc nihilominus paulo post veneno sustulit: tertiam Francisci Sfortiæ filiam, præclaram & modestam, quam tandem propriis etiam manibus, ut mensuram scelerum suorum impleret, apprehenso ac fortiter presso iugulo suffocauit. Vide Supplem. Chron. lib. 15.
units.tr: SIGISMUND Malatesta, prince of Rimini, the illegitimate son of Pandolfo Malatesta, is said to have been very warlike, splendid and generous; yet, meanwhile, stained by many crimes, he marked his name with a shameful stain, and for this reason he was exposed to the curses and arms of the Popes. He married three wives. The first was the daughter of the Count of Crimignola, whom he repudiated after her father's death, though he had received a very large dowry from her; the second was the daughter of Nicholas d'Este, prince of Ferrara, a noblewoman of good character, whom nevertheless he soon afterwards removed by poison; the third was the daughter of Francesco Sforza, an outstanding and modest woman, whom at last, so as to fill up the measure of his crimes, he seized by the throat with his own hands and, pressing hard, strangled. See the Supplement of the Chronicles, book 15.

units.la: ROBERTVS Malatesta Sigismundi filius, etiam nothus, patri in principatu Ariminensi succedit, anno mundi 5428. à Christo nato 1466.Fuit hic moribus patri dissimilis, belli etiam artibus, & præclaris rebus gestis ornatissimus. pro Venetis, sub quorum stipendiis diu militauit, varia mortis pericula adiit. Cum Galeatio Mediolanensium Duce, & Florentinis suas copias iunxit, & oppida omnia quæ Pontifex patri in Ariminensi agro ademerat recepit. Hic Alfonsum Calabriæ Ducem, alioqui fortissimum vicit, ac fugauit: quo in bello, præ ardore pugnæ nimio, in dysenteriam incidit, nec ita diu, hoc dolore correptus, superuixit. habuit in uxorem Elisabetam, Vrbini Ducis filiam. Vide ut supra. DVX MII[?] SP[?] IO GZ MAS SFORZ[?] M DVCES MELI[?] VI[?] BONA GZ[?]
units.tr: ROBERT Malatesta, son of Sigismund, likewise illegitimate, succeeded his father in the principality of Rimini, in the year of the world 5428, from the birth of Christ 1466. He was in his character unlike his father, and most distinguished in the arts of war and in brilliant deeds. He served for a long time under the pay of the Venetians, and faced many dangers of death. Together with Galeazzo, Duke of the Milanese, and the Florentines, he joined his forces and recovered all the towns which the Pope had taken from his father in the territory of Rimini. He defeated and put to flight Alfonso, Duke of Calabria, otherwise a most valiant man; in that war, through excessive ardour in battle, he fell into dysentery, and, seized by this illness, he survived not long. He had as his wife Elisabeth, daughter of the Duke of Urbino. See above. DUKE ... MILAN ... DUKES OF MILAN ... BONA ...

units.la: IO. MARIA, patre, ab Andrea à Lāpognano, interempto, à Senatu populóq; adhuc paruulus Mediolanensium Dux creatus est anno mundi 5438. à Christo nato 1476. Bonæ ipsius matri & consanguineis quibusdam, atque primoribus, regiminis cura commissa. Hic inter vivendum ac moriendum infelicissimus fuit. Nam tutores brevi Bonam à gubernatione repellunt: & Ludouicus patruus atque tutor, arte & astu principatum invadit, permittens adolescentem à virtutibus deflectere, & voluptatibus operam dare. Nec prius hic tantum suum malum advertit, quàm cùm morti esset vicinus, hausto iam veneno quod ei pararat patruus. Itaque hoc pacto, cum annos 26. mensésque 9. Ducem nomine tantùm egisset, inglorius diem clausit extremum, Francisco Sforza secundo, filio relicto, ex Isabella Ferdinaldi Neapolis Regis filia suscepto. Morti eius ac funebri pompæ Christianissimus Carolus Galliæ Rex, qui Neapolim tunc petebat, interfuit. Vide Supplem. lib.16. & Archie. Antoni.
units.tr: GIOVANNI MARIA, his father Andrea of Lampugnano having been killed, was created Duke of the Milanese by the Senate and people while still a little boy, in the year of the world 5438, from the birth of Christ 1476. The care of government was entrusted to his mother Bona and to certain of her relatives and nobles. He was most unhappy both in life and in death. For his guardians soon drove Bona from the government, and his uncle and guardian Ludovico seized the principality by craft and cunning, allowing the young man to turn aside from virtues and to devote himself to pleasures. Nor did he perceive his own misfortune until he was near death, the poison his uncle had prepared for him having already been drunk. And so, having held the title of Duke for only twenty-six years and nine months, he ended his last day without glory, leaving a son, Francesco Sforza II, born of Isabella, daughter of Ferdinand, King of Naples. The most Christian Charles, King of France, who was then heading for Naples, attended his death and funeral procession. See the Supplement, book 16, and Archidiaconus Antonius.

units.la: BONA, Sabaudiæ Ducis filia, inter omnes Heroides laudatissima, Galeatij Mariæ olim uxor, peperit illi quatuor liberos, duos mares, totidemque fœmellas. Hæc Io.Gal.Mariæ filio adhuc parvulo tutrix à viro moriente relicta, parùm admodùm in administratione perseveravit, à Ludouico Sforza, Mauro vocato, adolescentis patruo, & tutore deturbata, ac in ordinem redacta. Vide autores quos supra. FRANC·ACCOLTIVS AR. CEPOLA VER. BARTOLEMÆVS
units.tr: BONA, daughter of the Duke of Savoy, most praised among all heroines, formerly wife of Galeazzo Maria, bore him four children, two boys and as many girls. She, left by her dying husband as guardian of their son Gian Galeazzo Maria, still a little boy, persisted very little in the administration, and was driven out and reduced to the ranks by Ludovico Sforza, called Moro, the uncle and guardian of the young man. See the authors mentioned above. FRANCESCO ACCOLTI, ARETINO, CEPOLLA, VERONESE, BARTHOLOMEW

units.la: FRANCISCVS Aretinus Jurisconsultus excellens multa scripsit studiosis mirum in modum utilia, super Digesta, Codicem, & Decretales. Scripsit etiam Consilia, de Differentia inter sententiam interlocutoriam & definitiuam. Magnum nomen adeptus est per universam Italiam, præsertim in florentibus [?] Academiis, ut Patavi, Bononiæ, & aliis. Erat valde amatus à suis Discipulis, qui eum in quamuis Academiam migrantem, eius studio incensi, semper sequebantur, ut in Jure magis proficeret. Florebat anno salutis humanæ 1469. Vide Conradum Gesnerum, in sua Bibliotheca.
units.tr: FRANCIS of Arezzo, an excellent jurist, wrote many things wonderfully useful to students, on the Digest, the Code and the Decretals. He also wrote Consilia, on the difference between an interlocutory and a definitive sentence. He obtained a great name throughout all Italy, especially in the flourishing academies, such as Padua, Bologna and others. He was greatly loved by his pupils, who, zealous for his teaching, always followed him when he moved to whatever academy, so that they might make greater progress in law. He flourished in the year of human salvation 1469. See Conrad Gesner in his Bibliotheca.

units.la: BARTHOLOMEVS Cepolla Veronensis doctissimus Jurisconsultus fuit, numero celebriorum sui temporis ascriptus, maximè in practica Juris, ut videre licet ex magno volumine ab eo conscripto & hoc titulo nominato, Cautelæ causarum Ciuilium. Scripsit etiam volumen consilorum criminalium: Tractatum de seruitutibus: alium, De Ædilitio edicto, de Prædiis urbanis, De prædiis Rusticorum, De re militari, De furtis, De Imperatore militum, De simulatis Contractibus, & plures alios, si [?] per jus ciuile & criminale. Floruit anno salutis 1477. Vide Conradum Gesnerum, in sua Bibliotheca.
units.tr: BARTHOLOMEW Cepolla of Verona was a most learned jurist, counted among the more celebrated men of his time, chiefly in the practice of law, as may be seen from the large volume written by him and entitled Cautelae causarum civilium. He also wrote a volume of criminal consilia; a treatise on servitudes; another on the aedilician edict, on urban estates, on rural estates, on military matters, on thefts, on the commander of soldiers, on simulated contracts, and several others, both in civil and criminal law. He flourished in the year of salvation 1477. See Conrad Gesner in his Bibliotheca.

units.la: MARCILIVS Ficinus, Patria Florentinus diuinæ Philosophiæ amore incẽsus, Platonis vniuersum opus, maxima diligẽtia trástulit. Erat corpore admodũ pusillo, víxque semihominem æquare videbatur, sed tamen acuto ingenio erat pręditus, & vtriusq; linguæ admirabili facultate. Vnde Plotinũ, Iamblicũ, Synefium, & Psellum Platonicæ sectæ nobiles authores, Latinos effecit, hortante Cosmo Medice, & suffragantibus his qui Cosmo successerunt, à quibus, multis numeribus sese adauctũ & cumulatè ornatũ sensit. Fuit lætus & ad tuēda valetudinē exactus. Scripsit plures libros, qui feruntur Theologiæ naturalis lib. 1. de intelleƐtu & intelligentia lib.1. in conuiuiũ Platonis lib.1.Epistolarũ lib.plures, de triplici vita lib.tres, Apologiã, in qua agitur de Medicina & Astrologia, quod ad sacerdotes pertineant:&de vita mũdi, deque Magia & Magis, qui Christũ statim natũ salutarunt. Antidotũ Epidemiorũ & præseruatione secũdæ valetudinis, è Græco transtulit in Latinũ, lib. Xenocratis Platonici, de morte, Speusippi Alcinoi, & Pythagoræ opuscula traduxit, & multa alia. Claruit anno 1490. Tandem in Caregiana ipsius villa septuagenario prouectior febricula interiit.
units.tr: MARSILIO Ficino, a Florentine by birth, kindled with love of divine philosophy, translated the whole work of Plato with the greatest diligence. He was of very small body, and seemed scarcely to equal a half-man, yet he was endowed with a keen wit and an admirable facility in both languages. Hence he made Plotinus, Iamblichus, Synesius and Psellus, noble authors of the Platonic school, Latin, at the urging of Cosimo de' Medici, and with the support of those who succeeded Cosimo, by whom he felt himself advanced and richly honoured in many ways. He was cheerful and attentive to preserving his health. He wrote several books, which are cited: On Natural Theology, book 1; On the Intellect and the Intelligence, book 1; On the Symposium of Plato, book 1; Letters, several books; On the Triple Life, three books; an Apology, in which he treats of medicine and astrology, as they pertain to priests; and On the Life of the World, and on Magic and the Magi, who at once greeted Christ at his birth. He translated from Greek into Latin the Antidote against Epidemics and the Preservation of Second Health; he translated the work of Xenocrates the Platonist, On Death, the little works of Speusippus, Alcinous and Pythagoras, and many other things. He flourished in the year 1490. At last, in his villa at Careggi, having advanced to seventy years of age, he died of a slight fever.

units.la: ANGELVS Politianus à iuuentute admirabilis ingenij nomen adeptus est, quũ nouo, illustríque Poëmate Iuliani Medicis equestres ludos celebrasset, Luca Pulcio nobili Poëta omniũ cõfessione superato. Post edita Miscellaneorũ centuriã, publicatáq; Latina Poëmata, immatura mors eũ oppressit, vix qua dragefimũ quartũ ætatis annũ excedētē. Scripsit Epistolarũ lib. 12. miscellaneorũ centuriã 1. Transtulit in Latinã linguã Herodianũ historicũ, Enchiridion Epicteti, cum defensione ad Barthol. Scalam. Alexandri Aphrodisæi, super nonnullis Physicis dubitationibus, solutionum libr. 1. Plutarchi Chæronei amatorias narrationes: & multa alia, quæ excusa reperiuntur Lugduni apud Sebastianum Gryphium. Floruit circiter annum salutis humanæ 1483. MICHAELIS ANGELVS · FLORENTINVS · ANNAETATIS LXXV[?] RAPHAELIS · SANCTII · VRBINATIS
units.tr: ANGELO Poliziano, from his youth, obtained a name for admirable talent, when with a new and illustrious poem he celebrated the equestrian games of Giuliano de' Medici, Luca Pulci, a noble poet, being by general acknowledgement surpassed. After publishing a hundred Miscellanies and his Latin poems, an untimely death overtook him, scarcely exceeding the forty-fourth year of his age. He wrote twelve books of Letters; the first century of Miscellanies. He translated into Latin the historian Herodian, the Enchiridion of Epictetus, with a defence addressed to Bartholomew Scala; Alexander of Aphrodisias, on several physical problems, one book of Solutions; the Amatory Narratives of Plutarch of Chaeronea; and many other things, which are found printed at Lyon by Sebastian Gryphius. He flourished around the year of human salvation 1483. MICHAEL ANGELUS FLORENTINUS, IN HIS 75TH YEAR. RAPHAEL SANZIO OF URBINO

units.la: MICHAEL Angelus Florentinus Pictor maximé egregius,natus in Cosentino,anno Christi 1474. matre nobili & patre Ludouico Leonardo Buonarruoti ortus, quem quidē dicūt originē ducere è nobilissima & antiquissima familia Comitum ex Canossa.Hic Michael Angelus,puer,magnā de se parētibus & amicis expectationem dedit, quod semper videretur occupatus in his quæ ad pictūræ industriā spectarent. Reuera pictor omnium non solum suę ætatis, sed & eorum qui præcesserant, & post fuerunt consummatissimus & perfectissimus extitit, & stupendas picturas tam scitè designauit,vt spectantium oculos in earum admiratione traheret. Vixit satis senex,eiusque mortui omnium pictorum numerus ingens,amici, populusque ferè omnis, prosequutus est exequias.
units.tr: Michael Angelus of Florence, a most outstanding painter, was born in Caprese (in the Casentino) in the year of Christ 1474, to a noble mother and a father named Ludovico Leonardo Buonarroti. They say his family traces its origin to the most noble and ancient house of the Counts of Canossa. As a boy, Michael Angelus gave his parents and friends great hopes of himself, since he always seemed to be occupied with those things that pertain to the art of painting. Indeed he became the most accomplished and perfect of all painters, not only of his own age but of those who had gone before and those who came after, and he drew such astonishing pictures, so skilfully, that they drew the eyes of onlookers into admiration of them. He lived to a good old age, and when he died, a huge number of painters, friends, and almost the whole populace followed his funeral.

units.la: RAPHAEL Vrbinas pictor clarissimus,natus est in Vrbino ciuitate notissima in Italia, anno salutis humanæ 1483. Patrem habuit nomine Ioannem, pictorem quoque eum sed non admodū excellentem,qui tamen optimo fuit ingenio,curauitque vt Raphael à matre ipsa lactaretur,non ignarus, quantum materna educatio liberis prodesset, optimè temperata. Quam multis ingenij dotibus,hic Vrbinas fuerit ornatus, non opus est hic pluribus recensere, nullus est enim qui non sciat eum diuinis illius superioris Michaëlis Angeli vestigiis insistentem, in picturæ arte fuisse excellentem, multòsque longo post se interuallo, reliquisse. Obiit anno ætatis suæ 37. si plura quis desideret,videat eius & superioris vitam Italico idiomate à Georgio Vasari Italo pictore eleganter scriptam in libro cui titulus, est, Vite de pittori.
units.tr: Raphael of Urbino, a most famous painter, was born in Urbino, a city very well known in Italy, in the year of human salvation 1483. His father was named Giovanni, himself a painter, though not a very distinguished one, yet a man of excellent talent; he saw to it that Raphael was nursed by his own mother, knowing well how much a mother's careful upbringing benefits her children. There is no need to list here at length the many gifts of mind with which this man of Urbino was adorned; for there is no one who does not know that, treading in the footsteps of the divine Michael Angelo mentioned above, he excelled in the art of painting and left many far behind him at a long interval. He died in the thirty-seventh year of his age. If anyone wants more, let him see the life of both him and the earlier man, elegantly written in the Italian language by Giorgio Vasari, an Italian painter, in the book entitled Vite de pittori.

units.la: PICVS Mirandula Phœnix appellabatur, quòd in eum Dij superi supra familiæ claritatem omnis corporis, ac animi vel rarissima dona contulerint. Decorus fuit, moribus lectissimis, incomparabili facundia, qua omnes eius seculi sapientes in admirationem sui facilè conuertit. Astrologos insectatus est eo grauissimo opere, nec dum absoluto quo totius diuinationis vanitatem confutauit. Scripsit doctissimè de re Theologica, & Philosophia: huiusque opera sunt impressa Basileæ, vno volumine. Excessit è vita, trium & triginta annorum iuuenis, eo die quo Carolus Galliæ Rex Octauus, Napolim est ingressus, anno salutis 1483. Nepotem habuit Franciscum Picum Mirandulam, virum doctissimum, qui interfectus fuit cum Alberto filio, à Galeotto fratris filio.
units.tr: Pico of Mirandola was called the Phoenix, because the gods above bestowed on him, beyond the distinction of his family, the rarest gifts both of body and of mind. He was graceful, of most refined manners, and of incomparable eloquence, by which he easily turned all the wise men of his age to admiration of himself. He attacked the astrologers in that most weighty work, which he did not finish, in which he refuted the vanity of all divination. He wrote most learnedly on theology and philosophy, and his works have been printed at Basel in one volume. He departed this life at the age of thirty-three, a young man, on the very day on which Charles VIII, King of France, entered Naples, in the year of salvation 1483. He had a nephew, Francesco Pico of Mirandola, a most learned man, who was killed together with his son Alberto by Galeotto, the son of his brother.

units.la: GEORGIVS Agricola, insignis Medicus, propter eius magnam diuersamque eruditionem, dignus est adprimè qui eorum catalogo ascribatur, quorum memoria monumentis scriptisque est percelebris: quàm vt magis decoremus, eius figurâ nō noluimus hîc inserere. Conscripsit quinque libros, de pōderibus & mēsuris quinque alios, de pōderibus & mēsuris Romanorū & Græcorū: duos, de pōderibus & mēsuris exterarū nationum: tres, de pretio metallorum & monetarum: vnum, de animalibus subterraneis: duodecim, de re[?] metallica, in quibus ad amussim expressæ sunt imagines officiorū, instrumentorum, machinarum, omniumque aliarum rerum, quæ ad rem metallicam pertinent, lectu & memoria dignissimæ.
units.tr: Georgius Agricola, an distinguished physician, on account of his great and varied learning, is well worthy to be enrolled among those whose memory is most celebrated through monuments and writings; so that we may adorn him further, we did not wish to insert his portrait here. He wrote five books on weights and measures, another five on the weights and measures of the Romans and Greeks, two on the weights and measures of foreign nations, three on the price of metals and coins, one on underground animals, and twelve on metallurgy, in which images of the tasks, instruments, machines, and all other things pertaining to metallurgy are exactly portrayed, most worthy of being read and remembered.

units.la: INNOCENTIVS, huius nominis Papa octauus, Pontificatum obtinet anno mundi 5445. à Christo nato 1483. Hic patria Genuensis, in rebus gerendis prudens, magnanimus ac constans, merito Innocentius dictus est, ob morum sanctimoniam, sedit annis octo. Pluribus de hoc Innocentio tractat Iacobus Philippus Bergoma, qui eum, dum Cardinalis esset Innocentius, nouit, & cum eo aliquando verba fecit. Vide Supplem. Chron. lib. 16.
units.tr: Innocent, eighth pope of this name, obtained the pontificate in the year of the world 5445, from the birth of Christ 1483. He was a Genoese by birth, prudent in conducting affairs, magnanimous and steadfast, and was rightly called Innocent on account of the holiness of his morals. He sat for eight years. Jacobus Philippus of Bergamo, who knew Innocent when he was still a cardinal and once spoke with him, treats of this Innocent at greater length. See the Supplementum Chronicorum, book 16.

units.la: LAVRENTIVS Medices inter Florentiae nobiles & primores facile primus (tametsi non Princeps) summa prudentia, ac singulari virtute, omnia suo arbitrio, in patria administrauit. Angelus Politianus & Marsilius Ficinus, viri vndecunq; doctissimi, huius alumni fuere. Hic sapientissimus fuit, literarum, literatorumq; amantissimus, in quo probitas, iustitia, atque fides domicilium elegisse visae sunt. Praeterea fortis etiam atque magnanimus cum esset, pericula saepe a suorum ceruicibus bello propulsauit: nomen Thuscum ad barbaras gentes protulit, ampliata etiam ditione sua multis vrbibus ac oppidis. Quinetiam huic Reges atque respublicae, Sultanus denique ipse legatos & munera, tanquam alteri Octauio Caesari miserunt. Sixtus & Innocentius Pontifices hunc tanquam dilectissimum filium in pretio habuerunt. Hic in funere suo, ad aui Cosmae exemplum, nullam peragi pompam mandauit, quod & obseruatum est. Videto vt supra.
units.tr: Lorenzo de' Medici, easily the first among the nobles and leading men of Florence (though not its prince), governed his homeland in all things at his own discretion, with the greatest prudence and singular virtue. Angelo Poliziano and Marsilio Ficino, men most learned in every respect, were his protégés. He was a most wise man, a lover of letters and of men of letters, in whom uprightness, justice, and good faith seemed to have made their home. Moreover, since he was also brave and magnanimous, he often warded off dangers from his own people by war; he spread the name of Tuscany among barbarous nations, his dominion being enlarged with many cities and towns. Indeed, kings and commonwealths, and finally the Sultan himself, sent him ambassadors and gifts, as though to another Octavius Caesar. Popes Sixtus and Innocent held him in high esteem as their most beloved son. At his funeral, following the example of his grandfather Cosimo, he ordered that no solemn pomp be performed, and this was observed. See above.

units.la: CAROLVS, huius nominis octauus Fracorum Rex succedit patri Ludouico, anno mundi 5445. à Christo nato 1483. annum fere attingens 14. Hic bellum aduersus Britones mouit: ad fanum Aibini insignem de Britannis, seu Britonibus victoriam reportauit, vix liquidè dimidia pars exercitus aduersariorum superfuit. Rex religiosè nimis Hispano Regi Rufcinonis, & Perpiniani Comitatus reddidit. Regnum Neapolitanum recuperat, principibus & nobilibus militantibus suis sumptibus: Romæ à Papa Imperator Constantinopolitanus pronuntiatur. Alphonsus Portugalliæ Rex, cum filio Ferdinando in Siciliam fugit. Neapolim cum pompa, & triumpho ingreditur Rex. Vniuersi Italiæ principes & ciuitates coeunt vt obsessis itineribus Regem intercludat, qui nobilem & ingentem victoriā Fornouiensem reportans (cùm tamen perquàm modicas copias haberet) victor in Franciam rediit. Sed Neapolis ad Ferdinādū post annū defecit. Rex repentina morte obiit Amboesiæ, nullis relictis liberis, anno regni 14. sepultus est in æde Diui Dionysij ad Parisios. Vixit annos fere 27. porrò mortuus est, dum animi laxandi gratia ex ambulacro cum vxore pila ludentes aspicit. Vide Rober. Gaguin. lib. 10. & 11. & Paul. Aemyl. lib. 10. & vltimo. Latinè scire Carolum pater vetuerat, præter hoc vnū, Qui nescit simulare, nescit regnare. Collegium prostitutarum pœnitentium, hoc Rege, Lutetiæ instituitur: & conuentus trium ordinum in vrbe Turonum fit.
units.tr: Charles, eighth king of this name of the French, succeeded his father Louis in the year of the world 5445, from the birth of Christ 1483, being then almost fourteen years old. He waged war against the Bretons; at the famous shrine of Aibin he won a victory over the Britons, or Bretons, so that scarcely half of the enemy army survived. The king, too scrupulously religious, returned Roussillon and the county of Perpignan to the Spanish king. He recovered the kingdom of Naples, with his princes and nobles fighting at their own expense; at Rome the Emperor of Constantinople was proclaimed by the Pope. Alfonso, King of Portugal, fled to Sicily with his son Ferdinand. The king entered Naples with pomp and triumph. All the princes and cities of Italy came together to block the king by besieging the roads; but he, winning a noble and great victory at Fornovo (although he had very modest forces), returned victorious to France. However, Naples went over to Ferdinand a year later. The king died of a sudden death at Amboise, leaving no children, in the fourteenth year of his reign, and was buried in the church of St Denis near Paris. He lived about twenty-seven years; he died while, to relax his spirits, he was watching, from a gallery, his wife and others playing ball. See Robert Gaguin, books 10 and 11, and Paulus Aemilius, book 10 and the last. His father had forbidden Charles to learn Latin, except for this one saying: "He who does not know how to dissemble does not know how to reign." Under this king, a college of repentant prostitutes was founded at Paris, and a meeting of the three estates was held in the city of Tours.

units.la: ANNA, Francisci Britanniæ Ducis maior natu filia, patre mortuo nupsit Carolo octauo reconciliatis Britonibus, complurésque liberos ex eo peperit, quibus tamen omnibus superuixit pater. Cæterum repudiata Margareta Maximiliani Imperatoris filia, Annam hanc, prius eidem Maximiliano per legatum nuptam, in vxorē duxit Carolus octauus anno salutis 1489.
units.tr: Anne, the elder daughter of Francis, Duke of Brittany, on her father's death married Charles VIII, the Bretons having been reconciled; she bore him several children, though the father outlived all of them. Moreover, having repudiated Margaret, daughter of the Emperor Maximilian, Charles VIII married this Anne, who had earlier been wed to Maximilian himself by proxy, in the year of salvation 1489.

units.la: ALEXANDER, Papa huius nominis sextus, Pontifex creatur anno mundi 5453. à Christo nato 1491. Hic Calixti, huius nominis Papæ tertij, ex fratre nepos fuit, apud eum à puero educatus, atque institutus. Hunc valde terruit Francorum Rex Carolus, huius nominis octauus, quē postea acceptis conditionibus in vrbe excepit, parauitque ei palatiū Diui Martini: ipse verò Pōtifex timidus in arcem se recipit vsque in proximū diē: subiugata itaque à Carolo Roma, Papa, licet inuitus, eidem Carolo Turcarū Imperatoris fratre tradidit: atque Valentinum Cardinalem filiū (vt aiunt) obsidem dedit, vrbésque Neapolitano regno proximas. Hic etiam Carolo Neapoli redeūti, frustrà tetendit insidias, inito nouo fœdere cum Hispaniæ Rege, cum Venetis, ac cum Ludouico Sfortia, quorum ope fretus Regem Carolum in reditu intercludere tentabat Papa. Mortuo autem Carolo, pacem pepigit Papa cum Ludouico duodecimo, qui Carolo in regno Franciæ successit: sedit Alexander hic, annis vndecim. Vide Supple. Chro. lib. 15.
units.tr: Alexander, sixth pope of this name, was created pontiff in the year of the world 5453, from the birth of Christ 1491. He was a nephew, through his brother, of Callixtus III, and had been raised and educated by him from boyhood. King Charles VIII of France, eighth of this name, greatly terrified him; Alexander, afterwards receiving him on terms agreed, prepared for him the palace of St Martin. The Pope himself, fearful, withdrew into the castle until the next day. Rome having thus been subdued by Charles, the Pope, though unwilling, handed Charles over to the brother of the Turkish emperor, and gave as hostage his son, Cardinal Valentino (as they say), and the cities nearest the kingdom of Naples. He also, when Charles was returning to Naples, laid snares in vain, having made a new alliance with the King of Spain, with the Venetians, and with Ludovico Sforza; relying on whose help the Pope tried to cut off King Charles on his return. But after Charles died, the Pope made peace with Louis XII, who succeeded Charles in the kingdom of France. This Alexander sat for eleven years. See the Supplementum Chronicorum, book 15.

units.la: CÆS. Borgia, dictus Valentinus, Alexandri supradicti filius, Flaminiam provinciam, & Vmbriam sibi subiecit: verùm ciues, principis qui fugatus erat, amantissimi, eum hoc Valentino exacto, reuocarunt: hæc sub mortem Alexandri patris eius acta sunt. Videto vt supra. Hic relicto Cardinalitio pileo, galeam assumpsit.
units.tr: Caesar Borgia, called Valentinus, son of the Alexander mentioned above, subjected to himself the province of Flaminia and Umbria; but the citizens, who were very fond of their prince, who had been put to flight, recalled him once Valentinus was driven out. These things were done under the death of Alexander his father. See above. Here, having left aside the cardinal's hat, he took up the helmet.

units.la: MAXIMILIANUS, Friderici Imperatoris huius nominis tertij filius, post patrem solus imperat anno mundi 5454, à Christo nato 1492. Hic antequam imperaret, exercitum in Flandriam duxit, & Mariam Burgundam in uxorem accepit: nec multò post cum Ludovico Francorum Rege, huius nominis undecimo, graui prælio propter principatum Burgundiæ congreditur, postea cum eo in annos 7. inducias facit. Austriam, quam Matthias Hungariæ Rex occuparat, Maximilianus recuperat. Priore uxore defuncta, Blancam Mariam Galeatij Insubriæ Ducis filiam, uxorem duxit: Burgundiam statim invasit, varie pugnatum est, tandemque pax inita. Sforzia Mediolanū recipit, Gallis pulsis, quos dum insequitur, incautus capitur, & in Galliam ducitur, anno Domini 1500. Imperauit Maximilianus annos 27. literas, & literatos coluit, profitebatúrque eos se in precio habere qui aliis præstarent. Vide Baptistam Egnatium li. Romanorum principum tertio, & Paul. Aemy. in Ludovico supradicto: item Chro. Reg. Franc. & Chro. Carion. li.3.
units.tr: MAXIMILIAN, son of the Emperor Frederick III of that name, reigned alone after his father in the year of the world 5454, from the birth of Christ 1492. Before he reigned, he led an army into Flanders and took Mary of Burgundy as his wife. Not long after, he engaged in a severe battle with Louis, king of the French, the eleventh of that name, over the principality of Burgundy; afterwards he made a truce with him for seven years. Maximilian recovered Austria, which Matthias, king of Hungary, had occupied. When his first wife had died, he married Bianca Maria, daughter of Galeazzo, Duke of Insubria. He at once invaded Burgundy; there was fighting of various kinds, and at last peace was made. Sforza recovered Milan, the French having been driven out; while he pursued them, he was taken unawares and led into France, in the year of the Lord 1500. Maximilian reigned 27 years. He cultivated letters and men of letters, and professed that he held in esteem those who excelled others. See Baptista Egnatius, book 3 of Roman Princes, and Paul Aemilius under Louis above; likewise the Chronicle of the Kings of France and Carion's Chronicle, book 3.

units.la: MARIA, Caroli Burgundiæ Ducis filia unica, Maximiliano antequam imperaret nupsit: ac post annos quinque, relictis Philippo & Margareta liberis, ex equo decidés, fracta cervice, obiit anno mundi 5443. à Christo nato 1481. Vide ut supra. IASON MAYNO BARTOLVS SOCINVS[?]
units.tr: MARY, the only daughter of Charles, Duke of Burgundy, married Maximilian before he reigned. After five years, leaving behind her children Philip and Margaret, she fell from her horse, broke her neck and died, in the year of the world 5443, from the birth of Christ 1481. See above. JASON MAYNO, BARTOLUS SOCINUS [?]

units.la: IASON Maynus,nobilis Mediolanêsium Patricius, absolutissimus Iurisconsultus,ac orator facundissimus, Eques auratus,& Ducalis Senator , claruit tèporibus Friderici & Maximiliani,Imperatorû, apud quos legationes obiit nomine Ludouici Sfortiæ Mediolanêsium Ducis:atq; legationis munere egregiè defunctus,ab iisdem dona varia cum summis priuilegiis reportauit. Hic intra Oratores ab omnibus Christianis principibus ad Alexandrum sextû hoc nomine Papam missis, dû Pontificatum auspicaretur,palmam facilè retulit:facundia,necnon interim facetiis ornatus fuit.Papiç,Pisç, ac Paduæ ius interpretatus est annis 50.ex omnibus Europç finibus clarissimos ac nobilissimos alliciens auditores:tanti enim erat nominis, tătáque scientia percelebris , vt in eius commendationem Ludouicus Cerrus medicus ac Poëta clarissimus,sic cecinerit:
units.tr: JASON Maynus, a noble patrician of Milan, a most accomplished jurist and a most eloquent orator, a knight of the golden spur and senator of the Duke, flourished in the times of the Emperors Frederick and Maximilian, before whom he discharged embassies on behalf of Ludovico Sforza, Duke of Milan. Having discharged the office of ambassador with distinction, he brought back from them various gifts together with the highest privileges. Among the orators sent by all Christian princes to Pope Alexander VI under this name, while he was beginning his pontificate, he easily carried off the palm; he was also adorned with wit, and at the same time with charm of speech. He taught law at Pavia, Pisa and Padua for 50 years, attracting listeners from every corner of Europe, the most distinguished and noble men; so great was his name and so widely celebrated his learning, that in his praise Ludovicus Cerrus, a physician and most distinguished poet, sang thus:

units.la: Te quondam in terris hominem nouëre priores, Dum leges aperis, scitáque docta patrum: At nunc, more Deum, cùm des responsa petenti, Es Deus, oracli Numen ad instar habens.
units.tr: Once men knew you on earth as one of the former ages, while you unfolded the laws and the learned wisdom of the fathers; but now, as with God, when you give answers to one who asks, you are God, having the power of an oracle.

units.la: In Iure complures libros edidit.Orationes habuit ad Pontifices, & ad Imperatores supradictos: Cæterùm feliciter obiit anno ætatis 84[?]. Vide Supplem. Chro. lib. 16.
units.tr: He published several books on law. He delivered orations to the Pontiffs and to the Emperors named above. He died happily in the 84th [?] year of his age. See Supplement to the Chronicle, book 16.

units.la: BARTOLOMÆVS Socinus Senensis,domini Mariani legum interpretis celeberrimi filius, Iurisconsultus eximius inter legis interpretes in Hetruria extitit:doctrina siquidem & ingenio plurimum valuisse testantur adhuc plurima eius consilia quæ extât.Claruit eodem tempore quo Iason supradictus. Videto Supplem. Chro. lib. 16.
units.tr: BARTHOLOMEW Socinus of Siena, son of the most famous legal scholar Lord Marianus, was an outstanding jurist among the interpreters of law in Tuscany; for his learning and talent are attested by the very many of his opinions that still survive, which were of great worth. He flourished at the same time as the Jason mentioned above. See Supplement to the Chronicle, book 16.

units.la: LVDOVICVS Sfortia, cognomento Maurus, Franc. Sfor. filius, tutor nepoti Ioanni Galeatio à Senatu vnà cum Bona adolescentis matre, atque aliis primoribus datus est. Fuit ingenio astuto ac callido: Bonam, tutoresque alios à principatu Itatim detutbauit [?]: adolescentem principem vt genio indulgeret permisit: ne administrationi intenderet, dum voluptatibus ac deliciis irretitur: id etiâ forte eo astu fecit, vt inuisum iuuenem populo redderet. Porrò cùm adoleuisset Galeatius, atque administrationi esset idoneus, veneno eum praeuenit Ludouicus: arripuitque principatum, & in suam etiam sententiâ arte vel maxima Senatu ac primates traxit, omniumque suffragia sibi coparauit. Ducem itaque aut potius tyrānum, enecato adolescente annis 5. egit, ac mensibus 6. Quare ab exercitu Gallorū territus, in Germaniam aufugit: ac post annum reuersus, & cū aliquot Heluetiorum copiis per Nouarram Mediolanum petens, an. D. 1500. à suis proditus est, atque à Gallis captus, in Galliam perductus est, vbi quasi scelerum poenas luens, priuatus & vinctus interiit. Vide Pau. Iou. Supplem. Chro. lib. 16.
units.tr: LUDOVICUS Sforza, surnamed the Moor, son of Francis Sforza, was appointed guardian of his nephew Giovanni Galeazzo, together with Bona, the young man's mother, and other leading men, by the Senate. He was of a crafty and cunning disposition. He drove Bona and the other guardians out of power at once; he allowed the young prince to indulge his inclinations, so that he would be caught up in pleasures and delights and would not attend to the administration; perhaps he also did this by such cunning, in order to make the young man hated by the people. Then, when Galeazzo had grown up and was fit for administration, Ludovico forestalled him with poison; he seized the principality, and by the greatest art he also drew the Senate and the chief men to his own opinion, and procured for himself the votes of all. Thus he governed as Duke, or rather as tyrant, for five years and six months, after the young man had been done away with. Therefore, frightened by the French army, he fled into Germany; after a year he returned, and while making his way through Novara towards Milan with some troops of the Swiss, in the year of the Lord 1500 he was betrayed by his own people and captured by the French, and was led into France, where, as if paying the penalty for his crimes, he died deprived of liberty and in chains. See Paulus Jovius, Supplement to the Chronicle, book 16.

units.la: MAXIMILIANVS Sforria [?] Ludouici praedicti filius, in Flādria cum Frācisco fratre educatus, post varias rerū mutationes circa principatū suū, à Carolo quinto tandē reuocatus, Mediolano praeficitur, eo nomine vt Imperatoris res agat, ac pecuniā ei corradat. Verūm huic fatale fuit, forte ob scelera paterna, priuatum ac extorrem viuere. Nā vix principatū, ac naturale solum attigerat, cùm à Frācisco Valesio, qui ius suū armis repetebat, Mediolanū vnà cum Maximiliano capitur, an. D. 1515. attamen tanquam ab humanissimo & Christianissimo Rege, ac cōsanguineo, datur illi pēsio annua 36000. aureorum: facta potestate vt liberam in Frangia vitam ducat: in qua etiam obiit, princeps alioqui non contemnendus. Vide vt suprà. D. SAB. PHILIBERTVS MARGARETA MAX. FIL.
units.tr: MAXIMILIANUS Sforza [?], son of the aforementioned Ludovico, was brought up in Flanders with his brother Francis; after various changes of fortune concerning his principality, he was at last recalled by Charles V and placed in charge of Milan, on the understanding that he would manage affairs for the Emperor and raise money for him. But it was his fate, perhaps because of his father's crimes, to live deprived of his power and in exile. For scarcely had he reached the principality and his native soil, when he was taken at Milan, together with Maximilian, by Francis of Valois, who was pursuing his right by arms, in the year of the Lord 1515. Nevertheless, as by a most humane and most Christian king and a kinsman, he was given an annual pension of 36,000 gold crowns, and it was allowed that he might lead a free life in France; and there he also died, a prince otherwise not to be despised. See above. D. SAV. PHILIBERT. MARGARET. MAX. FIL.

units.la: PHILIBERTVS Sabaudiæ Dux octauus, succedit patri Philippo anno mundi 5457. à Christo nato 1495. Hic pietatem summopere coluit, magnanimus, speciosissimus, atque omnibus acceptissimus fuit, pulcher etiam ob elegantiâ cognominatus. Margaretâ coniugem accepit, quam ex Maria Caroli Burgūdię Ducis filia susceperat Maximilianus, obiit multa commendatione dignus, nullis interim relictis liberis: quare ei Carolus frater successit. Vide Allobrogum, siue Sabaudiæ Chro.*
units.tr: PHILIBERT, eighth Duke of Savoy, succeeded his father Philip in the year of the world 5457, from the birth of Christ 1495. He cultivated piety above all; he was magnanimous, most handsome, and most acceptable to all; he was also surnamed "the Handsome" for his elegance. He took as his wife Margaret, whom Maximilian had had by Mary, daughter of Charles, Duke of Burgundy. He died, a man worthy of much praise, leaving no children; therefore his brother Charles succeeded him. See the Chronicle of the Allobroges, or of Savoy.

units.la: MARGARETA Imperatoris Maximiliani filia, ut dictum est, ac Philiberti supradicti relicta, animum pudicũ atque amorem erga virum castissimum testata est, tum quòd nullum superinduxerit coniugem, vitâ perpetuò cælibem ac laudatissimam ducés:tum quòd in urbe quam vulgo Burgum in Bressia vocât, templũ nobile ac celebratissimum extruxerit, quod inter Europæ nuper structa ædificia, tanquâ opus rarum ac percelebre prædicatur: nec id quidem ob templi amplitudinem, sed potius ob artis ornamenta ac splendorem, ut omnium conspicientium oculos in admirationem trahat. Verùm ædificij decus ac splendorem longè superat sepulchrũ candidissimo marmore extructum: ubi extat amantissimi coniugis effigies ad vivum expressa: in quod signum quicquid ars sculpendi unquam valuit, contulisse, ac deprompsisse videtur: hæc Ducis effigies hinc & inde habet duarum Margaretarum marmorea simulachra ad vivum etiam formata: nempe Margaretæ uxoris prædictæ, & Margaretæ alterius, quæ Ducis mater extitit. Vide ut supra.
units.tr: MARGARET, daughter of the Emperor Maximilian, as has been said, and widow of the aforementioned Philibert, showed a chaste mind and love towards her most chaste husband, both in that she took no other husband after him and lived her whole life unmarried and most praised; and in that she built, in the town commonly called Bourg in Bresse, a noble and most celebrated church, which among the buildings of Europe recently erected is proclaimed as a rare and most renowned work: and this not indeed for the size of the church, but rather for the adornments and splendour of its art, so as to draw the eyes of all who behold it into admiration. But the glory and splendour of the building is far surpassed by the tomb built of the whitest marble, where there is a likeness of her most loving husband, shown to the life; into this figure, whatever the art of sculpture has ever been able to contribute or produce, seems to have been poured. This effigy of the Duke has on either side marble statues of two Margarets, likewise shaped to the life: namely, of the aforementioned Margaret, his wife, and of the other Margaret, who was the Duke's mother. See above.

units.la: MARCVS Antonius Coccius Sabellicus ad vicum Varronis in via Valeria iuxta Anienem. Fabro ferrario patre gentus, ingentem vim attulit ad perdiscendas literas: tamque citò in his profecit, vt plane imberbis apud Tiburtes dum aperiret. Inde collecta mercede, & togula caerulea excultus nobilioris doctrinae cupiditate in vrbem ad Pomponium se contulit, à quo vberrimi ingenij merito, in collegium sodalium solemni ceremonia coaptatus, Sabellici cognomen tulit, mutabat enim nomen qui in Quirinali sacra lauro coronabatur. Euocatus fuit à senatu Veneto ea conditione vt ciuitatis res gestas à fine Iustiniani conscriberet, & trecentis aureis in gymnasio profiteretur. In hoc munere perutilem iuuentuti operâ praestitit, & scribendo ad septuagesimum fermè annum peruenit, lue venerea consumptus. Scripsit de se viuens & incolumis hoc elogium, quod sepulchro insculperetur.
units.tr: MARCUS Antonius Coccius Sabellicus, at the village of Varro on the Via Valeria near the Anio. Born of a blacksmith father, he applied himself with great effort to learning his letters, and made such progress in them that while still beardless he taught at Tibur. Then, having gathered his wages and dressed in a blue little toga, out of a desire for higher learning he betook himself to the city to Pomponius, by whose judgement of his most abundant talent he was admitted with solemn ceremony into the college of fellows, and took the surname Sabellicus; for whoever was crowned with laurel in the Quirinal sacred grove changed his name. He was summoned by the Venetian Senate on condition that he should write the history of the city from the end of Justinian, and should lecture in the gymnasium for three hundred gold pieces. In this office he rendered very useful service to the young, and continued writing until about his seventieth year, being carried off by venereal disease. While living and unharmed he wrote for himself this epitaph, to be carved on his tomb.

units.la: Quem non res hominum, non omnis ceperat aetas,
units.tr: Whom the affairs of men, not every age, had seized,
This brief urn holds the writer Coccio.
He flourished around the year of human salvation 1498.

units.la: ANTONIVS Nebrissensis, post Punicum nomē, virtute Ferdinādi Regis, Hispania pulsum, ingenij acumine claruit, cū illud regnum, per mille amplius annos, Vandalicis, Punicisque armis occupantibus, Latinarum literarum splendore caruisset. Iste fuit par antiquis Grāmaticis, si par fortuna seculi ei respondisset. Multa scripsit, & docendo iuuentutem, multorum animos, ad antiquum decus literarum vehementer erexit, vtriusque vel etiam triplicis linguae cognitione clarus. Fatis cessit repentina paralysi, quum ad septuagesimum aetatis annum peruenisset.
units.tr: ANTONIO de Nebrija, after the Punic name had been driven out of Spain by the virtue of King Ferdinand, shone for the keenness of his wit, at a time when that kingdom, for more than a thousand years while the Vandal and Punic arms held it, had lacked the splendour of Latin letters. He was the equal of the ancient grammarians, had fortune of his age been equal to him. He wrote many works, and by teaching the young and by stirring the minds of many he vigorously raised up the ancient glory of letters; he was famous for his knowledge of two or even three languages. He yielded to the fates, struck by a sudden paralysis, having reached his seventieth year of life.

units.la: HIERONYMVS Sauonarola Ferrariensis ex ordine diui Dominici cucullatus, usque adeo austera vitæ disciplina, ac erudito subtilisque ingenio, & in sacris concionibus admirabili facundia valuit, ut populum instaurandis religionibus deditum, & tū nouo receptæ libertatis gaudio gestienté, quò vellet facilè impelleret, priuatisque familiariū, ac ipsis quoque summi magistratus consilijs misceretur. Scripsit quadragesimale vnū lib. r.[?] super Psalmos pœnitentiales commentū: super prophetas multos commētatus est. Prophetiā quoque emisit, qua multa de hoc nostro ævo, regnorúmque commotione prędixit. Alia quoque multa scripsit. Futura prędicere, veluti diuino ad flatū numine credebant: sed ambitione non caruit & capitale iudiciū de suspectis nobilissimis septem ciuibus, sęua sententia pręcipitauit: unde, cùm mores Alexandri summi Pontificis acerbè reprehederet, sacrosanctam potestatem in dubiū deuocauit: tandem reus maiestatis, deposcēte Pontifice, comprehensus miserabili supplicio affectus est, anno salutis humanæ 1499.
units.tr: JEROME Savonarola of Ferrara, a Dominican friar of the order of St Dominic, was so powerful through his austere discipline of life, his learned and subtle wit, and his admirable eloquence in sacred sermons, that he could easily drive a people devoted to renewing religion, and at that time eager with the new joy of recovered liberty, wherever he wished. He also meddled in the private counsels of his friends and even of the highest magistrates. He wrote a Lenten (quadragesimal) commentary on the penitential Psalms; he commented on many of the prophets. He also put forth a prophecy in which he foretold much about our own age and the upheaval of kingdoms. He wrote many other things too. People believed he foretold the future as if by the breath of divine power; but he was not free from ambition, and he rashly condemned seven of the most noble citizens to death on suspicion of capital crimes, with a harsh sentence. Consequently, when he sharply criticised the morals of Pope Alexander, he called the sacred power itself into doubt. At last, as a guilty party of treason, at the Pope's demand, he was seized and suffered a wretched execution, in the year of human salvation 1499.

units.la: THOMAS Morus, natione Anglus vir doctus & clarus, Cantuariensis Archiepiscopus, exilio primū à rege Angliæ damnatus, post etiam capitali supplicio affectus fuit circa annū salutis, 1535. quod furentis regis Henrici octaui (qui eū paulò ante ad summos honores extulerat, tanquam virtutis eximiæ admirator) nefariæ libidini, adulari noluisset. Iani vitalis de eo extat epitaphium quod sequitur,
units.tr: THOMAS More, an Englishman, a learned and distinguished man, Archbishop of Canterbury, was first condemned to exile by the king of England, and afterwards suffered capital punishment around the year of salvation 1535, because he would not flatter the lustful wickedness of the raging King Henry VIII, who had shortly before raised him to the highest honours as an admirer of his outstanding virtue. There is an epitaph on him by Janus Vitalis, which follows:

units.la: Dum Morus immerita submittit colla securi, Et fluit occasum, pignora chara suum, Immo, ait, infandi vitam deflete tyranni, Non moritur, facinus qui graue, morte fugit.
units.tr: While More submits his neck to the axe though he deserved no such thing, and his dear children weep as the sunset flows, he says: "Do not weep for my life, but for the tyrant's unspeakable crimes; he who escapes by death does not die, who flees a grave deed by death."

units.la: Hic clarus literarum Græcarum & Latinarum cognitione, Dialogos aliquot Luciani transtulit. Fecit Utopiam, & multa egregia epigrammata scripsit.
units.tr: He was famous for his knowledge of Greek and Latin letters, and translated some dialogues of Lucian. He wrote the Utopia and many fine epigrams.

units.la: PHILIPPVS Archidux Austriæ, Maximiliani filius, ex Maria, vnica Caroli Burgundiæ Ducis filia, vxorē duxit Ioānam, vnicā Ferdinādi Arragonū Regis filiā. Cuius nomine, post mortem Isabellæ socrus suæ, classe in Hispaniam profectus, Castellæ regnum hæreditario iure obtinuit. Post hæc ad coercendum vetus inter Brabantos & Sicambros bellum, anno 1505. in Flandriam reuersus, multas Gueldriæ vrbes partim vi expugnauit, partim ad deditionem compulit: ducémque ipsum nomine Carolum pueritiam vixdum egressum, captiuum abduxit, vnaque cū liberis suis in aula sua liberaliter educauit. Flandriæ & Artesiæ comitatus Ludouico duodecimo iure feudi acceptos retulit: idque Atrebati, delegatis ad id munus Guidone à Rupeforti, Galliæ Cancellario, & Ludouico à Lutzemburgo Ligniaci Comite. Rebusque ita compositis, cum denuo instructa classe in Hispaniam contenderet, vi tempestatis in Angliæ littus eiectus, ab Henrico Septimo Anglorum Rege summo honore est exceptus: ita tamen vt exitus ei non patuerit, donec Suffortij ducem qui ex Albe rosæ familia proximus Angliæ heres esse putabatur, quémque Henrici metu patria profugum in Sicambria receperat, Anglo tradidisset. Post hæc in Hispaniam prosectus, non multo post supremum diem obiit, anno à Christo nato 1506. die 27. Septembris, ætatis 28. Vide Genealogiam Imperatorum, & Chronica Chronicorum.
units.tr: PHILIP, Archduke of Austria, son of Maximilian, married Joanna, the only daughter of Ferdinand, king of Aragon, by Mary, the only daughter of Charles, Duke of Burgundy. After the death of his mother-in-law Isabella, in her name he set out for Spain with a fleet and obtained the kingdom of Castile by hereditary right. Afterwards, to end the old war between the Brabanters and the Sicambrians, he returned to Flanders in 1505; he partly took by force and partly compelled to surrender many cities of Guelders, and carried off their duke, Charles, scarcely out of boyhood, as a captive, and raised him liberally at his court together with his own children. He reported that the counties of Flanders and Artois had been received by him as fiefs from Louis XII; this was done at Arras, with Guy de Rochefort, Chancellor of France, and Louis of Luxembourg, Count of Ligny, appointed for the purpose. With matters thus settled, when he was hastening again to Spain with a fresh fleet, he was driven by a storm onto the English shore, and was received with the highest honour by Henry VII, king of the English; yet on such terms that he had no way out until he handed over to the Englishman the Duke of Suffolk, who was thought to be the next heir of England from the House of York, and who, having fled his country for fear of Henry, had been received in Sicambria. After this he set out for Spain, and not long afterwards died, in the year 1506 after the birth of Christ, on 27 September, at the age of 28. See the Genealogy of the Emperors and the Chronicle of Chronicles.

units.la: IOANNA Ferdinandi Hispaniæ Regis & Elisabetæ filia, vxor fuit Philippi supradicti, quæ peperit ei Carolum quintum Romanorum Imperatorem, & Ferdinādum Bohemiæ ac Hungariæ Regem, filios: & filias Leonoram, Isabellam, Mariam & Catharinam, Reginas Lusitaniæ, Galliæ, Daniæ & Hungariæ. Vide vt supra, & Paralip. rerum memorabil. REX FRA. LVDOVICVS ANNA. REG. FRAN.
units.tr: JOANNA, daughter of Ferdinand, king of Spain, and Elizabeth, was the wife of the aforesaid Philip. She bore him as sons Charles V, Emperor of the Romans, and Ferdinand, king of Bohemia and Hungary; and as daughters Eleanor, Isabella, Mary and Catherine, queens of Portugal, France, Denmark and Hungary. See as above, and the Paralipomena of memorable things. KING FRANCIS LOUIS ANNE QUEEN FRANCIS.

units.la: LVDOVICVS duodecimus Carolo octauo in regno Francię succedit anno domini 1497. atque ann. 1499. ducibus Io. Iac. Triuultio & Albiniaco, expeditionem in Insubriam fecit. Hi cùm Alexandriam ac Papiam cepissent, timore perculsus Ludouicus Sforsia, in Germaniam sese proripuit, Mediolanum illis tanquam bolum relinquens: hoc nuntio accepto Rex in Italiam penetrat, atque ouans Mediolanum ingreditur: inde exiens præfectum reliquit Triuultium. Porrò Sforsia è Germania redijs, Mediolanum recipit: statimque armis Fracicis[?] egredi cogitur: itaque Nouarram se confert, vbi à Francis capitur. Anno. 1502. regno Rex potitur Neapolitano, Duce Albiniaco: Fridericus regnum prius occupans, cum vxore ac filio in Galliam captiuus ducitur. Bononiam Rex à Bentiuolo occupatam, Papę reddit. Pręterea ad Aignadellum insignem de Venetis reportat victoriam, capto etiam Bartolomęo d'Aluiano copiis Venetis præfecto, quem in Galliam perduxit: omnem ditione quę tum Papę, tum Mediolanesi Ducatui adempta fuerat, recuperauit: quę ad Pontificem spectabant, ei reddidit. Tandem ann. 1512. Venetos, Hispanos, Papalesq; ad Rauenam debellauit. Hęc victoria maximum principum numerum captiuorum illi cum Rauenna vrbe tradidit. Obiit anno Regni 17. Vide Chro. Reg. Fran.
units.tr: LOUIS XII succeeded Charles VIII in the kingdom of France in the year of the Lord 1497, and in 1499, under the commanders Giovanni Giacomo Trivulzio and Aubigny, he made an expedition into Lombardy. When these had taken Alessandria and Pavia, Ludovico Sforza, struck with fear, fled into Germany, leaving Milan to them as a morsel; on receiving this news the King entered Italy and went triumphantly into Milan; leaving it, he left Trivulzio as its governor. Then Sforza, returning from Germany, recovered Milan; at once he was forced to go out with French arms; so he betook himself to Novara, where he was taken by the French. In 1502 the King gained the kingdom of Naples, with Aubigny as commander: Frederick, who had previously occupied the kingdom, was led captive into France with his wife and son. The King restored Bologna, which had been occupied by Bentivoglio, to the Pope. Moreover, he won a notable victory over the Venetians at Agnadello, also capturing Bartolomeo d'Alviano, the commander of the Venetian forces, whom he took into France; he recovered all the territory which had been taken from the Pope and from the Duchy of Milan, and handed back to the Pontiff what belonged to him. Finally, in 1512, he defeated the Venetians, Spaniards and papal forces at Ravenna. This victory gave him, together with the city of Ravenna, a very great number of princes as captives. He died in the seventeenth year of his reign. See the Chronicle of the Kings of France.

units.la: ANNA, Caroli octaui relicta, nupsit Ludouico duodecimo, ex quo suscepit Claudiam, quę data est in vxorem Francisco Valesio, tunc Angolismensium Duci: & Renatam, Ferrarię Ducis nunc vxorem. Vide vt supra. IO. IACO TRIVLZIVS TRIVL. THEODORVS
units.tr: ANNE, widow of Charles VIII, married Louis XII, by whom she had Claude, who was given in marriage to Francis of Valois, then Duke of Angoulême; and Renée, now wife of the Duke of Ferrara. See as above. JOHN JAMES TRIVULZIO TRIVUL. THEODORE

units.la: IOANNES Iacobus Triuu[?]lfius Mediolanensis, Franciæ Marefchalus seu Tribunus, ac præfectus militum Fracię in Italia, deuicta Alexandria Ludouicum Sfortiam Mediolano expulit, ac deinde Nouarra: quamobrem à Fracorum Rege cui erat addictissimus, Mediolano præficitur anno Domini 1499. Postea Lugdunum Galliæ rexit, vbi diligentissimè, atque accuratissimè præfuit anno Domini 1514. Ceterum Carnuti obiit non sine omnium planctu, ob synceram eius administrationè, anno ætatis 8o. iussitque corpus suum Mediolani sepeliendum deferri.
units.tr: JOHN James Trivulzio of Milan, Marshal or Tribune of France and commander of the French soldiers in Italy, having defeated Alessandria, drove Ludovico Sforza out of Milan, and then out of Novara; for this reason he was appointed governor of Milan by the King of France, to whom he was most devoted, in the year of the Lord 1499. Afterwards he governed Lyon in France, where he presided most diligently and carefully in 1514. He died at Chartres, however, not without the lamentation of all, on account of his sincere administration, in the eightieth year of his age, and he ordered his body to be carried to Milan for burial.

units.la: THEODORVS Triuulfius Marchio Picichitoni præfectus militum Regis Neapolitani, deinde Dux exercitus Venetorum ac Florentinorum, postea Eques ordinis à Francisco Valesio creatus, Mediolano præficitur: tandémq; Marefchalus, siue Tribunus militum ab eodem designatus, Lugduni præfuit: vbi summa fide, ac vigilantia, re administrata, eodem quo natus fuerat die obiit septuagenario maior, anno à Christo nato 1533. P. M. PIVS III. IVLIVS LIG. PON. MAX.
units.tr: THEODORE Trivulzio, Marquis of Pizzighettone, commander of the soldiers of the king of Naples, then general of the armies of the Venetians and Florentines, afterwards created a Knight of the Order by Francis of Valois, was appointed to Milan; finally, as Marshal or Tribune of the soldiers, appointed by the same king, he presided at Lyon, where he administered the office with the greatest faith and vigilance, and died, over seventy years old, on the same day of the month on which he had been born, in the year of Christ 1533. POPE III. JULIUS LIG. PON. MAX.

units.la: PIVS Papa huius nominis tertius, Pontifex creatur anno mundi 5464. à Christo nato 1502. hic natione Hetruscus, Senis oriundus, Pij secundi ex Laodamia sorore nepos, ingenio ac literis claruit, laboris & inediæ patientissimus fuit. Sed Pij avunculi exemplo in Gallos coiurauit, quòd ægrè ferret Apuliam & non modicam Italiæ partem eos subegisse:obiit mense 1.[?] quo in Alexandri Pontificis locum suffectus fuerat. Vide Platinam.
units.tr: PIUS, the third Pope of this name, was created Pontiff in the year of the world 5464, in the year of Christ 1502. He was a Tuscan by nation, born at Siena, the grandson through his sister Laodamia of Pius II. He was distinguished by his talent and learning, and was most patient of labour and hunger. But following the example of his uncle Pius, he conspired against the French, because he took it hard that they had subdued Apulia and a considerable part of Italy. He died in the month of 1.[?], to which he had been appointed in place of Pope Alexander. See Platina.

units.la: IVLIVS Papa huius nominis secundus, eodem anno Pontificatum obtinet quo Papa Pius supradictus, cui successit. Fuit hic patria Sauonensis, quæ urbs est Genuę subdita, parentibus natus obscuris, verùm cũ fortunę beneficio, tũ sua industria ad Pontificatum euectus est: acri & versuto ingenio fuit, animóque minimè abiecto. Patrimonium Petri nemo animosius tutatus est, neque callidius quisquam amplificare instituit. Gallis sub initium Pontificatus fauit: quare à Ludouico duodecimo adiutus, Bononiam Ioanni Bentiuolo eripuit: ingratum tamen Gallis postea se præstitit. Rauennam à Venetis occupatam obsedit, ac expugnauit: Seruiam, Imolam, Fauentiam, Foroliuium à Venetis quoque eripuit, atque alia non pauca loca: fuit equidem ut laborum patientissimus, sic iniuriarum impatientissimus, ac animo iracundo, quod vitium etiam generosissimos vrget ac rapit. Sedit annis 10. Vide ut supra. PHILIPPVS.DECIVS.MEDIOLANENSIS. HIERONYMVS. BVTICEL.
units.tr: JULIUS, the second Pope of this name, obtained the papacy in the same year in which Pope Pius, mentioned above, succeeded. This man was from Savona, a city subject to Genoa, born of obscure parents, but was raised to the papacy as much by the favour of fortune as by his own industry. He had a keen and crafty mind, and a spirit by no means cowardly. No one defended the patrimony of St Peter more boldly, and no one set about enlarging it more shrewdly. At the beginning of his pontificate he favoured the French; therefore, aided by Louis XII, he snatched Bologna from Giovanni Bentivoglio; yet he afterwards showed himself ungrateful to the French. He besieged and stormed Ravenna, occupied by the Venetians; he also wrested Cervia, Imola, Faenza and Forlì from the Venetians, and not a few other places. He was indeed as patient of labours as he was impatient of injuries, and of an irascible temper, a fault which even the most generous people are driven by.
