units.la: PHILIPPVS Decius Mediolanensis, Iureconsultus in profession humani, diuinìque præsertim iuris floruit, Mayni Iasonis æmulus, ac ætate simul æqualis, sed qui docendo & scribendo, in omnibus Italiæ gymnasiis superior censeretur. Enarrabat enim subtilissimè & omniũ acerrimè disputabat. A Pisis, vbi vxorem duxerat, Ticinum à Gallo præside optimis stipendiis euocatus, vnde belli violentia egressus, maximo incommodo accepto ab hostibus, qui domum eius, in expugnatione vrbis diripuerant, in Galliam fugit, & apud Bituriges sese recepit: vbi Ius diuinum edocuit per duos fermè annos. Et cùm reuersus esset in Italiam, Senenses eum conduxerunt, apud quos, octogenario maior, interiit, post quam vnica eius filia senensi patritio nupsisset. Reliquit in vtroque iure scripta doctissima, & præterea Consiliorum lib. 4. Lecturas eius super Decretales & super ff. & Cod. Commētarium de Regulis iuris, impressum Lugduni apud Paganum. Citantur ab eo scripta Consiliorum, volumina 4. repetition. in 1. ff. vet. de rei venditione. Item alibi Commentarios, super prima & secunda ff. vet. & prima & 2. Codicis. Claruit anno 1535. quo etiam Senis mortuus est. Vide librum, de vita Iurisconsultorum.
units.tr: PHILIPPUS Decius of Milan, a jurist who flourished in both human and especially divine law, a rival of Jason Mainus and his contemporary in age, but who, in teaching and writing, was judged superior in all the schools of Italy. For he lectured most subtly and disputed most sharply of all. Summoned from Pisa, where he had married, to Ticinum by the French governor with excellent salary, he left there because of the violence of war, having suffered great loss at the hands of the enemy, who had plundered his house when the city was stormed, and he fled to France and settled among the Bituriges, where he taught divine law for almost two years. And when he returned to Italy, the Sienese hired him, and he died among them, being more than eighty years old, after his only daughter had married a Sienese patrician. He left most learned writings in both laws, and besides, four books of Consilia, his lectures on the Decretals and on the Digest and Code, and a Commentary on the Rules of Law, printed at Lyon by Paganus. His writings cited by him are the Consilia, four volumes, a repetition on the first law of the Digest, de rei venditione. Likewise elsewhere he cites his Commentaries on the first and second of the Digest vetus and the first and second of the Code. He flourished in the year 1535, the year in which he also died at Siena. See the book On the Lives of the Jurists.

units.la: HIERONYMVS Buticella Patauinus, vir doctus in Iuris professione, scripsit vnum volumen de Repetitionibus, plurimásque lecturas in Digesta & Codice, quarum quidem pars in lucem edita est, alia minimè. Docuit Ius cum maxima grauitate & celebritate, Patauí & Papiæ, & in aliis celeberrimis Italiæ Academiis, ita vt ex eius schola, doctissimi adolescentes prodierint. Florebat anno salutis humanæ 1504. Vide Conadum Gesnerum, & librum de vita Iurisconsultorum. LEO + PON. MAX. P. MAX ADRIANVS VI
units.tr: HIERONYMUS Buticella of Padua, a learned man in the profession of law, wrote one volume of Repetitions and very many lectures on the Digest and the Code, of which part has indeed been published, but another not at all. He taught law with the greatest gravity and renown at Padua and Pavia, and in other most famous academies of Italy, so that from his school very learned young men came forth. He flourished in the year of human salvation 1504. See Conrad Gesner, and the book On the Lives of the Jurists. LEO + PON. MAX. P. MAX ADRIANVS VI

units.la: LEO Papa huius nominis decimus, in demortui supradicti Iulij locum suffectus est anno mundi 5474. à Christo nato 1512. Hic non obscuro loco natus (nempe ex clarissima apud Florentinos Medicum domo) educatus liberaliter fuit, bonisq; à prima ætate literis institutus: præceptoribus usus cū aliis, tum maximè Angelo Politiano: quē Medices familia, sicut & alios complures eruditos, indulgentissimè fouit. Fuit itaque Leo ut natura, ita disciplina ac consuetudine mansuetus. Doctos amauit, nimirum ipse eleganter doctus. Ducem Vrbinatem, quandam ob causam, Ducatu priuauit, atque in eius locum, quem habebat ex fratre nepotem, Laurentium Reginæ Francorum parentem substituit. In Ducem Ferrariensem idem tentauit, sed frustrà. Sedit annos 9. Vide Platinam.
units.tr: LEO, the tenth Pope of this name, was installed in the place of the aforementioned Julius, who had died, in the year of the world 5474, from the birth of Christ 1512. Born of no obscure family (namely, from the most distinguished house of the Medici among the Florentines), he was liberally educated and instructed in good letters from his earliest age. He had teachers of various kinds, but chiefly Angelo Poliziano, whom the Medici family, as well as many other learned men, cherished most indulgently. Leo was therefore as gentle in disposition as in upbringing and habit. He loved learned men, being himself elegantly learned. He deprived the Duke of Urbino of his duchy for a certain reason, and in his place he put in his nephew Lorenzo, the father of the Queen of the Franks, whom he had from his brother. He attempted the same against the Duke of Ferrara, but in vain. He sat for nine years. See Platina.

units.la: ADRIANVS huius nominis Papa sextus, Caroli, qui etiā nunc imperat, olim præceptor, Leoni prædicto absens substituitur anno mundi 5483. à Christo nato 1521. Hic summus Theologus doctrinam & grauitatem blanda quadam morum grauitate cōdiit: ut eius scripta testātur: cuius vita cùm frugalis esset, parum placuit Romanis non paucis. In conferendis sacerdotiis perquàm parcus fuit: quòd nullis ea nisi idoneis & doctis dāda iudicaret: fuit natione Teutho, è Traiecto, inferioris Germaniæ ciuitate. Pontificem egit annum unum. Vide ut supra. FRANCISCVS FRAN. R INVIC. CLAVDIA FRAN. REG.
units.tr: ADRIAN, the sixth Pope of this name, once tutor of Charles, who still rules as emperor, was substituted for the aforementioned Leo, who was absent, in the year of the world 5483, from the birth of Christ 1521. Being a most eminent theologian, he combined learning and gravity with a certain agreeable seriousness of manners, as his writings attest. Since his life was frugal, he pleased many Romans but little. He was very sparing in conferring ecclesiastical offices, because he judged that they should be given to none but the fit and learned. He was by nation a Teuton, from Utrecht, a city of Lower Germany. He held the papacy for one year. See above. FRANCIS, FRANCIS, R., INVICTUS, CLAUDIA, FRANCIS, REG.

units.la: FRANCISCVS Valesius, defuncto Ludouico huius nominis duodecimo, nulla relicta prole masculea, vt sanguine propior in Regem inungitur anno mundi 5476. à Christo nato 1514. Hic Mediolanum statim recuperat. Ducè Maximilianum Sfortiam capit: de Heluetiis victoriam reportat insignem. Posthæc in Flandriam Imperatorem Carolum quintum fugat anno Domini 1521. Hisdinum eodem anno Boibonio [?] Duce expugnatur, cuius arx tormentis bellicis per aliquot dies concussa, in deditionem regiâ venit. Anno sequente Fotarabia, in confinio Hispaniæ capitur, ac præsidio munitur, postea Angli cum Cæsarianis Hisdinensem arcem duobus mensibus frustrà obsident: extremámque Picardiæ oram latè populatur. At verò, post annum vnum atque alterum, dum Papiam obsidet Franciscus Valesius, subiugata iam tota serè Lombardia, à transfugis, qui fidem Imperatori dederant (ô fortem iniquam, ac in re bellica, si vsquam alibi dominatè!) in ipso pugnæ calore, fortiter se gerès ac dimicàs, nihilominus capitur, mense Februario anni à Christo nato 1524. fœdus tandem initur apud Cameracum, illustrium ac prudentissimarum Heroinarum Gallicarum opera, anno à Christo nato 1529. videlicet inter Franciscum Valesium, Carolum Imperatorè, & Papâ Clemetem 7. Videto Chro. Reg. Fran. Ioânem Cario. li. 3. & Paralipomena rerum memorabilium.
units.tr: FRANCIS of Valois, on the death of Louis the twelfth of this name, leaving no male offspring, was anointed king as being the nearer by blood, in the year of the world 5476, from the birth of Christ 1514. He at once recovered Milan. He captured the Duke Maximilian Sforza. He won a notable victory over the Swiss. Afterwards he put to flight the Emperor Charles the Fifth in Flanders, in the year of the Lord 1521. Hesdin was taken the same year by the Duke of Bourbon [?], whose citadel, shaken for some days by siege artillery, came into the king's hands in surrender. The following year Fontarabia, on the border of Spain, was captured and garrisoned. Afterwards the English, with the Imperialists, besieged the citadel of Hesdin for two months in vain, and widely ravaged the farthest edge of Picardy. But then, a year or more later, while Francis of Valois was besieging Pavia, and nearly all Lombardy had already been subdued, he was nevertheless captured in the heat of battle, where he was fighting bravely, by deserters who had pledged their loyalty to the Emperor (O unjust fortune, and, if ever anywhere, dominant in matters of war!), in the month of February of the year from the birth of Christ 1524. At last a treaty was concluded at Cambrai, through the work of illustrious and most prudent French heroines, in the year from the birth of Christ 1529, namely between Francis of Valois, the Emperor Charles, and Pope Clement the Seventh. See the Chronicle of the Kings of France by John Carion, book 3, and the Paralipomena rerum memorabilium.

units.la: CLAVDIA, maior natu filia Ludouici, huius nominis duodecimi, Francorum Regis, mense Maio anni mundi 5475. & à Christo nato 1513. Francisco Valesio, qui paulò post regnat, nupsit: erat tunc temporis Franciscus ille Valesius Angolismorum Dux: qui ex ea complures liberos suflulit: inter quos præcipui duo superstites hodie sunt, nempe Henricus Francorum Rex nobilissimus ac potentissimus, & Margareta eius soror illustrissima simul ac pientissima. Vide vt supra. IMP. CAES. CAROLVS V AV ISABELLA CAR. V[?]
units.tr: CLAUDIA, the elder daughter of Louis, the twelfth of this name, King of the Franks, in the month of May of the year of the world 5475, and from the birth of Christ 1513, married Francis of Valois, who shortly afterwards reigned; at that time Francis of Valois was Duke of Angoulême. From her he raised several children, of whom two principal ones survive today, namely Henry, the most noble and most powerful King of the Franks, and his most illustrious and at the same time most pious sister Margaret. See above. IMP. CAES. CHARLES V AV, ISABELLA CAR. V [?]

units.la: CAROLVS quintus, Philippi Austriæ Archiducis filius, post auum Maximilianum imperat anno mundi 5481. à Christo nato 1519. postea Bononiæ à Clemente Pontifice imperiali diademate coronatus est anno D. 1529. porrò anno sequente ingentem exercitum per Germaniam in Hügariā duxit aduersus Turcam Viennā obsidentē. Inde victoriam reportans in Hispaniam rediit. Anno autem 1535. in Tunetim expeditionē parans, quæ olim Carthago erat, eam Solimano Turcæ extorquet: Gouletā arcē expugnat: regnūque Tunitiū totū recipit, &c Regē Altzachenū antè pulsū restituit, multis Christianis captiuis liberatis. Frācia bis tētauit, sed Frāci milites validissimis armis eius impetū forti animo sustinuere. Semel in Francia tanquā amicus summo apparatu exceptus est, ex Hispania in Flādriā per Galliā iter sibi fecit. At enim an. 1543. cū potentissimo exercitu Germaniā tandē ingressus, eam ferè totā in suā vertit sententiā, captis etiā aliquot Germanorū Ducibus ac primoribus: à quibus atq; ab vrbibus Germaniæ olim liberis, ingētē auri vim corrasit. Anno verò 1551. in Africā Libyę ciuitatē exercitū traiecit, principe Doria præfecto, quam feliciter expugnauit, solutis nō paucis captiuis Christianis. An. 1552. Confœderatis aliquot Germanorum Principibus cū Henrico Christianiss. Francorū Rege, ea gratia vt eos ab Imperatoris iugo excuteret, pedem in Villacū Carolus quasi coactus reculit: sed intra paucos dies re cū aliquot Germanis primoribus cōposita, cōparato maximo Germanorū exercitu, ipse Mediomatricū, vrbē prius ab Hērico Rege captam, ac Francicis armis munitam obsedit: vbi nouercam fortunam expertus, obsidionem soluere cogitur, cum non modica suorum strage ac damno, partim ob temporis inclementiam, partim ob Francorum robur ac vigilantiam.
units.tr: CHARLES the fifth, son of Philip, Archduke of Austria, succeeded his grandfather Maximilian as emperor in the year of the world 5481, from the birth of Christ 1519. Afterwards at Bologna he was crowned with the imperial diadem by Pope Clement, in the year of the Lord 1529. Then in the following year he led a huge army through Germany into Hungary against the Turk, who was besieging Vienna. From there, having gained a victory, he returned to Spain. In the year 1535, preparing an expedition to Tunis, which was once Carthage, he wrested it from Suleiman the Turk; he stormed the citadel of La Goletta and recovered the whole kingdom of Tunis, and restored the king Muley Hassan, who had been driven out before, many Christian captives being freed. He twice attempted France, but the French soldiers with the most powerful arms sustained his attack with brave spirit. Once he was received in France with the greatest display as a friend, and he made his way from Spain through France into Flanders. But in the year 1543, with a most powerful army, he at last entered Germany and turned almost the whole of it to his own opinion, several German dukes and nobles also being taken; from these and from the cities of Germany, once free, he gathered a huge amount of gold. In the year 1551, under the command of the prince Doria, he transported an army to Libya, a city in Africa, which he successfully stormed, many Christian captives being released. In the year 1552, with some confederated German princes and with Henry, the most Christian King of the Franks, with the purpose of shaking them off from the yoke of the Emperor, Charles, as if compelled, withdrew his foot from Villach; but within a few days, the matter having been settled with some German nobles, and having gathered the greatest German army, he himself besieged Metz, a city previously taken by King Henry and fortified with French arms; there, having experienced an unkind fortune, he was forced to abandon the siege, with no small slaughter and loss of his men, partly because of the harshness of the weather, partly because of the strength and vigilance of the French.

units.la: ISABELLA Portugalliæ Regis filia, Caroli prędicti vxor peperit ei liberos quatuor, atque in partu vltimo emoritur. CAROLUS RUINUS REGIENSIS. FRANC. CURTIUS PAPIENSIS.
units.tr: ISABELLA, daughter of the King of Portugal, wife of the aforementioned Charles, bore him four children, and died in her last childbirth. CHARLES RUINUS OF REGGIO. FRANCIS CURTIUS OF PAVIA.

units.la: CAROLVS Ruinus, Regiensis Iurisconsultus inter alios celebris & magni nominis, qui ius Bononię docuit, tanto iudicio, ut ęqualem aliis doctioribus Iuris professoribus, gloria comparauerit. Indefessus fuit in obeundo munere, & plures discipulos habuit, à quibus & amatus est & summe reueritus. Scripsit super prima & secunda Digesti noui. Item Consiliorum volumina quinque impressa Venetiis & Lugduni. Floruit anno reparatę salutis humanę 1520. Vide Conradum Gesnerum, & librum, De vita Iurisconsultorum.
units.tr: CHARLES Ruinus, a jurist of Reggio, famous among others and of great name, who taught law at Bologna with such judgment that he won equal glory with the other more learned professors of law. He was tireless in discharging his duty, and had many pupils, by whom he was both loved and greatly revered. He wrote on the first and second of the New Digest. Also five volumes of Consilia, printed at Venice and at Lyon. He flourished in the year of restored human salvation 1520. See Conrad Gesner, and the book On the Lives of the Jurists.

units.la: FRANCISCVS Curtius Iurisconsultus clarissimus extitit, qui de iure itidem multa scripsit ad communem eorum utilitatem qui legibus dant operam. Scripsit super C. in tit. de iura. calumnię. Fecit additiones ad Practicam Ioannis Petri de Ferrariis. De moneta super 2. ff. veteris, si certum petatur, l.cum quid. Super 1. C. de prohib. seq. pecun. lege prima, Quoties. De sequestris. De testibus. Consiliorum volumen unum. Et plurima alia usui forensi accommodata. Franciscus Curtius Iunior, Papiensis ius etiam professus est, ut scriptis declarauit plurimis. Scripsit enim super 1. & 2. ff. veteris. De feudis. Consiliorum volumen. &c. Florebant anno. 1533. Vide Conradum Gesnerum, in sua Bibliotheca, & librum, De vita Iurisconsultorum. ERASM. ROT. GVILLERM. BVD.
units.tr: FRANCISCUS Curtius, a most distinguished jurist, also wrote much on law for the common benefit of those who devote themselves to the laws. He wrote on C. in tit. de iura calumniae. He made additions to the Practica of Johannes Petrus de Ferrariis. On the coinage, on 2 ff. veteris, si certum petatur, l. cum quid. On 1 C. de prohib. seq. pecun., the first law, Quoties. On sequestrations. On witnesses. One volume of Consilia. And many other works suited to the use of the courts. Franciscus Curtius the Younger, of Pavia, also taught law, as he made clear in many of his writings. For he wrote on 1 and 2 ff. veteris, on feuds, a volume of Consilia, etc. He flourished in the year 1533. See Conrad Gesner in his Bibliotheca, and the book De vita Iurisconsultorum. ERASM. ROT. GUILLERM. BUD.

units.la: ERASMVS Roterodamus, maximo honore, propter multiplicem eruditionem extollendus videtur: superauit enim omnes suę ętatis, ingenij fertilitate, scriptores. Is ab adolescentia, religiosa voluntate motus, ad cucullatos sacerdotes se contulit, quòd humana despiceret: sed paulo post vestem cucullatorum depositu, & septa ordinis pertransiliit, vt ad excolendum ingenium plane liber, per omnia Europę gymnasia vagaretur. Contendebat enim ingenti cura, ad summę glorię fastigiũ ad quod literarum omnium cognitione, peruenirì posse intelligebat, vt peruenit, quemadmodũ eius infinita scripta tàm humana quàm diuina testantur, quę sigillatim recensere non opus est, cũ eorũ titulos vix hęc pagina capere posset. Obiit apud Heluetios Basileę, septuagesimum excedens ętatis annum, quum Carolus Cęsar in Prouinciam irrumpens, ad aquas Sextias, Francisco Galliarum Regi graue bellum intulisset.
units.tr: ERASMUS of Rotterdam deserves to be praised with the greatest honour on account of his manifold learning. For in the fertility of his genius he surpassed all the writers of his age. From youth, moved by a religious impulse, he attached himself to the hooded priests, because he despised the things of humanity. But soon after he laid aside the habit of the hooded orders and leapt over the hedges of the order, so that, quite free to cultivate his talent, he wandered through all the schools of Europe. For he strove with great care towards the summit of highest glory, which he understood could be reached by a knowledge of all letters, as he did reach it, as his infinite writings, both secular and sacred, bear witness. There is no need to list these one by one, since this page could scarcely contain their titles. He died among the Swiss at Basel, in his seventy-first year, when Charles the Emperor, bursting into Provence, had waged grievous war on Francis, King of the French, at Aix.

units.la: GVLIELMVS Budęus Parisiensis, vtriusque linguę persecta cognitione ita excelluit, vt non Gallię modò, sed totius etiam Europę longè doctissimus certò haberetur. Perennem semper spectauit laudem: & rei familiaris fortunas honoresque ingenio suo & sperata gloria viliores arbitratus, sexaginta amplius ętatis annos, in studiis consumpsit: ita vt summę eruditionis libro de Asse, alterôque in Pandectas edito, ac infinita demũ lectione confectis Commentariis, quibus Græcę & Latinę facultatis ornamenta comparantur, nulli communicata laude, æquales omnes, doctrinę auctoritate superarit. Huius optimi viri otium Rex Franciscus ita fouit, vt eum supplicibus [?] libellis pręposuerit. Febre oppressus est cùm septuagesimum tertium annum ageret, & vita excedens, condito testamēto, omnes honores funeris & tumuli penitus abdicauit, ita vt noctu sepultus fuerit. Floruit anno salutis 1535. [?]URC. IMP. SELIMUS SULTAN SULIMAN[?]
units.tr: GUILLAUME Budé of Paris, through a perfect knowledge of both languages, excelled so greatly that he was certainly held to be by far the most learned not only in France but in all of Europe. He always aimed at lasting praise, and judging the fortunes and honours of his household to be of less worth than his talent and the glory he hoped for, he spent more than sixty years of his life in study. So much so that, by his books of the highest learning, On the As, and another published on the Pandects, and finally his commentaries completed by endless reading, by which the ornaments of Greek and Latin learning are provided, he surpassed all his equals in authority of learning, without sharing the praise with anyone. King Francis cherished the leisure of this excellent man so much that he placed him above the petitions and libels. Overcome by fever in his seventy-third year, he departed this life; having made his will, he entirely renounced all honours of funeral and tomb, so that he was buried by night. He flourished in the year of salvation 1535. [?]URC. IMP. SELIMUS SULTAN SULIMAN[?]

units.la: SELIMUS itaque pulso patre imperat Turcis anno mundi 5472. à Christo nato 1510. Is ad parricidium adiecit fratrum caedem, nepotumque strangulatione. Sophim vicit ac fugauit: & Sultanos duos, Campsonem & Tomobeium, multis deleuit praeliis. Aegyptum Arabiamque suo adiecit imperio. Reuersus Constantinopolim ulcus in renibus contraxit, quod canceris in morem serpens eum extinxit, anno regni 7. Vide Cosm.Munst. li. 4. Paul. Iou. & Riche. liu. 1.
units.tr: SELIM, therefore, having driven out his father, ruled over the Turks in the year of the world 5472, from the birth of Christ 1510. To his parricide he added the slaughter of his brothers and the strangling of his nephews. He conquered and routed the Shah of Persia, and destroyed the two sultans, Campson and Tomobeius, in many battles. He added Egypt and Arabia to his empire. Returning to Constantinople, he contracted an ulcer in the kidneys, which, creeping like a cancer, carried him off in the seventh year of his reign. See Cosmography of Münster, book 4, Paulus Jovius, and Richer, book 1.

units.la: SOLIMANUS Selimi, siue Zelimi filius unicus, Imperat Turcis post patrem anno mūdi 5480. à Christo nato 1518. eodem fere tempore quo Carolus, qui nunc imperat, creatus est. Hic Solimanus qui etiam nunc regnat, Belgradum, Christianorum propugnaculum anno regni 3. expugnat, atque anno 6. Rhodum, cum 400. nauibus ac 200000. Turcarum capit. Anno octauo Hungariam invadit, igne ferroque devastat: Ludovicū Regem Hungariae vincit, Budam in deditionem accipit. Anno vero 14. maximo exercitu Viennam oppugnans, auxilio Dei ac Germanorum virtute, fugatur. Hic natura gloriae cupidus, atque ob victorias quamplurimas imperiique magnitudine elatus, Romae, totiusque occidentis imperium ad se spectare contendit, cum Imperatoris Constantini, qui imperium transtulit Constantinopolim, legitimum successorem se profiteatur: sexagies centena aureorum millia quotannis habet: quoties populos censere libet, ex bellis plus lucratur quam in damno sit, plus gemmarum ac thesaurorum possidet, quam caeteri omnes orbis principes simul possideant. Vide Pau. Iou. qui etiam Papae negligentia Rhodum Turcis deditam fuisse scribit.
units.tr: SULEIMAN, the only son of Selim, or Zelim, ruled over the Turks after his father in the year of the world 5480, from the birth of Christ 1518, at about the same time as Charles, who now reigns, was created emperor. This Suleiman, who still reigns, took Belgrade, the bulwark of the Christians, in the third year of his reign, and in the sixth year took Rhodes with 400 ships and 200,000 Turks. In the eighth year he invaded Hungary and laid it waste with fire and sword; he defeated Louis, King of Hungary, and received Buda in surrender. In the fourteenth year, attacking Vienna with a very great army, he was put to flight by the help of God and the valour of the Germans. Being by nature eager for glory, and elated by his many victories and the greatness of his empire, he contended that Rome and the whole empire of the West pertained to him, and he professed himself the lawful successor of the Emperor Constantine, who transferred the empire to Constantinople. He has six thousand thousand gold pieces a year [sixty times one hundred thousand]; as often as one cares to assess the peoples, he gains more from wars than he suffers in loss; he possesses more jewels and treasures than all the other princes of the world possess together. See Paulus Jovius, who also writes that Rhodes was surrendered to the Turks through the negligence of the Pope.

units.la: CHRISTIERNVS Ioannis Daniæ Regis filius, post patris obitum Danorum Rex, nullum non lapidem mouit quo regnum Suecię suo regno adiiceret: quod & tandem partim vi armorum, partim dolo assecutus est: sed tamē non diu administrauit: quinimo tantum abest vt retinere potuerit, vt etiam patrio ac peculiari suo regno Daniæ ob tyrānidem deturbaretur, atque exul in Angliam vnà cū vxore profugeret, anno à mundo condito 5484. à Christo nato 1522. Cæterum cùm Daniam recuperare tentaret, à Christiano, patruo suo, captus est, atque in carcerem cõiectus, vbi diem clausit extremum. Vide Cosmog. Mun. li.4. de regnis Septentrionalibus: item nouam temporum continuationem Germani cuiusdam, ad Euse.Chro. adiectam: præterea Carionis Chro. li.3. qui loco Daniæ scribit Regē Christiernum Daciæ: vnde colligendum Daniam, & Daciam, interim confundi, nam & Volater. li. 7. sic inquit: Nunc sanè Cimbricam Chersonesum Daciam vocant, cui Rex præest qui Suetiam & Noruegiam, peninsulas, in eodem mari obtinet, Ptolemæo & antiquis minimè positas, quòd ignotæ atque incompertæ tunc essent.
units.tr: CHRISTIERN, son of John, King of Denmark, after his father's death became King of the Danes. He left no stone unturned to add the kingdom of Sweden to his own; this he finally achieved partly by force of arms, partly by guile. But he did not hold it long; indeed, so far was he from being able to keep it that he was even driven from his hereditary and particular kingdom of Denmark on account of his tyranny, and fled into exile in England with his wife, in the year 5484 from the creation of the world, 1522 from the birth of Christ. However, when he tried to recover Denmark, he was captured by Christian, his uncle, and thrown into prison, where he ended his last day. See the Cosmography of Münster, book 4, on the northern kingdoms; likewise the new continuation of the times by a certain German, added to Eusebius's Chronicle; besides Carion's Chronicle, book 3, which in place of Denmark writes King Christiern of Dacia. From this it is to be gathered that Denmark and Dacia are meanwhile confused; for Volaterranus also says in book 7: "Now indeed they call the Cimbrian Chersonese Dacia, over which a king presides who holds Sweden and Norway, peninsulas in the same sea, which were by no means placed there by Ptolemy and the ancients, because they were then unknown and unexplored."

units.la: ISABELLA Caroli Imperatoris huius nominis quinti soror, nupsit Christierno Danię Regi supradicto, qui ex ea liberos sustulit, Dorotheam Friderici Palatini vxorem, & Christianam, Lotharingiæ Ducissam. Vide vt suprà. ROMAN. REX. FERDINÃ DVS. ANNA FERDINA [?]
units.tr: ISABELLA, sister of the Emperor Charles the Fifth of that name, married the aforesaid Christiern, King of Denmark, by whom she bore children: Dorothea, wife of Frederick the Palatine, and Christina, Duchess of Lorraine. See as above. ROMAN. KING. FERDINAND. ANNA FERDINA [?]

units.la: FERDINANDVS Philippi Austriæ Archiducis ac Castellæ Regis minor natu filius, Caroli hoc nomine Imperatoris quinti frater, vxorem accepit Annam Vladislaj Hungariæ ac Bohemiæ Regis filiam vnicam, sororémq; eádem Ludouici Hungariæ ac Bohemiæ Regis vltimi per cuius obitũ iure hæreditario hæc regna possedit. Posthæc in Romanorum Regem Coloniæ creatus est anno D. 1530. atque anno proximè sequente Aquisgrani coronatus est. Porrò an. 1540. expeditionem in Budam suscepit aduersus Georgium Monachũ, Vaiuodæ filij tutorem, qui Budam occupabat. Verumenimuero Georgius hic implorato à Solymäno auxilio, Ferdinandũ pedem referre coegit: qui saluti suæ cõsules in trãsitu Danubij, vt sunt belli euentus varij, bonam exercitus partem amisit: quamobrẽ hac victoria potitus Solymanus, Budam ipsam occupauit, ac prædictum Georgium Monachum, vnà cum Vaiuodæ filio in Transsylvaniam expulit. Vide Chron. Carionis lib. 3. & Paralip. re. memo. Imperauit annos 6. menses 4. dies 13. & primo anno sui imperij, Carolus Quintus Augustus præclarissimæ memoriæ Imperator obiit xi. kalendas Octobris, in cænobio monachorũ Hieronymianorum S. Iusti, Toletanæ Diocesis. Fuit iste Ferdinandus multis virtutibus ornatus, & tam iustè imperauit, vt eius memoria non minus colatur, quàm Philippi patris, & Caroli fratris inuictissimi & bellicosissimi. Viennæ obiit octauo Kalendas Augusti, anno Domini 1563.
units.tr: FERDINAND, the younger son of Philip, Archduke of Austria and King of Castile, brother of the Emperor Charles the Fifth of that name, took as his wife Anne, the only daughter of Vladislaus, King of Hungary and Bohemia, and sister of the same Louis, the last King of Hungary and Bohemia, by whose death he possessed these kingdoms by hereditary right. Afterwards he was created King of the Romans at Cologne in the year of the Lord 1530, and in the following year was crowned at Aachen. Moreover, in the year 1540 he undertook an expedition against Buda, against George the Monk, guardian of the son of the Voivode, who was occupying Buda. But this George, having implored the help of Suleiman, forced Ferdinand to withdraw; and Ferdinand, taking thought for his safety while crossing the Danube, as the outcomes of war are various, lost a good part of his army. Wherefore Suleiman, having gained this victory, occupied Buda itself, and drove the aforesaid George the Monk, together with the Voivode's son, into Transylvania. See Carion's Chronicle, book 3, and Paralipomena rerum memorabilium. He reigned six years, four months, thirteen days; and in the first year of his reign, the Emperor Charles the Fifth Augustus, of most illustrious memory, died on the eleventh day before the Kalends of October, in the monastery of the Hieronymite monks of St. Just, in the diocese of Toledo. This Ferdinand was adorned with many virtues, and ruled so justly that his memory is honoured no less than that of his father Philip and of his brother Charles, most unconquered and most warlike. He died at Vienna on the eighth day before the Kalends of August, in the year of the Lord 1563.

units.la: ANNA Hungariæ Regis filia, prædicti Ferdinandi vxor, speciosa quidem, proba & viro gratissima fuit: ex quo etiam liberos complures, chara coniugalis amicitiæ pignora, suscepit. Vide vt suprà.
units.tr: ANNA, daughter of the King of Hungary, wife of the aforesaid Ferdinand, was indeed beautiful, virtuous, and most pleasing to her husband; from her he also received several children, dear pledges of conjugal affection. See as above.

units.la: CAROLVS Sabaudię Dux, ex antiqua ac illustri Saxoniæ familia oriundus, fratri suo Philiberto cognomine pulchro, qui nulla relicta stirpe obierat, successit. Porrò anno à Christo nato 1535. Carolus hic Allobrogum Ducatu, ac maxima Pedemontii parte deturbatus est: nam urbes atque arces quamplurimas partim expugnat, partim in deditionem accepit Frācifcus Valesius: tum quòd Gallicanis expeditionibus infestissima semper hæc gens esset, tum quòd ius suum persequeretur in hæc ipsa Sabaudiæ territoria. Vide Chro. Sabaudiæ, & Supplem. Chro.
units.tr: CHARLES, Duke of Savoy, sprung from an ancient and illustrious Saxon family, succeeded his brother Philibert, surnamed the Fair, who had died leaving no offspring. Moreover, in the year of Christ's birth 1535, this Charles was driven from the Duchy of the Allobroges and from the greater part of Piedmont; for Francis of Valois captured and took in surrender very many towns and citadels, partly by assault, partly by surrender; both because this people had always been most hostile to the French expeditions, and because he pursued his own right over these very territories of Savoy. See the Chronicle of Savoy and the Supplementary Chronicle.

units.la: BEATRIX Portugalliæ Regis filia, sorórque uxoris ipsius Imperatoris Caroli quinti, liberali ac eleganti forma Princeps, Carolo supradicto Duci nupsit, ex eóque Philiberti, qui Princeps Sabaudiæ vocatur, suscepit. Cęterùm hæc cùm deploratę sibi in Sabaudia & Pedemontio res essent, Niciam concessit, ac post paucos annos decessit. Vide Chron. P. M. CLEMENS VII ODET DE FOIX S DE LAL[?]
units.tr: BEATRIX, daughter of the King of Portugal and sister of the Emperor Charles V's wife, a Princess of gentle manners and elegant bearing, married the aforesaid Duke Charles and bore him Philibert, who is called the Prince of Savoy. However, since affairs in Savoy and Piedmont had come to a desperate state, she withdrew to Nice, and died a few years later. See the Chronicle.

units.la: CLEMENS, huius nóminis Papa septimus, Adriano supradicto in Pontificatu successit anno mundi 5484. à Christo nato 1522. Hic antea Iulius vocabatur, sed Cardinalium quorundam suasu, Clementis nomen assumpsit. Fuit Leo decimus huic patruelis. Dicitur Clemens fauisse Francorum Regi Francisco etiam capto, aduersus Cæsarem Carolu: ideoq; Romā ab exercitu Cæsaris, cui præerat Carolus Borbonius, direptā ac expilatam, nihilominus tamen ab hoc coronā accepit Carolus imperialem, præterea sacram vnctionem: fuit rarissimi ac callidissimi ingenij. Frācisci Valesij partes iterum secutus, ad Massiliam cum eo conuenit, initúmque est marrimoniū[?] proneptis suæ Catharinæ Laurentij Medices Ducis Vrbinatis filiæ, cum Henrico Duce Aurelianensi, nunc autem Francorum Rege. Florētiam vrbem patriam obsedit, quā post annum obsidionis cepit: Ducémque in ea constituit Alexādrū Medices, prædicti Laurentij Medices filium naturalem. Aiunt prouocatum à Florentinis id bellum gessisse, qui in cognatos ac necessarios huius Clementis infesti essent, atque etiā in ipsum Pontificem infensi: vitio tamen illi interim vertitur, quôd in patriam ita sæuierit, quam etiam velut sub iugum miserit: sedit annis 12. Vide Iouium, Supplem. Chro. & Platinam.
units.tr: CLEMENT, the seventh Pope of that name, succeeded Adrian in the pontificate in the year of the world 5484, from the birth of Christ 1522. He was previously called Giulio, but at the persuasion of certain Cardinals he took the name Clement. He was a cousin of Leo X. Clement is said to have favoured the French King Francis, even after his capture, against the Emperor Charles; and therefore Rome was sacked and plundered by the Emperor's army, which was commanded by Charles of Bourbon. Nevertheless, it was from this Pope that Charles received the imperial crown and, besides, the sacred anointing. He was a man of rare and most crafty genius. Following the party of Francis Valois again, he met him at Marseilles, and the marriage was arranged between Catherine, his great-niece, daughter of Lorenzo de' Medici, Duke of Urbino, and Henry, Duke of Orléans, now King of the French. He besieged his native city of Florence, which he took after a year's siege, and he appointed as its Duke Alessandro de' Medici, the natural son of the aforesaid Lorenzo de' Medici. They say the war was waged at the provocation of the Florentines, who were hostile to the relatives and dependants of this Clement, and indeed hostile to the Pontiff himself; yet he is meanwhile blamed for having raged so fiercely against his fatherland, which he also sent, as it were, under the yoke. He sat for 12 years. See Giovio, the Supplement to the Chronicle, and Platina.

units.la: ODETVS de Foix, dictus Lautretius, Mediolani sub Francisco Valesio praefectus, deinde exercitus Gallici in Italia Dux, Papiā & Alexandriā expugnauit: Neapolim exercitu duxit: quô dū tederet Clementi, quē Aurafiensis Princeps sub custodia tenebat, opē attulit: Porrò vbi Neapolim peruenit, arridētis fortunæ occasione captare nesciuit: nā cominus si vrbē aggressus esset, hāc facilè cepisset: sed interim dū eminus nimis cūctatur, Neapolis auxiliares Hispanos milites recipit: tandē tum ob aeris intemperantiam, tum ob aquas veneno infectas cum multis aliis Gallorū primoribus periit an. D. 1528. Vide Suppl. & Iouium. BOR. CAROL. DUX. LEVA. ANTONIUS DE
units.tr: ODET de Foix, called Lautrec, appointed governor of Milan under Francis Valois and afterwards Duke of the French army in Italy, took Pavia and Alessandria; he led the army to Naples, where he brought aid to Clement, who was held under guard by the Prince of Orange, since he was growing weary of it. But when he came to Naples, he did not know how to seize the opportunity that fortune offered: for if he had attacked the city at close quarters, he could easily have taken it; but meanwhile, while he delayed too long from a distance, Naples received Spanish auxiliary soldiers. At length, partly because of the unhealthiness of the air, partly because of water infected with poison, he died, with many other leading Frenchmen, in the year of the Lord 1528. See the Supplement and Giovio.

units.la: CAROLUS Borbonij Dux, Comitis Gilberti à Montepēserio filius,Janam Ducatus Borbonij hęredem unicam,duxit uxorem:hunc Gilbertum præfectum Neapoli reliquit Carolus octauus.Porrò Carolus eius filius Magister equitum , seu Connestabilis , à Francisco Valesio creatus est anno à Christo nato 1516. Fuit quidem princeps hic magnanimus ac bellicosus , sed qui ob factionem quandam ad Imperatorem deficiens,cladem patriænon minimam attulit:tandémque in expugnatione Romæ occisus est. Nam ipsi stanti in scalis , globusænej[?] tormenti parum caute à suis emissus(ut est plena periculi eiu,[?] generis armorum tractatio)crus alterum sub femore perfregit, quo ex vulnere post unum atque alterum diem , animam exhalauit. Vide Chron. Regum Franc. & re. memor.Paral.
units.tr: CHARLES, Duke of Bourbon, son of Count Gilbert of Montpensier, married Jeanne, the sole heiress of the Duchy of Bourbon. Charles VIII left this Gilbert as governor of Naples. Moreover, his son Charles, appointed Master of the Horse, or Constable, by Francis Valois, in the year of Christ's birth 1516. This Prince was indeed magnanimous and warlike, but, deserting to the Emperor because of a certain faction, he inflicted no small disaster upon his fatherland; and at last he was killed in the storming of Rome. For while he was standing on the ladders, a cannonball, carelessly fired by his own men (as the handling of such weapons is full of danger), broke his other leg below the thigh, and from this wound, after a day or two, he breathed his last. See the Chronicle of the Kings of France and the Memorable Deeds of Paralipomenon.

units.la: ANTONIUS Leva,Mediolano primùm,deinde expediti-oni Cæsarianæ præfectus , cùm paralysi laboraret, in cathedra sedens circumferebatur:industrius quidē ille , ac in rebus bellicis arte Pelasga, quasi alter Sinon instructissimus. Moritur præ dolore uani ac casi in Massiliam conatus:cùm eius spe potiunde , à Melforum Principe ad eam recipiendā ex Italia prudenter ac callidè euocatus esset:nempe ea arte ut in Taurinũ susceptam ab ipso expeditionem auerteret,anno à Christo Seruatore nato 1535.
units.tr: ANTONIO de Leyva, first governor of Milan, then of the Imperial expedition, since he suffered from paralysis, was carried about seated in a chair. He was a diligent man, and in matters of war most skilled in the Pelasgian art, like a second Sinon most thoroughly equipped. He died of grief at his vain and fruitless attempt on Marseilles, since, when he had been prudently and craftily summoned from Italy by the Prince of Melfi to take it, with the hope of gaining that city, he had in fact been led on by the art of turning aside from Turin the expedition undertaken against it by himself, in the year of Christ our Saviour's birth 1535.

units.la: ANDREAS Doria, nobili apud Genuenses ortus familia, ineũte ętate nō vno sub principe stipedia meruit. Verùm cū se terrestri Marte laudē inuenturū dissideret, ad suū rediit elemētū:quatuórque triremibus à ciuibus suis præfectus, Gallorum primū, mox Pōtificis partes fouit:à quo duabus auctus triremibus,denuo sese ad Gallos cōuertit.Nec multò post vniuersę regiæ classi præfectus, & insigni equitum D. Michaëlis torque exornatus, strenuam aliquandiu Regi operā nauauit. Post hæc Marchione Vasti,aliísq; nōnullis Cæsarianarū partiū ducibus, Philippini nepotis suí opera non procul à Neapoli captis, cùm Rex eos ad se mitti identidem iuberet, iustúmq; redemptionis pretiū eorum nomine offerret,Doria tantarū rerū successu elatior factus,constanter id recusauit: tādémque Marchionis Vasti suasu[?] ad Cæsarem defecit: qui ob singularem rei naualis peritiam,tātum honoris ei detulit,vt non alio,quàm Patris nomine, eum vnquam salutauerit. Ciuibus quoque suis tam charus extitit,vt marmoream illi statuam in foro posuerint, Patrísque patriæ appellatione exornarint. Vide Paulum Iouium, & Supplem. Chron.
units.tr: ANDREA Doria, born in the noble family among the Genoese, earned his pay under more than one prince in his early youth. But when he despaired of winning glory by land warfare, he returned to his own element, and, appointed by his fellow citizens to command four galleys, he first favoured the French, and then the party of the Pontiff; having been strengthened by two galleys from him, he turned again to the French. Soon after, appointed commander of the whole royal fleet and adorned with the distinguished collar of the Order of St Michael, he rendered for some time vigorous service to the King. After this, when the Marquess of Vasto and some other leaders of the Imperial party had been captured near Naples through the work of his nephew Filippino, and the King repeatedly ordered them to be sent to him and offered a just ransom price for them, Doria, growing more elated by the success of such great affairs, steadfastly refused it; and at last, at the persuasion of the Marquess of Vasto, he defected to the Emperor, who, on account of his singular skill in naval affairs, bestowed such honour upon him that he never greeted him by any other name than that of Father. He was so dear to his fellow citizens that they placed a marble statue of him in the forum and adorned him with the title Father of the Fatherland. See Paulus Jovius and the Supplement to the Chronicle.

units.la: PHILIPPINVS Doria, edito sub Vrbinatiū Duce singularis suæ virtutis specimine, Comitis dignitatē &prouentum est adeptus.Rebúsq; deinde plurimis præclarissimē gestis, tandem Andreæ patrui, Gallicæ classis præfecti, vice fungens, cum Cæsarianis non procul à Neapoli nauali prælio congressus, insigni victoria potitus est, anno 1527. capto Marchione Vasti, aliísque non paucis tũ Italorū tũ Hispanorū proceribus, triremibúsque aliquot, partim captis, partim depressis. Et Biennio pòst incredibili pōpa copiarū Genuēsiū Dux adoptatus, post res plurimas Caroli Cæsaris auspiciis feliciter gestas, fatis concessit. FERRA IIII HERCULES II D[?] HERC FERD D VXOR. UXOR[?] RENATA
units.tr: PHILIPPINO Doria, having displayed a singular specimen of his courage under the Duke of Urbino, obtained the dignity and revenue of a Count. Then, after performing very many most distinguished deeds, at last, acting as deputy for his uncle Andrea, commander of the French fleet, he engaged the Imperialists in a naval battle not far from Naples and gained a notable victory in the year 1527, the Marquess of Vasto being captured, together with not a few other leaders, both Italian and Spanish, and several galleys, some taken, some sunk. And two years later, having been adopted as Doge of Genoa with incredible pomp of troops, after many deeds performed successfully under the auspices of Charles the Emperor, he died.

units.la: HERCULES Estensis, Alphonsi Ferrariæ Ducis filius, non tam parentis gloria aut stabili illius, pacatóque Principatus statu, quàm singulari sua virtute, ac moribus planè heroïcis, Renatę Ludovici duodecimi Gallorū Regis filię coniugio est potitus: quam incredibili apparatu, pōpáque prorsus regia uxorem duxit Lutetię Parisiorū anno 1528. Post hæc Alphonso patre è vivis sublato, in Principatu ei successit anno 1534. multáque heroicarum, non modò specimina, verum etiam exempla edidit. Ditionem singulari prudētia administravit, & inter tot belli tumultus, quibus tota propemodum concussa est Italia, trāquillā incolumémque conservavit. Jus severè & integrè imprimis dicendum curavit: Academiam celeberrimā, disciplinarum omnium altricem, Ferrariæ instituit, eámque accitis undique maximi nominis professoribus, singulari studio ac liberalitate fovit. Sub huius Principatu cùm alij propemodum innumeri, tum singulare illud Italicorum Poëtarum decus, Ludovicus Ariostus emicuit.
units.tr: HERCULES of Este, son of Alfonso, Duke of Ferrara, obtained the marriage with Renée, daughter of Louis XII, King of the French, not so much through his father's glory or the stable and peaceful condition of his principality, as through his own singular virtue and truly heroic character. He married her at Paris in the year 1528, with an incredible preparation and pomp altogether royal. After this, when his father Alfonso was taken from the living, he succeeded him in the principality in the year 1534, and he displayed many instances, indeed not only examples, of heroic qualities. He administered his dominion with singular prudence, and amid the many tumults of war by which almost all of Italy was shaken, he preserved it calm and unharmed. Above all he took care that justice was administered strictly and impartially; he established at Ferrara a most celebrated Academy, the nurse of all the disciplines, and, summoning professors of the greatest renown from everywhere, he cherished it with singular zeal and generosity. Under his principate, along with almost countless others, that singular glory of Italian poets, Ludovico Ariosto, shone forth.

units.la: RENATA, è regia Gallorum stirpe Princeps prudentissima, Ludovici duodecimi filia natu minor, Regisque Henrici, qui hodie florentissimi Galliarum regni gubernacula tenet, matertera, Herculi Estēfi[?] Principi clarissimo nupsit: cui & multos sexus utriusque, & generosissimæ indolis liberos peperit: è quibus filia natu maxima, Aumaliæ Principi, Guisiæ Ducis filio nupsit: qui deinde patri è vivis sublato in Principatu successit.
units.tr: RENÉE, of the royal stock of the French, a most prudent Princess, the younger daughter of Louis XII and aunt of King Henry, who today holds the reins of the most flourishing kingdom of France, married the most illustrious Prince Hercules of Este. To him she bore many children of both sexes, of most noble disposition; of whom the eldest daughter married the Prince of Aumale, son of the Duke of Guise; who afterwards succeeded his father, taken from the living, in the principality.

units.la: LVDOVICA Exclarissima Sabaudię Ducũ familia,illustrissimo Angolismorũ Duci nupsit:cui & duo præcipua nostrę ætatis lumina peperit, Francifcũ Valesiũ, quipost Ludouici 12. mortem Gallici regni habenas tenuit,& Margaretā postea Hērici inclyti Nauarrę Regis vxorem. Hęc tanto ingenio mulier, tantáque in arduis rebus obeũdis dexteritate fuit, vt nō immerito filius loginquiore expeditione suscepta,regni totius administrationem amplissima cũ potestate ei semper crediderit. Ex præclarissimis eius in rem Christianam promeritis, illud præcipuè memoria dignum est,quòd anno 1529. mense Augusto, initio Cameraci cũ Margareta Maximiliani filia colloquio,pacem stabilierit,liberósque regios, Francifcum Delphinũ, & Hēricũ Aurelianorum id temporis Ducem, paternorum pastorum in Hispania obsides,paretis patrięque desiderio restituerit.Supremum diem clausit 11. Cal.Octob. anno 1531. singularis quandiu vixit,ingeniorum & virtutis fautrix. Vide Chr. Cari. & Galliæ,.
units.tr: LOUISE, of the most illustrious house of the Dukes of Savoy, married the most illustrious Duke of Angoulême. To him she bore two outstanding lights of our age: Francis Valois, who after the death of Louis XII held the reins of the French kingdom, and afterwards Margaret, wife of Henry, the renowned King of Navarre. This woman was of such great talent and such skill in undertaking difficult affairs that her son, when he undertook a more distant expedition, always entrusted to her the administration of the whole kingdom with the fullest power. Among her most distinguished services to the Christian cause, this is especially worthy of remembrance: that in August 1529, at the beginning of a conference at Cambrai with Margaret, daughter of Maximilian, she established peace, and restored the royal children, Francis the Dauphin and Henry, then Duke of Orléans, hostages for their father in Spain, to their parents and their longing homeland. She closed her last day on 11 October 1531. As long as she lived she was a singular patron of talents and of virtue.

units.la: MARGARETA Austriaca,Maximiliani Cęsaris,& Mariæ Burgundæ filia, anno salutis nostræ 1479. vitæ limen ingressa est.Nupsit primùm Georgio Hispaniarũ Principi, eóque è viuis sublato, Philiberto Allobrogum Duci, quo præmaturè orbata,cũ in cœlibatu persisteret,nomine Caroli quinti, fratris sui filij,Flandrię Germanięque inferioris gubernacula suscepit. Anno deinde 1529. habito Cameraci cum Ludouica Francifci Regis matre colloquio,compositis Principum cõtrouersiis, lætam suis pacem peperit:annóque in sequenti magno suorũ desiderio factis concessit. Vide Genealog. Carol. quinti. MARIA VID. D. G. REG. HVNGARIAE ET BOHEMIAE [?] CATARINA REG. PORTVG.
units.tr: Margaret of Austria, daughter of the Emperor Maximilian and Mary of Burgundy, entered the threshold of life in the year of our salvation 1479. She first married George, Prince of Spain; when he was taken from the living, she married Philibert, Duke of the Allobroges. Left prematurely widowed by him, and remaining unmarried, she took up the government of Flanders and Lower Germany in the name of her nephew Charles V, the son of her brother. Then in the year 1529, after a conference at Cambrai with Louise, mother of King Francis, and after the disputes between the princes had been settled, she brought about a happy peace for her own people; and in the following year she departed this life, to the great longing of her people. See the Genealogy of Charles V. MARIA, WIDOW, QUEEN OF HUNGARY AND BOHEMIA [?] CATHERINE, QUEEN OF PORTUGAL.

units.la: MARIA, Philippi Archiducis Austriæ, & Ioannę Reginę Hispaniarũ filia, & Caroli quinti Imperatoris soror, nupsit admodum puella Ludouico inferioris Pannoniæ Regi, qui in ipso statim adolescētiæ suæ limine, anno 1527. cum aduersus Turcas infeliciter pugnasset, fuga sibi salutem quærens, in palude quadã interiit, superincumbentis equi pondere suffocatus. Cuius memoriæ tantũ tribuit Maria, vt nulla vnquam ratione adduci potuerit, vt aut ad secundas nuptias animũ adiiceret, aut vestẽ lugubrẽ cultu amœniore mutaret. Nec multò post à Carolo fratre inferioris Germaniæ gubernaculis admota, strenuè imprimis munus sibi creditũ obiuit: multáque Cæsare absente bella Gallis, Sicābris, & Menapiis partim vltro intulit, partim ab illis illata sustinuit. In omni denique vitæ ratione virilē potius, quàm muliebrē animũ præ se tulit, à principũ mulierũ deliciis prorsus abhorres. Tādē vt nominis sui memoriæ cõsuleret, in Eburonũ, & Namurcēsiũ finibus oppidũ egregiè munitũ cõdidit, quod de nomine suo Mariæ Burgum voluit appellatum.
units.tr: Mary, daughter of Philip, Archduke of Austria, and Joanna, Queen of Spain, and sister of the Emperor Charles V, married Louis, King of Lower Pannonia, while still a very young girl. He, at the very threshold of his youth, in the year 1527, after fighting unsuccessfully against the Turks, sought his safety in flight and perished in a certain marsh, suffocated by the weight of his horse falling on him. Mary paid such honour to his memory that she could never by any means be induced either to turn her mind to a second marriage or to change her mourning dress for more pleasant attire. Not long afterwards she was raised by her brother Charles to the government of Lower Germany, and she discharged the office entrusted to her with great vigour. During the Emperor's absence she waged wars against the Gauls, the Sicambri and the Menapii, sometimes attacking them of her own accord, sometimes withstanding their attacks on her. Finally, in every part of her life she showed a spirit more manly than womanly, utterly abhorrent to the pleasures of princesses. At last, to secure the memory of her name, she founded, in the lands of the Eburones and the Namurcenses, a well-fortified town, which she wished to be called Marienburg after her own name.

units.la: CATHARINA, quarta Philippi Archiducis Austriæ filia, nupsit Ioanni Emanuelis Lusitaniæ Regis filio, qui hodie regni eius sceptra tenet, quem & quatuor liberorum Emanuelis, Philippi, Mariæ, & Isabellæ parētem fecit. Hæc præter insignem formæ venustatem, eruditionis nomine in primis commēdatur aliis etiam virtutibus, regia matrona dignis, egregiè dotata. FLOREN. I. ALEX. DVX FLOREN. II. COSMVS DVX
units.tr: CATHERINE, fourth daughter of Philip, Archduke of Austria, married John Emmanuel, son of the King of Portugal, who today holds the sceptre of that kingdom, and by him she became the mother of four children: Emmanuel, Philip, Mary and Isabella. Apart from her remarkable beauty of form, she is especially commended for her learning, and she was richly endowed with other virtues worthy of a royal matron. FLOREN. I. ALEX. DUKE OF FLORENCE. II. COSMUS, DUKE.

units.la: ALEXANDER Laurentij Medicis Urbinatiü Ducis filius,secundo fortunę flatu, & immodico Clementis Pontificis propinqui sui fauore, primus Florētinorū Dux creatus est anno nostrae salutis 1532. Hic prudentissimorū hominū consiliis parens,quos Clemens ei consiliarios addiderat,summa aliquādiu cum laude patriæ suæ præfuit. Ius summa æquitate dicēdū curauit:rebúsque multis per seipsum iudicatis,nō obscura & cordati iuuenis,& Medicei sanguinis specimina edidit. Caroli Cęsaris filiam,tori confortem sibi adsciuit: ex qua nullos suscepit liberos.Postremò cùm neque tanta fortunę suę amplitudine,neque tā generoso contentus coniugio, pudicis nobilium thalamis insidiaretur, anno 1537. à Laurētino Medice suo propinquo, & in eam usque diē spectatissima erga se fide,fraude circūuentus, multis vulneribus confossus interiit.
units.tr: ALEXANDER, son of Lorenzo de' Medici, Duke of Urbino, lifted up by a second gust of fortune and by the excessive favour of his kinsman Pope Clement, was created the first Duke of the Florentines in the year of our salvation 1532. Guided by the counsels of the wisest men, whom Clement had assigned to him as advisers, he governed his country for some time with the highest praise. He took care that justice was administered with the greatest equity, and after judging many matters himself, he gave clear evidence of a shrewd young man and of Medici blood. He took as his wife the daughter of Charles the Emperor, but had no children by her. At last, not content with so great an elevation of his fortune nor with so noble a marriage, he laid snares for the chaste beds of noblewomen; and in the year 1537 he was ensnared by fraud from his kinsman Lorenzino de' Medici, who had remained most faithful to him to that day, and was killed, pierced with many wounds.

units.la: COSMVS Medices[?], fecundus Florentinorū Dux, patre natus est Ioannino Medice, viro omnium suę ętatis rei militaris gloria clarissimo.Hic anno salutis 1537. principatū auspicatus,subitò saluberrimis multis promulgatis legibus(quod ab ea ętate nemo expectarat) ditionis suę tranquillitatem stabiliuit. Scelerum omnium acerrimū se vindicem præbuit:literatos verò, atque adeò bonos omnes,singulari studio fouit. Academia Pisis regia prorsus magnificentia extruxit,præstantissimisque omnium disciplinarum professoribus exornauit:in qua bonę spei ingenia, rei familiaris angustia à liberalibus studiis exclusa, in sextum usque annū ali voluit. Uxorē duxit Leonorā Proregis Neapolitani filiā,tanto sibi,eóque mutuo amore deuinctam,ut non immerito inter præcipua amantiū paria debeat connumerari. Hic locis non paucis ditioni suę adiectis, principatus sui fines non parum propagauit. FRANCISCVS FRAN·R·INVIC·[?] LEONORA D·G·FR·[?]
units.tr: COSMUS de' Medici, second Duke of the Florentines, was born of the father Giovanni de' Medici, a man most famous in the military glory of all his age. He began his rule in the year of salvation 1537, and suddenly, after promulgating many most salutary laws (which no one had expected from that age), he stabilised the tranquillity of his realm. He showed himself the most fierce avenger of all crimes, but he cherished men of letters, and indeed all good men, with singular devotion. He built the royal Academy at Pisa with truly magnificent splendour and adorned it with the most outstanding professors of all the disciplines; in it he wished promising minds, excluded from liberal studies by the narrowness of their family means, to be supported until the sixth year. He married Leonora, daughter of the Viceroy of Naples, bound to him by so great and so mutual a love that she may not unjustly be counted among the foremost pairs of lovers. He also added many places to his realm and not a little extended the borders of his principate. FRANCIS, FRAN·R·INVIC·[?] LEONORA D·G·FR·[?]

units.la: FRANCISCVS Valesius Galliarum Rex clarissimus, literarum atque adeo liberalium omnium studiorum (quę superiorum Principum incuria diu neglecta iacuerant) unicus Mecoenas & singularis instaurator extitit. Celeberrimam Parisiorum Academiam, conductis amplissimis stipendiis trium linguarum aliarumque disciplinarum professoribus, & frequentiore reddidit, & ornatiore. Quid multa? ea cura, eoque animi conatu in hanc rem incubuit, ut Parens literarum nō immerito debeat appellari. Neque vero rei militaris gloria inferior fuit: cuius non obscura indicia pręse ferunt pręclara aliquot ab eo conscripta de disciplina militari volumina. Post hęc rebus plerisque iam felicissime gestis, Allobrogū Ducatum, & bona Subalpinę regionis partem, quorum ius tum morte Margaretę Borbonię auię fuę, Philippi Ducis vxoris, tum ex testamento Comitis Narbonensis Provincię ad se deuolutū contendebat, finibus suis adiecit. Denique suis Landrisij à Cęsare obsessis, iamque ad extremam rerum omnium penuria redactis, suppetias tulit, recentique in hostis conspectu inuecto cōmeatu, ad eam consilij inopiam Cęsarem redegit, ut abiecta spe potiundi oppiduli, obsidionem soluere fuerit coactus.
units.tr: FRANCIS Valois, most illustrious King of the French, proved to be the sole patron and singular restorer of letters and of all the liberal studies, which under the negligence of earlier princes had long lain neglected. He made the most celebrated Academy of Paris both more crowded and more splendid, by hiring professors of the three languages and of other disciplines with very ample salaries. What more? He applied himself to this matter with such care and such effort of mind that he may not unjustly be called the Father of Letters. Nor was he inferior in military glory: several distinguished volumes on military discipline written by him bear clear witness to this. Afterwards, with most of his affairs already happily accomplished, he added to his own borders the Duchy of the Allobroges and part of the lands of Subalpine Gaul, the right to which had devolved upon him, he claimed, partly by the death of Margaret of Bourbon, his grandmother and the wife of Duke Philip, and partly by the will of the Count of Narbonne, Governor of Provence. Finally, when Landrecies was besieged by the Emperor and had already been reduced to the utmost want of everything, he brought aid: having introduced provisions into sight of the enemy, he so reduced the Emperor to a loss of counsel that, abandoning hope of seizing the little town, he was forced to raise the siege.

units.la: LEONORA Philippi Archiducis filia, & Caroli quinti Imperatoris soror natu maxima, primum Emanuelis Lusitanorū Regi nupsit: eoque è viuis sublato, anno 1530. Francisco Valesio Regi secundis nuptiis coniuncta, non parum ad sedandas viri fratrisque discordias momenti attulit: eodemque anno regni diadema accepit. MAN·TVRC·IMP. [?] SVLEY[?] ROSSA·VX [?] S·OL·
units.tr: LEONORA, daughter of Philip, Archduke, and eldest sister of the Emperor Charles V, first married King Emmanuel of the Portuguese; and when he was taken from the living, in the year 1530 she was joined in a second marriage to King Francis of Valois, contributing not a little to the calming of the discord between her husband and her brother. In the same year she received the diadem of the kingdom. MAN·TURC·IMP. [?] SULEY[?] ROSSA·VX [?] S·OL·

units.la: [The first word is printed in capitals.] SOLYMANUS Turcarum Rex, ex re feliciter prouisa, cui euentus responderit, nomē tulisse fertur, quod Salomonem Sapientiæ gloria inclytū, immutatis syllabis referat. Itaq; Solymano secus ac patri contigisse constat, qui à contrario sensu Selymus, hoc est mafuetus, autorque pacis, sit vocatus: quo nemo Othomanorū ferocior & bellicosior fuerit. Sed Solymani res gestæ, paternæ famæ nomen æquasse censeri possunt. Recepta namque Syria, interfecto Gazelle qui rebellarat, Belgradū fortiter expugnatū, Rhodus manu capta, Buda bis occupata, Austriacus exercitus in fuga cæsus, Rocādulphi ingentes copiæ ad Budā superatæ, expugnatū Strigoniū, & Alba Regalis præclaræ Hungariæ ciuitates, an. 1543. & paulò ante Hispani in Dalmatia ad Castrum nouū expugnati, classibus eorum, quæ insuperabiles viderentur, ad Leucadem fugatis: hæc, inquā, Solymanum patri, ausu nec imparem, nec gloriæ minus auidū testabuntur. Assyriæ præterea & Mesopotamiæ regna, cum Babylonia vrbe, magnæ Memphi æquada, quæ suo Solymanus adiecit Imperio, captæ à patre Aegypto opponi possunt. Quinetiam Solymanus maioris Armeniæ, Mediæ, Perfidisque fines, vsque ad sinū Persicū, vastauit: Taurim Persarū Regiam, bis cepit: Tamasum Sophim, Hismaëlis filium, refugientem ad mōtes, fugauit. Verum quod ad Solymani mores etiā attinet, fatentur sanè Turcę, eius subditi, eum suprà cæteros Othomannorum principes, qui per ducentos regnarint annos, iustitiæ, sobrietatis, & continentiæ laude clarissimum. Vide Paulum Iouium.
units.tr: SOLYMAN, King of the Turks. It is said that from an event happily foreseen, to which the outcome corresponded, he received a name which, with its syllables changed, refers to Solomon, renowned for the glory of wisdom. Thus it is established that Suleiman fared otherwise than his father, who was called Selim, from the contrary sense, that is, gentle, and author of peace; yet no one of the Ottomans was fiercer or more warlike than he. But the deeds of Suleiman may be judged to have equalled the fame of his father's name. For Syria was taken, Gazelle, who had rebelled, was killed, Belgrade was bravely stormed, Rhodes was captured by force, Buda was occupied twice, the Austrian army was cut down in flight, the vast forces of Roccandolfo were overcome near Buda, and the famous Hungarian cities of Esztergom and Székesfehérvár were stormed, in the year 1543; and shortly before, the Spanish were defeated at New Castle in Dalmatia, their fleets, which seemed invincible, were routed at Leucas. These things, I say, will bear witness that Suleiman was not unequal to his father in daring, nor less eager for glory. Moreover, the kingdoms of Assyria and Mesopotamia, with the city of Babylon, which Suleiman added to his empire, may be set against Egypt, taken by his father, the great Memphis being matched. Suleiman also laid waste the borders of Greater Armenia, Media and Persia, as far as the Persian Gulf; he twice took Tabriz, the royal city of the Persians; he put to flight Tahmasp, the Shah, son of Ismail, who fled to the mountains. But as far as Suleiman's manners are concerned, the Turks, his subjects, indeed confess that he, above the other princes of the Ottomans who reigned for two hundred years, was most famous for the praise of justice, sobriety and self-restraint. See Paulus Jovius.

units.la: ROSSA omnium Solymani vxorum pulcherrima, præter formā multis etiam virtutibus dotata est: quare apud Solymanum præ cæteris omnibus vxoribus maxima pollet gratia, ab eóque vnicè amatur, ac colitur.
units.tr: ROXELANA, the most beautiful of all Suleiman's wives, besides her beauty, is also endowed with many virtues; therefore she holds the greatest favour with Suleiman above all his other wives, and is loved and courted by him alone.

units.la: SOPHI nomine Tammas, Persarum Rex potentiss. urbe Tauris, ac parte regni pulsus à Solymano anno D. 1534. Punicis artibus voluit hostem circumuenire: nā cūm viribus esset inferior, fingens longius aufugere, perduxit Solymanum in loca invia, ac praerupta, Turcisque ipsis incognita, unde vix egredi potuerit Solymanus, hostē 8. dies prosecutus. Porrò Sophi per vias quasdam sibi notas iter faciés, partem exercitus, nempe 60000. hominum armatorum, transmisit: Taurínque urbem, media nocte aggressus, recuperauit, omnibus qui in ea erant Turcis trucidatis. Erat autem haec urbs Turcicis thesauris nō minimis, atque armis aucta & ornata. Solymanus itaq; subito quaqua via pedē referre coactus est, féque in suæ ditionis castellū quàm citissimè recipere. Anno autem 1549. Solymani primogenitus ad Persas defecit, quòd fratrem suū à patre in Imperio praeferedū praesentiret. coacto itaque exercitu Persico, in patrē insurgit, locáq; paterna, Persis finitima oppugnat. tū verò pater cum 500000. militū eò profectus Persas metu perculsos retrocedere cogit: sed incensis à Persis villis, pagísq; omnibus quacunque dierū 5. spatio profugiebant, ad tantam rerum penuriā adactus est Solymanus ut 100000. fuorū peste ac fame extinctis, reuerti sit coactus. huius Tammę frater germanus Helcas, ad Solymanū transfugit, cuius hortatu bellum renouatū est, qui cūm eius belli Dux esset ut perfidiae poenas daret, ad Persicum sinum est interceptus. Cęterum ipse Sophi roseo vultu, vegetísque oculis dignā Imperio faciem praefert, equitandi, & sagittandi peritiss. conatúrque in Oriente Imperiū reparare: egregiísque factis maiorem suorum gloriam reuocare. Vide Iou. Munst. & Cario.
units.tr: SHAH Tahmasp, King of the Persians, most powerful, driven from the city of Tabriz and part of his kingdom by Suleiman in the year of our Lord 1534, wished to outwit his enemy by Punic arts: since he was inferior in strength, feigning to flee far away, he led Suleiman into pathless and precipitous places, unknown even to the Turks themselves, from which Suleiman could scarcely get out, having pursued the enemy for eight days. Moreover, the Shah, making his way by certain routes known to him, sent across a part of his army, namely 60,000 armed men; and attacking the city of Tabriz at midnight, he recovered it, all the Turks who were in it being slaughtered. This city, however, was enriched and adorned with no small Turkish treasures and arms. Suleiman therefore was suddenly forced to retreat by every road and to withdraw as quickly as possible into a fortress of his own dominion. In the year 1549, Suleiman's firstborn revolted to the Persians, because he sensed that his father would prefer his brother in the Empire. Having therefore assembled a Persian army, he rose against his father and attacked his paternal lands bordering on Persia. Then indeed his father, setting out there with 500,000 soldiers, compelled the Persians, struck with fear, to retreat; but, with all the villages and districts which the Persians had set on fire, through which they fled on every day of a five-day journey, Suleiman was reduced to such a want of supplies that, with 100,000 of his men carried off by plague and famine, he was forced to return. The brother of this Tahmasp, Alqas, deserted to Suleiman, at whose urging the war was renewed; and he, being commander in that war, was intercepted at the Persian Gulf to pay the penalty for his treachery. Moreover, the Shah himself has a rosy countenance and lively eyes, a face worthy of empire, most skilled in riding and archery, and he strives to restore the empire in the East, and to recall the greater glory of his people by distinguished deeds. See Johannes Jovius, Munster and Cario.

units.la: UXOR Sophi speciosissima, more quidem antiquarū Heroinarum incedit, omni cultu ac mundo muliebri ornatissima.
units.tr: The wife of the Sophi is most beautiful; she walks in the manner of the heroines of old, adorned with every feminine ornament and finery.

units.la: PAVLVS hoc nomine Papa tertius, Alexander Farnefius antea vocatus, vna omnium voce in demortui Clementis septimi locum substituitur anno D. 1534. Hic ab adolescentia literis latinis ac Græcis, liberalibúsque disciplinis probè est institutus: atque, ante Pontificatum initum, Petrum Aloyfium, & Cõstantiam, matrem Vidonis Afcanij Cardinalis à S.Flora, peperit. Postea Pontifex creatus, concilium generale indixit, eíque locú assignauit, primum Mantuam, deinde Vicentiam, nouiffimè Tridetum, vbi & inchoatum est. Hic sex expeditas triremes ad Imperatorem aduersus Aenobarbũ misit. Præterea cũ Galliæ Rege Francifco Valefio, & Imperatore Carolo ad Niciam cõuenit: vbi decennales paãtæ sunt inducie inter Imperatorem & Regem: initum est etiam matrimonium inter Oãtauiũ Pauli nepotem, & Imperatoris filiam, Alexandri Medices Florentiæ Ducis viduã. Deinde assentiente Imperatore, prædictus Petrus Aloyfius Parmæ ac Placentiæ Dux designatus est: hac quidem conditione vt Papa 12000. peditum ad Imperatorem aduersus Protestantes mitteret: quod præstitit Pontifex: auxiliaribúsque hic copiis, quasi Cleri Coryphæus, creatus est Octavius. Sedit Paulus hic annos 16. vixit 84. Vide Iouium.
units.tr: Paul, the third Pope of this name, previously called Alessandro Farnese, was elected by the unanimous voice of all in the place of the deceased Clement VII in the year of our Lord 1534. From youth he was thoroughly trained in Latin and Greek letters and the liberal arts. Before he entered the pontificate, he begot Pier Luigi and Costanza, the mother of Vidonio Ascanio, Cardinal of San Flora. Afterwards, created Pope, he called a general council and assigned it a place: first Mantua, then Vicenza, and most recently Trent, where it was also begun. He sent six galleys to the Emperor against Barbarossa. Moreover, he met with the King of France, Francis I, and the Emperor Charles at Nice, where a truce of ten years was agreed between the Emperor and the King. A marriage was also arranged between Ottavio, Paul's nephew, and the Emperor's daughter, the widow of Alessandro de' Medici, Duke of Florence. Then, with the Emperor's assent, the aforesaid Pier Luigi was designated Duke of Parma and Piacenza, on condition that the Pope send 12,000 foot soldiers to the Emperor against the Protestants. The Pope did this, and Ottavio was created, as it were the leader of the clergy, with these auxiliary troops. Paul sat for sixteen years and lived to 84. See Giovio.

units.la: IVLIVS Papa hoc nomine tertius, Ioânes Maria de Monte antea vocatus, Pontifex designatur anno D. 1550. Hic cùm iam antea valde eruditus ac eloquens effet, concilio Tridetino Pauli Legatus præsederat. Iubilæum statim celebrauit, nam in annum 50. eius electio incidit. Primo etiam Pontificatus sui anno concilium Tridetinum inchoatum, sed aliquantisper intermissum, resumedum indixit. Aduersus Hericum Regem Chriftianis. in Italia ad Parmam ac Mirandulam, bellum aliquādiu gessit: verùm tandem res inter eos componitur: cuius fœderis componendiautor fuit Cardinalis Turnonius. M. FRANCISCVS II DV[?] D. F. FRANS II VXOR CHRISTIERNA
units.tr: Julius, the third Pope of this name, previously called Giovanni Maria del Monte, was designated Pope in the year of our Lord 1550. Although he was already very learned and eloquent, he had presided at the Council of Trent as legate of Paul. He at once celebrated a jubilee, since his election fell in the fiftieth year. In the first year of his pontificate he called the Council of Trent, which had been begun but then suspended for a while, to be resumed. For some time he waged war against Henry, the Christian King, in Italy at Parma and Mirandola; but at last the matter was settled between them, and the treaty was arranged chiefly by the efforts of Cardinal Tournon.

units.la: FRANC. Sfortia secundus, Mauri filius, Dux vltimus Mediolani, anno Salutis 1523. à Prospero Colonna, generali Duce copiarum Caroli quinti Imperatoris & Leonis decimi Pontificis, atque ab vniuerso Senatu Tridenti, vbi morabatur, ad Mediolanensem principatū reuocatus est. Nō multo ante ipse populus à Gallo Rege deficiēs, Regiū Præsidem Lautrec omnésque Gallos milites, quòd insolēter viueret, vnanimiter expulerant. Receptus est summo cum gaudio, & applausu incredibili. Anno verò Salutis 1534. Christiernam Daniæ Serenis. Regis filiam summo Imperatori neptē, vxorem duxit. At post fatales dolores & fugam, populíque sui graues querelas, ob aurū Cæsari persoluendum, longa alterius oculi ægritudine prægrauatus, quem & amisit, die 24. Octobris 1535. decessit, suos relinquens Cæsareis Præfectibus expilandos. Eo exenterato cor subaridum & inflatum repertum est. Vide Supplem.Chro.& Gazzo.
units.tr: Francesco Sforza II, son of Ludovico, the last Duke of Milan, was recalled to the Milanese principality in the year of salvation 1523 by Prospero Colonna, general commander of the forces of the Emperor Charles V and Pope Leo X, and by the whole senate at Trent, where he was staying. Not long before, the people themselves, having revolted from the French King, had unanimously expelled the royal governor Lautrec and all the French soldiers, because they lived insolently. He was received with great joy and incredible applause. In the year of salvation 1534 he married Christina, daughter of the serene King of Denmark and granddaughter of the Emperor. But after fatal sorrows and flight, and serious complaints from his people over the gold to be paid to Caesar, weighed down by a long illness of one eye (which he also lost), he died on 24 October 1535, leaving his people to be plundered by Caesar's officials. When he was disembowelled, his heart was found dried up and swollen. See the Supplementum Chronicorum and Gazzo.

units.la: CHRISTIERNA Serenis. Daniæ Regis filia, Carolo quinto Cæsari, ex sorore neptis, anno Salutis, quo suprà, Franc. Sfortiæ hoc nomine secundo, & vltimo Mediolanēsium Duci, matrimonio iuncta est, applausu sanè incredibili. Verùm, tum ob perlõgam viri ægritudinem, in qua & oculum perdidit, tum quòd populum vexari ac expilari cerneret, tũ demũ ob Imperij breuitatē, quandò paulò plus anno principatũ tenuit, hę nuptiæ parùm illi lætæ fuerũt. Nam pullis, lugubribúsque cooperta vestibus, gemēs ad patriam remeauit: postea nupsit Antonio Lotharingię Duci. Vide autores quos suprà. IOAN. STOEFLERUS IMAGO ALBERTI DURERI ÆTATIS SUÆ LVI
units.tr: Christina, serene daughter of the King of Denmark, niece of the Emperor Charles V through his sister, was joined in marriage in the year of salvation mentioned above to Francesco Sforza II, the last Duke of the Milanese, with truly incredible applause. But, partly because of her husband's long illness, in which she also lost an eye, partly because she saw the people being harassed and plundered, and finally because of the brevity of his rule, since he held the principality barely a little over a year, this marriage brought her little joy. For she returned to her homeland in mourning, clothed in black, and sighing; afterwards she married Antoine, Duke of Lorraine. See the authors cited above.

units.la: IOANNES Stœflerus Iustingensis, insignis fuit Astronomus & Cosmographus, ut testantur multa eius opera accuratissimè elaborata. Scripsit opus Ephemeridum, à capite anni Christi 1532. in alios viginti proximè sequētes, ad veterum imitationem, excusum Tubingę: item variorum Astrolabiorum composi-tionis seu Fabricę libros duos, cum explanatione usuum eorundem, quos quidem postremò ab authore recognitos Petrus Iordan excudit Moguntię, anno domini 1535. In Procli Diadochi Sphæram mundi Commentarium: Calendarium Romanum: Tabulas Astronomicas: Cosmographicas aliquot descriptiones De Sphæra Cosmographica, hoc est de globi terrestris artificiosa structura: De duplici terræ proiectione in planum, hoc est qua ratione commodius chartæ Cosmographicæ, quas mappas mundi vocant, designari queant: quę quidem edita sunt à Ioanne Dryandro Mapurgi. Constat eum claruisse anno salutis 1530.
units.tr: John Stoeffler of Justingen was a distinguished astronomer and cosmographer, as his many carefully wrought works attest. He wrote a work of Ephemerides, from the beginning of the year of Christ 1532 for the following twenty years, printed at Tübingen in imitation of the ancients; likewise two books on the composition or construction of various astrolabes, with an explanation of their uses, which Peter Jordan printed at Mainz in the year of the Lord 1535, the author having revised them last. A Commentary on Proclus Diadochus' Sphere of the World; a Roman Calendar; Astronomical Tables; several Cosmographical descriptions; On the Cosmographical Sphere, that is, on the skilful construction of the terrestrial globe; On the double projection of the earth onto a plane, that is, by what method the cosmographical charts, which are called world maps, can be drawn more conveniently. These were published by John Dryander of Marburg. He is known to have flourished in the year of salvation 1530.

units.la: ALBERTUS Durerus Norimbergensis pictor celeberrimus, scripsit institutionum Geometricarum libros 4. lingua Germanica, quos deinde doctus quidam Latinitate donavit, pictoribus, fabris aerariis ac lignariis, lapidicidis, statuariis & universis qui circino, gnomone, libella, aut alioqui certa mensura, opera sua examinant, utilissimos. Exaravit plures alios libros, qui non mediocrē[?] utilitatem possunt afferre his, qui hac arte & professione nobilissima maximè delectantur, quorum elenchum hic recensere superuacaneum esse haud videtur. Scripsit libellum de urbibus, arcibus, castellisque condendis & muniendis, impressum Lutetiæ 1535. Item de Symmetria partium in rectis formis humanorum corporum, libros quos in Latinum convertit Ionstinus[?] Camerarius, Norimbergæ impressos, annos domini 1532. cum figuris. Præterea de varietate figurarum & flexuris partium, ac gestibus imaginum, ibidem impressos anno 1534. cum figuris plurimis. Floruit anno salutis 1534. Vide Gesnerum. VIC. TRINCAVELA. [?] ANT. MVS. BRASSAVOLVS
units.tr: Albrecht Dürer of Nuremberg, a most celebrated painter, wrote four books of Geometrical Instruction in the German language, which a learned man afterwards rendered into Latin; they are most useful to painters, metalworkers, carpenters, stonemasons, sculptors, and all who test their work with compass, gnomon, level, or other certain measure. He wrote several other books which can bring no small benefit to those who take especial delight in this art and noble profession; it seems superfluous to list them here. He wrote a little book on founding and fortifying cities, castles and fortresses, printed at Paris in 1535. Likewise, on the symmetry of parts in the straight forms of the human body, books which Joachim Camerarius translated into Latin, printed at Nuremberg in the year of the Lord 1532, with figures.
