Moreover, on the variety of figures and the bending of parts, and the gestures of images, printed there in 1534 with very many figures. He flourished in the year of salvation 1534. See Gesner.

units.la: TRINCAVELLA insignis Medicus fuit,quem dignifsimum esse existimauimus qui huic numero virorū in arte medica doctissimorum adscriberetur, ut ex eius exactissimis commentationibus perspicere licet.Scripsit de compositione medicamentorū quaedam, multáque alia, quae medicis non mediocre utilitatem adferunt,quęque ei immortalem gloriæ & nominis famā pepererunt.Claruit circiter annū salutis humanae 1538.
units.tr: Trincavella was a distinguished physician, whom we thought most worthy to be enrolled among this number of men most learned in the medical art, as may be clearly seen from his most exact commentaries. He wrote certain works on the compounding of medicines, and many other things which bring no small usefulness to physicians, and which won him immortal glory and the fame of his name. He flourished about the year of human salvation 1538.

units.la: ANTONIVS Musa Brassauolus Medicus Ferrariensis, cuius hic imaginem ad viuum expressam vides, floruit circiter annum salutis 1538. Is multos libros composuit de arte medendi. Scripsit praeterea multa alia utilissimè, quorum bona pars in lucem prodiit, reliqua expectantur: quibus omnibus studiosis innotescit eius doctrina & perfecta eruditio, in diuerso literarum genere. Scripsit Examen omnium simplicium medicamentorum impressum Romę, & Lugduni. In octo libros aphorismorum Hippocratis & Galeni expositionem,Commentaria & annotationes. De Syrupis librum, per dialogū inter ipsum Antonium & Pharmacopolam senem.Scripsit praeterea vitam Iesu Christi seruatoris Italica lingua,in qua paraphrasticè,quatuor euangelistas interpretatur.Dialogum,quod mors nemini placeat. Muricis encomium:de coena & prandio: de temperie Ferrariensis aeris.De laudibus dialecticae. De ordine librorum Logicae. De utilitate & necessitate Logicae:de suppositionibus secundum antiquos. Commentaria in Paulum Venetum. Commentarios in praedicamenta Aristotelis:in librum de interpretatione: in posteriora analytica:in libellum Boëtij de diuisionibus.Commentaria in librum Auerrois de substantia orbis. In libros Physicorum Aristotelis. In libros de anima. Commentaria in Aphorifmos Hippocratis quae post primam editionem ad incudem revocauit,& alia infinita. Floruit anno salutis 1538.
units.tr: Antonius Musa Brassavolus, physician of Ferrara, whose portrait, drawn from life, you see here, flourished about the year of salvation 1538. He composed many books on the art of healing. He also wrote many other things most usefully, of which a good part has been published, and the rest is awaited; by all these his learning and complete erudition in a diverse kind of literature become known to scholars. He wrote the Examen of all simple medicines, printed at Rome and Lyons; an exposition, commentaries and annotations on the eight books of the Aphorisms of Hippocrates and Galen; a book on Syrups, in the form of a dialogue between Antonius himself and an old pharmacist. He also wrote, in the Italian language, a life of Jesus Christ our Saviour, in which he paraphrases the four Evangelists. A dialogue, that death pleases no one; a eulogy of the murex; on dining and supper; on the climate of the air of Ferrara; on the praises of dialectic; on the order of the books of Logic; on the usefulness and necessity of Logic; on suppositions according to the ancients; commentaries on Paul of Venice; commentaries on the Categories of Aristotle; on his book On Interpretation; on the Posterior Analytics; on Boethius' little book on divisions; a commentary on Averroes' book on the substance of the sphere; on the Physics of Aristotle; on the books On the Soul; commentaries on the Aphorisms of Hippocrates, which he recalled to the anvil after the first edition, and countless others. He flourished in the year of salvation 1538.

units.la: [The two final lines, "Floruit anno salutis 1538", are in the text block and carry no note.] D. LVDOVICVS ARIOSTVS P. PETRVS ARETINVS P. SATIR.
units.tr: [The two final lines, "Floruit anno salutis 1538", are in the text block and carry no note.] D. LVDOVICVS ARIOSTVS P. PETRVS ARETINVS P. SATIR.

units.la: LVDOVICVS Ariostus Ferrariensis, inter celebres & magnos Poëtas numeratur, vixítque tèpore Herculis d'Est Ducis clarissimi Ferrariensium, qui eum fouit eiúsque statum ampliauit, cum inter primos esset sui consilij. Composuit Italicè librum Poëticum, inscriptum, Orlando Furioso, in quo historiam scribit duodecim Pariū Franciæ & Caroli magni Regis Francorum, tã appositè & doctè, vt omnes tam viri quàm fœminæ hunc librum sibi legendum proponant: nam præter elegantem, iucundum & disertum sermonem, plurima videre licet in eo exépla virtutis (vnde magni fructus possunt exhauriri) & plures historiæ quæ suo tempore acciderunt. Fuit translatus in Gallicum idioma, Hispanum & alia. Scripsit etiam Tragœdias, Comœdias aliósque versus elegantissimos, floruítque supradicto tempore Ducis Herculis, anno salutis humanæ 1540.
units.tr: Ludovico Ariosto of Ferrara is counted among the famous and great poets, and he lived in the time of Ercole d'Este, the most illustrious Duke of Ferrara, who cherished him and enlarged his position, since he was among the foremost of his counsellors. He composed in Italian a poetic book entitled Orlando Furioso, in which he writes the history of the twelve peers of France and of Charlemagne, King of the Franks, so aptly and learnedly that all men as well as women propose this book for their reading; for besides its elegant, pleasant and eloquent style, one may see in it very many examples of virtue (from which great fruit can be drawn) and many histories which happened in his own time. It was translated into the French and Spanish languages and others. He also wrote tragedies, comedies and other most elegant verses, and flourished in the aforesaid time of Duke Ercole, in the year of human salvation 1540.

units.la: PETRVS Aretinus fuit magnus & præstãs orator, qui Venetiis plerúque habitabat, vbi plurimis nobilibus Venetis valdè charus erat. Composuit & edêdos [?] curauit plures libros, sed magna ex parte satyricos. Scripsit Tragœdias, Comœdias, Epistolas & inuectiuas. Erat maledicus maximè in magnos viros, qui vt ei silentium imponerent, magnis muneribus eum afficiebat. Inter alios magnus ille Franciscus primus Christianissimus rex Galliæ, ingenti catena linguis aureis compacta eius maledicentiam compescuit, & eandem ob causam Carolus quintus Imperator monile ad eum misit formam aurium aurearum referens, quo quidem eum obsurduisse nunciatum fuit Imperatori, ita vt à duobus his tantis Principibus ceu Monarchis, deinde abstinuerit. In alios inuectus, in magnum vitæ discrimê sese coniecit propter vim ei illatam. Dein maledicum eius animũ mutando stylum quoque mutauit, floruitque tempore Ariosti. CLEMENT MAROT. MAURITIUS SEVA. P.
units.tr: Pietro Aretino was a great and outstanding orator, who lived for the most part at Venice, where he was very dear to many of the noble Venetians. He composed many books and had many of them published, but for the most part they were satirical. He wrote tragedies, comedies, letters and invectives. He was especially abusive towards great men, and to make them keep silent, they paid him large gifts. Among others, that great man Francis I, the most Christian king of France, restrained his slander with a huge chain of gold links; and for the same reason the Emperor Charles V sent him a necklace representing a pair of golden ears, and it was reported to the Emperor that he had become deaf to them. So, having been silenced by these two so great princes, as if by monarchs, he then refrained from attacking others. Attacking others, he exposed himself to great danger of life, because violence was done to him. Afterwards, changing his abusive disposition, he also changed his style, and he flourished in the time of Ariosto. CLEMENT MAROT. MAURITIUS SEVA. P.

units.la: CLEMENS Marotus Gallus magnā est adeptus gloriam ex eo tempore,quo primum poësis gallica in precio haberi cœpit. Eius carmina,quamuis nitida & salsa, hac tēpestate exigua videntur, si eorum comparatio fiat cum his quæ scribuntur à quibusdam recentioribus Poëtis, quos omnes hic enumerare difficile esset: principem tamen eorum paulò post subiiciam. Hic Marotus Psalmos aliquot Gallico carmine reddidit, transtulit Metamorphosim Ouidianam, Eglogas Virgilij, Minois iudicium, Encomium Beraldi, & multa alia festiuitatis plena.
units.tr: Clément Marot, a Frenchman, won great fame from the time when French poetry first began to be held in esteem. His poems, though polished and witty, seem slight at this time, if they are compared with those written by some more recent poets, whom it would be difficult to list here all; yet I shall shortly place the chief of them below. Marot rendered some Psalms in French verse, translated Ovid's Metamorphoses, Virgil's Eclogues, the Judgement of Minos, the Encomium of Beraldus, and many other things full of wit.

units.la: MAURICIUS Sceva Lugdunensis Poëta Gallus, longè omnium qui sua ætate floruerunt maxima doctrina & ingenij admirabili acumine celeberrimus, multa poëmata composuit & scripsit,quibus eius nominis fama nunquam sanè intercidet. Hic Dantis Poëtę Italici,longe difficillimi, animū prope gerēs, tam alto argumento, suam Deliam conscripsit, ut ab omnibus Poëtis nostræ ætatis,pro tanto tamque eximio opere,existimetur plurimum. Omnia is sua industria invenit,vir perspicacissimus,stemmata,trophæa,& imagines,quibus præclarissimus Henrici secundi,in urbem Lugdunēsem introitus, magna omnium civium concomitante lætitia & oratione,& magnificentissimo apparatu,fuit honoratus, anno 1544. composuit etiam librum inscriptum Microcosmos, id est parvus mundus, in cuius scriptis, quamuis elegantissimis, magis res, quam verba admirari debemus. PETR. BEMBVS. CARDI. AN. AGENS. LXXXVIII[?] PAVL. IOVI VS. COMENSIS
units.tr: Maurice Scève, a French poet of Lyon, by far the most celebrated of all who flourished in his age for his very great learning and admirable keenness of wit, composed and wrote many poems, by which the fame of his name will certainly never perish. He, bearing almost the spirit of Dante, the Italian poet, far the most difficult, wrote his Délie on so lofty a subject that among all the poets of our age it is held in the highest regard for so great and so remarkable a work. This most perceptive man devised by his own diligence all the emblems, trophies and images with which the most illustrious entry of Henry II into the city of Lyon was honoured in 1544, with the great joy and speech of all the citizens accompanying it and with a most magnificent display. He also composed a book entitled Microcosmos, that is, the little world, in whose writings, however elegant, we ought to admire the matter more than the words. PETR. BEMBVS. CARDI. AN. AGENS. LXXXVIII[?] PAVL. IOVI VS. COMENSIS

units.la: PETRVS Bembus Venetus Cardinalis, vir doctissimus, & eloquentiæ Ciceronianæ summus imitator fuit, vt videre licet ex eius scriptis prope infinitis, summa eruditione, sale & iucunditate ita conspersis, vt ad ea perlegenda lectores alliciantur: tanta vis est eius orationis. Scripsit opuscula aliquot impressa Lugduni: Epistolas, De imitatione sermonis lib. 1. cum Ioannis Francisci Pici, quibusdam opusculis: Poëma heroïcum, cum variis poëmatis: de Aetna, libellũ: Historiæ Venetæ libros duodecim. Scripsit etiā elegantissimè de Culice, vt refert Nicolaus Erythreus, & multa alia. Claruit anno reparatæ salutis humanæ 1540.
units.tr: Pietro Bembo, a Venetian cardinal, a most learned man and the supreme imitator of Ciceronian eloquence, was, as can be seen from his almost countless writings, so steeped in great erudition, wit and charm that readers are drawn to read them through; so great is the power of his style. He wrote several small works printed at Lyon: Letters; On the Imitation of Style, book 1, together with some small works of Giovanni Francesco Pico; a heroic poem, together with various poems; On Etna, a little book; the twelve books of the History of Venice. He also wrote most elegantly On the Gnat, as Nicolaus Erythraeus reports, and many other things. He flourished in the year of restored human salvation 1540.

units.la: PAVLVS Iouius Nouocomēsis Episcopus Nucerinus ad vivum sic exprimitur, quod ad corporis delineationem sive decorā effigiē attinet: eius animus admirabilis cuivis innotescit, q; eius historias incredibili facūdia & gravitate scriptas plegerit. Constat hunc medicum fuisse, medicinámque exercuisse antequam Episcopatus amplissimum gradum attigisset. Scripsit de Romanis piscibus libellum: de vita Iacobi Muti, Attedulæ, Cottig-nolæ, Sforciæ &c. librum impressum Basileæ: de rebus Turcicis: vitas omnium Turcicorum imperatorum: item de ordine ac militia Turcicæ militiæ: vitas duodecim Vicecomitum Mediolani principum: vitam Leonis x. Pontif. Max. & Adriani, Pompei Columnę Cardinalis, & infinita alia. Florebat tempore magni huius Cosmi Medicæi. FVXIVS[?] LEON[?] CONR. GESNERVS [?] MED.
units.tr: Paolo Giovio, bishop of Nocera and Novocomum, is portrayed to the life in respect of the outline of his body and his fine appearance; his remarkable mind becomes known to anyone who has read his histories, written with incredible eloquence and dignity. It is established that he was a physician and practised medicine before he reached the very high rank of bishop. He wrote a little book on Roman fishes; a book on the life of Jacopo Mutus, of Attedula, Cottignola, Sforza and so on, printed at Basel; on Turkish affairs; the lives of all the Turkish emperors; likewise on the order and military organisation of the Turkish army; the lives of the twelve princes of the Visconti of Milan; the life of Leo X, Supreme Pontiff, and of Adrian, and of Pompeo Colonna, cardinal, and countless other things. He flourished in the time of the great Cosimo de' Medici. FVXIVS[?] LEON[?] CONR. GESNERVS [?] MED.

units.la: LEONHARTVS Fuchsius, Germanus, medicus insignis, ex eius infinitis prope & pernecessariis cōmentationibus, quandiu medicinæ vsus seruabitur, summis laudibus erit extollēdus: quod plures, vt crediderim, ex eius schola, prodierint medici, quā ex equo Troiano, olim, milites. Scripsit Methodū medicinæ, seu rationem compendiariam, perueniendi ad vērā solidámque medicinam: item de vsitata huius tēporis cōponendorū miscendorúmque medicamentorum ratione libros tres, iis qui praxim medicam exercent maximè necessarios. Eiusdem extant de sanandis totius humani corporis, eiusdéque partium tam internis quam externis malis lib.5[?]. Tabulæ aliquot vniuersæ medicinæ summam & diuisionem, compendio complectentes. Tabulę sex in Galeni libros de morborum causis & symptomatibus: Paradoxorum medicinę lib.3. in quibus multa à nemine adhuc prodita. Arabum ætatisque nostræ medicorum errata confutantur. Floruit anno 1540. & obiit Tubingæ anno 1566.
units.tr: Leonhart Fuchs, a German, an outstanding physician, is to be extolled with the highest praise for his countless and most necessary commentaries, for as long as the practice of medicine endures. Indeed, more physicians, I believe, have come forth from his school than soldiers once came out of the Trojan horse. He wrote a Method of Medicine, or a short way of reaching true and sound medicine; likewise three books on the customary method, in this age, of compounding and mixing medicines, most necessary for those who practise medicine. There also survive from him books on curing the diseases of the whole human body and of its parts, both internal and external (book 5 [?]). Several tables setting out in brief the sum and division of all medicine. Six tables on Galen's books on the causes and symptoms of diseases. Three books of Paradoxes of medicine, in which many things are refuted that no one had yet put forward, and the errors of the Arabs and of the physicians of our own age are confuted. He flourished in the year 1540 and died at Tübingen in the year 1566.

units.la: CONRADVS Gesnerus Tigurinus, medicus & Philosophus clarissimus, cùm ipse plurima scripsit, tū multa etiam aliorū in lucem edidit & rempublicā literariā maximè iuuit. Conscripsit Bibliothecam vniuersalem, siue Catalogum omniū scrip-torū locupletissimum: in tribus linguis Latina, Græca & Hebraica, extantium & non extantium, veterum & recentiorum: opus nouum, & non Bibliothecis tantùm publicis priuatisque instituendis necessarium, sed studiosis omnibus cuiuscúmque artis aut scientiæ, ad studia melius formanda, vtilissimum. Floruit anno salutis 1540. CHRISTOFOR. LONGOLIVS G. ORONTIVS FINAEI.
units.tr: Conrad Gessner of Zürich, a most distinguished physician and philosopher, while he himself wrote very many works, also published many works of others and greatly helped the republic of letters. He compiled the Universal Library, or the most comprehensive catalogue of all writers, in the three languages Latin, Greek and Hebrew, both extant and non-extant, ancient and recent: a new work, and necessary not only for public and private libraries to be established, but most useful to all scholars of every art or science for forming their studies better. He flourished in the year of salvation 1540. CHRISTOFOR. LONGOLIVS G. ORONTIVS FINAEI.

units.la: CHRISTOPHORVS Longolius Parisiensis,suo tempore,eloquetia magna prestitit, vtpote qui plures scripserit Latinè elegantissimas orationes, Epistolas,Epigrámata, & Elegias. Porro inter orationes,vnā exarauit in laudem Ludouici Regis, vndecimi,alteram in laudem Plinij , quinquealias in laudé vrbis Romę,& vnā aduersus Lutheranos. Scripsit etiā amicis plures Epistolas,vt Erasmo,Budęo, Bembo, Sadoleto & aliis. Scripsit quoque in Ius ciuile,cū publicè Iurisprudentiā profiteretur in Academia Piętonū. Erat valde comis & humanus,vnde omniū amicitiā sibi cōparabat. Sed cū videamus sepissimè chariores & virtutibus ornatiores potius quā vitiosos immatura ætate è viuis excedere , florentibus adhuc annis,vitā cū morte mutauit,cū trigētisimū sextū suę ætatis annū nōdū attigisset. Omnia eius opera fuerūt impressa Lugduni, à Sebastiano Gryphio,& in pluribus locis Germanię & Italię.Florebat circiter annū 1536. Vide Conradum Gesnerum, in sua Bibliotheca.
units.tr: Christophe de Longueil of Paris excelled greatly in eloquence in his own time, as one who wrote many most elegant Latin orations, letters, epigrams and elegies. Among the orations, he composed one in praise of King Louis XI, another in praise of Pliny, five others in praise of the city of Rome, and one against the Lutherans. He also wrote many letters to friends, such as Erasmus, Budé, Bembo, Sadoleto and others. He also wrote on civil law, when he taught jurisprudence publicly in the Academy of Poitiers. He was very courteous and humane, and so he won the friendship of all. But since we often see that those more dear and more adorned with virtues, rather than vicious men, depart from the living at an immature age, in the flourishing years still, he exchanged life for death, when he had not yet reached the thirty-sixth year of his age. All his works were printed at Lyon by Sebastian Gryphius, and in many places in Germany and Italy. He flourished about the year 1536. See Conrad Gessner, in his Bibliotheca.

units.la: ORONTIVS Fineus Delphinas Regius Mathematicarū profeßor,in oppido Briansonio natus,patre medico & Philosopho egregio,nec non Mathematico nobili: quo mortuo,Lutetiā venit, vbi perfectis iā suis studiis, vxorē duxit Dionysiā cognomine & re candidā,cū qua vixit paulò minus viginti annis. Quantū laboris insumpserit assiduis cōmentationibus, testantur tot eius scripta, quorū serie reperies in Bibliothec.Gesneri. Floruit anno salutis 1545. Et obiit Lutetię in suis ędibus pridie nonas Octobris,anno reparatę salutis hominū 1555. hora à meridie quarta, qua ille in lucem venerat, natus annos LXI. ferè: iacet in cœnobio Carmelitarum. P. ALOISIVS. DVX. CASTRI [?]VRSINA. HIERONYMA
units.tr: Oronce Fine of Briançon, royal professor of mathematics, was born in the town of Briançon, his father being an outstanding physician and philosopher and also a noted mathematician. When his father had died, he came to Lutetia, where, his studies now complete, he married Denise, surnamed Candide and fair in wealth, with whom he lived a little less than twenty years. How much labour he expended on constant studies is attested by so many of his writings, the series of which you will find in Gessner's Bibliotheca. He flourished in the year of salvation 1545, and died at Lutetia in his own house on 4 October in the year of restored salvation of men 1555, at the fourth hour after noon, the hour at which he had come into the light, having lived about 61 years; he lies in the convent of the Carmelites. P. ALOISIVS. DVX. CASTRI [?]VRSINA. HIERONYMA

units.la: PETRUS Aloysius, Alexādri Farnesij(qui postea ad Pontificatum euectus, Pauli tertij nomine innotuit)filius, opera parentis Parmæ & Placentiæ Principatū consequutus, cū immodico Placentinæ urbis exornandæ studio, edixisset ditionis suæ Comitibus, cęterēque nobilitati, in eā usque die in villis suis castellisve agere assuetis, ut Placentiam domicilium suum transferrent:ægrè id illis ferentibus (ut pote qui sub Pontificū imperio, summæ semper libertati assueuerant) nonnullos non infimę autoritatis, qui imperium suū detrectabat, exilio multauit, bonaq; eorū fisco adiudicauit. Qua occasione irritatis nobiliū animis, illorū coniuratione circuuentus, in arce Placentina multis vulneribus obtruncatur: mortuíque corpus in publicū protractū, cōcursu plebis fœdè discerpitur, anno nostræ salutis 1547.
units.tr: Pietro Luigi, son of Alessandro Farnese (who afterwards was raised to the pontificate and became known as Paul III), obtained the principality of Parma and Piacenza through the efforts of his father. With an immoderate zeal for adorning the city of Piacenza, he issued an edict to the counts of his dominion and to the other nobility, who were accustomed to spend that time on their estates or in their castles, that they should transfer their residence to Piacenza. Since they bore this with ill grace (as those who had always been accustomed, under the rule of the Popes, to the greatest liberty), he punished with exile some men of no small authority who refused to obey his command, and adjudged their goods to the treasury. On this occasion the minds of the nobles were roused, and, surrounded by their conspiracy, he was cut down with many wounds in the citadel of Piacenza; and his corpse, dragged out into the public square, was foully torn to pieces by the crowd, in the year of our salvation 1547.

units.la: HIERONYMA Ursina, Romanæ castitatis matrona, uni cumque virtutis omnis exēplar, Petro Aloysio nupsit, Alexandri Farnesij (qui postea Pontifex creatus, Pauli Tertij nomen adsciuit)filio:cui præter Victoriam filiam, Urbinatiū Duci iam elocatam, quatuor liberos mares peperit, totidem ætatis nostræ lumina: quorū duos hodie omni disciplinarū genere ornatissimos, rarissimo exemplo, in Cardinaliū ordinem videmus cooptatos, Alexandrū nimirum, & Raynutiū Farnesios, ambos amplissimos legatorum munere, illum apud Auenionenses, hūc in Flaminia fungētes. E reliquis duobus, Octauius Parmesiū Dux, militaris gloria imprimis illustris, & Caroli quinti gener, remotissimos orbis Christiani angulos nominis sui splendore impleuit. Horatius verò Castri Dux, generosi animi iuuenis, & in adeūdis periculis prorsus intrepidus, hoc ipso anno incredibili apparatu, Herici Regis filiā cōiugē sibi adsciuit: nemini fortitudinis gloria cessurus, nisi nimia hominis virtus, ad manifesta pericula incautius impulsum, pręmatura nece eū nobis pręripuisset.
units.tr: Hieronyma Ursina, a matron of Roman chastity and a model of every virtue, married Pietro Luigi, son of Alessandro Farnese (who was later created Pope and took the name Paul III). By him she bore, besides Victoria, already married to the Duke of Urbino, four sons, all of them lights of our age. Two of these, Alessandro and Ranuccio Farnese, both most distinguished in every branch of learning, we see today admitted, in a most rare example, into the college of Cardinals: Alessandro, as legate at Avignon, and Ranuccio, in the Flaminia. Of the other two, Ottavio, Duke of Parma, illustrious above all for his military glory and son-in-law of Charles V, has filled the most remote corners of the Christian world with the splendour of his name. Orazio, Duke of Castro, a young man of noble spirit and utterly fearless in facing dangers, this very year took as his wife, with incredible pomp, a daughter of King Henry, being in no way inferior to anyone in the glory of courage, had not his excessive virtue, driving him too rashly into obvious dangers, snatched him from us by an untimely death.

units.la: HENRICVS Albretius illustrissimus Nauarrorum Rex, Francisci Valesij Regis Christianissimi fidus belli comes, eíque semper intimus fuit:cum quo etiâ aduersus Cæsarianos ad Papiam strenuè dimicans, captus est. Hic literas, literatósque semper impensè coluit: Margaretam principem omnium lõgè illustrissimam, prædicti Regis Valesij sororem vxorem accepit: ex qua filiam vnicam suscepit inclytâ, nobilissimi simul ac magnanimi Vindocinensium Ducis vxorem.
units.tr: Henry d'Albret, most illustrious King of Navarre, was a faithful companion in arms to King Francis of France, and always his intimate friend. With him, fighting valiantly against the Imperialists at Pavia, he was taken prisoner. He always cultivated letters and men of letters with great zeal. He took as his wife Margaret, by far the most illustrious princess of them all, sister of the aforesaid King Francis; by her he had an only daughter, famous and at once of most noble and magnanimous character, wife of the Duke of Vendôme.

units.la: MARGARETA Heroinarum omnium in toto orbe facilè Princeps, pietate ac doctrina præ cæteris omnibus celebris, Francisci Valesij soror illustrissima, primùm nupsit Alenconio Duci, ex quo nullos peperit liberos: post cuius obitū nupsit secundò, ac in virum accepit illustrissimum Regem prædictum, Henricum Albretium: cui splendidissimam forma ac moribus filiam peperit, nomine Ianam: quæ in coniugem data est clarissimo, simul ac humanissimo Vindocinēsiū Duci. Migrauit autem Heroina Margareta ex hac in alteram quam præoptabat vitam, anno Domini 1549. Vide Chro. Franc. Cæterùm, vt de eadem Margareta hoc vnum addam, quisquis sanè, huius Margaritæ seu perlustris vnionis splendorem tentat animo perlustrare, atque oculis, etiam si perspicacissimis, assequi: eadem certè opera deductis cilijs[?] in splendidissimum, simulac ardentissimū solem [illegible, ~4 letters] ac illæsa acie contendat.
units.tr: Margaret, easily the foremost of all heroines in the whole world, renowned above all others for piety and learning, the most illustrious sister of Francis of Valois, first married the Duke of Alençon, by whom she bore no children. After his death she married a second time, taking as her husband the aforesaid most illustrious King, Henry d'Albret, by whom she bore a daughter most splendid in form and character, named Jeanne, who was given in marriage to the most famous and at once most courteous Duke of Vendôme. Heroine Margaret, moreover, passed from this life to the other, which she desired more, in the year of the Lord 1549. See the Chronicle of France. But, to add only this one thing about this same Margaret: whoever, indeed, attempts with his mind to survey the splendour of this pearl, this peerless union, and to take it in with his eyes, however sharp-sighted, let him by the same work of drawing the eyelids open, strive with unharmed sight toward the most splendid and most burning sun [illegible, about 4 letters].

units.la: ÆNOBARBVS, vulgò Barbaroffa vocatus, Rex Algerij.Christiana matre natus, à pueritia per inopiam urgentem apud Hispanos importandis venùm caseolis, aliisque id genus opsoniolis victum sibi quærere coactus est.Ex hoc Pirata factus, non mediocriter rem auxit: comparatáque perditissimorum hominum manu, per vim ac insidias, Algerij in Mauritania Regnum occupauit.Mox Turcarum Principi fœdere iustus maritima prælia feliciter gessit. Hispanias infestauit. Tuneti Regem sedibus expulit:qui tamē paulò post à Carolo Augusto v.est restitutus: neque enim tanta erat Aenobarbi Piratæ potentia, ut Imperatori obsistere posset. Eius etenim potentia soli Turcarum adminiculo nitebatur. Vide Paulum Iouium, & Gazzo.
units.tr: Aenobarbus, commonly called Barbarossa, King of Algiers. Born of a Christian mother, from boyhood, under pressing poverty, he was compelled among the Spaniards to earn his living by carrying cheeses for sale and other such small provisions. From this he became a pirate and greatly increased his wealth; having gathered a band of the most desperate men, by force and treachery he seized the kingdom of Algiers in Mauritania. Soon after, becoming a vassal of the Prince of the Turks by covenant, he successfully waged naval battles. He harassed Spain. He drove the King of Tunis from his seat; yet a little later he was restored by Charles Augustus V, for the power of the pirate Aenobarbus was not so great that he could withstand the Emperor; indeed his power rested on the help of the Turks alone. See Paulus Jovius and Gazzo.

units.la: MVLEASEM suo Tuneti Regno per Barbarossam expulsus, mox per Carolũ Cæsarem v. fuit restitutus, anno 1535. Qui anno deinde 1541. huius Muleasem fretus auxiliis, Barbarossam Algerij Principatu frustrà deturbare conatus est, traiecto eā in spē Libyco mari, & ciuitate cincta obsidione. At obortá statim tempestate, imbribus densis, & cōtinuis, & ventis colluctantibus, Algeriani occasione arrepta, & fauēti sydere adiuti, eruperunt impetu magno, castrāq; Cæsaris assiduis iactata calamitatibus, frigore, siti, & fame debilitata, & pluuiarum inūdationibus stagnantia diripuerunt, Cæsare ab obsidione depulso non citra insignem iacturam, cum rerum, tum Illustrium hominum, Ducū exercitus, strenuorūmque militū, & instructissimæ classis. Tāta verò, & tam infesta Cæsari tempestas sæuiit eodem anno circa principium Octobris. Vide Gaz. & Iouium.
units.tr: Muleasses, driven from his kingdom of Tunis by Barbarossa, was soon restored by Charles V in 1535. In the year after, 1541, relying on this Muleasses' auxiliaries, he tried in vain to dislodge Barbarossa from the principality of Algiers, crossing the Libyan sea with that hope and besieging the city. But a storm arose at once, with dense and continual rains and contending winds; the Algerians seized the occasion, and aided by a favouring star, they burst out with great force and plundered the Emperor's camp, already battered by constant calamities, weakened by cold, thirst and hunger, and standing in flood waters from the rains; the Emperor was driven from the siege, not without a notable loss of property and of illustrious men, dukes, the army, brave soldiers, and a most well-equipped fleet. Such a great and such a hostile storm raged against the Emperor in the same year, about the beginning of October. See Gazzo and Jovius.

units.la: FRANCISCVS FILIVS · DEL.D.B. (legends of the left medallion)
units.tr: FRANCISCVS FILIVS · DEL.D.B. (legends of the left medallion)

units.la: CAROLVS · ANGOI DVX (legends of the right medallion)
units.tr: CAROLVS · ANGOI DVX (legends of the right medallion)

units.la: FRANCISCVS Francisci Regis filius primogenitus, natus anno D. 1517. Franciæ Delphinas indole verè regia, & præsumptis à natura virtutis omnis heroïcæ egregiis principiis, artium (quæ liberalem Principem decent) præcipuè verò militaris disciplinæ studiosissimus, spē de se dedit mirabilē. Sed dum contra hostilia Cæsaris arma Massiliam versus, expeditionem parat, Lugduni obiter confidens, veneno necatus est à Sebastiano quodam Montis Cuculli Comite, qui comprachensus, veneficiúmque non dissessus, neque sceleris conscios, pœnas luit, in quatuor partes membratim helciariis equis distractus. Hic Princeps ad hunc modum veneno intus cruciante malè affectus, ardore tamen adeundi ad Provincialia bella patris, vix Turnonem perlatus, magno omnium mœrore expirauit, anno suæ ætatis 20. mense Augusti, 1536. Vide Chron. Franc. & Paulum Iouium.
units.tr: Francis, the eldest son of King Francis, born in the year of the Lord 1517, Dauphin of France, of truly royal character and with excellent beginnings of every heroic virtue presumed from nature, being most devoted to the arts that befit a liberal prince, and above all to military discipline, gave a wonderful promise of himself. But while he was preparing an expedition against the hostile arms of Caesar toward Marseille, staying at Lyon on the way, he was poisoned by a certain Sebastian, Count of Montecuculli, who, being seized, and not denying the poisoning nor his accomplices in the crime, paid the penalty, being torn limb from limb by four horses. This Prince, thus grievously afflicted by poison burning within him, yet with eagerness to join his father's wars in Provence, had barely been carried as far as Tournon when he expired, to the great grief of all, in the twentieth year of his age, in the month of August 1536. See the Chronicle of France and Paulus Jovius.

units.la: CAROLVS Aureliæ Dux, Regalium liberorū ex Francisco Franc.Rege natu minimus, adolescens fuit perhumanus, liberalis, & magnanimus, præbito iam de se heroïcæ magnanimitatis exemplo, in expugnatione Iuodij, oppressione Arluni, Viretonij, ac Luxemburgi, omniúmque locorum, castrorum, & arcium circū circa inuasione, munimento, confirmatione, præsidio, & commeatu, anno 1542. Bellicosissimus hic Regis filius, in florentissimo dilectæ iuuentutis decore, acutissima febri properè extinctus est anno 1545. Vide vt supra.
units.tr: Charles, Duke of Orléans, the youngest of the royal children of King Francis, was a most courteous, liberal and magnanimous youth, having already given an example of heroic magnanimity in the storming of Ivoy, the subjugation of Arlon, Virton, and Luxembourg, and in the attack, fortification, garrisoning and provisioning of all the places, castles and fortresses round about, in the year 1542. This most warlike son of the King, in the flowering grace of his beloved youth, was swiftly carried off by a most acute fever in the year 1545. See as above.

units.la: ALPHONSVS Daualus, Vuasti Marchio ex nobilissima Comitum Aquinatum familia ortus, literis & armis à pueritia exercitus, post mortuum in Prouincia Narbon. Ant.Læuam, Cæsarianæ militiæ in Italia Dux creatus, & Imp. Legatus anno 1536. Casalium, primam Montisferrati vrbem à D. Buriano Gallo captam, mirabili celeritate intra biduum illuc quasi peruolans recuperauit. Anno deinde sequenti, multis & magnis rebus gestis suam in rebus bellicis strenuitatem comprobauit. Reparatisque viribus Albam, Carmanolium, Cherium, Montemcalerium, omnémque circa regionem vastans cepit, Pignerolio etiam, ac Taurino obsessis. Verùm adueniens Delphinus Franciæ omnia rursus victor recepit, ipsúmque Marchionem longè repulit. Expugnata deinde Montisdiuisi ciuitate munitissima, necnon Saluiliano, & Salutio, aliisque locis, dum Carinianum victus commeatu instruere molitur, fortunam expertus est admodum sinistram. Nam sub Cerisoliorum ignobili pago Fracorum virtute, & auspiciis Francisci Borbonij Anguiani, acie profligata, & maxima suorum parte cæsa, victus, & in fugam versus est anno 1544. Denique post certas pacis conditiones inter Regem Francorum, & Imperatorem confirmatas, de[?]essit vir maximi animi Alphonsus Daualus, anno 1546. mense Martio. Vide Gazium.
units.tr: Alphonso d'Avalos, Marquis of Vasto, sprung from the most noble family of the Counts of Aquino, trained from boyhood in letters and arms, after the death of Antonio Leyva in the province of Narbonne, was created Captain-General of the imperial soldiery in Italy and Imperial Legate in the year 1536. With wonderful speed he recovered Casale, the first city of Montferrat, taken by Lord Burian of Gaul, flying there almost within two days. In the following year, after many great deeds, he proved his vigour in war. Having restored his forces, he took Alba, Carmagnola, Chieri, Montecalvo, ravaging the whole region round about, while Pinerolo and Turin were besieged. But the Dauphin of France, arriving, recovered everything again as victor, and drove the Marquis himself far away. Afterwards, having stormed the most strongly fortified city of Montedivisi, and likewise Saluzzo, Saluzzo and other places, while he was striving to supply Carignano with provisions, he met with very unfavourable fortune. For at the obscure village of Cerisoles, by the valour and auspices of the French under Francis de Bourbon, Count of Enghien, his army was routed, most of his men were slain, and he was defeated and put to flight, in the year 1544. Finally, after certain conditions of peace were confirmed between the King of the French and the Emperor, the man of greatest spirit, Alphonso d'Avalos, died in March of the year 1546. See Gazzo.

units.la: MARIA Tarraconensis, seu Aragonia, Alphonsi Dauali Vuastensis Marchionis vxor, forma elegantì, nec minori gratia fuit. Verùm prudētia longè magis excelluit. Heroina pudicissima virum fecit pulchra prole parentem, liberis vtriusque sexus eductis, quibus etiam maturè pater viuens promisum voluit. Vide vt supra. HENRIC[?] ANG. R.[?] D. ADOAR R. ANG.
units.tr: Maria of Tarragona, or of Aragon, wife of Alphonso d'Avalos, Marquis of Vasto, was of elegant form and no less grace. But she excelled far more in prudence. This most chaste heroine made her husband a father by a beautiful offspring, the children of both sexes being brought up, to whom the father, while still living, had also given the promise of early marriage. See as above. HENRIC[?] ANG. R.[?] D. ADOAR R. ANG.

units.la: HENRICVS octauus, Angliæ Rex, patri Henrico septimo successit in Regno, anno Christi 1510. Qui traiecto in Galliam exercitu, Neruiorum vrbem Tornacum certis conditionibus recepit: quam quinque post annis Francisco Valesio Regi restituit, pactus filiæ suæ Mariæ connubium, cum Francisco Franciæ Delphino. Postea vero anno 1520. in Galliam reuersus visendi gratia Regis Francisci, pacem cum eo firmauit. Tragœdias vero turbulētissimas[?] quas excitauit, quásque[?] sævitias exercuit, & in Clerum, & in suas vxores, nunc commemorare non libet: qui fusius hæc videre volet, legat Iouij primum, & secundum tomum, & Supplementum Chronicorum. Regnauit annos 36. & mortuus est anno 1546.
units.tr: Henry VIII, King of England, succeeded his father Henry VII in the kingdom in the year of Christ 1510. Having led an army across into France, he took Tournai, the city of the Nervii, on certain conditions; this he restored five years later to King Francis of Valois, having arranged the marriage of his daughter Mary with Francis, Dauphin of France. Later, in the year 1520, returning to France to visit King Francis, he confirmed peace with him. The very turbulent tragedies that he stirred up, and the cruelties he practised both against the clergy and against his own wives, I do not now wish to recall; whoever wishes to see these things at greater length, let him read the first and second volumes of Jovius and the Supplement of the Chronicles. He reigned 36 years and died in the year 1546.

units.la: EDVARDVS sextus, Angliæ Rex supradicti Henrici filius, annos natus octo patri successit, anno mundi 5508. & à Christo nato 1546. Hic puer fuisse dicitur (quantum tulit ætas) multum eruditus, ac pius: pacis amantissimus, & animo ad tranquillitatem inclinato. Bononiam maritimam Henrico 2. Regi Franciæ reddidit, annos quinque prius occupatâ à patre Henrico octauo. Inter eos denique post grauissima bella de pace conuentum[?] est, iis legibus, vt odiorum veterum inter Gallos, & Britannos[?] perpetua fieret amnestia: idque omnium Magnatum consensu, & populi diutinorum bellorum vtrinque pertæsi. Quasanè[?] pax, & concordia omnibus fuit quàm gratissima. Vide Chronica Franciæ[?], & Iouium.
units.tr: EDWARD the Sixth, King of England, son of the aforesaid Henry, succeeded his father at the age of eight, in the year of the world 5508 and of Christ's birth 1546. This boy is said to have been (so far as his age allowed) very learned and pious, a great lover of peace, and inclined in mind to tranquillity. He restored Boulogne, the seaport, to Henry the Second, King of France, which his father Henry the Eighth had occupied five years earlier. Finally, after very grievous wars, a peace was agreed between them on these terms: that there should be a perpetual amnesty for the old hatreds between the French and the British. This was done with the consent of all the nobles and of the people, who were weary of long wars on both sides. Indeed, the peace and concord were most welcome to all. See the Chronicles of France and Jovius.

units.la: HENRICVS secundus anno 1547. die suo natali Martij vltimo, in regno Franciæ successit patri Francisco Valesio. Sequenti deinde anno, Scotis veteris iure amicitiæ fœderatis aduersus infestantes Anglos suppetias tulit, hostilémq; exercitum fudit, fœdus cū Heluetiis iam olim à patre initum denuo cōfirmauit, ac amplificauit. Deinde, arte, viribus, & impetu Bononiā maritimam ab Anglis occupatam adgressus est, captis omnibus quæ circunstabant arcibus: sic vt Anglorum Regem ad pacem impulerit, dimissa Bononia. Postea vero multorū precibus allectus Principum Germanorum, qui pro sua libertate vindicanda ipsius opem implorabant: cum eis fœdus iniit: & in Germaniam ipse Rex cum apparatissimo exercitu profectus est: & inter eundum Metas nobilissimam Lotharingiæ ciuitatem sibi subdidit. Redeundo autem Danuillarium, Iuodiū, Montemmedium, & alia pleraq; oppida, & castella expugnauit, in quibus erat tutissimum hostibus profugium. Interim cum Rege rediit in gratiam Iulius tertius Pont. Max. Idem Rex Mirandulā tutatus est, Parmam stabiliuit, Senas, expulsis Hispanis, antiquæ restituit libertati. Dum hæc in Italia geruntur: Cæsar qui prudéter retro cesserat, resumptis spiritibus, ad obsidionē Metarum (quas prouidus Rex valetissimo strenuorum Ducum, Equitum, ac Militum præsidio firmarat) reuersus est cum 100000. armatorum, vel amplius. Sed Gallorum virtute recedere iterum coactus est, re infecta, multis suorum ferro, fame, & frigore amissis.
units.tr: HENRY the Second, on the last day of March 1547, his birthday, succeeded his father Francis of Valois in the kingdom of France. In the following year, he came to the aid of the Scots, who were bound to him by an ancient friendship, against the invading English, and he routed the hostile army. He also confirmed and extended the alliance with the Swiss, which his father had long before entered into. Then, by skill, force and dash, he attacked Boulogne, which the English had occupied, and captured all the fortresses round about it, so that he drove the King of England to peace, and Boulogne was given up. Afterwards, moved by the prayers of many German princes, who implored his help in defending their liberty, he made an alliance with them. The King himself set out for Germany with a very well-equipped army, and on the way he took Metz, the noblest city of Lorraine. On his return he stormed Damvillers, Jametz, Montmédy and many other towns and castles, in which the enemy had a very safe refuge. Meanwhile the Pope, Julius the Third, was reconciled with the King. The same King protected Mirandola, secured Parma, and, after the Spaniards were expelled, restored Siena to its ancient liberty. While these things were happening in Italy, the Emperor, who had prudently withdrawn, recovered his spirits and returned to besiege Metz (which the provident King had strengthened with a very strong garrison of brave captains, horsemen and soldiers) with 100,000 armed men or more. But by the valour of the French he was again compelled to retreat, having achieved nothing, with many of his men lost to the sword, famine and cold.

units.la: CATHARINA de Medicis, Henrici Regis coniúx, virtutibus, morū integritate, ac pietate sic excellit, vt tantū in Heroina encomion vix cuiquam credibile videatur. Propter quod populis honorata, Principibus grata, Regi suo viro supra modū est dilecta, quem sex liberorum patre in cōiugalis testimonium amoris iam effecit. ANTONIVS BOVRBON[?] DVX[?] VINDOC[?] DV ALEBRET D.V.[?] IOANNA[?]
units.tr: CATHERINE de' Medici, wife of King Henry, excelled in virtues, integrity of life and piety, so greatly that what is said in praise of this heroine would scarcely seem credible to anyone. For this reason she was honoured by the people, pleasing to the princes, and very dearly loved by her husband the King, whom she had already made the father of six children as a testimony of conjugal love. ANTHONY BOURBON, DUKE OF VENDÔME, OF ALBRET ... JOANNA

units.la: ANTONIVS Borbonius Dux Vindocinensis inclytus, Christ. Franc. Regis in Belgica legatus anno 1542. Turnæam arcem vi expugnatā solo æquauit, Ducem Riuiū Atrebati Gubernatore fugauit, captis plærisq; arcibus, & castellis intra Atrebatensium fines. Anno mox 1543. Insularium, & Bapalmam quantūlibet valido propugnarētur præsidio, simulque alia quædam munitissima loca subegit, eaque ad tollendum belli nidum, funditus diruit. Anno hinc 1552. cùm intellexisset Dux vigilantissimus suprà memoratum Heroa Riuiū Imperatoris vices gerentem satagere ne Morinorum ciuitas annona, & cibariorum commeatu instrueretur, comparata ad hoc impediendū numerosa Flandrorum Belgarum expeditione, illi mox occurrit: vbi cæsis quàm plurimis, nonnullisque captiuis: eodē momēto Castellum Comitum vi cœpit: maximū obstaculū hostibus futurū. Regisque imperio idipsum subdidit. Sequenti mēse Decembri, Hedino per Legatum Riuium expugnato, repentè fortissimus Heros tāto impetu, ac ardore adcurrit: vt intra breue temporis spatium in pristinum statū restituerit. Deniq; inuictus hic & inclytus Princeps egregios conatus suos tantis animis, prudentia, & strenuitate persequitur adhuc nobis superstes: vt immensæ sublimitatis maiorem in dies spem ostendat.
units.tr: ANTHONY of Bourbon, the renowned Duke of Vendôme, legate of the Christian King of France in Belgium, in the year 1542 stormed and levelled with the ground the citadel of Thérouanne, and put to flight Duke Rivius, the governor of Arras, capturing most of the fortresses and castles within the borders of the people of Arras. In the following year, 1543, he subdued Aubigny and Bapaume, however strongly they were defended by a garrison, and at the same time several other very well-fortified places, which he razed to the ground to destroy the nest of war. Then in 1552, when this most vigilant Duke learned that the aforesaid hero Rivius, acting as the deputy of the Emperor, was striving to supply the city of the Morini with food and provisions, he gathered a large Flemish and Belgian expedition to prevent this, and went straight to meet him. There, after very many had been slain and some taken captive, at that same moment he took by force the Castle of the Counts, which would have been a great obstacle to the enemy, and by the King's command he put it under his authority. In the following month of December, after Hesdin had been taken by the legate Rivius, the most brave hero suddenly came up with such impetus and ardour that within a short space of time he restored it to its former state. Finally, this unconquered and renowned Prince pursues his splendid undertakings with such courage, prudence and vigour, and still survives among us, that he shows greater hope of immense eminence day by day.

units.la: IOANNA d'Albret Regis Nauarræ, & clarissimæ Principis illius Margaretæ Regiæ sororis filia vnica, Moliniis incredibili nobiliū & popularium applausu nupsit supradicto illustriss-imo Duci Vindocinensi. Porrò ea nulla ex parte à tantis, talibúsque parentibus degenerat: quin protinus æmulatur moribus, ac virtutibus planè Regiis, & summo amore literarum, ac virtutum, quibus ipsa etiam est ornatissima. EGVIN. BARONI. I.C. ANDR. ALCIAT.
units.tr: JOANNA d'Albret, the only daughter of the King of Navarre and of that most illustrious princess Margaret, the sister of the King, married the aforesaid most illustrious Duke of Vendôme at Moulins, to the incredible applause of the nobles and common people. Moreover, she in no way degenerates from such great and such parents; indeed, she emulates them in manners and virtues truly royal, and in the highest love of letters and virtues, with which she is herself most richly adorned. EGUINARIUS BARO. I.C. ANDREAS ALCIATUS.

units.la: EGVINARIVS Baro Jurisconsultus excellens, de jure etiā multos edidit libros plenos utilitatis. Scripsit etiā in Quintiliani oratorias institutiones, tabulas, universam dicendi rationem quodam quasi fasciculo complectentes, quibus certè palam fit omnibus eum indefesso labore semper studuisse, ut literarum decus & præcipuè juris prudentiæ augesceret & conferturetur magis ac magis. Jus docuit apud Biturigies, tanta nominis fama & existimatione, ut ad eum audiendum plures discipuli, ex longinquis etiam regionibus, concurrerent. Floruit anno salutis humanæ 1542. eodem, quo Alciatus, tempore. Scripsit de diuiduis & indiuiduis obligationibus, seu stipulationibus: de servitutibus. In Pandectas & institutiones commentaria edidit. Item quæstiones de jurisdictione: ad Digesta seu Pandectas manualium libros septem.
units.tr: EGUINARIUS Baro, an excellent jurist, also published many useful books on law. He also wrote commentaries on Quintilian's Institutes of Oratory, tables embracing the whole method of speaking in a kind of bundle, by which it is clearly evident to all that he always strove with tireless labour that the glory of letters, and especially of jurisprudence, might grow and be increasingly advanced and enriched. He taught law at Bourges, with such fame and esteem for his name that many students, even from distant regions, flocked to hear him. He flourished in the year of human salvation 1542, at the same time as Alciatus. He wrote on divided and undivided obligations, or stipulations, and on servitudes. He published commentaries on the Pandects and the Institutes. Likewise, questions on jurisdiction, and seven books of manual notes on the Digest or Pandects.

units.la: ANDREAS Alciatus Mediolanensis Jurisconsultus clarissimus, quanto ingenij acumine, quanquè scientia & eruditione valuerit, non opus est hic pluribus aperire. Fuit valde acutus & subtilis in scribendo, præcipuè verò in suis emblematibus, quæ varias picturas circiter centum, tanquàm hieroglyphica continét, quorum significationem, quæ singulas sequuntur elegiaca epigrammata, argute explicant. Composuit infinitos propè libros, partim de legibus, partim aliis de rebus, quæ ad humaniores literas spectare videntur. Edidit libellum de ponderibus & mensuris: historiæ encomium: in P. Cornelii Tacitum castigationes, ac difficilium aliquot locorū expositiones. Orationem composuit in laudem juris Civilis, & alia plurima scripsit. Excessit è vita anno àreparata salute humana 1550. ANDREAS TIRAQVELLVS
units.tr: ANDREAS Alciatus of Milan, a most distinguished jurist: how great his keenness of wit and how much he excelled in learning and erudition, there is no need to explain here at length. He was very sharp and subtle in writing, especially in his emblems, which contain some hundred various pictures, as if they were hieroglyphics, whose meanings the elegiac epigrams that follow each one explain with wit. He composed an almost endless number of books, some on laws, others on various subjects which seem to belong to the more humane letters. He published a small book on weights and measures, a eulogy of history, corrections of Publius Cornelius Tacitus, and explanations of some difficult passages. He composed an oration in praise of civil law, and wrote many other things. He departed this life in the year of human salvation 1550. ANDREAS TIRAQUELLUS.

units.la: ANDREAS Tiraquellus Iurisconsultus celeberrimus & regius in curia Parisiensi Senator, iure omnium suorum æqualium doctissimus erat existimatus. Laboris ingentis admodum patiens, scripsit & doctissimè quidem est interpretatus plures nobilisimos titulos iuris. Inter alia, scripsit super tit. de legibus connubialibus & iure maritali, magnum volumen inscriptum, de utroque Retractu municipali & conuentionali, opus maximi pretij & momenti: de reuocandis donationibus, in l. Si unquam, Item de nobilitate & iure primogeniorum, commentarios, & plures alios admirabiles iuris tractatus. Quod ad literas humaniores attinet, Dierum Genialium Alexandri ab Alexandro Iurisperiti Neapolitani, libros sex diligentissimè commentatus est, & commentationes suas in eumdem, Semestria appellat: opus ingens & valde utile quod quidem est præ manibus Gulielmi Rouillij, qui breui illud in lucem missurus est, ut studiosi hoc thesauro diutius abdito, huius opera, potiantur. Obiit Lutetiæ, die 23. Decembris, anno salutis 1556.
units.tr: ANDREAS Tiraquellus, a most celebrated jurist and royal councillor in the Parliament of Paris, was esteemed the most learned in law of all his equals. Very patient of immense labour, he wrote and most learnedly interpreted several most noble titles of law. Among other things, he wrote a great volume on the title concerning marriage laws and marital right, entitled "On both kinds of municipal and conventional redemption," a work of the greatest worth and importance; on the revoking of gifts, on the law Si unquam; likewise commentaries on nobility and the right of primogeniture, and several other admirable treatises on law. As far as the more humane letters are concerned, he very diligently commented on the six books of the Genial Days of Alexander ab Alexandro, the Neapolitan jurist, and he calls his own commentaries on the same work the Semestria: a huge and very useful work, which is indeed in the hands of William Rouillé, who is about to bring it to light shortly, so that students may enjoy the labours of this man, the treasure having been hidden for too long. He died at Paris, on 23 December, in the year of salvation 1556.

units.la: PETRVS Rebuffus celeberrimus iuriū [?] doctor & Comes, memoriâ suâ ita nobis cōmendauit, ut nemo non eius nomen summa cū laude celebret. Natus est circiter annū Domini 1500. in loco, de Ballanicis, nō procul à Mōtepessulo [?], ex clara familia. Docuit celebriter in ciuitate Pictauensi, & Postea Lutetiæ professus est ius canonicum, à Senatu supremo ferè coactus circiter annū 1533. & ab hinc in supremo illo senatu causas foreses quādiu vixit, cū docendo, tū scribendo & cōsulendo exercuit. Fuit mitis, castus, sobrius, pauperum amator, fidei Catholicæ religiosissimus obseruator, ita studiis addictus ut sexagenarius literas Hebraicas & Græcas ediscere voluerit. Scripsit multa egregia opera in ius ciuile & canonicū: quæ quia sunt infinita, hæc pagina capere non potest. Obiit febre correptus die 2. Nouēb. 1557. MARIANVS. SOCINVS. SENENSIS. HIER. CAGNOL. [?]
units.tr: PETER Rebuffus, the most celebrated doctor of laws and Count, has so commended his memory to us that no one fails to celebrate his name with the highest praise. He was born about the year of the Lord 1500, in the place of Balaruc, not far from Montpellier, of a distinguished family. He taught publicly in the city of Poitiers, and afterwards at Paris he professed canon law, almost compelled by the Supreme Senate about the year 1533, and from then on, as long as he lived, he practised in that Supreme Senate the cases he pleaded, both by teaching, writing and giving counsel. He was gentle, chaste, sober, a lover of the poor, a most religious observer of the Catholic faith, and so devoted to his studies that at sixty years of age he wished to learn Hebrew and Greek. He wrote many excellent works on civil and canon law, which, since they are endless, this page cannot hold. He died of a fever on 2 November 1557. MARIANUS SOCINUS OF SIENA. HIER. CAGNOLUS.

units.la: MARIANVS Socinus Senensis Iunior celeberrimus iuris professor, quanto ingenio quantáque doctrina emicuerit, testantur tot eius non minus elegátia quàm grauia scripta. Docuit Pisis, Senis, deinde Patauij annos quā plurimos: postremò Bononiam euocatus, ibi summa cùm laude semper est professus, in magna auditorum frequentia. Claruit anno Christi 1566. Scripsit tria magna consiliorum volumina. Commentaria quæ in celebrioribus Italiæ gymnasiis vulgò leguntur, & alia plurima, quorum elenchum potes videre in Bibliotheca Gesneri.
units.tr: Marianus Socinus the Younger of Siena, a most celebrated professor of law, is attested by the many writings of his, no less elegant than weighty, to have shone with how great a talent and how great a learning. He taught at Pisa, at Siena, then at Padua for very many years; at last, called to Bologna, he always lectured there with the highest praise, before a great crowd of listeners. He flourished in the year of Christ 1566. He wrote three large volumes of opinions (Consilia). Commentaries, which are commonly read in the more famous schools of Italy, and very many others, whose list you may see in Gesner's Bibliotheca.

units.la: HIERONYMVS Cagnolus patritius Vercellésis eques & Iurisconsultus clarissimus, illustrissimi Ducis Sabaudiæ Senator, ac professor Iuris Cæsarei Patauij: de re literaria optimè meruit, utpote qui ad promouenda studia legum, multa memoriæ tradiderit scriptisque mandauerit, unde non mediocrem honorem est adeptus. Scripsit de Origine Iuris. Item copiosam & subtilem interpretationè omnium legum tituli ff. de reg. iuris. Floruit circiter annum salutis 1540. Omnia eius opera in tres tomos distributa impressa sunt Lugduni 1569. in folio. AVR. PARACELSVS D. MED.
units.tr: Hieronymus Cagnolus, patrician of Vercelli, knight and most distinguished jurist, senator of the most illustrious Duke of Savoy, and professor of Imperial Law at Padua, deserved very well of literature; for in promoting the study of the laws he handed down much to memory and committed it to writing, whence he won no small honour. He wrote On the Origin of Law. Likewise a full and subtle interpretation of all the laws of the title Digest, de regulis iuris. He flourished around the year of salvation 1540. All his works, distributed into three tomes, were printed at Lyon in 1569, in folio. Aurelius Paracelsus, Doctor of Medicine.

units.la: THEOPHRASTVS Paracelsus Heluetius novæ me-dicinæ author, Hippocratis, Galeni & Avicennæ institutis omnino contrariæ, maximos labores pertulit, ut humano generi prodesset: maximè verò Leprosis, podagricis, pestis tetræ contagione affectis, Hydropicis & omnibus aliis, quorum morbis, Galeni sectatoribus, quos Barbaros vocat, succurrere difficile existimat. Docuit Basileæ magno stipendio invitatus, libros, quorum ipse autor fuit. Dicitur fuisse, animi integritate, pietateque in egenos nulli secundus. Vixit annos XLVIII. Anno Domini M. D. XLI. die XXIIII. Septembris vitam cum morte mutavit: sepultus est Salisburgę in Nosocomio ad S. Sebastianum, cuius lapidi, multa de eo præclara epitaphia conspiciuntur.
units.tr: Theophrastus Paracelsus of Switzerland, author of a new medicine wholly contrary to the teachings of Hippocrates, Galen and Avicenna, endured very great labours so that he might benefit the human race; above all he tried to help lepers, the gouty, those afflicted with the foul contagion of plague, dropsical patients and all others whose diseases, he judges, are hard to cure for the followers of Galen, whom he calls barbarians. He taught at Basel, invited there at a large salary, and the books of which he himself was the author. He is said to have been second to none in integrity of mind and in piety toward the needy. He lived forty-eight years. In the year of the Lord 1541, on the 24th day of September, he exchanged life for death; he was buried at Salzburg in the hospital of St Sebastian, on whose tombstone many praiseworthy epitaphs about him may be seen.

units.la: IACOBVS Hollerius Stempanus Medicus, vir magnus, & suæ, id est Hippocraticæ artis ac doctrinæ peritissimus, scripsit multa, maximè verò est interpretatus & cōmētatus[?] magni Hippocratis coacca præsagia, opus planè divinū, & veræ medicinæ tanquam thesaurus, multum temporis consumpsit in isto immenso labore, multaque lucubrationes reliquit, viginti plusquam annis iam exactis: sed mors immatura eius vitæ simul & laboribus fine imposuit. Unde opus fuit ut Jacotius Vandoperanus (adiectis, suo marte, libris 13.[?] ad idem opus commentariis, tribus sectionibus distinctis ne nimis obscurum prodiret) illud perficeret, cùm multa essent perturbata & lituris deformata: multa imperfecta. Id autem fuit diligenter & accuratè excusum Lugduni à Gulielmo Rouillio, anno 1573. Florebat autem Lutetiæ anno 1550. I. FERNELIVS. D. MED. IACOB. SILVIVS.
units.tr: Jacobus Hollerius of Stempan, physician, a great man, and most skilled in his own art, that is, the Hippocratic art and doctrine, wrote many things; above all he translated and commented on the great Hippocrates' Prognostics, a work truly divine and like a treasure of true medicine. He spent much time on that immense labour and left many lucubrations, more than twenty years having already passed; but an untimely death put an end both to his life and to his labours. Hence it was necessary that Jacotius Vandoperanus should complete the work (adding, on his own initiative, commentaries on the same work in thirteen books, distinguished into three sections so that it would not come out too obscure), since many things were disordered and disfigured by erasures, and many unfinished. This was printed carefully and accurately at Lyon by Guillaume Rouille, in 1573. He flourished at Paris in the year 1550. J. Fernelius, Doctor of Medicine; Jacob Silvius.

units.la: IOANNES Fernelius Ambianus Medicus præstantissimus, nullū non lapidem mouit, vt rem medicam magis ac magis illustraret atque promoueret, tot aliorum exemplo, qui in medicina & docenda & elucidanda semper sudarunt. Scripsit, inter alia, de abditis rerum causis lib.duos: Medicinam ad Henricum 2. Galliarū Regem: Cosmotheoriæ libros duos, impressos Parisiis apud Colinæum: de naturali parte medicinæ libros septem: de vacuandi ratione, vnum. In eius Medicina côtinentur Physiologię libri septem, de elementis, de temperamētis, de spiritibus & innato calido, de animę facultatibus, de functionibus &humoribus, de hominis procreatione atque de femine Pathologię libri sex: Item Therapētices vniuersalis, seu de medendi ratione libri septem. Floruit anno salutis 1547.
units.tr: Johannes Fernelius of Amiens, a most outstanding physician, left no stone unturned to illustrate and advance the medical art more and more, following the example of so many others who always laboured in both teaching and clarifying medicine. He wrote, among other things, two books On the Hidden Causes of Things; Medicine, addressed to Henry II, King of the French; two books of Cosmotheoria, printed at Paris by Colinaeus; seven books On the Natural Part of Medicine; one book On the Method of Purging. In his Medicine are contained seven books of Physiology: on the elements, on the temperaments, on the spirits and innate heat, on the faculties of the soul, on the functions and humours, on the procreation of man and on the seed; six books of Pathology; likewise seven books of Universal Therapeutics, or on the method of healing. He flourished in the year of salvation 1547.

units.la: IACOBVS Siluius Medicus etiā inter alios celebris fuit: in quem multa beneficia collata fuere à Stephano Poncherio Baionensi Episcopo, tum integerrimo, tum doctissimo, vt ipse testatur in ea epistola, qua eius Præsulis dignitati dedicauit Ioannis Mesuæ medici præstantissimi interpretationem: opus equidem arduum & ante impeditum, nuncautem eius cura atque summa diligentia expeditum atque expolitum, vt iam doctis nõ placere modo, sed etiam prodesse possit plurimū. Vnde, quam noster Syluius laudem meruit ex eo facilè est perspicere, quòd difficillimum sit rebus longa & obscura caligine mersis, & velut illuuie sordida obsitis, dare aut verius reddere splendorem. Maxima ei cum Manardo ætatis suæ medico etiam doctissimo intercessit familiaritas, quiquidem ipsius etiam Mesuę obscuram & sordidam versionem potius quam Mesuen, emaculare alicubi & clariorem reddere tentauit. Huius Siluij præceptor fuit in re medica Ioannes Tagaultius vndequaque absolutus. Floruit anno reparatæ salutis humanæ 1557. HIER. CARD. Q. MED. C. SCALIGERVS
units.tr: Jacobus Silvius, a physician, was likewise among the other famous men; many benefits were conferred upon him by Stephen Poncher, Bishop of Bayonne, a most upright and most learned man, as he himself attests in the letter with which he dedicated to that prelate's dignity his translation of the most excellent physician John Mesue: a work indeed arduous and formerly obstructed, but now, through his care and very great diligence, cleared and polished, so that it can now please the learned, and not merely please but be of very great use. Hence it is easy to perceive what praise our Silvius deserved, since it is most difficult to give, or rather to restore, brilliance to things sunk in long and obscure darkness and covered over as with a dirty filth. He had the greatest intimacy with Manardus, a physician of his own age and also most learned, who indeed tried in places to clean up the obscure and dirty translation of Mesue himself, and to render it clearer rather than Mesue. The teacher of this Silvius in medicine was John Tagault, complete in every respect. He flourished in the year of restored human salvation 1557. Hieronymus Cardanus, Doctor of Medicine; J. C. Scaliger.

units.la: HIERONYMVS Cardanus, Medicus Mediolanensis subtilissimus, multa scripsit tam acute & diligenter, vt merito ab omnibus literatis, ob eius summum ingenium exactamque plurimarum rerum cognitionem, passim existimetur. Scripsit Arithmeticam absolutissimam: Practicam Arithmeticae & mesurandi singularem, Artis magnae, siue de regulis algebraicis, librum vnū, qui & totius operis de Arithmetica, quod opus perfectum inscripsit, est in ordine, decimus: de Sapientia libros quinque: de consolatione libros tres, ab authore recognitos: de immortalitate animae, librū excusum à Gryphio, Lugduni anno Domini 1545. in 8. chartis 20. Contradicentium medicorū librum, continentem contradictiones 1081. de malo recentium medicorum medendi vsu, libellum, 100. errores illorum, continentem: & infinitos alios, quos hæc pagina non potest capere. Floruit anno salutis 1544.
units.tr: Hieronymus Cardanus, a most acute physician of Milan, wrote many things so keenly and diligently that, on account of his outstanding talent and exact knowledge of very many things, he is rightly esteemed by all men of letters everywhere. He wrote a most complete Arithmetic; a singular Practice of Arithmetic and Measuring; one book Ars Magna, or On the Rules of Algebra, which, as the tenth in order, is also part of the whole work on Arithmetic, which he titled a finished work; five books On Wisdom; three books On Consolation, revised by the author; a book On the Immortality of the Soul, printed by Gryphius at Lyon in the year of the Lord 1545, in octavo, twenty sheets. A book Against Contradicting Physicians, containing 1081 contradictions; a little book On the Bad Use of Medicine by Recent Physicians, containing 100 of their errors; and infinitely many others, which this page cannot contain. He flourished in the year of salvation 1544.

units.la: IVLIVS Cæsar Scaliger, Iosephi Scaligeri frater, vir magni nominis hic laudandus venit, qui de causis linguę Latinę 13. lib. scripsit: de comicis dimensionibus: commentarios in Hippocratis librum de somniis, adiecto etiam textu ab eodem converso: commentarios in libros duos, qui inscribuntur de plantis, Aristotele autore: plurima acutè & solidè confutauit ab Hieronymo Cardano scripta, in libris de subtilitate: composuit de Poëtica libros sex, varia eruditione refertos: commentarios in Theophrasti libros de plantis: verae Alchimiae artisque metallicae citra ænigmata doctrinam certumque modum scripsit: de sapientia & beatitudine libros 8. quos Epidormides inscripsit: unde & plurimis aliis frugiferis commentationibus magnam gloriam est assecutus. Floruit tempore Cardani. [illegible, ~8 letters] ANDREAS MATTHIOL [?] D. MED DON. ANTONI. ALTOMAR [?] VS. D MED.
units.tr: Julius Caesar Scaliger, brother of Joseph Scaliger, a man of great name who is to be praised here, wrote thirteen books On the Causes of the Latin Language; On Comic Measures; commentaries on the book of Hippocrates On Dreams, with the text also translated by the same man added; commentaries on two books which are entitled On Plants, the author being Aristotle; he sharply and solidly refuted very many things written by Hieronymus Cardanus, in the books On Subtlety; he composed six books On Poetics, filled with varied learning; commentaries on the books of Theophrastus On Plants; he wrote the doctrine and certain method of true alchemy and the metallic art, without enigmas; eight books On Wisdom and Blessedness, which he entitled Epidormides; whence, by very many other fruitful commentaries too, he obtained great glory. He flourished in the time of Cardanus. [illegible] Andreas Matthiolus, Doctor of Medicine; Donatus Antonius Altomarus, Doctor of Medicine.

units.la: PETRVS Andreas Matthiolus Senēsis Medicus præstātissimus, studiosis inservire cupiens, scripsit de morbi Gallici curatione librum, per dialogū digestū, inter se & Franciscum Aligerum:Commentarios longè doctissimos in libros sex D ioscoridis, de medica materia, qui sæpius Italicè editi, postremò ab ipso authore in Latinam linguā translati sunt. Adiectæ sunt innumeræ plantarum & animalium imagines ad viuum expressæ. Et quia in tanto opere nihil quicquam deest quod ad delectationem & maximam non medicorum tantùm & Pharmacopoeorum utilitatem faciat, quæ duo, scripta quævis reddunt absolutiora & digna quæ in manus hominum doctorum & ingeniosorum deveniant, Gulielmus Rouillius curavit, ut tàm necessarium opus, viri doctissimi opera, in linguam Gallicam converteretur, eorum gratia qui Latinam ignorant. Hic plura alia literis mandavit quæ brevitatis causa prętermittenda censui. Floruit anno 1536.
units.tr: Petrus Andreas Matthiolus of Siena, a most outstanding physician, wishing to serve students, wrote a book on the treatment of the French disease, arranged as a dialogue between himself and Francis Aliger; very learned commentaries on the six books of Dioscorides On Medical Matter, which were often published in Italian and at last translated into Latin by the author himself. Countless images of plants and animals, drawn from life, were added. And since in so great a work there is nothing lacking that contributes to delight and to the very great usefulness not only of physicians and pharmacists, which two things make any writings more complete and worthy to come into the hands of learned and clever men, William Rouille took care that so necessary a work, the labour of a most learned man, should be turned into the French language, for the sake of those who do not know Latin. He committed many other things to writing here, which I have judged should be passed over for the sake of brevity. He flourished in the year 1536.

units.la: DONATVS Antonius ab Altomari Philosophus & medicus Neapolitanus, doctissimus plura scripsit opuscula, quæ sparsa, fusa & mendis referta, in unum cogenda & limatius imprimenda curavit: quod se fecisse profitetur, non ut eius opera essent præclara, ut ipse inquit, 'ingenij sui monimeta, sed ut amicorum petitioni satisfaceret, & fructus extarent ocij pomeridianiad Gal. semper & Hippoc. mentem, ex eius instituto. Adiecit novissimè suis operibus, vir studiosissimus tractatum de venæ sectione in utero geretibus ad mentem Senis & Galeni lucidatum, atque recognitum. Demum de latitudine sanitatis opusculum: quibus universa artis medicæ dubia à confusoribus ducta facillimè eluuntur. Floruit anno 1547.
units.tr: Donatus Antonius ab Altomari, Neapolitan philosopher and physician, most learned, wrote several small works, which, scattered, poured out and full of errors, he took care to gather into one and to print more polished; this he professes to have done not so that his works might be illustrious, as he himself says, "memorials of his own talent," but so as to satisfy the request of friends, and so that the fruits of his afternoon leisure might survive, always according to the mind of Galen and Hippocrates, in accordance with his plan. Most recently he added to his works, as a most studious man, a treatise on bloodletting in pregnant women, clarified and revised according to the mind of Siena and Galen. Finally, a little work On the Breadth of Health; by which all the doubts of the whole medical art, raised by confusers, are most easily cleared away. He flourished in the year 1547.

units.la: ANDREAS Vesalius, Bruxellensis vir clarus, de re anatomica,& humani corporis fabrica,'adiectis figuris,elegantissimè scripsit,cuius scripta medicis sunt in magno precio, vtpote quæ ad medicinæ perfectam cognitionem & praxim, necessaria esse dubium non sit. Scripsit paraphrasim in 9. librum Rasis ad regem Almâsorem, De affectuum singularum corporis partium curatione. Item Epistolam, qua docet venam axillarem dextri cubiti,in dolore laterali secandam:aliam, qua rationem docet propinandi radicis Chynæ decocti, & tractat anatomica multa,quauis titulus non promittat.Emendauit etiâ translationè anatomicorum aliquot Galeni librorum, qui cum cæteris Galeni operibus excusi sunt Venetiis apus Iuntas. Floruit anno 1540.
units.tr: Andreas Vesalius of Brussels, a distinguished man, wrote most elegantly on anatomy and the structure of the human body, with figures added. His writings are held in high esteem by physicians, since there is no doubt that they are necessary for a complete knowledge and practice of medicine. He wrote a paraphrase of the ninth book of Rhazes, addressed to the king Almansor, On the treatment of the disorders of the individual parts of the body. He also wrote a letter teaching that the axillary vein of the right arm should be opened in cases of pleurisy; another, teaching the method of administering a decoction of China root, and treating of many anatomical matters, though the title does not promise this. He also emended the anatomical translation of some books of Galen, which were printed together with the rest of Galen's works at Venice by the Giunta press. He flourished in the year 1540.

units.la: IOANNES Argenterius,Castellonouensis,Medicus clariffimus,Pisis rem medicam professus est : scripsit multa ad medicinæ perfectâ notitiam spectantia. Quocirca censuimus eum inter viros egregios numerandum,eiúsque imaginem studiosis promendâ, vt ne huic tanto viro & de literis bene merito, suus aliqua ex parte honos deesset, qui tamen ex eius ipsius scriptis satis superque laudatur. Scripsit de consultationibus medicis, siue de collegiandi ratione librum : item de erroribus veterum medicorum , librum:præterea de somno & putrefactione contra Aristotelem, libellos nondum editos, vt existimo ,Glossemata in Aphorismos Hippocratis:Commentarios tres in artem medicinalem Galeni : De somno & vigilia, de spiritibus & calido natiuo, libros duos , in quibus multæ veterum scriptorum: ac recentium sententiæ expenduntur. Claruit anno reparatæ salutis humanæ 1550. GVIL. RONDELETIVS DOC. MEDIC. HIPPOLITVS SILVIANVS.
units.tr: Johannes Argenterius of Castellonovo, a most distinguished physician, taught medicine at Pisa and wrote much bearing on a complete knowledge of medicine. For this reason we have judged that he should be counted among the outstanding men, and that his likeness should be brought forward for scholars, so that some measure of honour might not be lacking to so great a man, one who has deserved well of letters, although he is already praised more than enough by his own writings. He wrote a book On medical consultations, or on the manner of consulting together; likewise a book On the errors of the ancient physicians; moreover, the small books On sleep and putrefaction, against Aristotle, which have not yet been published, as I believe; Glosses on the Aphorisms of Hippocrates; three commentaries on Galen's Art of Medicine; and two books On sleep and waking, On the spirits and the innate heat, in which the opinions of many ancient writers and of recent ones are weighed. He flourished in the year of restored human salvation 1550. William Rondelet, Doctor of Medicine; Hippolytus Salvianus.

units.la: GVLIELMVS Rondeletius, Doctor medicus,& medicinæ in schola Monspelienfi, profeffor Regius, & Cancellarius magnam est adeptus nominis existimationem in docēdo. Scripfit de piscibus marinis plures libros, in quibus veræ piscium imagines expressæ conspiciuntur:ita studiosus visus est rei medicæ, etiam calamitosis temporibus, propagandæ. Non potuit autem,morte præuentus, Methodum suam curandorum omnium corporis morborum,prælo mandare,vt alia perutilia opera:sed factum est doctorum medicorum cura, vt ad fideliorem quàm fieri potuit exemplaris typum eadem Methodus excuderetur:quanquam pluribus in locis,non solum autoris fui iam defuncti,sed& diligentissimi emēdatoris egeret censura. Deus enim omnia in omnes diuidit,alter vt ope alterius indigeat. Ac cessit igitur ante huius editionem, diligens opera & accurata præleētio doēti cuiufdam Medici(Rondeletij olim perfamiliaris) qui exemplar à fe emendatum, cúmque optimis exemplaribus collatum Gulielmo Rouillio diligentissimo typographo dedit excudendum. Hic fertur nunquam bibisse vinum. Floruit autem anno 1550.
units.tr: William Rondelet, Doctor of Medicine and Regius Professor of Medicine in the school at Montpellier, and its Chancellor, gained great reputation for his teaching. He wrote several books on sea fishes, in which true images of the fishes are seen expressed. He seemed so devoted to the advancement of medical science, even in troubled times. However, prevented by death, he could not send his Method of curing all bodily diseases to the press, as he did with other very useful works. But it was by the care of learned physicians that the same Method was printed, as faithfully as the copy could be made to allow, although in many places it needed the scrutiny not only of its author, now deceased, but of a most diligent corrector. For God divides all things among all, so that one may need the help of another. Thus, before this edition, the diligent labour and accurate reading of a certain learned physician, once a very close friend of Rondelet, came about: he gave his copy, corrected by himself and compared with the best manuscripts, to William Rouillé, a most diligent printer, to be printed. He is said never to have drunk wine. He flourished, moreover, in the year 1550.

units.la: HIPPOLITVS Saluianus Typhernas Medicus Romanus, iure inter doctos censendus, qui librum scripsit de Aquatilibus cum iconibus seu figuris centum,ęri elegăter insculptis. Impressus est autem hic liber Romę, in authoris ædibus,1557. in filio magnæ chartæ. Floruit anno 1550.
units.tr: Hippolytus Salvianus of Tuscania, a Roman physician, rightly to be counted among the learned, who wrote the book On aquatic animals, with one hundred images or figures elegantly engraved. This book was printed at Rome, in the author's own house, in 1557, in a large folio. He flourished in the year 1550.
MARCELLUS II, POPE, OF MONTEPULCIANO, TUSCAN.

units.la: MARCELLVS secundus Iunior Politianensis Tuscus, Marcellus Ceruinus Ricardi filius, ex episcopo Neocastrensi praesbyter Cardinalis, tt. Sãctæ Crucis in Hierusalé à Paulo tertio factus, Carolo v. Augusto, sedit in Pontificatu, dies 21. Natus in oppido agri Piceni Montis Fani pridie Nonas Maij, anno 1501. creatus Romæ, v.
