Idus Aprilis, 1555. hora 24. à triginta sex Cardinalibus. Postridie coronatus. Obiit die Mercurij Kal. Maij, inter septimam & octauam horam noctis precedentis. Vixit annos quinquaginta quatuor, menses vndecim, dies viginti quinque: sepultus est ad Sanctum Petrũ: vacauitque sedes eo mortuo, dies 22. Fuit autem ducentesimus vigesimus septimus Pontifex. Vide Platinam, in eius vita.
units.tr: Marcellus II, junior, of Montepulciano, Tuscan, son of Richard Cervini Marcellus, formerly Bishop of Nocera, made a priest-cardinal, with the title of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, by Paul III, under Charles V Augustus, sat in the papacy for 21 days. Born in the town of Monte San Giovanni in the district of Picenum on 6 May 1501; created at Rome on 11 April 1555, at the twenty-fourth hour, by thirty-six cardinals. Crowned the day after. He died on Wednesday, 1 May, between the seventh and eighth hours of the preceding night. He lived fifty-four years, eleven months and twenty-five days; he was buried at St Peter's, and the see was vacant for 22 days after his death. He was the two hundred and twenty-seventh Pontiff. See Platina, in his life.

units.la: PAVLVS 1111. Neapolitanus, Ioannes Petrus Carafa, Ioannis Alfonsi Matalunæ comitis filius, archiepiscopus Neapolitanus, ex presbytero tt. Sancti Clementis, presbyter tt. Sanctæ Mariæ Transtiberim, Episcopus Cardinalis Albanus, & Sabinus à Paulo tertio factus, Tusculanus & Ostiensis, à Iulio 111. Decanus, Imperatoribus Cæsare Carolo v. & Ferdinando Aug. sedit in pontificatu, annos 4. menses 2. dies 27. Natus est in oppido sancti Angeli de scala, 1111. Kal. Iulij, anno 1476. in Hirpinis, haud procul à Beneuento. Creatus Romæ, authore Farnesio Cardinale, à xliiii. Cardinalibus, die Iouis festo Ascésionis x. Kal. Iunij, anno 1555. hora xvi. Coronatus ad sanctum Petrum die dominico proximo vii. Kal. Iunij. Ordinationibus tribus, mensibus Iunio, & Decembri, factis. Cardinales creauit xix: presbyteros xx. & diaconos iiii: Obiit Romæ, die Veneris, x v. kal. Septembris, hora inter xxi. & xxii. anno 1559. vixit annos xxciii. mensem vnum & dies xxii. sepultus ad sanctũ Petrum, postea ad Mineruam translatus. Vacauit eo mortuo Romana sedes, menses 4. & 7. dies. Fuit Pontifex nume-ro 228. Vide Platinam. HOSIVS POLON. EPISC. DOCTOR. NAVARRVS. MAR. AZPIL. CVETA.
units.tr: PAUL IV, Neapolitan, Giovanni Pietro Carafa, son of Giovanni Alfonso, Count of Matalona, Archbishop of Naples, formerly priest of San Clemente, priest of Santa Maria in Trastevere, Cardinal Bishop of Albano and Sabina, made by Paul III, Tusculan and Ostian, Dean under Julius III, under the Emperors Charles V and Ferdinand Augustus, sat in the papacy for 4 years, 2 months and 27 days. Born in the town of Sant'Angelo de Scala, on 1 June 1476, in the Hirpini region, not far from Benevento. Created at Rome, by the authority of Cardinal Farnese, by 44 cardinals, on Thursday, the feast of the Ascension, 23 May 1555, at the sixteenth hour. Crowned at St Peter's on the following Sunday, 26 May. He made three ordinations, in June and December. He created nineteen cardinals, twenty priests and four deacons. He died at Rome on Friday, 18 August, between the twenty-first and twenty-second hours, in the year 1559. He lived 83 years, one month and 22 days. He was buried at St Peter's, and afterwards translated to Minerva. The Roman see was vacant for four months and seven days after his death. He was the Pontiff number 228. See Platina. Hosius of Poland, bishop, doctor; Navarrese; Mar. Azpilcueta; Cueta.

units.la: STANISLAVS Hosius,Cardinalis Polonus,Episcopus Vuarmensis, legatus Romani Pontificis, & Præses in Concilio Tridentino,vir doctissimus, & fidei catholicæ accerrimus propugnator Scripsit Confessione fidei sæpius impressam & ab auctore nunc demum ita auctā,ut nouū opus videri possit. Hæc est tanti momenti, ut etiā è Latino in Gallicū idioma conuersa sit nuperrime à Ioanne de Lauardin. Scripsit præterea de expresso Dei verbo: Dialogum num calice laicis,& uxores sacerdotibus permitti fas sit : & plura alia. Viuit adhuc Romæ,cum supradicto Azpilcueta.
units.tr: Stanislaus Hosius, Polish Cardinal, Bishop of Warmia, legate of the Roman Pontiff, and President at the Council of Trent, a most learned man and a very zealous champion of the Catholic faith. He wrote the Confession of Faith, printed many times, and now at last expanded by the author so that it may seem a new work. It is of such importance that it was very recently translated from Latin into the French language by John de Lauardin. He also wrote On the express word of God, and a Dialogue on whether it is lawful to permit the laity the chalice and wives to priests, and many other things. He still lives at Rome, together with the aforesaid Azpilcueta.

units.la: MARTINVS ab Azpilcueta doctor Nauarrus, insignis & literarū cognitione præstās, pietatis obseruatissimus,& iuris Pontificij cōsultissimus, ita ut in prælegendo & interpretando eo iure in celebri Academia Corymbricensi, primū locū obtinuerit,laudis alienæ minime cupidus: cū dicat in quadam epistola, huius usurpationem esse veluti notā furti, ut ait Iurisconf. in l. hæreditatum. §. sin. ff. ad l. falc. Is iam octogenarius, magno studio & labore proprio, versioni sui Enchiridij siue Manualis Confessariorū & Pœnitentiū, incubuit:cum multi pro sua in Deū & republica pietate,& in authore beneuolentia, Latinè, Hispanéque callētes, sacræque Theologiæ & utriusque iuris professores id præstare vellent, bonāque iam parte prestitissent:verū id non fecit gloriæ causa, sed ut plenius satisfaceret Reip. Christianæ, & quā plurimis utriusque Hesperiæ viris,erudita pietate claris, auctoritate Pontificia Reuerendiss. imo & Cardinalitia dignitate illustriss.ad id eū vehementer exortatibus. Scripsit tractatum de edditibus beneficiorū,super ca. Quicquid 16.q 1.quo docetur quibus usibus sint impedēdi, & quibus personis dādi aut relinquēdi:de finibus humanorū actuū,tractatū:& plures alios libros ex quibus vir dignitate clarus non mediocrē laudem meretur. FRANCISCVS DVA RENVS IVRISC. FRAN. BALDVIN.
units.tr: Martin of Azpilcueta, Navarrese doctor, excelling in his distinguished knowledge of letters, most observant of piety, and most learned in Pontifical law, so that in lecturing on and interpreting that law at the famous Academy of Coimbra he obtained first place, being in no way eager for the praise of others, since he says in a certain letter that the use of another's work is, as the jurist says, like a mark of theft. Now an octogenarian, by great zeal and his own labour, he has applied himself to the translation of his Enchiridion, or Manual, for Confessors and Penitents. Though many, out of their piety towards God and the commonwealth, and their goodwill towards the author, who knew Latin and Spanish, and professors of sacred theology and of both laws, wished to do this, and had already done a good part of it, he did not do so for the sake of glory, but so that he might more fully satisfy the Christian commonwealth, and because many men of both Hesperias, distinguished for their learned piety, most strongly urged him to it, the most reverend, indeed most illustrious, by Pontifical authority and Cardinalate dignity. He wrote a treatise On the revenues of benefices, on the chapter Quicquid, 16 q. 1, in which it is taught for what uses they are to be employed, and to what persons they are to be given or bequeathed; a treatise On the ends of human acts; and several other books, by which a man of distinguished rank deserves no small praise. Francis Duaren, jurist; Francis Baldwin.

units.la: FRANCISCVS Duarenus Iurisconsultus clarissimus, quē hæc nostra ætas proximè habuit, quandiu orbis diuina stabit prouidentia, celebrabitur. Quantū enim coluerit Iuris prudentiā, eiúsque studia promouerit, testantur tot eius grauissimi viri opera, quæ omnia edita sunt Lugduni apud Gulielmū Rouilliū, qui hoc præstantissimū opus Iconū concinnē & verè, & Laconica breuitate confectū, elegantibus (vt solet omnia) typis excudendū curauit. Docuit in celebri Biturigū Academia, tótque discipulos habuit, vt omniū tunc tēporis Iuris professorum facilè princeps haberetur. Scripsit de in litē iurādo, iudiciisqne bonę fidei & arbitrariis cōmētariū. His adiicitur Decretū quod dā senatus Biturigū: scripsit Epistolā de docendi discendiqué iuris ratione: Apologiā de iurisdictione & imperio: libros octo de ministeriis ecclesiæ & beneficiis: super 1. & 2 ff. veteris: super 1. & 2. Infortiati: super 1. ff. noui: super 1. Cod. & plura alia. Eius opera omnia auctiora edita sunt Lugduni apud Gulielmū Rouillium. Claruit anno 1555.
units.tr: Francis Duaren, the most famous jurist, whom our age has lately had, will be celebrated as long as the divine providence of the world endures. For how much he cherished the science of law and promoted its studies is attested by the many weighty works of his, all of which were published at Lyons by William Rouillé, who had this most excellent work, composed neatly and truly and with Laconic brevity, printed with elegant type, as he always did with everything. He taught in the famous Academy of Bourges and had so many pupils that he was readily regarded as the foremost of all the professors of law of that time. He wrote a commentary On the oath in litigation, on judgments of good faith and arbitrary judgments. To these is added a certain decree of the senate of Bourges. He wrote a letter On the method of teaching and learning law; an Apology on jurisdiction and empire; eight books On the ministries of the Church and benefices; on the first and second books of the Digest "Vetus"; on the first and second of the Infortiatum; on the first of the Digest "Novum"; on the first of the Code; and many other things. His complete works were published, enlarged, at Lyons by William Rouillé. He flourished in the year 1555.

units.la: FRANCISCVS Balduinus Iurisconsultus nobilis non parū luminis & ornamenti huic nostrę ætati attulit, ius per tot annos, tanta cū laude professus in omnibus fermè Galliæ celeberrimis Academiis, maximè vero in illa percelebri Andegauensium, in qua ad eū tanquā ad sacrū Apollinis oraculū, vidi plures cōcurrere, vt iuris difficilioris nodos soluerēt, dubia elucidaret, & secreta panderet atque summa facilitate reseraret. Habuit is memoriā admodū fœlicē, fuitque in dicēdo grauissimus atque eloquentissimus. Tandē post multos exantlatos labores in docēdo iure, cū Lutetiā euocatus esset à Carolo Nono Galliarū Rege, vt Poloniæ legatis responderet, qui in Galliā venerant, inuictissimū Henricū Regis fratrē, nunc Regē nostrum Christianissimū nominaturi qui Polonis imperaret, cūque munus suū, cū maximo honore obiisset, fatis cessit anno à Mundi salute, 1573. Florebat anno 1560. PETR. VICTORIUS. FLORENTINUS M. ANTONIUS MURETUS I. C.
units.tr: Francis Balduin, a noble jurist, brought no small light and ornament to our age. He taught law for so many years, with such great praise, in almost all the most celebrated academies of France, and above all in that most famous one at Angers, where I saw many gather around him as around the sacred oracle of Apollo, to untie the knots of more difficult law, to clear up doubtful points, to open up hidden matters and unlock them with the greatest ease. He had a very happy memory and was most grave and most eloquent in speaking. At last, after many labours undergone in teaching law, he was summoned to Paris by Charles IX, King of France, to reply to the envoys of Poland who had come to France to name the most invincible Henry, the King's brother, now our most Christian King, to rule over the Poles. Having discharged this office with the greatest honour, he met his end in the year of the world's salvation 1573. He flourished in the year 1560. PETER VICTORIUS. FLORENTINE. M. ANTONIUS MURETUS, J.C.

units.la: PETRUM Victoriū inter viros præcipuos & eruditos non infimū locū tenere, omnibus eruditis cōstat ex diuersis eius scriptis, quibus eloquentiā maximè coluit. Ciceronis libros castigauit, & adiecit explicationes castigationū. Denique hoc unū curauit vir disertus & in omni literarum genere versatus, ut sui nominis memoria, nulla unquā ætate, intercideret. Scripsit annotationes in Catonem, Varronem, Columellam: Cōmentaria in libros tres Aristotelis, de arte dicendi: variarū lectionū libros viginti quinque ad utriusq; linguæ illustrationē utilissimos pariter iucundissimósque: orationē ad Iuliū iii. Pōtificem Romanū habitā & excusam Florentiæ. Correxit Politica Aristotelis: scripsit etiā alios variarū lectionū libros 4. & plura alia. Hodie viuit & Florentię habitat, à Duce valdè amatus, propter eius summam doctrinam.
units.tr: That Peter Victorius holds no minor place among the outstanding and learned men is agreed by all the learned from his various writings, in which he cultivated eloquence above all. He corrected the books of Cicero and added explanations of his corrections. Finally, this one thing the eloquent man, who was versed in every kind of literature, took care of: that the memory of his name should never perish in any age. He wrote annotations on Cato, Varro and Columella; commentaries on the three books of Aristotle's De arte dicendi (the Rhetoric); twenty-five books of Miscellaneous Readings, equally useful and pleasant for the illustration of both languages; an oration addressed to Pope Julius III, delivered and printed at Florence. He corrected Aristotle's Politics; he also wrote four further books of Miscellaneous Readings, and many other things. He is still alive today and lives at Florence, greatly loved by the Duke on account of his outstanding learning.

units.la: MARCUS Antonius Muretus Lemouix, eloquentissimorū nostræ ætatis hominū numero iure adscribēdus est, cui pura, nitida & elegans oratio, ęternam nominis gloriā peperit, præter eius multiplicem eruditionem, qua Terentiū locis propè innumerabilibus emendauit, ac argumenta in singulas comœdias & annotationes addidit, quibus tum correctionū magna ex parte ratio redditur, tū loci obscuriores explicantur. Scripsit etiā annotationes in Horatiū, Catullum, Tibullū, Propertium, Philippicas Ciceronis, & in Catilinā, orationes, multáque alia ad promouenda studia literarum. Huius extant Iuuenilia Lutetiæ excusa: oratio de studij Theologici præstantia: annotationes in Andriam & Eunuchum Terentij. Quintus Ethicorum Aristotelis, ab eo versus & annotationibus illustratus, & plurima alia. Viuit hodie & Romæ habitat maximè conspicuus. VALERIOLA D. M. FRANCISCVS IAC. DALEC AMPIVS. D. MED.
units.tr: Marcus Antonius Muretus of Limoges is rightly to be counted among the most eloquent men of our age, whose pure, polished and elegant style has won him eternal glory of name, besides his manifold erudition, by which he emended Terence in almost countless places, and added arguments to each comedy and annotations, which both give the reason for many of the corrections and explain the more obscure passages. He also wrote annotations on Horace, Catullus, Tibullus, Propertius, Cicero's Philippics, and on the Catilinarians, and many other works to advance the study of letters. Of his are extant his Juvenilia, printed at Paris; an oration on the excellence of the study of theology; annotations on Terence's Andria and Eunuchus; the fifth book of Aristotle's Ethics, which he illustrated with a verse translation and annotations, and very many other things. He is alive today and lives at Rome, most conspicuous.

units.la: FRANCISCVS Valeriola, præstãtissimus huiusce ætatis medicus, magnam est adeptus nominis existimationem, & artis peritia &Philosophiç totius cognitione.Parua statura fuit, sed maximo ingenio,vt testantur eruditissima eius scripta:quorũ extant in lib. Galeni de constitutione artis medicæ Cõmentarij.Enarrationes medicinales. Loci communes medicinæ ,in tres libros digesti. Obseruationes medicinales lib. 6. Quæ omnia excusa sunt Lugduni apud Gruphium. Docuit Augustæ Taurinorum euocatus ab Emanuele Philiberto clarissimo Sabaudiæ duce,vbi tandem postquam,stipendiis satis magnis,per multos annos,tanta cum celebritate, ius professus est,fatis cefsit nouissimis annis.
units.tr: Francis Valeriola, the most excellent physician of this age, has gained great reputation for his name, both by his skill in the art and by his knowledge of all philosophy. He was small of stature but of very great genius, as his most learned writings attest, of which there are extant commentaries on Galen's De constitutione artis medicae, medicinal expositions, common places of medicine digested into three books, and medicinal observations in six books. All of these were printed at Lyons by Gryphius. He taught at Turin, called there by Emmanuel Philibert, the most illustrious Duke of Savoy, where at last, after he had professed law for many years with such celebrity and with fairly large salary, he met his end in his final years.

units.la: IACOBVS Dalechampius,Cadomensis,Medicus clarissimus,multis abhinc annis, Lugduni rem medicã exercet, tãta eius nominis fama & Reipublicæ Lugdunensis vtilitate,vt omnes æquales suos doctrinæ præstantia & artis experientia longè superet. Sed quid tantùm dicã eũ populi Lugdunensis salutem diuinis remediis tam celebriter curare, cuius nomen clarissimũ nõ solũ vniuersam Galliã, sed plures alias regiones peruagatur, propter eius multiplicem eruditionẽ ,& in medendo non dico solùm præstantiam, sed & facilitatẽ atque summã fœlicitatem? Multis profuit olim docendo,multis profuit scribendo: at pluribus propediem est profuturus diuinis eius cõmentationibus, & stupenda illa Athœnei Græci Latina translatione . quam sese breui euulgaturum & prælis cõmissurũ audio eum promisisse. Docuit, antequam Lugdunum sese reciperet,pluribus in Academiis,magna cũ laude:transtulit è Græco in Gallicũ sermonẽ librũ Galeni de vsu partiũ,in Latinũ verò,Theophrastũ:restaurauitque Pliniũ.Vnde non minorẽ certẽ laudẽ,vt mihi videtur, quàm ex medicinæ praxi meretur. Scripsit quoque de peste,& chirurgia libros aliquot vtiles & pernecessarios.
units.tr: James Dalechamps of Caen, a most distinguished physician, has for many years practised medicine at Lyons, with such fame of his name and such usefulness to the Lyonnais republic, that he far surpasses all his peers in the excellence of his learning and the experience of his art. But why should I say only that he cares so celebratedly for the health of the people of Lyons with divine remedies, whose most famous name is spread abroad not only through all of France but through many other regions, on account of his manifold erudition, and his excellence, I will not say only, but also his ease and supreme success in healing? He has profited many in the past by teaching, he has profited many by writing; but he is soon going to profit more by his divine commentaries and by that wonderful Latin translation of the Greek Athenaeus, which I hear he has promised he will shortly publish and entrust to the press. Before he withdrew to Lyons, he taught in several academies with great praise; he translated Galen's De usu partium from Greek into French, and Theophrastus into Latin; and he restored Pliny. For these things he deserves no smaller praise, as it seems to me, than from the practice of medicine. He has also written several useful and very necessary books on the plague and on surgery.

units.la: PIVS Quartus Mediolanensis, Joânes Angelus Medices, Bernardini filius, ex presbytero Cardinale tt. Sanctæ Pudentianæ, presbyter tt. Sancti Stephani in mõte Cælio, post tt. Sanctæ Anastasiæ, post tt. Sãctę Prisce[?], à Paulo tertio factus, Imperatore Cæsare Ferdinando Austrio Augusto, & Maximiliano secundo Cæsare, sedit in Pontificatu, annos quinque, menses undecim, & dies quindecim. Natus est die Paschę, pridie Kalendas Aprilis, anno 1499. Mediolani. Creatus Romæ à xliii. Cardinalibus, vii. Kalend. Ianuarij, die Martis nocte praecedenti, hora inter septimā & octauā prope finito anno 1559. Coronatus die Sabbato proximo Epiphaniæ festo, viii. Idus Ianuarij, anno 1560. Ordinationibus quatuor, mensibus Ianuario & Martio, habitis. Cardinales creauit xlvi. presbyteros xxxix. & diaconos vii. Obiit noctu, ante diem quartum Iduū Decebris, hora secunda: anno, 1565. ætatis 66. Vacauit, eo mortuo, sedes; dies viginti novem. Sub eo Pontifice, Concilium Tridentinum xxv. sessionibus habitis, fuit absolutum & confirmatum. Fuit Pontifex numero 228. Vide Platinam.
units.tr: Pius IV, of Milan, John Angelus Medici, son of Bernardino, made Cardinal priest of the title of Santa Pudenziana, then priest of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill, then of Santa Anastasia, then of Santa Prisca[?], was created by Paul III, under the Emperor Ferdinand of Austria, Augustus, and Maximilian II, Caesar. He sat in the pontificate five years, eleven months and fifteen days. He was born on Easter Day, on the day before the Kalends of April, in the year 1499, at Milan. Created at Rome by forty-three cardinals on the seventh day before the Kalends of January, on the Tuesday night before, between the seventh and eighth hour, the year being nearly finished, in 1559. Crowned on the Saturday next after the feast of the Epiphany, on the eighth day before the Ides of January, in the year 1560. Four ordinations were held, in the months of January and March. He created forty-six cardinals, thirty-nine priests and seven deacons. He died in the night, before the fourth day before the Ides of December, at the second hour, in the year 1565, aged 66. The see was vacant for twenty-nine days after his death. Under this Pope the Council of Trent was completed and confirmed, with twenty-five sessions held. He was the 228th Pope. See Platina. PHILIP, BY THE GRACE OF GOD, KING OF SPAIN, II OF SPAIN, KING; ANNE, HIS WIFE, FOURTH; CHILDREN[?]

units.la: PIVS v. Alexādrinus, Frater Michaël Gislerius ex oppido Boschi, Alexādrinæ dicecesis, Lombardus Insuber, ordinis prædicatorū, lector officij, sanctæ inquisitionis cōmissarius; ex Episcopo Sutrino, & Nepesino presbyter Cardinalis tt. Sanctæ Mariæ super Mineruam & summus inquisitor à Paulo iiii. Papa factus, postea Episcopus Montis Regalis in Subalpinis & tt. S. Sabinæ, demum iterum tt. S. Mariæ super Mineruam à Pio iiii. creatus, Imperatore Cæsare Maximiliano secundo Austrio Augusto, sedit in pontificatu, annos 6. menses 3. dies 16. Natus xvi. Kal. Februarij, anno 1505. creatus Romæ à lij.[?] Cardinalibus, vii. Idus Ianuarij hora 22. die Lunæ. Coronatus die natalitio suo, xvi. Calend. Ianuarij, in festo S. Antonij, ineunte anno eius vitæ lxii. super gradus ante basilicam Vaticanam ab Vrbinate Cardinale. Vide Platinam. PHILIPPVS DEI GRA. HISPA. REX II. HISP. REG. ANNA. VX. IIII. FIIL. [?]
units.tr: Pius V, of Alessandria: Brother Michael Ghislieri from the town of Bosco in the diocese of Alessandria, a Lombard of Insubria, of the Order of Preachers, reader in his office, commissioner of the Holy Inquisition; made presbyter Cardinal of the title of Santa Maria sopra Minerva and Supreme Inquisitor by Pope Paul IV, from the bishop of Sutri and Nepi; afterwards Bishop of Mondovì in Piedmont and of the title of S. Sabina, and at last again of the title of S. Maria sopra Minerva, created by Pius IV, under the Emperor Maximilian II of Austria, Augustus. He sat in the pontificate six years, three months and sixteen days. Born on the 16th day before the Kalends of February, in 1505. Created at Rome by fifty-two[?] cardinals, on the seventh day before the Ides of January, at the twenty-second hour, on Monday. Crowned on his birthday, the 16th day before the Kalends of January, on the feast of St Anthony, at the beginning of the sixty-second year of his life, on the steps before the Vatican basilica, by Cardinal Vitelli of Urbino. See Platina. PHILIP, BY THE GRACE OF GOD, KING OF SPAIN, II OF SPAIN, KING; ANNE, HIS WIFE, FOURTH; CHILDREN[?]

units.la: PHILIPPVS Hispaniæ Rex Catholicus, quot quātísque regiis virtutibus ornatus sit, indicant ea omnia quæ ad hàc vsque diem præclarè egerit, quemadmodum vnusquisque ex historia rerũ ab eo gestarum perspicere poterit. Iustitiam semper coluit & fidei Catholicæ super omnes alios reges fuit accerrimus defensor, talémque adhuc in dies, magis ac magis sese profitetur: cùm tot præliis aduersus Imperatorem Turcarũ, Christianæ religionis hostem teterrimũ, dimicauerit: eáque de causa vt omnes de fide ortodoxa sentiat quæ par est sentire, omnibus christianis in religione constantibus & nouarum rerum minimè cupidis, inquisitores instituit, qui populum suæ ditioni subiectum omnésque alios in Hispania, etiam ad tempus commorantes, in religionis catholicæ cultu & obseruatione, perpetuò contineant: multum enim interesse ad Regni gubernationem existimat, si populus ab Ecclesiæ sanctæ amplexu & gremio non discedat, & vt regia edicta, sic diuina obseruet. Plures hic duxit vxores, quæ fatis cessere: nunc autem matrimonio sibi iunxit Annam Maximiliani 2, Imperatoris nouissimè defuncti filiam, ex qua plures liberos suscepit.
units.tr: Philip, Catholic King of Spain: how many and how great the royal virtues with which he is adorned are shown by all that he has accomplished so far, as anyone may perceive from the history of the things done by him. He has always cultivated justice, and has been the most zealous defender of the Catholic faith above all other kings, and he still declares himself such more and more every day, since he has fought so many battles against the Emperor of the Turks, the most foul enemy of the Christian religion. For this reason, so that he may think about the orthodox faith as it is right to think, he has set up inquisitors for all Christians who remain constant in religion and are not at all eager for novelties, who keep the people subject to his rule, and all others in Spain, even those staying there for a time, constantly within the worship and observance of the Catholic religion. For he thinks it greatly matters to the government of the kingdom that the people should not depart from the embrace and bosom of the holy Church, and that they should observe divine law as they observe the royal edicts. He has had several wives here, who have died by the fates; but now he has joined in marriage Anne, daughter of the most recently deceased Emperor Maximilian II, by whom he has begotten several children.

units.la: ANNA Philippi Regis Hispaniæ vxor quarta, Maximiliani secundi Romanorum Imperatoris filia, ea pulchritudine est, à qua tamen grauitas non absit, ea prudentiā, quæ vtramque adæquet: benignitate & humanitate tãta, quantam in principe fœmina quisquam viderit, iis denique virtutibus ornata, quibus maiorum claritati egregiè respondeat. MARIA REG. HISP. PHILIP. II. VX. I. PHILIP. II VX. II. MARIA REG. HISP. ISABEL. VX. III. PHIL. II. HISP. REG.
units.tr: ANNA, fourth wife of Philip, King of Spain, daughter of Maximilian II, Emperor of the Romans: she has such beauty, yet not without gravity, and such prudence as matches both; with a kindness and courtesy as great as anyone has seen in a princess, and finally adorned with those virtues which answer well to the renown of her ancestors. MARIA, QUEEN OF SPAIN, FIRST WIFE OF PHILIP II. PHILIP II, SECOND WIFE. MARIA, QUEEN OF SPAIN. ISABELLA, THIRD WIFE. PHILIP II, KING OF SPAIN.

units.la: MARIA Regis Hispaniae Philippi uxor prima, Ioānis Regis Portugaliae filia, aspectu, ad beneuolentiam conciliandam apto, graui acutoque sermone, in omni actione mirè prudens, intra paucos annos, confecto vitae cursu, ad æternas sedes, id est ad capiendum virtutis & innocentiae suae fructum, euolauit.
units.tr: MARIA, first wife of Philip, King of Spain, daughter of John, King of Portugal: in appearance apt to win goodwill, of grave and sharp speech, wonderfully prudent in every action, she passed away within a few years, her course of life finished, and flew off to the eternal seats, that is, to receive the fruit of her virtue and innocence.

units.la: MARIA, Regis Hispaniae Philippi uxor secunda, Henrici VIII. Angliae Regis filia, miram prudentiam, & seueritatem in omni vita persecuta, cumque magni motus in Regno excitaretur, virili animo perduelles extinxit, quanquam inter sacras virgines educata, animo his cogitationibus exculto, nullam gerendi belli partem nouisset, sed nimirum defendenti catholicam religionem, Regiamque maiestatem, Deus ipse malorum ultor affuit, Regnumque in summa obedientia conseruauit.
units.tr: MARIA, second wife of Philip, King of Spain, daughter of Henry VIII, King of England: she pursued a wonderful prudence and severity in her whole life; and when great commotions were stirred up in the kingdom, she crushed the rebels with a manly spirit, although she had been brought up among holy virgins, and her mind, cultivated in such thoughts, had known no part in waging war. But God himself, avenger of evils, was present to defend the Catholic religion and the royal majesty, and he kept the kingdom in the highest obedience.

units.la: ISABELLA Regis Hispaniae Philippi uxor tertia, Henrici secundi Galliae Regis filia, læta facie, sic, ut iucunditatē intuētibus afferret, dignitate tamen ea quę Reginam deceat: quamdiu vixit, summa & beneuolentia & obseruatia apud omnes adepta, multis naturae, fortunę, animi que bonis instructa, vim tamen fortunę vitare non potuit. Patrem amisit, immatura morte ereptum: nec multo post, edito immaturi temporis infante, incredibili & Philippi Regis & omnium dolore decessit.
units.tr: ISABELLA, third wife of Philip, King of Spain, daughter of Henry II, King of France: with a cheerful face, so that she brought delight to those who looked upon her, yet with a dignity fitting for a queen; as long as she lived she obtained the highest goodwill and esteem from all, furnished with many goods of nature, fortune and mind, yet she could not avoid the force of fortune. She lost her father, snatched away by an untimely death; and not long after, having brought forth an infant before its time, she died to the incredible grief of King Philip and of all.

units.la: PHILIBERTVS Emanuel Dux Sabaudiæ & princeps Pedemōtanus, amisso eius dominio, quod Rex Gallorum Henricus 2. obtinebat, diutissime pro Carolo quinto Imperatore, aduersus ipsum Henricum dimicauit. Quid is egerit, præfectus Imperatoris exercitui, in obsidione Hesdini, satis notum est ex historia bellorum quæ inter hos duos potentissimos principes, totius prope orbis detrimento, gesta sunt. Huius pater Carolus Dux Sabaudiæ, propriis sedibus & toto suo dominio expulsus, mortuus est anno salutis 1553. éstque sepultus Vercelliis. Post eius obitum Imperator Carolus dedit Philiberto Emanueli, paterna hereditate destituto, Comitatum Astensem, vt eo potiretur donec suam hæreditatem recuperasset, quę illi postea fuit restituta omnino à Rege, qui etiā dedit illi nuptui sororē suam vnicam Margaretam, Francisci 1. Francorum regis filiam, quæ paulo post Henrici tertij è Polonia reditum in Galliam, fatis cessit, magno omniū luctu, & præcipuè Ducis qui celebrē illam Augustæ Taurinorum Academiā, in studiosorum vsum instituit.
units.tr: PHILIBERT Emanuel, Duke of Savoy and Prince of Piedmont, having lost his domain, which King Henry II of the French held, fought for a very long time for Emperor Charles V against Henry himself. What he did, as commander of the Emperor's army at the siege of Hesdin, is well enough known from the history of the wars which were waged between these two most powerful princes, to the detriment of almost the whole world. His father, Charles, Duke of Savoy, driven from his own seat and his whole domain, died in the year of salvation 1553, and was buried at Vercelli. After his death Emperor Charles gave to Philibert Emanuel, deprived of his paternal inheritance, the County of Asti, to hold until he recovered his inheritance, which was afterwards fully restored to him by the King. The King also gave him in marriage his only sister Margaret, daughter of Francis I, King of the Franks, who, shortly after the return of Henry III from Poland to France, died, to the great grief of all, and especially of the Duke, who founded that famous Academy at Augusta Taurinorum for the use of students.

units.la: MARGARETA Valesia, Heroinarum omnium quotquot fuerunt longè illustrissima, pietate ac in omnes literatos homines præcipuè Gallos humanitate ac liberalitate valde insignis, Christianissimi & inuictissimi illius Henrici secundi soror vnica, Philiberto Emanuelî gloriosissimo Sabaudiæ principi, nupsit eodem tempore quo Elizabetha Franciæ filia natu maior, collocata est in matrimonium Philippo regi Hispaniæ, quorum Hymenæorum ratione, pax sancita & confirmata fuit inter Imperatorem, Regem Hispaniæ, & Christianissimum Francorum regem Henricum. Hæc sanè digna est, propter eius virtutes infinitas, quę ęuo omniū scriptis cumulatissimè celebretur. DVX ALBÆ FERD. ALVARES IO. DVX MOSCOVIÆ &c.
units.tr: MARGARET of Valois, by far the most illustrious of all the heroines who have ever lived, very distinguished for her piety and for her kindness and generosity towards all learned men, especially the French, the only sister of that most Christian and unconquered Henry II, was married to Philibert Emanuel, most glorious Prince of Savoy, at the same time as Elizabeth, the elder daughter of France, was given in marriage to Philip, King of Spain. By the arrangement of these marriages, peace was sanctioned and confirmed between the Emperor, the King of Spain, and the most Christian King of the French, Henry. She is indeed worthy of this, on account of her infinite virtues, which are celebrated most abundantly in the writings of all ages. THE DUKE OF ALBA, FERDINAND ALVAREZ; JOHN, DUKE OF MUSCOVY, etc.

units.la: FERDINANDVS Aluarez à Toledo Albæ Dux præstantissimus & multarũ rerum experientia,omniũ qui in Hispania fuerunt magnorum virorũ maximus,à Rege catholico semper amatus fuit:& cum res Belgicæ malè sese haberet,& Belgæ, Margaretæ Parmæ &Placentiæ duci illustrissimæ nollent obtemperare,quæ apud eos Gubernatrix erat constituta, ab eodé missus est, cum exercitu:vt magnæ calamitati iamiam ingrueti aliquod remediũ adferret, vir prudens & ætate proueƈtior quàm opus esset ad populum ferocem gubernandum. Hunc tamen cùm armis domuisset, statua quæ eius ipsius imaginem referebat, in arce Antuerpiana erecta est, cum his literis lapidi infernè incifis , F. A. A. T. A. D. PH. II. H. A. B. P. Q. E. S. R. P. R. P. I. C. P. P. F. R. O. M. F. P. quarum hæc est significatio, Ferdinando Aluarez à Toledo Albæ duci Philippi I I. Hispaniarum apud Belgas præfecto, quod extincta seditione, rebellibus pulsis, religione procurata, iustitia culta,prouinciæ pacem firmarit,regis optimi ministro fidelißimo positum. Cùm tamen in patriam reuersus esset, à rege euocatus, multa bella subsecuta sunt.
units.tr: FERDINAND Alvarez of Toledo, Duke of Alba, a most distinguished man and of great experience in many affairs, the greatest of all the great men who were in Spain, was always loved by the Catholic King. When affairs in the Netherlands went badly, and the Belgians were unwilling to obey Margaret of Parma and Piacenza, a most illustrious duchess, who had been appointed their governess, he was sent by the same King with an army to bring some remedy to the great calamity now almost upon them; a man prudent, and older than was needed for governing a fierce people. Yet when he had subdued them by arms, a statue representing his very image was erected in the citadel of Antwerp, with these letters cut in the stone below: F. A. A. T. A. D. PH. II. H. A. B. P. Q. E. S. R. P. R. P. I. C. P. P. F. R. O. M. F. P., of which the meaning is: "To Ferdinand Alvarez of Toledo, Duke of Alba, Governor of Philip II, King of Spain, among the Belgians, who, the sedition being quenched, the rebels driven out, religion restored and justice maintained, has firmly established peace in the province, placed here by the most faithful minister of the best of kings." However, when he had returned to his homeland, having been recalled by the King, many wars followed.

units.la: IOANNES Dux Moscouiæ, tanta præstantia & animi magnitudine suis subditis semper imperauit,támque humaniter reipublicæ gubernaculis præfuit,vt eum sanè dignum existimauerimus, qui inter præstantissimos principes hîc referretur, cuiusque vera effigies, & ad viuum expressa pröptuario nostro Iconum misceretur & cuiuis proponeretur, vt aliquid honoris, nostra opera,percipiat apud exteras gentes,quæ eius nomen & gloriam perpetuam ignorant. Hic persæpè & quasi perpetuò bellum gerit aduersus Saromatas, aut Sarmatas, quòd populi sint Moschis quos vulgò Moschouites vocant admodum finitui, vt meminit Lucanus libros 3. -Sanisque affinis Sarmata Moschis.
units.tr: JOHN, Duke of Muscovy, ruled his subjects always with such excellence and greatness of mind, and presided over the government of the commonwealth so humanely, that we have thought him truly worthy to be listed here among the most excellent princes, and his true likeness, drawn to the life, has been placed in our store of images and set before anyone, so that, by our labour, he may obtain some honour among foreign nations, which are ignorant of his name and his lasting glory. He very often, and almost continually, wages war against the Saromatae, or Sarmatians, because these peoples are very near to the Muscovites, whom they commonly call Moscovites, as Lucan recalls in book 3: "And the Sarmatian, neighbour to the Muscovites of the sands."
FRANCIS II, BY THE GRACE OF GOD, KING OF FRANCE.
MARY, BY THE GRACE OF GOD, QUEEN OF FRANCE AND SCOTLAND.

units.la: FRANCISCVS, huius nominis secundus, Rex Francorū, ætatis suæ annū decimū sextū non excedens, patri inuictissimo Hérico successit, anno salutis 1559. Viuente patre, Mariā Stuart, defuncti Regis Scotorū filiam, vxorem duxit: cuius matrimonij ratione fuit etiam Rex Scotiæ. Decimo octauo die Septembris 1559. fuit sacratus, in solita vrbe, Rhemorum à Cardinale Lotharingiæ, eiusdem archiepiscopo. Hinc comitatus sororem suam, Lotharingiæ ducis vxorē, vsque ad Barleducū, Ambasiā sese recepit, iuxta quam conuenerunt quidam cum armis (unde Ambasię tumultus paulò post prodiit) qui dicerent se supplices ad Regem venire, vt ei quędam super religione & gubernaculo proponerēt: verum, quod armati venissent, alij mortis supplicio affecti sunt, alij edicto regio sedati, recesserunt. Postea, habito apud Fontembelęum consilio, cùm omnium ordinum, vulgò statuum, conuentum impe[?]asset, aliquid sinistri suspicatus, cum armis Aureliam profectus est, vbi cùm regni rebus afflictis prouidere iamiam incipere vellet[?], in morbum incidit, ob catharri in aurem grauissimum defluxum, qui illum interemit die 5. Decembris, anno salutis 1560. iacétque in vrbe D. Dionysij, in sepulcreto auorum.
units.tr: FRANCIS, second of this name, King of the Franks, not yet exceeding sixteen years of age, succeeded his most unconquered father Henry in the year of salvation 1559. While his father was still living, he married Mary Stuart, daughter of the late King of the Scots; by this marriage he was also King of Scotland. On the 18th day of September 1559 he was consecrated, in the customary city of Reims, by the Cardinal of Lorraine, archbishop of the same place. Thence, accompanied by his sister, wife of the Duke of Lorraine, he withdrew as far as Bar-le-Duc, and then to Amboise, near which certain men came with arms (whence the tumult of Amboise arose shortly afterwards), who said they came as suppliants to the King, to lay before him certain matters concerning religion and government; but because they had come armed, some were put to death, and others, quieted by a royal edict, withdrew. Afterwards, having held a council at Fontainebleau, when he had summoned an assembly of all the orders, commonly called the States, he suspected something untoward, and set out with arms for Orléans, where, when he was about to begin providing for the troubled affairs of the kingdom, he fell ill from a very grave flow of catarrh into the ear, which carried him off on the 5th day of December in the year of salvation 1560. He lies in the city of Saint-Denis, in the burial vault of his ancestors.

units.la: MARIA Stuart, defuncti Regis Scotię filia, Christianissimo Francorum Regi Francisco secundo, nupsit, antequam Regni gubernacula is teneret, superstite Henrico patre eius inuictissimo. Cū hęc esset Franciæ Regina, habita est ab omnibus omnium formosissima & virtute præstantissima: verum fortunę iniuriis, post regis obitum, in patriam reuersa, fuit obnoxia, & hodie, ob suspicionem alicuius facinoris, in carcere detinetur. FRAN. A LOTH. / D. G. GVIS. [?] DEST. D. G. / ANNA
units.tr: MARY Stuart, daughter of the late King of Scots, married the most Christian King of the Franks, Francis II, before he held the government of the kingdom, while her father Henry, most unconquered, was still alive. While she was Queen of France, she was regarded by all as the most beautiful of all women and most outstanding in virtue; but, after the king's death, returning to her homeland, she was exposed to the injuries of fortune, and today, on suspicion of some crime, she is held in prison. FRANCIS OF LORRAINE, DUKE OF GUISE, BY THE GRACE OF GOD. [?] BY THE GRACE OF GOD. ANNE.

units.la: FRANCISCVS Lotharenus Dux Guisius, princeps omnium virtutū genere clarus, in bello maximè prę̈stitit, multásque victorias est adeptus. Nam ad Frugum, prope Rentiā ciuitatem quasdam Imperatoris turmas fudit fugauitque anno 1554. mensis Augusti decimo tertio. At Regis locum tenēs, mira industria & arte militari Caletum vrbem Regię ditioni subiecit, anno 1557. octauo mensis Ianuarij, quam Angli posse expugnari minimè existimabant. Anno 1558. vicesimo tertio mensis Iunij, Thionuillam iamdiu obsessam deditione cepit. Rex Franciscus secundus, in tumultu Ambosiaco, vt eius authores persequeretur, suæ maiestatis Locum tenentem eum constituit, anno 1559. At paulò post cùm Carolus nonus regnaret, eiúsque regni fere initio, prælium Druidense comissum est tanta huius Ducis prudentia & consilio, vt is victoriam Regi reportarit, anno 1562. 19. mensis Decembris. Anno subsequēte parata tam insigni victoria cum Aureliam obsessam teneret, à traditore Ioanne Poltrot fuit occisus 24[?] Februarij, magno Reipublicæ dispendio, & totius Franciæ luctu acerbissimo.
units.tr: FRANCIS of Lorraine, Duke of Guise, a prince distinguished in every kind of virtue, excelled above all in war, and gained many victories. For at Frogs, near the city of Renty, he routed and put to flight certain troops of the Emperor on the 13th day of August 1554. But holding the King's place, with wonderful industry and military skill he subjected the city of Calais to the royal dominion, on the 8th day of January 1557, which the English had thought could by no means be taken. On the 23rd day of June 1558 he took Thionville, long besieged, by surrender. King Francis II, after the Amboise tumult, appointed him his lieutenant in 1559, to pursue its authors. But a little after, when Charles IX reigned, and near the beginning of his reign, the battle of Dreux was fought, and by the great prudence and counsel of this Duke he brought victory to the King, on the 19th day of December 1562. In the following year, while he held Orléans besieged, with such a notable victory already prepared, he was killed by the traitor Jean Poltrot on the 24th of February, to the great loss of the commonwealth and to the most bitter grief of all France.

units.la: ANNA d'Est, nobilissima & illustrissima familia orta, patre nempe Hercule generosissimo Duce Ferrariæ, & matre Reta ex stirpe regia Franciæ, digna est quę propter singulares eius virtutes[?], hic comitetur magnum illum Franciscum Lotharenum Ducem Guisium, cui primum data est nuptui, peperitque ex eo copula hos nobilissimos & præstantissimos principes Henricum[?], Carolum[?] & Ludouicum: vnde non minorem laudem merentur[?] quam ex nobilitate familiæ. CAR. IX. FRANC. REX. ISABEL. CAROLI IX. GAL. REG. VX.
units.tr: Anna d'Este, a most noble and illustrious family, born of her father Hercules, the most generous Duke of Ferrara, and her mother Renée of the royal stock of France, was worthy, on account of her singular virtues, to accompany that great Francis of Lorraine, Duke of Guise, to whom she was first given in marriage; and from this union she bore the most noble and excellent princes Henry, Charles and Louis, whence they deserve no less praise than they have from the nobility of their family. CHARLES IX, KING OF FRANCE. ISABELLA, WIFE OF CHARLES IX, QUEEN OF FRANCE.

units.la: CAROLVS nonus Francorũ Rex successit Francisco secũdo fratri, anno Domini,1560. Et qui ætatis suæ, vndecim annorũ numerũ non excedebat, Regina mater regni gubernaculis præfuit cũ Antonio Borbonio Rege Nauarræ, maiestatis Regiæ summũ Locũ tenente: id quod omnibus Francię ordinibus, qui tunc Aurelię conuenerant, pergratũ fuit. Decimo octauo Maij, 1561. Carolus fuit sacratus, Rhemis à Cardinali Lotharingię Rhemorũ Archiepiscopo. Paulo post bellũ est exortũ. Plures vrbes captę à nouæ religionis professoribus, quarũ aliquot à Rege recuperatis, Rege Nauarræ in obsidione Rothomagi ad mortem vulnerato; pugna cõmissa, victoribus catholicis: in qua Cõdęus princeps capitur. Fit pacificationis edictũ 19. Martij, 1563. & iussis Regis & Condęi copiis, Portus Gracię, quem Angli tenebăt, capitur. Paulò post, ortum nouum bellum & præliũ cõmissum, inter Lutetiã & D. Dionysiũ, in quo Cõnestabilis Môtmorencius ad mortẽ vulneratur. Denuò pax interuenit, quam paulò post subsecuti sunt noui & ingentes tumultus bellorũ, quibus sedatis, Pacificationis edicto nouo publicato, xi. Augusti. 1570. Rex [?]Meseriis, Elisabetha Austriã Imperatoris Maximiliani filiã vxorem ducit, & paulò post, fracto denuò pacificationis edicto, respublica Gallica miserè afflictatur. Rex obiit 3. Iunij, 1574.
units.tr: Charles IX, King of the Franks, succeeded his brother Francis II in the year of the Lord 1560. Since he was not yet eleven years old, the queen mother governed the realm together with Antoine de Bourbon, King of Navarre, who held the highest place of royal majesty; this pleased all the orders of France who had then assembled at Orléans. On 18 May 1561, Charles was consecrated at Reims by the Cardinal of Lorraine, Archbishop of Reims. Soon afterwards war broke out. Several cities were taken by the professors of the new religion, some of which were recovered by the King; the King of Navarre was mortally wounded at the siege of Rouen; a battle was joined, won by the Catholics, in which the prince of Condé was taken. The edict of pacification was issued on 19 March 1563, and by the orders of the King and the forces of Condé, the Port of Grace, which the English held, was taken. Shortly afterwards, a new war arose and a battle was fought between Paris and Saint-Denis, in which the Constable Montmorency was mortally wounded. Peace came again, which was soon followed by new and enormous tumults of war; these being quelled, a new edict of pacification was published on 11 August 1570. The King married Elisabeth, daughter of the Emperor Maximilian of Austria, and shortly afterwards, when the edict of pacification was broken again, the Gallic commonwealth was miserably afflicted. The King died on 3 June 1574.

units.la: ELISABETHA Austria Imperatoris Maximiliã filia, Carolo nono Francorũ Regi nupsit, 26. Nouembris 1570; peperit filiam nomine Mariam Elisabetham. Fuit ea omnium virtutis, modestię, humanitatis & prudentię exemplar: quũ omnibus accedebat & faciei & totius corporis pulchritudinis [?]summa præstantia. IAC. A SAB. [?] D. GE. ETNEM. [?] DEST. D. G. [?] ANNA
units.tr: Elisabeth of Austria, daughter of the Emperor Maximilian, was married to Charles IX, King of the Franks, on 26 November 1570; she bore a daughter named Mary Elisabeth. She was a model of all virtue, modesty, kindness and prudence; to all who approached her there was the highest excellence both of face and of the beauty of her whole body. JAC. A SAB. D. GE. ETNEM. DEST. D. G. ANNA

units.la: IACOBVS è Sabaudia, Dux Nemorensis præstantissimus princeps, & rei bellicæ laude & maxima sagacitate & prudētia, hostibus Franciæ, multis in locis, ardente bello inter Imperatorem & Regem Francorum, sese fortissimè opposuit. Bellorum ciuilium flammas, quanta potuit diligentia restinguere semper conatus est, effecitque prudentissimè vt Rex Francorum, coniuratorum manus semel effugerit in vrbe vulgo, Meaux, vocata Lutetiæ proxima, quæ illum iam iam interceptura videbantur. Moderatus est aliquot annos Lugdunensem prouinciam, tâta cum laude, vt merito tantus princeps ab omnibus non dico tantum eius prouinciæ, sed etiam totius Regni incolis, existimetur. Hic, anno 1566. viduam defuncti Ducis Guisij duxit vxorem, quorū magnificentissimæ nuptiæ celebratæ fuerunt ad sanctum Maurum fossarum prope Lutetiam, quibus etiā Rex interesse voluit.
units.tr: Jacob of Savoy, Duke of Nemours, a most excellent prince, both by his renown in warfare and by his great shrewdness and prudence, opposed himself most bravely to the enemies of France in many places, while war raged between the Emperor and the King of the Franks. He always strove, with all the diligence he could, to quench the flames of civil wars, and he most prudently brought it about that the King of the Franks escaped the hands of the conspirators, in the town commonly called Meaux, near Paris, where they seemed about to seize him at any moment. He governed the province of Lyons for several years with such praise that a prince so great is esteemed by all, I do not say only the inhabitants of that province, but of the whole kingdom. In 1566 he took as his wife the widow of the late Duke of Guise; their most magnificent wedding was celebrated at Saint-Maur-des-Fossés near Paris, and the King also wished to attend.

units.la: ANNA d'Est, cuius nobilissimas virtutes superius attigimus, quę illam hoc tēpore reddunt tanquam splendidissimum lumen inter illustrissimas heroīnas: secundò, in matrimonium locata est magnanimo Duci Nemorensi, qui ex ea suscepit filium generosissimum & paternæ fortitudinis sectatorem. II. IMP. MAXIMILIANVS MARIA RO. IMP. MAXIM. VXOR [?]
units.tr: Anna d'Este, whose most noble virtues we have touched on above, which at this time render her as a most splendid light among the most illustrious heroines: secondly, she was given in marriage to the magnanimous Duke of Nemours, by whom she received a most noble son, a follower of his father's courage. II. EMPEROR. MAXIMILIAN. MARIA. ROMAN EMPEROR. MAXIMILIAN'S WIFE.

units.la: MAXIMILIANVS secundus Iunior Austrius Ferdinandi filius,à rege Boëmiæ,Frácfortdiæ Rex Romanorũ Cæsarque octauo Kalendas Decembris,1562. creatus fuit,ibidémque coronatus, regnauit cum patre Ferdinando, per anni spatiũ & octo mesiũ:quo tępore,ordo militiæ S.Stephani Papæ in Insula Iluæ,à Cosmo Medice Florentinorum Duce institutus, à Pio 4. pontifice maximo cõfirmatur, & bella plusquam hostilia in regno Galliarũ,ob religionẽ excitata, Ducis Guisij viri præclarissimi,acerba catholicis cæde, sedantur.Hic tanto amore non solũ à suis sed etiã ab omnibus est ( non immerito ) prosecutus, ut humani generis amor & delitiæ, appellatus fit. Imperauit post patris obitũ,annos plures,tanta cum moderatione & iustitia,ut erepti mortem omnes sui ægrè tulerint & defleuerint diù. Huius filia prudentissima Elisabetha collocata est in matrimonium Carolo nono Francorũ Regi,qui filiam ex ea suscepit,quę paulo post eius obitum,& matris apud suos reditum,mortua est.
units.tr: Maximilian II, the younger, Austrian, son of Ferdinand, was created King of the Romans and Caesar at Frankfurt on 24 November 1562, and was crowned there; he reigned with his father Ferdinand for a span of one year and eight months. In this time the order of the knights of St Stephen, instituted on the Island of Elba by Cosmo de' Medici, Duke of the Florentines, was confirmed by Pope Pius IV, the Supreme Pontiff; and the wars more than hostile in the kingdom of the Gauls, stirred up on account of religion, were quelled by the bitter slaughter of Catholics, the cruel death of the most illustrious Duke of Guise. He was pursued with such love not only by his own people but by all (not undeservedly) that he was called the love and delight of the human race. He ruled for many years after his father's death with such moderation and justice that all his people took it hard, and mourned for a long time, when he was snatched away. His most prudent daughter Elisabeth was given in marriage to Charles IX, King of the Franks, who had a daughter by her, who died shortly after her death and her mother's return to her own people.

units.la: MARIA Caroli v. filia,Maximiliani ii. Romanorum Imperatoris defuncti uxor,Ferdinandi nurus: & Philippi, Hispaniarum Regis soror, ea pignora suis tradidit, quæ summorum, summæque familiæ principum nomina illis renouarent, idque viuens ipsa vidit, quod in maxima fœlicitatis parte omnes locandum putant, filias duas summis orbis terrarum Regibus in matrimonium collocatas. Hæc maxima sunt, quæque nescio an unquam contigerint: sed maiora illa, quæ ipsi propria sunt, Pietas in Deũ, charitas, qua tenuiores assiduè subleuat, & præcipuum studium catholicæ religionis: quæ posteritas non silebit ulla.
units.tr: Mary, daughter of Charles V, wife of the late Maximilian II, Roman Emperor, daughter-in-law of Ferdinand, and sister of Philip, King of the Spains, handed down those offspring who would renew for them the names of the greatest princes of the greatest house; and she herself lived to see what all think to be the greatest part of happiness: two daughters given in marriage to the highest kings of the world. These are great things, and such as I know not whether they have ever befallen anyone else; but greater still are those which are proper to her own person: piety towards God, charity, by which she constantly relieves the poorer sort, and her chief zeal for the Catholic religion; these no posterity will ever pass over in silence.

units.la: SELIMVS huius nominis secundus, Turcarum Imperator, post mortem Solimani patris sui, aliquamdiu occultatam in Hungaria, capta Zighet, imperio successit Mehemeti Bassæ industria, antequam patris mors patefacta esset. Hic Aimanum qui in Arabia rebellauerat, armis compressit, bellum Venetis intulit, rupto cum his fœdere{¹}, & multis locis in Albania expugnatis, Insulam Cypriam occupauit anno salutis 1571. Tandem commissa pugna adversus confœderatos, ingētem cladem accepit, classe à Christianis victa, sed paulò post, eam restituit, fœdere rursus inito, cum republica Venetorum: & recuperatis in Africa, Aphrodisio & Guletta à Rege Hispaniæ antea occupatis, mortuus est, anno salutis 1574. Porrò hæc omnia quæ recensui, gesta sunt, dum lascivus Imperator genio indulgeret, mulieribus & gulæ omnino deditus.
units.tr: Selim, the second of that name, Emperor of the Turks, after the death of his father Suleiman, which had been kept hidden for some time in Hungary, succeeded to the empire, through the diligence of Mehmed Pasha, after capturing Zigetvar, before his father's death was made known. He crushed by arms Aimán, who had rebelled in Arabia; he waged war on the Venetians, breaking the treaty with them; and after storming many places in Albania he occupied the Island of Cyprus in the year of salvation 1571. At last, when battle was joined against the confederates, he suffered a huge defeat, his fleet being beaten by the Christians; but shortly afterwards he restored it, making a new treaty with the Venetian commonwealth; and after recovering in Africa Aphrodisium and Goletta, previously occupied by the King of Spain, he died in the year of salvation 1574. Moreover, all these things I have recounted were done while the wanton Emperor indulged his appetites, wholly given over to women and gluttony.

units.la: AMVRATH, huius nominis tertius, Selimi filius, creatus est Turcarum Imperator, Imperióque potitus, post patrem mortuum diebus octo, anno salutis humanæ 1574. Immani & barbarogetis Turcicæ more, qui jamdiu invaluit, quinque fratres eius (proh Deum atque hominum fidem) interfici iussit, ut solus sine ullo metu & suspicione quæ reges plerumque comitari solet, imperaret: & vitam ageret pacificam, & omnibus impedimentis, quæ frequenter intellexerat posse intervenire inter plures consortes & in eadem prope fortuna constitutos, immunem. Imperium cœpit gubernare juvenis, annos natus viginti octo: religionis Mahumetanæ imprimis studiosus, eíque vehementer addictus, quem constat justitiæ mirum inmodum observantissimum, Solimani eius avi imitatorem esse.
units.tr: Amurath, the third of that name, son of Selim, was created Emperor of the Turks, and took possession of the empire eight days after his father's death, in the year of human salvation 1574. In the savage and barbarous manner of the Turks, which has long prevailed, he ordered his five brothers to be put to death (O God and faith of men!), so that he alone might rule without any fear or suspicion, which usually accompanies kings, and might live a peaceful life, free from all the obstacles which he had often understood might arise among many co-heirs placed in nearly the same fortune. He began to govern the empire as a young man of twenty-eight years; especially devoted to the Mahometan religion, and strongly attached to it, he is known to observe justice in a wonderful degree, an imitator of Suleiman, his grandfather.

units.la: CAROLVS Philippi Hispaniarum Regis filius, qui paucis abhinc annis, nescio quo fato, interiit, dignus nobis visus est qui magnorum virorum catalogo hic adscriberetur, tum quòd tanto patre prognatus esset, tum etiam, quòd magni & generosissimi animi principem præ se ferret. Erat humeris paulò eminentioribus, facie satis decora, statura prægradi:at ingenio tanto tamque alto pollebat, vt non nisi magna meditaretur. Equitabat lubenter & sepissimè: pius erat erga egenos, vt de eo proferatur hoc exemplum, Cum miles quidam veteranus & egens ad eum venisset petiissetque eleemosynam, princeps eum interrogauit, quo sub principe militasset & stipendia meruisset, & cum respondisset se pro Carolo Quinto suo avo militasse: Tu, inquit princeps, dimicauisti pro principe magnanimo & suis nepotibus probitate maiore: & tunc imperauit vt certa pecunia cum quibusdam vestimentis, ei daretur.
units.tr: Charles, son of Philip, King of the Spains, who died a few years ago by some strange fate, seemed worthy to us to be enrolled here in the catalogue of great men, both because he was born of so great a father, and also because he displayed the character of a prince of a great and most generous spirit. He had somewhat prominent shoulders, a fairly handsome face, and a tall stature; yet he excelled in an intellect so great and so lofty that he meditated nothing but great things. He rode gladly and very often; he was kind towards the needy, so that this example is told of him: when an old soldier, poor and in want, came to him and asked for alms, the prince asked him under what prince he had served and earned his pay; and when he answered that he had served under his grandfather Charles V, he said: "You fought for a magnanimous prince, and for his grandsons of greater uprightness"; and then he ordered that a certain sum of money, with some clothing, be given to him.

units.la: IOANNES Austriacus, princeps virtute præstàs & re bellica clarus, diu præfuit, magna nominis sui fama, exercitui à rege Hispanorum misso aduersus Turcarum Imperatorem, quòd Venetis & Põtifici fœdere iunctis, belli socius, suppetias ferret. Vnde magni certè principis nomen est adeptus, rerum à se gestarum gloria: maximè verò insigni illa victoria, quam Christiani, in hoc bello eo duce, prœlio maritimo, consequuti sunt, contra ingentes hostium copias: quibus deletis prope ad internecionem, quindecim millia Christianorum liberati fuere è vinculis, multæ naues captæ, aliæ aquis obrutæ. Sed quid egerit nouissimis his annis in Belgas rebelles, à Rege Philippo missus, satis notum est ex historia quam de tumultu Belgico, & eius causa scripsit nuperrimè quidam Hispanus, translata & Gallico idiomate donata. Obiit apud Belgas, anno 1578. IAC. CVIATIVS. IVRISC. THOL.
units.tr: John of Austria, a prince distinguished for his valour and famous in matters of war, long commanded the army sent by the King of Spain against the Emperor of the Turks, since he was to bring aid as an ally in the war, the Venetians and the Pope being joined in alliance. Hence he certainly gained the name of a great prince, from the glory of his deeds; and especially from that famous victory which the Christians, under his leadership in this war, won in a naval battle against the enormous forces of the enemy. When these had been almost wholly destroyed, fifteen thousand Christians were freed from chains, many ships were captured, and others were sunk. But what he accomplished in these last years against the rebellious Belgians, sent by King Philip, is well enough known from the history which a certain Spaniard recently wrote about the Belgian tumult and its cause, and which has been translated and given to the French language. He died among the Belgians in the year 1578. JACOBUS CUJACIUS, JURIST, THOLOSAN.

units.la: IACOBVS Cuiatius, magnus Iurisconsultus Gallus, liberalibus disciplinis instructus, quibus pater eum à pueritia instituendum semper curauit, & literarū tū Græcarū tū Latinarum cognitionem adeptus, à domino Ferrario Iuris professore adductus est, vt Tholosæ legibus operam daret, in quibus paruo temporis spatio ita profecit, vt dignum sese reddiderit qui legendi gratia publicum suggestū ascenderet. Ascendit igitur illud, & tam fœliciter docuit iuuenis, vt ab omnibus fuerit admiratus. Porro tantam nominis famam, etiam initio consequutus est, vt omnes Gallicæ Academię supplices eum appellarint, Bituriges obtinuerint: apud quos aliquādiu docuit & suis discipulis multūm satisfecit. Cadurci de in illum asciuerunt, postea Valentini Delphinates, apud quos vxorem duxit: denique tātum effecerunt Bituriges vt illum denuò euocarint. Augustam Taurinorū tandem ab illustrissima Margareta Valesia ascitus, cū ibi annum commoratus esset, multis precibus Valentiam reuocatus est: & paulò post à Rege Consiliarij officio, in sua Gratianopolis Curia, ornatus, in qua residere minimè teneretur. Sed cūm in Delphinatu bellum flagraret, Biturigū ciuitatem, desideratus repetiit, cum vniuersa familia, vbi percharus est & ciuibus & omnibus legum studiolis. Doctissima eius scripta nulla egent commendatione, quòd satis perspecta sint & omnium manibus terantur.
units.tr: Jacques Cujas, the great French jurist, was trained in the liberal arts, in which his father always took care to instruct him from boyhood, and having attained a knowledge of both Greek and Latin letters, he was drawn by Master Ferrier, professor of law, to devote himself to the laws at Toulouse. In these studies he advanced in so short a time that he made himself worthy to mount the public chair for the purpose of lecturing. He mounted it, therefore, and taught so successfully, being still young, that he was admired by everyone. Moreover, he gained such a reputation, even at the start, that all the French academies begged him to come; the Bourges academy secured him, where for some time he taught and gave great satisfaction to his students. The people of Cahors then claimed him, afterwards the people of Valence in Dauphiné, where he married a wife; finally the people of Bourges so prevailed that they called him back again. At last the people of Turin took him up, at the invitation of the most illustrious Margaret of Valois, and when he had stayed there for a year, he was recalled to Valence with many entreaties; and shortly afterwards, by the King, he was adorned with the office of councillor in the court of his own Grenoble, though he was not bound to reside there. But when war raged in Dauphiné, he sought again, and was wanted again, the city of Bourges, with his whole household, where he was greatly beloved both by the citizens and by all the students of law. His most learned writings need no commendation, since they are sufficiently well known and are worn in everyone's hands.

units.la: ANTONIVS Augustinus Hispanus, tam cognitus est & inter homines doctos celebratus, vt non opus sit eius summam doctrinam commemorare, quāquidem eius doctissimi libri in Ius Ciuile & Pontificium editi, satis testari mihi videntur. RONSARD. P. PETRVS PONTVS DE THIARD
units.tr: Antonius Augustinus of Spain is so well known and celebrated among learned men that there is no need to recount his great learning; indeed, his most learned books on civil and pontifical law, which have been published, seem to me to bear sufficient witness to it. RONSARD. P. PETRUS PONTUS DE THIARD.

units.la: PETRVS Ronsardus, Vindocineus Poëtarum omnium huiusce ætatis, quamuis infinitorum, longè princeps, nobili ortus familia, Poësim Gallicam eò extulit & doctissimis eius scriptis ita ditauit & ornauit, vt Vergilianæ ferè vel etiā Homericæ (vnde tamen flores quosdā decerpsit) iure cōparari ea possit. Quid enim tot eius Poëmatibus eruditius, quid ornatius? quid nitidius vnquam dici& iuueniri queat? Ex his, tanquam è limpidissimo fonte emerserunt Poëtæ infiniti in hac Gallia, quorum alij Poëtarum nomine iure possunt insigniri, alij Simiarū: quod inepti sint & ridiculi huius nostri Gallici Maronis imitatores. Nam dum rithmi aut numeri, ex arte versificatoria, rationem habere sibi visi fuerint, inuentionem elegantem, dispositionem elocutionē, & fictionē ritè accommodatam (quæ est Poëticæ pars præcipua) valere sinunt: denique res negligunt dummodò plura verba effutierint. Huius Ronsardi, Rex Henricus 2. & Carolus 9. Henrici filius, studia præcipuè fouerūt, quibus vita functis, ferè semper tacuit.
units.tr: Pierre de Ronsard, of Vendôme, by far the prince of all the poets of this age, though there are countless others, sprang from a noble family and raised French poetry to such a height, and so enriched and adorned it with his most learned writings, that it may rightly be compared with Virgil's or even Homer's (from whom, nevertheless, he plucked some flowers). For what could be more erudite or more ornate than so many of his poems? What could ever be said or found more polished? From these, as from a most clear spring, have sprung forth countless poets in this France, of whom some may rightly be marked with the name of poets, others with the name of apes, because they are foolish and ridiculous imitators of our French Maro. For while they have thought that rhythms or metres, according to the art of versification, are all that matters, they let go the elegant invention, the arrangement, the diction, and the fitting fiction (which is the chief part of poetics); in short, they neglect the subject matter, provided only that they have poured out a great many words. King Henry II and Charles IX, son of Henry, especially fostered the studies of this Ronsard; after they had died, he almost always kept silent.

units.la: PONTVS Thiardus Matisconensis dignus est certè, qui virorum huiusce temporis doctrina illustrium numero ascribatur. Cum igitur effet in manibus eius effigies, eam hīc inserere non nolui, quamuis maiori laude dignū omnes docti eum existiment: verum summa eius eruditio, per vniuersam Galliā vel etiam alibi, ita est perspecta, vt eius laudes hīc decantare superuacaneum mihi videatur, cūm eius doctissimis operibus, tum Poëticis satis laudetur. Reges Galli semper illum amplexi sunt, & merito ab Henrico Christianissimo rege nostro, nunc amatur, qui quidem nuper, ob eius merita, Episcopatu Cabullinensi eum donauit. MATH. JOANNES. STADIUS. FRANC. IUNTINUS. FLOR.
units.tr: Pontus de Thiard of Mâcon is certainly deserving to be counted among the illustrious learned men of this time. Since his likeness was in my hands, I was not unwilling to insert it here, although all learned men consider him worthy of greater praise; but his great erudition is so well known throughout France, and even elsewhere, that to sing his praises here seems superfluous to me, since he is praised enough both by his most learned works and by his poetry. The kings of France have always embraced him, and rightly he is loved now by Henry, our most Christian king, who indeed lately, on account of his merits, bestowed on him the bishopric of Châlons. MATH. JOHANNES STADIUS. FRANC. JUNTINUS. FLOR.

units.la: JOANNES Stadius Leonouthensis Mathematicus egregius & Astrologus, nostra tepestate floruit. Hic eruditissimum librum Chronologiorum, & a doctis maximè desideratum inchoauit, quem tamen morte praeuentus non absoluit. Idem novam caelestium motuum diurnam dispensationem, quâ vocant Ephemerides, evulgavit: nã cùm eas, quas primus Joannes Regiomontanus, ignotas antea in lucem protulit: deinde Joannes Stoeflerus numeris ex eisdem hypothesibus produxit: demũ nostra ætate Cyprianus Leovitius splendida ac magna operis mole auxit: caelestium motuũ momētis non ita ad amussim respondere, per frequentes ac diligentes obseruationes deprehendisset, earũ emendatione est molitus. Idẽ operã in re Mathematica Serenissimo Sabaudiæ duci navavit. Tandem Parisiis Regii doctoris munere, publicè Mathematicis disciplinis tradendis, maxima cum laude functus est, quo tempore & mortuus est, anno domini M. D. LXXIX. ætatis verò suæ LI.
units.tr: Johannes Stadius of Leuven, an outstanding mathematician and astrologer, flourished in our time. He began a most learned book of chronologies, much desired by the learned, which, however, he did not complete, being prevented by death. He also published a new daily arrangement of the celestial motions, which they call Ephemerides; for when Johannes Regiomontanus first brought out those tables, previously unknown, then Johannes Stoeffler extended them with numbers from the same hypotheses, and finally in our age Cyprianus Leovitius enlarged them with a splendid and great mass of work; and, finding through frequent and careful observations that the moments of the celestial motions did not correspond so exactly, he set about correcting them. The same man devoted his labour to mathematics for the most serene Duke of Savoy. At last, at Paris, with the office of royal teacher, he discharged with the greatest praise the public teaching of the mathematical disciplines; at which time he also died, in the year of the Lord 1579, and in the fifty-first year of his age.

units.la: FRANCISCVS Iunctinus Florentiæ ex Iunctinorũ familia anno M.D.XXII. Nonis Martii natus est: qui cùm a parentibus ordini Ecclesiastico dicatus esset, sedulo est curatum, ut omnibus liberalibus disciplinis institueretur: in quibus per gradus omnes ita profecit, ut adolescens Doctoris Theologi insignibus summo cũ omniũ applausu decoraretur. Hic Lugduni tũ concionibus, tum scriptis sæpissimè de hæreticis splendidos triumphos reportauit: quod vel maximè ex disputationibus (quæ & exstant) de sanctissima Eucharistia habitis patet. Neque verò solũ in re Theologica excellit: verũ & quantũ ingenio valeret in Hætruscis scriptis, Francisci Petrarchæ Epigrammatibus illustrandis, adolescens ostendit. Sed licet in omnibus disciplinis nemini cedat: in Mathematicis tamen cũctis, in Astrologia præsertim, plurimorũ[?] qui in ea præstare videntur, luminibus officit: quod plurima ab eo opera edita, & propediem, Deo dante, edenda manifestant. GREGORIVS . XIII . PONT . MAX . AN . III. CARDIN . RENAT . ABIRAGIA [?]
units.tr: Francesco Giunti was born at Florence, of the family of the Giunti, on the Nones of March in the year 1522. Since his parents had dedicated him to the ecclesiastical order, care was diligently taken that he should be trained in all the liberal disciplines; in these he advanced through every grade, so that as a young man he was adorned with the insignia of a Doctor of Theology, with the highest applause of all. Here at Lyon, both in sermons and in writings, he very often won splendid triumphs over heretics; this is most clearly shown by the disputations on the most holy Eucharist, which were held and which still survive. Nor did he excel only in theology; as a young man he also showed how much he could do in Tuscan writings, in illustrating the epigrams of Francesco Petrarca. But although he yields to no one in any discipline, he nevertheless outshines the most eminent in all the mathematical sciences, especially astrology, as the many works published by him, and others soon to be published, God willing, make clear. GREGORY XIII, SUPREME PONTIFF, IN THE THIRD YEAR. CARDINAL RENATO ABIRAGIA [?]

units.la: GREGORIVS xiii. Bononiensis Hugo Boncopagnus Presbyter Cardinalis tt. Sãcti Sixti, 230. Christianorum Episcopus creatus, tertio Idus Maij, consecratus 8. Kalendas Iunij. Anno Domini 1572. Numeratur is ducetesimus [?] & trigesimus Pontifex, cui cura omnis & cogitatio, de utilitate ac salute communi: unde summam apud omnes admirationem & auctoritatem obtinet. Difficile mihi esset, quae is in pontificatu usque ad hac die instituerit aut egerit, subtiliter persequi: plus enim illa operae ac laboris desiderat, & nos ab eo maiora in dies expectamus. Tantu dicam, quod res est, & de Pio v. praedecessore suo, iam dictum est, eum adhuc id religionis, iustitiae, patientiae, liberalitatis, grati animi specimen dedisse, ut si ei tam longa dabitur vita, quam longam & ex admirabili quadam ipsius victus temperantia sperare debemus, & tempus reipublicae postulat, ad bene administrandam Dei ecclesiam consequentibus deinceps pontificibus exempla minime defutura videantur.
units.tr: Gregory XIII, Hugo Boncompagni of Bologna, priest and cardinal of the title of Saint Sixtus, created bishop of the Christians, was consecrated on the third day before the Ides of May, and crowned on the eighth day before the Kalends of June, in the year of the Lord 1572. He is counted the two hundred and thirty-first (or thereabouts) pontiff, one whose every care and thought concerns the common utility and salvation; whence he holds the highest admiration and authority among all. It would be difficult for me to trace in detail what he has established or accomplished in his pontificate up to this day; for that requires more effort and labour, and we expect greater things from him day by day. I will say only this, as the truth is, and as has already been said of Pius V, his predecessor: he has already given such a proof of religion, justice, patience, generosity and a grateful mind, that if he is granted so long a life as we ought to hope for, on account of a certain remarkable temperance in his way of living, and as the state of the commonwealth demands, the examples for the bishops who come after him, in administering God's Church well, will hardly seem to be lacking.

units.la: RENATVS Biragus Mediolanensis ex nobilissima familia adolescens adhuc in Senatorum collegiu cooptatus est: qui honor Mediolani est amplissimus, postea vero legatus in Gallia ad Francisci primum de maximis rebus missus, ab eo in Senatorum numeru Parisiensis curiae est allectus. Deinde Lugdunensi praesecturae praeponitur, quo munere administrato, in castris pecuniae tractandae quaestor summo cum imperio praeficitur: paulo post publicorum sigillorum regni custodia ei demandatur, & mortuo magno Cancellario, in demortui locum sufficitur. Tot muneribus ciuilibus integerrime administratis, ad Ecclesiasticos quoque, eosque praecipuos magistratus adscisciturnam [?] comitiis pontificiis maximo cum applausu est Cardinalis renunciatus: homo natus ad agendu, ac ita in negotiis pertractandis solers, ut omnia mira quadam dexteritate ex animi sententia tandem conficiat. CAROL. A LOTHARING. CARD. P. DEPINAC AR. ET C. LUG. GALLI PRI.[?]
units.tr: Renato Birago of Milan, of a most noble family, was co-opted into the college of senators while still a young man; this is a most distinguished honour in Milan. Afterwards he was sent as legate to France, to Francis I, concerning very important affairs, and by him was admitted to the number of senators of the Parisian court. Then he was placed over the prefecture of Lyon; after administering this office, he was given command of the finances in the camp, with supreme authority; shortly afterwards the custody of the royal seals of the kingdom was entrusted to him, and on the death of the great Chancellor he was put in the dead man's place. After administering so many civil offices with the utmost integrity, he was also taken into the ecclesiastical offices, and those the chief ones, and at the papal elections he was proclaimed cardinal with the greatest applause. A man born for action, and so skilful in handling affairs that he brings everything at last to completion according to his own mind, with a certain marvellous dexterity. CAROL. A LOTHARING. CARD. P. DEPINAC AR. ET C. LUG. GALLI PRI.[?]

units.la: CAROLUS Lotharenus Cardinalis unus est in toto orbe Christiano, qui praestantissimorum principum catalogo annumerari debeat, cū propter eius virtutem admirabilem, tum magnam eruditionem & eloquentiam, ecclesiae praesidium, qui semper hęresibus & Ecclesiae catholicae hostibus fortiter se opposuit, cuius rei, doctissimae orationes quas habuit, testimonium nobis proferunt. Concionabatur saepissimè, cum maxima auditorum frequentia, in suo Rhemorum Episcopatu, ubi percelebre gymnasium constituit. Galliae reges optimo eius consilio semper usi sunt, sine quo nihil fere agebatur. Henricus II. (qui eum magnis muneribus ornavit) Franciscus II. Carolus nonus Galliae Reges vita functi, eum semper unicè dilexerunt: Rex noster Henricus III. illum magni fecit, cuius maiestatem, in suo, è Polonis reditu, Lugduno, Avinionem sequutus est, ubi febre continua obiit, anno Domini 1575.
units.tr: Charles of Lorraine, Cardinal, is the one man in the whole Christian world who deserves to be counted among the most outstanding princes, both for his remarkable virtue and for his great learning and eloquence, a bulwark of the Church who has always stood firm against heresies and the enemies of the Catholic Church. The most learned orations he delivered bear witness to this. He preached very often, before very large audiences, in his own see of Reims, where he founded a most celebrated academy. The kings of France always made use of his excellent counsel, without which almost nothing was done. Henry II (who honoured him with great offices), Francis II and Charles IX, kings of France, when they died, always loved him above all others. Our king Henry III held him in high esteem, and followed his majesty from Poland to Lyons and then to Avignon, where he died of a continuous fever in the year of the Lord 1575.

units.la: PETRUS Depinac Archiepiscopus & Comes Lugdunensis, primatum in Galliis obtinens, nobilissima ortus familia, nobilissimi ingenij & optimae erga suos volùtatis specimè aliquod in dies magis ac magis edere videtur, ita ut eum tàto gradu, ad quem pervenisse illum videmus, dignissimum omnes qui illius generosissimam voluntatem agnoscunt, liberè profiteantur. Liberalis est erga eos qui eius beneficiis digni ab eo fuerint existimati: non enim ignorat, vir prudens, quomodo in quemuis quisque beneficia debeat collocare. Caeterū admirabili rerum propè omnium scientia & praecipuè Theologiae doctrina, pollet, & se talem reipsa praebet, qualè certè vult videri: tanta est enim eius probitas, ut quemadmodū authoritate & dignitate omnibus aliis praestat, sic vitae & morum integritate facillimè omnes alios superet. Quam propensò sit animo erga religionē catholicam, & universam Rempublicam indicat ea doctissima oratio, quam Blesiis, in publico ordinum Galliae conventu, habuit.
units.tr: Peter Dépinac, Archbishop and Count of Lyons, holding the primacy in France, of a most noble family, seems to show some specimen of his most noble talent and excellent goodwill towards his own people more and more with each passing day, so that all who recognise his most generous will freely declare him most worthy of the rank to which we see him have risen.
